title: Nutrient addition regulates plant fungal diseases through functional group-specific pathways in an alpine meadow
abstract: The response of plant fungal diseases to nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) addition is crucial for ecosystem stability, yet the functional group-specific mechanisms and interannual dynamics remain unclear. We conducted a three-year N and P factorial experiment in a typical alpine meadow. We found that nutrient-pathogen interactions are highly functional group-specific. N addition directly increased forb pathogen load, whereas P addition indirectly suppressed it by enhancing plant diversity. Conversely, grass pathogen loads were synergistically promoted by both N and P, while legume and sedge diseases responded only to N. Furthermore, interannual climate variability (warm-season temperature and humidity) independently drove disease dynamics exclusively in grasses. Despite these pathogen fluctuations, community-level aboveground biomass was largely maintained through potential compensatory mechanisms. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that nutrient enrichment regulates plant diseases through divergent pathways. We propose that functional group-specific pathogen loads can serve as sensitive ecological indicators for monitoring global change impacts in alpine ecosystems.

title: Sensitive response range of alpine meadow degradation on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau: Nonlinear fragmentation under pika and mowing disturbances
abstract: The morphological evolution of degraded patches and their sensitive response ranges in alpine meadows are key scientific issues in grassland ecosystem management. Based on a two-factor, three-gradient controlled experiment conducted on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau (QTP) from 2018 to 2022, this study extracted landscape metrics of bare patches in alpine meadows using UAV imagery. By integrating K-means clustering, landscape ecological indices, linear mixed models, and the adjacent gradient change rate method, we systematically analyzed the spatiotemporal dynamics of landscape fragmentation and its sensitive response ranges in alpine meadows. The results showed that: (1) Several area-related landscape indices, particularly AREA, MNA, and PLAND, exhibited a pronounced “V”-shaped temporal pattern, with 2020 as the critical turning point. Thereafter, driven by the significant interactions among mowing, pika density, and year (Year × Mowing × Pika, P < 0.01), meadow degradation was characterized by an increase in patch number, expansion of patch area, and enhanced landscape connectivity, reflecting a two-stage process of patch initiation, expansion, and coalescence; (2) The K2 area class (28.63 m 2 ) represents a key potential transitional form in the degradation process and is highly sensitive to disturbances; (3) Among the two disturbance factors, mowing intensity plays a decisive role in determining patch geometry and edge expansion, whereas pika density primarily influences the degree of spatial isolation among patches; (4) Adjacent gradient change rate analysis identifies that the sensitive disturbance ranges associated with nonlinear transitions in landscape patterns occur under medium-high pika densities and medium-high mowing intensities. Therefore, adaptive management of alpine meadows should prioritize monitoring the dynamics of K2 patches to prevent their transition into large patches, while strictly controlling mowing intensity and pika density below the moderate level. Early intervention (within three years of disturbance onset) is also recommended to prevent irreversible nonlinear degradation of landscape patterns. These results will provide a theoretical reference for the early warning and disturbance regulation of patchy degradation of alpine meadows.

title: A hierarchical NFI–GEDI approach for aboveground biomass estimation and uncertainty propagation in subtropical forests of southeastern China
abstract: The GEDI mission provides critical data for estimating forest aboveground biomass (AGB), but it relies on plot-calibrated models. The National Forest Inventories (NFIs) offer an extensive plot network to support modeling while minimizing field costs. Nevertheless, GEDI footprints seldom coincide with NFI plots, and studies that couple them to monitor AGB while tracking uncertainty propagation remain limited. We developed a hierarchical approach for AGB estimation while propagating uncertainty and applied it in a case study in Zhejiang Province, China. First, airborne laser scanning (ALS)-based height-transformation models mitigated footprint–plot misalignment by converting mean tree height from NFI plots into a GEDI-compatible RH95 proxy, enabling NFI plots to train GEDI-based AGB models and expanding samples by 6.5-fold relative to ALS-supported plots alone. Second, Environmental Similarity and Random Forest were fused via a geostatistical ensemble meta-model (ER-GEM) with spatially varying coefficients to capture covariate similarity, nonlinear relationships, and spatial heterogeneity. The ER-GEM achieved moderate predictive performance (R 2 = 0.65; RMSE = 27.63 Mg/ha). Third, uncertainty was quantified and propagated, and Shapley decomposition was applied to apportion uncertainty. The dominant contribution came from RH95 mapping uncertainty and ER-GEM parameter and residual uncertainty, accounting for 69.12% of total predictive uncertainty. The resulting AGB estimate (96.16 Mg/ha) was consistent with the NFI estimate (95.90 Mg/ha) and fell within the 95% confidence interval. County- and prefecture-level rRMSEs (11.40% and 12.15%) were lower than those of five public AGB products. This study supports NFI-consistent regional AGB estimation and provides a pathway for quantifying the propagation of associated uncertainties.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of carbon storage economic value in the Poyang Lake Basin: A multi-scenario simulation and machine learning approach
abstract: Understanding the dynamic response of carbon storage (CS) economic value to land use and cover change (LUCC) is pivotal for achieving regional carbon neutrality and sustainable spatial planning. However, existing research often overlooks the synergistic effects of multi-scenario simulations and the non-linear driving mechanisms of carbon economic fluctuations in complex watershed systems. In this study, we proposed an integrated assessment framework by coupling the Patch generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model, the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model, and the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) method to quantify the spatiotemporal evolution of CS economic value in the Poyang Lake Basin (PYLB) from 1980 to 2020. Furthermore, these dynamics were projected through 2040 under three distinct scenarios: natural development (NDS), ecological protection (EPS), and urban development (UDS). An interpretable XGBoost-SHAP approach was employed to decipher the non-linear impacts of socioeconomic and environmental factors on carbon value distribution. The results indicate that although total CS decreased by 97.889 Tg from 1980 to 2020, its economic value increased nearly sixfold, driven by the dramatic appreciation of carbon shadow prices. By 2040, the EPS is projected to achieve a CS gain of 12.611 Tg and the highest economic returns, whereas the NDS and UDS exhibit persistent declines in carbon sequestration potential. Specifically, the digital elevation model (DEM) emerged as the primary determinant shaping the spatial heterogeneity of carbon value, followed by slope and proximity to urban centers. This study concludes that strategic land use optimization, particularly through ecological conservation mandates, can effectively mitigate carbon loss and maximize regional ecological wealth. These findings provide a robust quantitative reference for carbon market design and the implementation of carbon neutrality policies in rapidly urbanizing watersheds.

title: Plantation expansion reshapes water and carbon patterns in Northeast China's forests: A high carbon sink at the cost of inefficient water use
abstract: Climate warming is reshaping forest ecosystems by altering both carbon and water cycles, yet it remains poorly understood whether rapid plantation expansion can match the ecological efficiency of natural forests. This knowledge gap is critical, given global afforestation efforts amidst escalating climate stress. Here, we challenge the simplistic ‘high carbon gain–high water demand’ paradigm by positing that plantations and natural forests operate under fundamentally distinct biogeochemical regimes. Across Northeast China (2005–2020), we integrated multi-source remote sensing and meteorological data to quantify gross primary productivity (GPP), evapotranspiration (ET), and water-use efficiency (WUE). Both forest types increased in GPP, ET, and WUE, yet plantations consistently showed higher GPP and ET but lower WUE. In long-term stable stands, mean WUE was 1.84 g C m −2 mm −1 in natural forests, higher than 1.80 g C m −2 mm −1 in plantations. Mean GPP was 1067.72 g C m −2 in plantations, exceeding 965.42 g C m −2 in natural forests, and its annual increase was markedly greater in plantations (6.04 vs. 5.63 g C m −2 yr −1 ). ET increased significantly in plantations (1.89 mm yr −1 ) but not in natural forests. Structural equation and random forest models revealed contrasting association patterns: stand structural and compositional factors made the largest contribution to WUE in both natural and planted forests, accounting for 60.9% and 52.7% of the total normalized importance, respectively, while soil factors also played an important role in planted forests, contributing 30.1%. These results indicate that plantation expansion in temperate humid forests can enhance carbon uptake, but often was associated with greater water consumption and lower WUE.

title: Invasive aquatic species drive losses in functional diversity despite no apparent loss in taxonomic diversity
abstract: Invasive species are a major threat to global biodiversity, yet their functional impacts on ecosystems are less studied than dispersal and establishment. These impacts are multifaceted, cascading through ecosystems via trophic interactions and indirect habitat alteration, and may intensify through interactions with other invaders. This study investigated the impacts of apple snail ( Pomacea maculata ) and blue crab ( Callinectes sapidus ) on habitat quality, and the taxonomic and functional composition of macroinvertebrate communities in the Lower Ebro River, Spain. A set of a priori hypotheses about expected effects were tested, providing a framework for future research in other invaded systems. Results show that both invaders are associated with degraded habitat quality. Suspended solids were twice as high and chlorophyll- a fourfold higher in invaded than control habitats, indicating intensified nutrient mobilization. These changes cascaded to impact community structure. While taxonomic richness, abundance, and diversity remained stable, composition shifted. Sensitive taxa like Ephemeroptera and Trichoptera declined, replaced by tolerant taxa including Coleoptera, Odonata, and Gastropoda. Functional indicators revealed strong homogenization in invaded sites, with reduced functional richness and diversity. Traits like small body size, resistance forms, and predatory feeding were more prevalent in invaded habitats. Impacts intensified where both invaders co-occurred, supporting the invasional meltdown hypothesis. This is one of the first studies assessing ecological consequences for two co-occurring invasive species, from distinct trophic levels without shared evolutionary history. We conclude that functional indicators are more sensitive than taxonomic metrics and provide mechanistic information about the impacts of invasive species in aquatic ecosystems.

title: Visual structure, perceived experience and flow-direction effects in canyon river landscapes: An integrated GIS–VR study of the Xiling gorge, China
abstract: Canyon river landscapes combine complex topography, dynamic hydrological processes, and human interventions, creating highly heterogeneous visual environments. This study proposes an integrated GIS–VR framework to examine visual structure, perceptual experience, and flow-direction effects in the Xiling Gorge, the longest and most complex section of the Three Gorges, China. GIS-based visual metrics identified eight landscape visual character types along the river corridor. A VR immersive experiment with 40 participants evaluated perceptual responses across 41 panoramic viewpoints and revealed four experiential dimensions: Perceived Grandeur–Arousal, Hydrodynamic Dynamics, Spatial Compression, and Landscape Purity. Multiple linear regression showed that Grandeur–Arousal was the strongest predictor of landscape preference, followed by Spatial Compression and Hydrodynamic Dynamics. Correlation analysis further indicated that terrain complexity, visual openness, natural landscape compositions, and anthropogenic elements acted as key structural drivers of perception. Flow-direction analysis demonstrated that upstream versus downstream navigation systematically influenced perceptual indicators, particularly in reservoir and transitional segments. These results suggest that canyon river perception emerges from interactions between visual structure, experiential dynamics, and directional movement, highlighting the importance of considering movement-based viewing sequences in understanding linear landscape perception. The findings provide implications for landscape management, tourism planning, and conservation of large-scale river corridors.

title: The negative effects of invasive plants on ecosystem multifunctionality weaken with increase in temperature
abstract: Invasive plants introduced outside their native ranges by human activities are posing significant threats to ecosystem functions. Nevertheless, the effects driven by plant invasions are scantily described in relation to the ability of ecosystems providing multiple functions simultaneously (i.e., ecosystem multifunctionality, EMF). Given that climate warming has been shown to influence the ecological consequences of invasive plants, how these impacts vary along temperature gradients also requires further in-depth investigation. Meanwhile, the impact of indigenous species provides a better reference for assessing the consequences of invasive species. In this study, we collected plant and soil samples from beneath either invasive Xanthium species ( Xanthium spinosum L. and Xanthium italicum Moretti) or indigenous Xanthium species ( Xanthium sibiricum Patr.) and their adjacent areas without Xanthium at 12 sites in northwest China. We found that invasive Xanthium was associated with lower EMF compared to the ‘without Xanthium ’ treatment, while indigenous Xanthium exhibited a non-significant upward trend. The negative association between invasive Xanthium and EMF became weaker with increasing temperature, while there was no significant interaction between indigenous Xanthium and warming. According to the results of piecewise structural equation modelling (pSEM), abiotic factors were more strongly associated with EMF responses in invaded ecosystems, whereas biotic factors showed stronger associations in indigenous ecosystems. Our study highlights that the negative association between invasive plants and EMF is less pronounced with increasing temperature. This may provide a theoretical basis for understanding the consequences of plant invasions and for managing invasive plants under different climatic conditions.

title: Exploring climate change exposure of the Mediterranean Sea through 3D climate velocity
abstract: Climate change is increasingly challenging the durability of marine conservation and spatial planning approaches that rely on contemporary climate baselines. In response, the identification and protection of climate refugia – areas expected to remain relatively stable under climate change – has emerged as a key strategy for climate-smart conservation. However, in marine systems, refugia are commonly delineated using surface conditions alone, overlooking the vertical structure of the ocean. Here, we assess climate change exposure across the entire Mediterranean Sea water column using an analogue-based climate velocity framework in three-dimensional space. We compared present (2006–2030) and near-future (2031–2055) temperature conditions using nine climate variables, constraining the search for climatic analogues within ecologically meaningful depth ranges. Projected temperature conditions shifted in three dimensions across most of the basin: 45.8% of the Mediterranean exhibited combined horizontal and vertical displacement of climate conditions, while an additional 13.4% showed predominantly vertical shifts, indicating that climate change does not operate solely through horizontal redistribution. The basin-wide mean three-dimensional climate velocity was 2.98 km yr −1 , with pronounced depth- and region-specific differences. Climate exposure was highest in the euphotic zone and in deep regions such as the Ionian Sea, whereas deeper biozones of the Western Mediterranean appeared comparatively more stable than those of the Eastern region. By integrating depth-resolved climate data within a fully three-dimensional framework, this study provides the first basin-scale assessment of climate velocity across the Mediterranean water column and offers a robust foundation for climate-smart conservation and planning.

title: Remote sensing reveals nesting habitat vulnerability for sea turtles in Costa Rica over forty years
abstract: Sandy beaches are dynamic ecosystems where erosion and accretion continually modify shorelines and sea turtle nesting habitat, conditioning their reproductive success. Although quantifying beach dynamics is essential for evaluating erosion risk and habitat vulnerability, long-term assessments remain scarce worldwide. Here, we provide the first consistent four-decade (1984–2024) satellite-based assessment of nesting-habitat change for sea turtles in Northwest Costa Rica, using shoreline change rates as indicators of habitat vulnerability across eight major nesting beaches. Our findings showed that six of the eight studied beaches remained stable over time, suggesting a capacity for shoreline recovery despite the observed long-term negative trends. Playa Grande and Ventanas, at Las Baulas National Park (PNMB), experience moderate erosion, retreating at a rate of −0.79 m yr −1 (95% CI: −0.96 to −0.73 m yr −1 ) and − 0.50 m yr −1 (95% CI: −0.62 to −0.37 m yr −1 ), respectively. Although all beaches showed alternating erosion-accretion cycles, four sites, especially PNMB beaches, shifted to sustained erosion after 2008 without recovery to this date, suggesting changes in sediment dynamics that may be linked to watershed and coastal management outside the park. Kernel density analysis revealed high vulnerability at Playa Grande, where erosion hotspots overlapped historically important nesting zones for the critically endangered East Pacific leatherback population. Conversely, Nancite, Naranjo, and Zapotillal were less vulnerable (minimal retreat or stable trends) and may serve as key nesting refugia under accelerating coastal change. Our study provides a transferable shoreline indicator framework applicable to nesting beaches worldwide to assess habitat vulnerability, identify early warning signals of nesting habitat change, and support adaptive conservation and coastal management.

title: Grassland expansion increases evapotranspiration-linked precipitation contributions in the Qilian Mountains through moisture recycling
abstract: Land use changes induced by afforestation and grassland restoration can alter evapotranspiration (ET), thereby influencing precipitation (Prec) through atmospheric moisture recycling. The land use in the Qilian Mountains of Northwest China (QLMs) has undergone obvious changes over the past four decades. In particular, the grassland has been expanded rapidly, and resulted in its dominant role in absolute area (59% of the entire region) and change area (37% of the total change area). However, the influence of these changes on atmospheric hydrological processes remains unclear. Hence, we aim to explore the impacts of grassland expansion on ET and the resulting ET-linked Prec contribution in the QLMs based on moisture trajectories analysis. The results showed that grasslands contribute to approximately three-quarters of the ET. Notably, grassland expansion accounted for 24% of the regional ET changes, which subsequently increased its contribution to local Prec via moisture recycling. Under a fixed-trajectory assumption, ET from grasslands contributes 53.7 mm/year to local Prec, accounting for 14% of local total Prec. Of this amount, 34.6 mm/year of Prec is linked to the expanded grassland ET. The contributions of ET from the QLMs to Prec of the Hexi Corridor are strongest in the Shiyang River Basin, followed by the Heihe River Basin, and weakest in the Shule River Basin. This study quantifies the increased ET linked Prec contribution associated with grassland expansion in the QLMs and the Hexi Corridor. These findings offer new insights into the vegetation and atmospheric interactions of hydrological processes in the context of land use and climate change.

title: Assessment of ecological network resilience under SSP-RCP scenarios: Multi-scenario simulations and conservation zoning along the urban-rural gradient
abstract: Enhancing ecological network (EN) resilience is a critical measure for maintaining ecosystem stability under the combined stresses of climate change and human activity. However, existing research has primarily focused on large-scale assessments of current ecological networks, with limited attention to disturbance resistance under future development scenarios. Furthermore, current EN optimization strategies overlook spatial heterogeneity along the urban-rural gradient, limiting local-scale conservation applicability. This study employs the System Dynamics (SD) model, the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model, and node dynamic disturbance simulation to explore EN resilience in Jiangsu Province under different socio-climatic scenarios from 2000 to 2035. The urban-rural gradient analysis method is applied to assess ecological protection areas at the local scale. The results indicate that: (1) From 2020 to 2035, ecological source area declined to 9142 km 2 under SSP5-RCP8.5 (7.0% below 2000) and to 9368 km 2 under SSP2-RCP4.5 (4.7%), with corridor numbers decreasing under both scenarios. (2) EN resilience thresholds declined under both scenarios, reaching 0.41 under SSP5-RCP8.5—7.9% below the 2000 baseline—while the decline was less pronounced under SSP2-RCP4.5 (0.43), highlighting the critical role of socioeconomic pathways in shaping EN resilience trajectories. (3) The gradient protection strategy indicates that 78.38% of ecological protection areas are located in outer suburban and ecological zones, with resilience node density increasing 3.5-fold from urban (3.81%) to ecological areas (13.27%). This research provides a scientific basis for regional ecological conservation planning and proposes management and optimization strategies at an operational scale, holding significant practical implications.

title: Integrating ecological niche modeling and machine learning to optimize alfalfa variety deployment for climate-resilient forage systems
abstract: Rising demand for livestock products intensifies pressure on forage systems globally, yet continuous climate change threatens alfalfa ( Medicago sativa L.) productivity and stability due to mismatches between variety traits and local environments. Here we coupled MaxEnt ecological niche modeling with Random Forest regression to assess current and future (2021−2100) climatic suitability and yield potential for 27 major alfalfa varieties across China under three shared socioeconomic pathways (SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, SSP5–8.5). Models achieved excellent predictive accuracy (mean AUC = 0.81–0.96). Under future scenarios, 11 varieties exhibited consistent yield increases (0.68–66.70% above current levels), while 12 showed persistent declines (1.75–39.67% losses), a bifurcation reflecting contrasting adaptive strategies. Optimized variety deployment in three representative regions achieved yield gains of 8.7–35.7%, translating to additional protein output of 0.44–1.46 t ha −1 and enhanced carbon sequestration of 4.30–14.28 t ha −1 . Our findings demonstrate that data-informed variety deployment can simultaneously enhance forage productivity and ecosystem services under climate change, providing a framework that is applicable to the same crop types in other regions and moderately transferable to neighboring countries with similar ecological conditions.

title: Weighted Jaccard similarity: A threshold-free multivariate indicator of correlation-network reorganization across coral, freshwater, and climate systems
abstract: Detecting ecological tipping points remains a central challenge for environmental monitoring. Classical early warning signals based on critical slowing down operate on univariate time series and are structurally insensitive to multivariate correlation reorganization. The Weighted Jaccard (WJ) similarity index has been proposed as a threshold-free indicator of such reorganization. The current study presents a revision of a prior submission in response to reviewer concerns regarding the appropriateness of independent identically distributed (IID) permutation inference for spatially and temporally dependent ecological data. We re-analyse three canonical tipping point datasets — global coral reef bleaching (Global Coral Bleaching Database, 41,361 records, 36 environmental variables, 1980–2020), U.S. lake eutrophication (EPA National Lakes Assessment 2007, 2012, 2022, 23 water-chemistry variables, three independent surveys spanning 15 years), and global climate teleconnection networks (19 monthly NOAA indices, 1950–2024) — under substrate-matched structure-preserving null inference. Across all three substrates, WJ values are robust and replicable; their statistical significance is contingent on the cluster scale at which the structure-preserving null is applied, and the cluster scale itself functions as a parameterized measurement axis. In coral, the architectural reorganization signal survives the finest spatial null tested (site-level clustering at K ≈ 10,000 sites) in every window-and-method combination examined. In lake, the signal weakens at the canonical 9-region EPA ecoregion clustering and stabilizes at finer resolutions; the trophic-gradient WJ signature replicates across all three independent surveys. In climate, the signal collapses by 6-month block permutation and is not distinguishable from the null under multivariate phase-randomized surrogates. Three substrate-fingerprint dimensions (continuous-discrete Type 1 gap, sign-treatment Type 2 gap, substrate-projection Type 6 gap, and direct pair-level sign-flip rate) are formally distinguishable across substrates (Kruskal-Wallis p < 10 −3 for the asymmetric-Tversky Type 3 gap). Sign-preservation is universal at meaningful correlation magnitudes (|r| ≥ 0.2) across all three substrates (< 3% sign-flip rate). Findings position WJ as a substrate-fingerprint indicator with explicit inferential boundary conditions for ecological monitoring rather than as a universally significant tipping-point detector. The conditions under which WJ is appropriate, and the substrate-specific cluster scale at which dependence is appropriately modeled, are derived empirically from the same dataset to which the indicator is applied.

title: Verification of microhabitat adjustment on the improvement of periphytic algae integrity in undammed river: Evidence from the Chishui River basin, China
abstract: To enhance the integrity of periphytic algae communities in the Chishui River, we conducted four systematic sampling surveys (March 2023, July 2023, November 2023, and March 2024) and one in-situ experiment across the Chishui River basin in China. Based on three core parameters—Shannon index, cell density, and species richness—we successfully developed the Periphytic Algae Index of Biotic Integrity (P-IBI) and employed Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS) to conduct an in-depth analysis of periphytic algae community structure in the Chishui River. The results revealed significant structural differences between the upstream and midstream-downstream periphytic algae communities. Accordingly, we established tailored ecological health restoration benchmarks specifically for the upstream and midstream-downstream sections of the Chishui River. Further experimental investigations demonstrated that the Periphytic Algae Index of Biotic Integrity and its core parameters exhibited high sensitivity to water depth (H) and flow velocity (V). Utilizing P-IBI as the key response variable, in conjunction with five modeling factors— ammonia nitrogen (NH₃-N), total phosphorus (TP), total nitrogen (TN), water depth (H), and flow velocity (V)—we constructed a P-IBI predictive mathematical model through Generalized Additive Models (GAM). Building upon this foundation, we developed hydrodynamic models for typical river reaches in Chishui Town (CST) and Chishui City (CSC), respectively, using the Mike21 hydrodynamic simulation modeling framework, and subsequently implemented microhabitat adjustments. Following these adjustments, the P-IBI values in the two river reaches achieved substantial improvements of 2%–3% and 20%–30%, respectively, which compellingly validated the effectiveness of our constructed models and implemented measures. Microhabitat adjustments yield greater ecological benefits in degraded river reaches than in near-natural systems, as demonstrated by contrasting P-IBI responses (2%–3% vs. 20%–30%) between geomorphologically stable and hydromorphologically altered reaches.

title: Beyond outcome variance: addressing ranking instability via an RSSI-SA-ADF framework for adaptive ecological restoration decision-making
abstract: Traditional variance-oriented sensitivity analysis (e.g., the Sobol’ index) cannot identify whether parameter uncertainty undermines the ranking of restoration strategies — a critical gap, since management failures in ecological restoration commonly arise from structural ranking reversals rather than outcome fluctuations. This study proposes the Ranking Stability Sensitivity Index (RSSI), a decision-oriented metric quantifying each parameter's marginal contribution to ranking reversals, and integrates it into a Sensitivity Analysis-driven Adaptive Decision Framework (SA-ADF) that activates multi-objective optimisation only when structural instability is detected. Validated on 24-month longitudinal data from three heavy-metal-contaminated farmland restoration projects in Henan Province, China, results reveal a “risk-driver reversal” phenomenon: remediation cost dominates outcome variance (Sobol’ S T = 0.35) yet stakeholder preference weight β ESV drives ranking reversals (RSSI = 0.25). In independent Phase II testing, the RSSI-based early-warning system reduces both false-alarm and miss-detection rates by 7 percentage points relative to a fixed-threshold benchmark (Cohen's d > 2.00). A controlled adaptive-baseline experiment further demonstrates that replacing RSSI with Sobol’ within the identical SA-ADF architecture increases total cost by 324% (0.53 vs. 2.25 M CNY), isolating RSSI's specific contribution beyond adaptivity alone. Adaptive interventions reduce replanting rates by 68.6% and yield a conservative ROI of 109.0%. These findings indicate that ecological restoration governance should prioritize structural parameters (e.g., preference weights) over high-variance but ranking-stable technical inputs, and that RSSI provides a tractable tool for implementing this shift.

title: Spatiotemporal changes and projections of suitable habitat for the Hainan Eld's deer under climate change
abstract: The Hainan Eld's deer ( Rucervus eldii hainanus ) is a nationally protected Class I species in China and one of the most endangered cervids globally. Climate change is profoundly affecting its population dynamics by driving habitat loss and fragmentation and altering the extent of suitable habitat. To assess habitat suitability, we employed an optimized MaxEnt framework integrating 154 species occurrence points and 14 environmental predictors, which uniquely included extreme climatic indicators for heat-induced drought and torrential precipitation. Suitability maps were generated for the present-day baseline, contemporary extreme events, and three future scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, SSP585) for the 2050s and 2070s. Six bioclimatic factors emerged as primary drivers shaping the deer's distribution: precipitation during the driest month (Bio14), mean temperature of the driest quarter (Bio9), isothermality (Bio3), precipitation in the warmest quarter (Bio18), mean diurnal temperature variation (Bio2), and precipitation in the wettest quarter (Bio16), together accounting for 73.4% of the permutation importance. Under current baseline climate, potential habitat (totaling 8501.60 km 2 ) predominantly occurs within open savanna landscapes of southwestern Hainan, whereas highly suitable zones cover merely 956.47 km 2 , equivalent to 2.82% of the island's total area. Relative to baseline estimates, suitable areas expanded substantially under drought extremes but diminished under anomalously wet conditions. Future projections reveal habitat expansion across all climate trajectories, with the most pronounced gain under SSP126 in the 2050s, expanding total suitable habitat to 12,746.68 km 2 . Concurrently, the centroid of suitable habitat shifts southwestward. Collectively, these findings suggest that across diverse climatic regimes, the Hainan Eld's deer consistently favors relatively warm and arid environments. This work offers a scientific foundation for climate-resilient conservation strategies, habitat rehabilitation, and population stewardship of island-endangered ungulates.

title: Structural gains mask functional declines in forest landscape connectivity: the role of compound thresholds under urbanization
abstract: Forest Landscape Connectivity (FLC) serves as a pivotal ecological indicator for preserving process integrity and informing forest management, which is commonly represented by the complementary dimensions of structural (FLSCI) and functional connectivity (FLFCI). However, the distinct response mechanisms between them have not been systematically explored. In rapidly urbanizing regions, forest landscapes are increasingly shaped by the spatial competition between developmental encroachment and ecological restoration, leading to intensified divergence in the responses of FLSCI and FLFCI. Focusing on Guangdong Province, a highly urbanised region in China, this study evaluates FLC from both structural and functional dimensions. By integrating multi-scenario land-use simulations with interpretable machine learning methods, we analyze their spatial-temporal dynamics and underlying driving mechanisms. Results indicate: (1) under all projection scenarios, FLSCI shows a continuous improvement, whereas FLFCI exhibits significant spatial degradation, declining from 68.38% to 67.19% by 2034. This divergence reveals that structural gains do not necessarily synchronize with the recovery of ecological functions. Notably, the reduction in high-connectivity patches and the intensity of negative growth at the county scale under the moderate-intensity development pathway exceed those of the high-intensity pathway, indicating a higher potential risk of degradation. (2) FLFCI exhibits a heightened sensitivity to changes in driving factors compared to FLSCI, characterized by distinct non-linear relationships and threshold effects. The overall response magnitude of FLFCI with SHAP values spanning −25,000 to 10,000 is greater than that of FLSCI (−50 to 30), confirming the unique value of functional connectivity as an early-warning indicator. And the compound threshold lowers the trigger point for functional collapse. (3) the spatial effects of driving forces are non-stationary, with their contribution patterns exhibiting significant differentiation across both the north-south gradient and the structural-functional dimensions. Low-low (LL) clusters of FLFCI are highly clustered with steep profiles in the Pearl River Delta and coastal areas. This study suggests that relying solely on structural connectivity indicators may underestimate the risks of ecological network degradation, whereas functional connectivity indicators can capture latent ecological losses under moderate development scenarios at an earlier stage. Forest management should transition from area-based compensation to threshold-guided precision interventions, prioritizing the protection of high-connectivity patches within high-high clusters and the restoration of low-connectivity patches within LL clusters, thereby enhancing ecological security in rapidly urbanizing regions

title: Spatial non-stationarity and causal pathways of hydro-thermal responses in alpine grasslands intertwined with climate warming and surface disturbances
abstract: Against a backdrop of climate warming and increasing humidity, alpine grasslands along the northeastern margin of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau have exhibited a widespread “greening” trend. However, the mechanisms underpinning this apparent recovery are characterized by pronounced spatial non-stationarity. Conventional approaches based on global assumptions are insufficient to disentangle the complex interplay between climatic benefits and anthropogenic disturbances in heterogeneous terrain. Focusing on Tianzhu County in the eastern Qilian Mountains, this study integrates long-term (2001−2023) net primary productivity (NPP) data with multi-source environmental variables, employing spatial clustering, geographically weighted regression (GWR), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to systematically unravel the nonlinear drivers and causal pathways of alpine grassland dynamics. The results indicate that: (1) NPP increased significantly across 98.45% of the study area, although the quality of recovery exhibits marked spatial heterogeneity. (2) Multidimensional clustering identifies a representative “low-elevation ecological trap” (Zone 2), which, despite possessing the highest moisture-driven potential in the region ( Coef f Pre = 0.28 ), is highly exposed to anthropogenic disturbances due to the absence of topographic barriers, resulting in substantial interannual variability ( CV = 0.20 ). In contrast, mid to high-elevation areas (Zone 4) demonstrate compensatory growth following the release of environmental pressures. (3) SEM analysis confirms a causal feedback loop characterized by “topographic constraint–hydrothermal offset–disturbance interception”: elevation imposes a metabolic ceiling on ecosystem development ( β = − 0.413 , p < 0.001 ), while warming induces a pronounced hydrothermal offset effect ( r = − 0.36 ). Critically, in areas lacking topographic protection, human activities bypass natural mediating processes and exert a direct suppressive impact on ecosystem functioning ( β = − 0.185 , p < 0.001 , Partial R 2 = 3.99 % ). These findings demonstrate that grassland recovery in arid and semi-arid regions is not governed solely by climatic benefits, but rather by the dynamic interplay between natural potential and anthropogenic interception. The proposed mechanistic framework of a “structural ecological trap” provides a novel basis for differentiated, precision-oriented management and adaptive governance in ecologically fragile alpine regions.

title: Reconciling multiple planning objectives at the county level in China: A novel landscape functional zoning approach considering both landscape services synergy and landscape character integrity
abstract: As urbanization rapidly advances, the coordination issues among multiple spatial planning initiatives at the county level in China are becoming increasingly severe. Problems such as landscape fragmentation and the loss of distinct landscape characteristics due to improper management are becoming more pronounced. Therefore, reconciling the contradictions between various planning objectives is crucial for the effective overall governance of county landscapes. This study focuses on harmonizing multiple planning goals and priorities, proposing a new method for landscape functional zoning that takes into account both the synergy of landscape services and landscape integrity. Using Anlu County in Hubei Province as the empirical research site, cluster analysis based on six landscape character elements identified 34 landscape character types and 894 landscape character units. These units were used to assess seven key landscape services related to ecological maintenance, agricultural production, and human living conditions. Based on the systematic conservation planning, flexible scenarios were then created using Marxan with Zones to explore the trade-offs and synergistic effects among these services to establish primary landscape functional zones. Subsequently, secondary zoning was conducted in eCognition using the semi-automatic image segmentation technology based on the identified landscape character types, and tailored landscape management strategies for each zone were proposed. This method resulted in the delineation of 4 primary and 36 secondary landscape functional zones in Anlu County. Each zone maximizes the synergistic effects of landscape services while maintaining the integrity of landscape characters, transforming landscape management and protection from fragmented elements to a cohesive landscape space. This enhances zoning management efficiency and holds significant implications for the overall management and protection of county landscapes.

title: Multi-objective optimization of the water-land-energy-food-carbon nexus under structural constraints
abstract: Against the dual backdrop of increasingly stringent resource-environmental constraints and economic growth pressures, the Water-Land-Energy-Food-Carbon ( W-L-E-F-C ) system faces a triple trade-off challenge between environmental mitigation, economic growth, and structural adjustment. Existing optimization studies often focus on optimizing a single physical objective, neglecting the degree of deviation of the optimized solution from the baseline structure, which may result in excessively large adjustments. To address this, the W-L-E-F-C system footprint was calculated based on multi-regional input-output analysis, a multi-objective optimization framework incorporating a novelty objective was developed, where novelty is defined as the normalized deviation of the optimized footprint structure relative to the baseline year. Using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), the research identified Pareto-optimal solutions that balance the reduction of resource-environment pressures with the control of structural deviation at both national and provincial scales. Furthermore, the coupling coordination degree (CCD) model and clustering analysis were employed to characterize changes in system coordination before and after optimization and to explore differences in provincial optimization pathways. The results indicated that: (1) The optimization achieved synergy between resource reduction and economic growth at the national level. Specifically, energy and land footprints decreased significantly (by 29.16% and 18.91%, respectively), while the overall system coupling coordination degree improved by 11.08%. (2) Comparative scenario analysis revealed that ignoring novelty led to drastic systemic restructuring. Conversely, incorporating the novelty objective effectively reduced the normalized deviation of the optimized footprint relative to the baseline, resulting in smaller structural adjustments. (3) Optimization patterns at the provincial level exhibited significant spatial heterogeneity. We identified four typical modes—efficiency-enhancing, reshaping, steady-state, and balanced—revealing differentiated optimization pathways based on regional resource endowments. The above results indicate that W-L-E-F-C system optimization is not merely the reduction of a single footprint or improvement of a single objective. Rather, it represents a comprehensive trade-off among resource-environment pressure reduction, maintenance of economic output, changes in system coupling coordination degree (CCD), and control of structural deviation. Compared with existing studies that primarily focus on pressure minimization or efficiency improvement, this study introduces novelty as an objective in the multi-objective optimization framework, providing a new analytical perspective for quantifying the magnitude of adjustment of the optimized scheme relative to the baseline configuration. The study results can serve as a reference for comparing changes in resource environment pressures and the magnitude of adjustments across different regions under various W-L-E-F-C system optimization pathways.

title: How land-use scenarios shape sustainability? An indicator-based analysis to identify leverage points
abstract: Ensuring sustainable land use through governance is challenging due to the complex and future-oriented nature of sustainability. We present a framework that combines land-use scenarios, sustainability indicators, and multivariate analysis to identify leverage points for policy decisions. We apply it to a multi-use protected area in Argentina's Andean Patagonian Forests. Six policy scenarios (conservation, informal tourism, formal tourism, livestock, forestry, and urban development) were scored using 38 sustainability indicators. Conservation performed higher (83%), and urban development was the least sustainable scenario (24%). Formal tourism scores closer to conservation (72%), whereas informal tourism aligns with urban development (32%). A subset of 15 indicators preserves the multivariate structure of the full assessment. Analysing the subset of indicators, we associated them with leverage points of the system for intervention, such as institutional capacity, accessibility and tourism. Overall, outcomes are not only shaped by land-use designation, indicating that sustainability is governance dependent rather than inherent to a given land use.

title: Tracking ecological shifts across the Antarctic polar front: A regional remote sensing model for phytoplankton size classes
abstract: Accurate retrieval of phytoplankton size classes (PSCs), crucial ecological indicators of marine biogeochemical cycles, remains challenging in the highly dynamic Southern Ocean (SO) when using conventional global remote sensing models. Traditional Diagnostic Pigment Analysis often introduces structural uncertainties due to the ambiguous mathematical partitioning of shared marker pigments. In this study, we demonstrate that a regionally optimized, taxonomically informed CHEMTAX scheme yields substantially more robust and ecologically consistent in situ PSC baselines. Building upon this foundation, we developed a novel suite of regional abundance-based PSC satellite inversion models tailored for the SO. Independent validation reveals that these models achieve high predictive accuracy relying solely on total chlorophyll- a . Notably, the framework yields highly accurate microphytoplankton estimates (MAPE = 25.32%, R 2 = 0.98) and superior improvements in nanophytoplankton retrievals (MAPE = 49.94%, R 2 = 0.63). Crucially, it effectively mitigates the severe overestimation of picophytoplankton commonly produced by global algorithms at low chlorophyll concentrations south of the Polar Front (PF). Applying these models to basin-scale satellite data significantly refines the spatial mapping of PSCs, revealing that microphytoplankton dominated, while nanophytoplankton also contributed a substantial fraction, particularly south the PF zone. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses highlight that accurate a priori taxonomic parameterization is essential to minimize structural uncertainties in PSC retrievals. Ultimately, this accurate, satellite-based framework provides an indispensable suite of monitoring indicators for assessing the efficiency of the biological carbon pump and tracking the response of fragile SO marine ecosystems to global climate change.

title: Corrigendum to “A meta-analysis of trade-offs between agricultural production and ecosystem services: a biplot-based synthesis” [Ecol. Indic. 188 (2026) 14996]
Water quality improvements correspond with increased human use and occurrence of fish, aquatic insects, and freshwater mussels
abstract: Documenting species responses to ecosystem level policy and conservation actions is critical to slow or reverse the global biodiversity crisis. We quantified changes in water quality, fish and insect assemblages (1978–2023), and freshwater mussels (1970–2023) over time associated with implementation of broad environmental regulations including the Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act and other best management practices across seven major river basins in the state of Ohio, USA. Water quality improvements were characterized by declines in zinc, nitrite, and lead across the state, and declines in ammonia and total phosphorus in most river basins. Occurrences of fish and insect species classified as intolerant to poor water quality increased across river basins, especially in large rivers. Seventy-one fish species and 171 insect taxa increased in occurrence and few species decreased. However, freshwater mussels had mixed responses over time, with 9 species increasing and 10 decreasing in occurrence, indicating the need for continued water quality improvements and potentially conservation efforts to repatriate mussels with low dispersal capabilities. This study documents long-term improvements in water quality and increased occurrence of aquatic species that are likely associated with environmental regulations and best management practices. Our results highlight the need for regulations to remain in place to maintain conservation gains for fishes and insects and potentially expanded regulations to facilitate gains for freshwater mussels. These results are critically important as the US federal government reconsiders implementation of environmental policy and funding of agencies enforcing environmental regulations.

title: Construction and application of an aquatic ecological health assessment system based on multi-source data and multi-method integration: A case study of key water bodies in the Yangtze River
abstract: To achieve a systematic and basin-wide assessment of Aquatic Ecological Health in the Yangtze River Basin, we developed an integrated assessment system based on multi-source data. The system synthesizes hydrological monitoring records, remote sensing products, long-term water quality observations, and literature-derived biological surveys to address data heterogeneity, extensive spatial coverage, and variability among water body types. By integrating long-term and spatially continuous datasets, the system captures longitudinal upstream–downstream gradients and the distinct ecological characteristics of rivers and lakes across the basin. Building on this data foundation, a hierarchical and multi-scale framework was constructed comprising three core dimensions: physical habitat, physicochemical properties, and biological condition. Indicator weights were determined using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), with consistency ratios (CR) below 0.1 to ensure reliability. To account for spatial heterogeneity among regions and water body types, benchmark values were derived through an integrated approach combining the reference condition method, generalized additive models (GAMs), the ASCETS method, and expert judgment, with parameters calibrated to local environmental conditions. Application to nine representative water bodies yielded an overall basin-wide ecological health score of 66.92, corresponding to a “Good” status. Upstream reaches generally exhibited higher ecological health than downstream reaches, and rivers performed better than lakes. In rivers, biological condition was identified as the primary limiting factor, whereas lakes were more strongly affected by eutrophication pressures. Overall, the assessment system balances scientific rigor with operational feasibility and provides a practical basis for ecological assessment and management in large river basins.

title: New methodology of a two-scale IUES-ternary framework for assessing urban greenspace abundance and ecosystem-service potential
abstract: Urban green spaces serve as places for recreation and relaxation and provide ecosystem services to urban residents. They are particularly needed in metropolitan areas with high population density. Proportionately to their population size, these areas should have extensive green spaces to meet society's demand for ecosystem services. Research in this area is scientifically important to determine the quantity and quality of ecosystem services. The proposed IUES (Index of Urban Ecosystem Services) index is based on the area of green spaces and the strength of ecosystem services. It assesses the potential of green spaces to provide ecosystem services. Using a model based on Ossan Triangle, it enables the classification of cities according to this potential. The proposed model represents a new approach to assessing ecosystem services in cities and allows for the development of IUES maps, city typologies, and micro-scale location scores. The aim of this article is to evaluate a new methodology for assessing the potential supply proxy to provide ecosystem services. The methodology is based on the IUES index and Ossana's Triangle at two spatial scales—macro and micro—with the goal of testing its versatility.

title: Anthropogenic perturbations in the Yellow River drive decadal phytoplankton shifts in the Bohai Sea and North Yellow Sea
abstract: Understanding long-term phytoplankton dynamics is essential for explaining contemporary ecological change and informing coastal management. In this study, we reconstructed decadal-scale variations in phytoplankton biomass and community structure in the Central Bohai Sea (CBS) and North Yellow Sea (NYS) using sedimentary sterol biomarkers from multiple sediment cores, with brassicasterol and dinosterol serving as indicators of diatoms and dinoflagellates, respectively. The results revealed that both regions experienced substantial 4–8-fold increases in proxy-inferred diatom and dinoflagellate biomass after 1980. The proxy-inferred diatom to dinoflagellate ratios (Diatom/Dino ratios) exhibited interdecadal oscillations, characterized by a decreasing shift around 1960 and an increasing shift around 2002. The proxy-inferred long-term biomass increase was mainly associated with anthropogenic nitrogen enrichment, whereas the shifts in Diatom/Dino ratios were likely linked to anthropogenic perturbations in the Yellow River. Furthermore, inter-regional comparisons based on rate-of-change (RoC) analysis indicated that both proxy-inferred diatom and dinoflagellate biomasses and their relative ratios in the NYS were more sensitive to allochthonous nutrient inputs than those in the CBS. This study provides valuable long-term baselines and new insight into the mechanisms underlying phytoplankton dynamics in the CBS and NYS, and highlights the important role of Yellow River perturbations in regulating diatom and dinoflagellate community shifts.

title: Integrated SWAT–LSTM modeling with sentinel-2 for chlorophyll-a prediction under climate change in an estuarine reservoir
abstract: Monitoring chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) dynamics in estuarine reservoirs is essential for assessing eutrophication and algal bloom risk under climate change. This study developed an integrated prediction framework combining Sentinel-2 derived Chl-a, the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT), and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to evaluate future Chl-a dynamics in Namyang Reservoir, South Korea, under SSP1–2.6 and SSP5–8.5 scenarios. The SWAT model was calibrated and validated to simulate inflow and water quality variables, including suspended solids, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and water temperature and parameter induced uncertainty was further assessed using 95% prediction uncertainty. These outputs, integrated with meteorological variables and Sentinel-2 derived Chl-a data, were used to train site-specific LSTM models for grid-based forecasting, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were applied to interpret predictor importance. The SWAT model satisfactorily reproduced hydrological and water quality conditions, while the LSTM framework captured the overall magnitude and temporal variability of Chl-a across the reservoir. SHAP analysis identified water and air temperature as dominant predictors, with nutrient related variables showing higher influence in the midstream region and meteorological factors dominating the downstream region. Under future climate scenarios, SSP5–8.5 produced higher Chl-a concentrations, intensified seasonal peaks, and expanded upstream hotspots, indicating increased eutrophication risk. The integrated framework provides a practical tool for climate responsive reservoir management and adaptive planning in vulnerable systems.

title: The current natural ecological disturbance baseline of fire activity in the southern European Alps – climate or humans?
abstract: Fire is a crucial disturbance agent in many ecosystems, such as in the Southern European Alps, where a considerable increase in fire activity is projected under anthropogenic climate change. However, currently it remains unclear whether natural or human factors mainly control the regional fire regime, since a current natural ecological disturbance baseline of regional fire activity is still missing. Therefore, we analyzed polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) as a novel paleofire proxy on a well-dated ∼8 ka sediment record from Lake Pusiano in northern Italy. Fire activity was low during the Mid Holocene (ΣPAH of <1.8 ng g −1 yr −1 ) and increased since the Bronze Age (∼4 cal ka BP; average ΣPAH of 4.1 ng g −1 yr −1 ), being maximal during the Roman period (∼1.7 cal ka BP; ΣPAH of 10.8 ng g −1 yr −1 ). This agrees with multiple regional charcoal-based paleofire records, making the reconstruction of the regional paleofire history robust. The observed paleofire pattern contrasts with past climate changes and is instead highly consistent with human activities, indicating a human-driven fire regime. Therefore, without human influence, there should be little to no notable regional fire activity in the Southern Alpine ecosystems, which thus constitutes the current regional natural ecological disturbance baseline. During recent climate change, however, observed droughts increasingly exceed Holocene levels. Therefore, the naturally not fire-prone southern Alpine ecosystems may already be shifting towards a drought-driven fire regime. These findings offer an original perspective that may reshape the view on fire risk and management also for other sub-Mediterranean regions.

title: Evaluating ecological health of the Chishui River using a multi-taxa index of biological integrity (IBI)
abstract: Understanding the biodiversity and ecological status of aquatic ecosystems is critical for riverine conservation and management. However, spatiotemporal patterns of biological integrity remain unclear, and single-taxon assessments often yield inconsistent or biased results due to divergent responses of different biotic communities to environmental change. In this study, we used eDNA metabarcoding to investigate phytoplankton, invertebrate, and fish communities in the upper Chishui River across four seasons and three longitudinal sections (BJ, ZT, RH). We developed taxon-specific biological integrity (BI) indices using four core metrics: taxon richness, dominance, network density, and phylogenetic distance. We further constructed a comprehensive index of biological integrity (IBI) by calculating the unweighted arithmetic mean of the three BI values, enabling a holistic evaluation of ecosystem health. Our results showed clear spatiotemporal variations in community composition and diversity. BI values exhibited asynchronous responses among taxa and differed from diversity patterns. Phytoplankton BI was generally good or moderate; invertebrate BI was stable but poor at some sites in summer; fish BI increased longitudinally from poor to good (except summer). Correlation analysis showed that community diversity and BI were driven by different environmental factors, whereas the integrated IBI showed no significant correlation with individual environmental variables, indicating greater stability. The asynchronous responses among single taxa confirm the limitations of relying on single taxon-based BI. In contrast, the multi-taxa IBI provided a comprehensive assessment of overall ecological health, which was generally good to moderate in the upper Chishui River. This study demonstrates that integrating multiple biological communities improves the reliability of bioassessment, supporting more effective river management and conservation.

title: Grasshopper re-surveys unravel threats to wet grasslands: drought, nitrogen deposition, and abandonment
abstract: Wet semi-natural grasslands are biodiversity-rich ecosystems that are increasingly threatened by climate change and land-use alteration. However, long-term empirical evidence on how invertebrate communities respond to these pressures remains scarce. Using a large-scale re-survey, we assessed changes in grasshopper communities in wet semi-natural grasslands across Germany over the past 20–35 years. We compared historical and recent species communities by re-surveying 107 grassland patches originally sampled between the late 1980s and early 2000s. Community responses were evaluated using species richness, functional groups based on mobility and habitat specificity, the Community Temperature Index (CTI), the Community Farmland Index (CFI), and Simpson dissimilarity ( SI ). Total species richness increased over time, driven by strong gains in highly mobile generalist species. By contrast, species currently classified as threatened and low-mobility habitat specialists both declined markedly. Communities became increasingly dominated by warm-adapted species, as indicated by rising CTI values, while decreasing Simpson dissimilarity revealed pronounced biotic homogenization. Mixed-effects models identified drought, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and increasing cover of abandoned grasslands as major drivers of species losses. Our results demonstrate that gains in species richness can mask ongoing functional degradation of wet grasslands. Grasshoppers proved to be sensitive bioindicators of climate- and land-use-driven degradation pathways. To counteract these trends, maintaining high groundwater levels and continued low-intensity management—such as grazing with low stocking rates or conservation mowing with uncut refuge strips—are crucial to prevent further degradation and to sustain ecosystem functioning in wet grasslands.

title: Tracking functional shifts in fishpond wetlands of Hong Kong's Deep Bay and their implications for conservation planning
abstract: Fishponds are important components of coastal wetland landscapes, supporting aquaculture, biodiversity conservation, and multiple ecosystem services. A key challenge in wetland management is to identify long-term ecological trajectories indicating functional transitions in managed fishpond landscapes. These transitions often evolve gradually through interacting shifts in hydrological condition, vegetation dynamics, and land use practices. This challenge is especially evident in Hong Kong's Deep Bay Area (DBA), where fishponds are subject to both changing management policies and increasing development pressure. To characterize these transitions, this study developed an integrated framework for deriving and assessing long-term ecological indicators of fishpond functional changes from 1986 to 2020. For this, we used annual Landsat composites and time-series analysis of the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). A multi-threshold classification framework was used to characterize hydrological and vegetation conditions, and temporal breakpoints were identified using the Breaks for Additive Season and Trend (BFAST) approach to distinguish stable, transitional, and functionally shifted fishponds. Mapping accuracy was evaluated using high-resolution WorldView-3 imagery and field-based reference data. The results showed that nearly half (51.4%) of the fishponds experienced functional shift, abandonment, or conversion, whereas only 48.6% retained relatively stable hydrological and ecological characteristics. These changes were accompanied by increasing vegetation cover and localized wetland succession including mangrove expansion along parts of the coastal fringe. The results demonstrate that long-term water and vegetation trajectories can serve as effective ecological indicators of fishpond functional change and wetland transition. This provides evidence to support adaptive conservation and land-use strategies for multifunctional wetland landscapes in Deep Bay and comparable coastal environments.

title: Comparative analysis of bioacoustic indices: Performance and limitations
abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) increasingly uses bioacoustic indices to assess biodiversity, although their application remains controversial. Therefore, this study evaluates the performance and limitations of five commonly used indices: Acoustic Entropy ( H s ), von Neumann Entropy ( H v ), Acoustic Diversity Index (ADI), Bioacoustic Index (BIO), and Acoustic Evenness Index (AEI), across different levels of species richness and two taxonomic groups. For this purpose, we used two datasets: (i) 26,028 synthetic assemblages with controlled species richness, including birds, anurans, and background-noise segments; and (ii) 10,163 manually annotated raw soundscapes containing bird vocalizations, including calls and songs, and anuran calls, with and without noise filtering. The results indicate that index values may be misleading when distinguishing background-audio segments from soundscapes with varying levels of species richness, as background-audio segments exhibited values similar to, or even higher than, those observed in soundscapes with high species richness. The use of noise filtering to minimize the problem of noisy segments showed inconclusive results, modifying the correlations between indices and species richness in an inconsistent way. In some cases, it converted positive correlations into negative ones for bird calls and songs, or negative correlations into positive ones for anuran calls. Therefore, it was not possible to establish a consistent rule ensuring that the filter should always be applied. Furthermore, two case studies showed that the distribution of spectral energy and the syllable repetition rate over time significantly influence index values, indicating that these indices are not reliable proxies for species richness.

title: A multi-Indicator time-series approach for assessing wildfire vulnerability of habitat suitability and landscape connectivity in Neurergus derjugini
abstract: Wildfires are increasingly threatening biodiversity in the Zagros Mountains, impacting habitat suitability and connectivity for endemic and range-restricted species such as the endangered Kurdistan salamander ( Neurergus derjugini ). Despite its conservation significance, no study has evaluated the spatiotemporal vulnerability of this species to fire. Here, we developed a distance-based, time-series-integrated indicator to assess wildfire impacts on habitat suitability, landscape connectivity, and population cores of N. derjugini across its distribution in Iran and Iraq. Habitat suitability was modeled using an ensemble of six algorithms, with binary maps derived via True Skill Statistics. Sub-basins were delineated from hydrological flow accumulation, and connectivity among population cores was assessed using circuit theory. Surface resistance was derived from the fuzzy overlap of habitat suitability, Stream Power Index, and sediment transport. Fire dynamics were analyzed using the MODIS MCD64A1 product (2002−2023) and Mann-Kendall trend tests. Results revealed 12 sub-basins with burned areas increasing significantly over time ( p < 0.0001), particularly in Iraq. Average burned area within suitable habitats over 22 years was 65.124 km 2 . Twenty-seven population cores exhibited decreasing distances from burned areas, indicating heightened vulnerability, with sub-basins 4 and 11 showing the most pronounced effects. Connectivity pathways intersecting burned zones were particularly sensitive, highlighting the role of linear hydrological corridors in mediating salamander dispersal. This framework enables identification of vulnerable habitats and prioritization of conservation actions. Integrating spatial fire patterns with habitat and connectivity analyses provides a transferable tool for proactive management of N. derjugini and other fire-prone species in the transboundary Zagros region.

title: Moisture recycling sustains precipitation despite net water vapor export from China's drylands
abstract: Drylands are water-limited systems that collectively sustain hundreds of millions of people, yet land–atmosphere feedbacks such as terrestrial moisture recycling remain poorly quantified. In particular, the origins of precipitation in China's drylands and their atmospheric water vapor budgets remain unclear. Here we use a Lagrangian moisture-tracking model to quantify atmospheric moisture sources and budgets for precipitation across China's drylands from 2001 to 2020. We find that local moisture recycling dominates drylands precipitation, with most precipitation originating from evapotranspiration within the drylands themselves. Vegetation transpiration constitutes the primary recycled component, accounting for more than half of atmospheric moisture supply in most source regions. About 80% of precipitation sources occurred during the growing season. At the provincial scale, Shannxi (261 mm yr −1 ), Xizang (260 mm yr −1 ), Qinghai (235 mm yr −1 ), Shanxi (225 mm yr −1 ), Sichuan (209 mm yr −1 ), and Henan (195 mm yr −1 ) contributed the most to precipitation in China's drylands through moisture recycling. From 2001 to 2020, although 71% of source areas exhibited an increase in water vapor transported to China's drylands, China's drylands still experienced an overall water vapor deficit, acting as sources of atmospheric water vapor and contributing to precipitation in downwind areas. Additionally, the water vapor budget exhibits spatial variability: eastern regions of China's drylands suffer severe water vapor deficits, while western areas have a surplus. This explains the observed trends of increasing dryness in the east and rising humidity in the west in recent years. Together, our results highlight the central role of vegetation-mediated moisture recycling in sustaining dryland precipitation and emphasize the need to incorporate land–atmosphere coupling into water management, climate adaptation and ecosystem restoration strategies.

title: Spatio-temporal evolution and driving factors of provincial grain crop water footprint in China from 2000 to 2023
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasingly stringent water resource constraints and continually reinforced food security strategies, it is essential to accurately quantify the water consumption intensity of grain production, clarify its spatiotemporal evolution patterns, and identify key driving mechanisms for optimizing regional grain production patterns. Based on water footprint theory, this study quantifies the spatiotemporal evolution of water footprints for major grain crops in China at the provincial level from 2000 to 2023. Using spatial autocorrelation models and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) model, it comprehensively analyzes the geographical distribution characteristics and driving factors of water footprints. The results indicate the following: (1) Overall, the water footprint of grain crops exhibits an upward trend, primarily driven by growth in the blue water footprint, with an annual average of approximately 8,414.71×10⁸m³. Of this, green, blue, and grey water account for 45%, 41%, and 14%, respectively. (2) Structurally, there is a pattern of "stable major crops with regional differentiation", where rice dominates and corn continues to rise. High water footprints persist in North, East, and Central China, with a notable increase in the Northeast due to expansion of rice cultivation. In contrast, the Southwest and Northwest regions exhibit lower water footprints due to natural conditions and water-saving practices. (3) Spatially, the total water footprint shows significant positive spatial correlation, with clustering intensifying over time. The spatial pattern of the grey water footprint shifts from clustering to random distribution by 2023. (4) Regarding driving factors, production technology and irrigation management are key negative factors suppressing water footprint growth. However, water-saving measures have not been effectively translated into actual water reduction overall, showing significant effects only during periods of strong policy implementation, such as 2012-2013. This study provides a scientific basis for region-specific agricultural water resource management.

title: Mixed plantations regulate soil microbial-mediated ecological processes along the root–soil continuum in sandy ecosystems
abstract: Sandy ecosystems have low nutrient availability and strong environmental stress, so vegetation restoration in these areas depends greatly on plant-microbe interactions. Mixed plantations are widely used to improve ecosystem stability in desert regions, but their effects on fungal community assembly along the root-soil continuum are still not clear. Here, we investigated fungal communities associated with Populus simonii monocultures and three mixed plantations ( P. simonii * Salix psammophila , P. simonii * S. psammophila , P. simonii * Caragana korshinskii , P. simonii * Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica ) in the Kubuqi Desert of northern China. We used high-throughput sequencing of the fungal ITS region together with functional guild prediction, ecological network analysis, and null model analysis to study community diversity, assembly processes, and environmental drivers across root (R), rhizosphere (RS), and non-rhizosphere soil (NRS) compartments. Mixed plantations significantly altered soil physicochemical conditions and reshaped fungal community structure along the root–soil continuum. RS harbored the highest fungal richness, whereas root-associated communities exhibited strong compositional differentiation, indicating pronounced host filtering effects. Ectomycorrhizal fungi dominated the fungal functional structure, suggesting that symbiotic strategies play a central role in plant adaptation to nutrient-poor sandy environments. Mixed stands also increased fungal network complexity, particularly in the PC stand, implying stronger microbial interactions and potentially greater ecosystem stability. Null model analysis revealed that stochastic processes, especially dispersal limitation, predominantly governed fungal community assembly, while deterministic selection became more important in the rhizosphere. Soil water content and available potassium emerged as the key environmental drivers shaping fungal community composition. Overall, our findings demonstrate that mixed plantations regulate fungal community assembly through both plant-mediated microbial filtering and modifications of soil environmental conditions. These results highlight the importance of species mixtures in structuring belowground microbial networks and provide new insights into the microbial mechanisms underlying vegetation restoration in sandy ecosystems.

title: Dominant constraints on the long-term trends of global vegetation restoration potential patterns
abstract: Vegetation restoration potential (VRP) represents the attainable upper bound of vegetation recovery under existing environmental and habitat constraints. Quantifying VRP is essential for identifying restoration priorities and evaluating the long-term sustainability of global greening under accelerating climate change and widespread land degradation. However, the global spatial patterns, dominant drivers, and regional disparities of VRP remain insufficiently understood. We integrated multi-source remote sensing and environmental datasets to assess the spatiotemporal dynamics of VRP and vegetation restoration potential achievement degree (VRPAD) from 2000 to 2022 under similar-habitat conditions, and applied the Local Indicator of Stratified Power (LISP) to characterize the spatial heterogeneity of dominant drivers. Results showed that global kernel normalized difference vegetation index (kNDVI) increased significantly, with greening hotspots concentrated in eight major regions, whereas VRP declined significantly at −0.01 per decade (10a). High VRP values were mainly distributed in Eastern Europe, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Central Africa, whereas low values occurred in arid–semiarid and high-latitude regions. Global VRPAD increased significantly at 0.03 per decade (10a), particularly in tropical and subtropical regions, indicating progressive realization of restoration potential but persistent constraints in drylands and cold environments. Climatic factors dominated the global spatial pattern of VRP, with solar radiation (SR), precipitation (PRE), and temperature (TEM) jointly explaining 81.22% of the land surface. SR showed stronger control in low-latitude arid and plateau regions, PRE was more influential in tropical monsoon and temperate humid regions, and TEM exhibited stronger explanatory power in mid- to high-latitude plateaus and temperate steppe regions, whereas topography and land use exerted stronger localized effects. These findings indicate that recent global greening has been accompanied by a contraction of remaining restoration space and that restoration outcomes are strongly constrained by regional environmental endowments. This study provides a global benchmark for identifying restoration priority areas and supports region-specific restoration planning and climate-adaptive ecosystem management.

title: Dam-induced increases in phytoplankton biomass and the effects on zooplankton productivity in a karst watershed
abstract: The cascade dam participate in the natural river environment as artificial factors through altering the original natural conditions and forming new human-interrupted ecosystems, and at the same time forming a new habitat for all the aquatic creatures. Enhancing habitat complexity and further management of river-reservoir ecosystem promotes the productivity of primary producers. By stimulating the productivity of lower trophic levels (phytoplankton and zooplankton), critical food resources are pro-vided for the declining populations of higher trophic levels.
