We investigated Tongzi River Basin, which exhibits typical karst watershed characteristics. The study covered both the river channel and five cascade dams from the upper to lower sections of the basin. We found that phytoplankton biomass(expressed by Chlorophyll-a Concentra-tion) in reservoirs were higher than in the river channel. In phosphorus-limited, high-alkalinity (ALK) karst catchments, differences in phosphorus availability, ALK buffering capacity drive con-trasts in phytoplankton biomass and microbial loop structure between reservoirs and river channels. Under “bottom-up” control, zooplankton biomass in reservoir is higher due to the higher trophic transfer efficiency between phytoplankton and zooplankton. In conclusion, we suggest that the karst reservoirs can alleviate key constraints (phos-phorus availability, pH, and alkalinity) on the river primary production system, thereby enhancing primary productivity and providing greater food resources for the aquatic ecosystem.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns of cultural ecosystem service supply, demand, and flows in urban green–blue spaces: A case study of Hangzhou, China
abstract: Rapid urbanization has intensified spatial mismatches between the supply and demand of cultural ecosystem services (CES) in urban green–blue spaces. This study developed an indicator-based spatiotemporal framework to assess CES supply, demand, and service flows in Hangzhou, China, for 2014, 2019, and 2024. Spatial matching and spatial autocorrelation analyses were applied to examine supply–demand relationships and their temporal evolution. A raster-based service flow model was further used to simulate CES transmission pathways under spatial resistance constraints. Results show pronounced spatial heterogeneity and an increasing supply–demand mismatch. Spatial coupling between supply and demand weakens over time, shifting from a core–periphery structure to a fragmented, multi-center pattern. Service flow analysis further indicates that the effectiveness of CES delivery is constrained by the spatial configuration of transmission networks rather than by supply capacity alone. Despite improvements in urban transport infrastructure, service flows have become increasingly concentrated along several dominant corridors, with maximum flow intensity rising from 0.33 in 2014 to 0.59 in 2024. Meanwhile, the maximum potential satisfied CES declines from 0.91 to 0.80, and service cold spots expand toward newly urbanized districts. These findings highlight the structural nature of CES imbalance and provide indicators to support urban ecosystem service assessment.

title: A biomass-based trophic indicator approach for assessing fisheries sustainability: a case study of Jatigede reservoir, Indonesia
abstract: Sustainability assessment of fisheries as freshwater provisioning services requires indicators that reflect trophic structure and ecosystem function. This Study applies a biomass-based trophic indicator approach to evaluate the sustainability of fisheries in the Jatigede Reservoir, Indonesia. Data were collected from seven sampling stations during 2022–2023, including fish sampling, water quality measurements, and stakeholder interviews. The framework integrates fish diversity, productivity, condition factor, and predator biomass into a composite sustainability index. All indicators were standardized and combined into a composite assessment framework. The ecological status remained moderate (index = 2.0) in both years. Fish diversity increased slightly, whereas productivity declined. Predator biomass remained relatively high (45.7%), suggesting a possible trophic imbalance within the reservoir ecosystem. Compared with the abundance-based indicator, the biomass-based approach may provide an alternative perspective for evaluating trophic dominance and ecosystem structure. Sensitivity analysis using a one-at-a-time (OAT) approach showed that the sustainability classification remained unchanged across most weighting scenarios (Wp = 0.10–0.60), with no category shift observed in approximately 85% of cases. These results suggest that the index classification was relatively stable under the tested weighting assumptions, although broader validation is still required. The main contribution of this study lies in applying biomass-based trophic dominance as a diagnostic indicator within a case-study-based sustainability framework. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution due to limited temporal coverage, expert-derived threshold assumptions, and the absence of external validation. Overall, although the system remained in a moderate condition, the observed decline in productivity and persistent trophic imbalance may indicate early signs of ecological stress, highlighting the need for adaptive management and further validation across different reservoir systems.

title: Resilience-based crop patterns navigate multi-dimensional trade-offs in arid northwestern China
abstract: Understanding the resilience of farmland ecosystems under drought and salinization is essential for navigating agricultural trade-offs and ensuring long-term sustainability in arid northwestern China. By coupling the regionalized WHCNS model with ecological trajectory analysis, this study constructed a multidimensional state space including yield, water consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, and soil moisture, thereby quantifying the evolutionary characteristics and resilience threshold of farmland ecosystems. Finally, crop patterns in arid northwestern China were reconstructed to maximize systemic resilience and achieve optimal trade-offs. The findings indicate that: (1) Environmental conditions and crop traits jointly govern the trajectories of farmland ecosystems. Even in highly favorable, non-arid and non-salinized zones (e.g., BJ2), crops on 30.1% of farmland do not meet the resilience threshold, associated with an overemphasis on yield. This reveals a structurally vulnerable, high-yield system arising from insufficient systemic buffering. In contrast, Nanjiang converged toward a homogeneous, risk-averse steady state under strong environmental filtering. (2) Resilience-based optimization effectively resolves non-linear, multi-dimensional trade-offs. By phasing out low-stability maize (−33.7% area) and consolidating dominant crops, it established a robust crop pattern, with cotton dominance in Xinjiang and a grain-production core in the Hexi Corridor. (3) The reconstruction effects demonstrate the strategic value of trading carbon for water. Although the optimized patterns incurred a 7.8% decline in total yield and a 5.6% increase in carbon emissions, they simultaneously increased regional economic output per unit area by 3.3% and enhanced mean soil moisture content by 2.7%. This demonstrates that such strategic trade-offs fundamentally enhance the sustainable development capacity of farmland ecosystems. This study provides a framework for shifting agricultural management from yield maximization to resilience-oriented strategies. Through the resolution of multi-dimensional trade-offs and the alignment of crop traits with environmental carrying capacities, farmland ecosystems can sustain long-term viability under increasing climate uncertainty.

title: An indicator framework for cultivated land ecological compensation based on net ecosystem service value in China
abstract: Cultivated land ecological compensation is a core policy tool for resolving conflicts among food security, ecological conservation, and regional economic development. However, existing compensation schemes lack a coordinated mechanism that balances efficiency and equity in spatial allocation. To address this, this study uses Shandong and Henan two typical Chinese provinces as case studies. Drawing on five sets of data from 2005 to 2023, the study constructs a comprehensive framework encompassing compensation quantification, zoning standards, and a system for driving factor analysis. The results indicate that: (1) During the study period, the net ecosystem service value (NESV) of arable land in both provinces showed an overall upward trend; while Henan Province had a higher average absolute ecosystem value, Shandong Province's final ecological compensation standards were generally higher than those of Henan Province; (2) The High Performance & High Urgency Zone continues to expand, while the distribution of the Low Performance & Low Urgency Zone remains relatively stable. Some inland cities exhibit clear patterns of dynamic shifts within the High Performance & Low Urgency Zone whereas the Low Performance & High Urgency Zone appeared infrequently and only briefly during the study period; (3) The increase in per capita disposable income among urban residents and improvements in the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) serve as long-term positive drivers of the ecological value of farmland; conversely, the intensity of nighttime lights which reflects high levels of human activity and urban expansion constitutes the primary negative constraint, although its inhibitory effect has shown a significant trend toward convergence and weakening since 2015. (4) Policy formulation should be based on the results of regional zoning and the identification of driving factors to implement differentiated and coordinated strategies, strictly enforce constraints on non-point source pollution and responsibilities for cross-regional compensation payments, and supplement these measures with ecological assistance and market-based compensation mechanisms, thereby establishing a cross-regional compensation system that balances efficiency and equity. These findings provided a transferable indicator framework and decision-support tool for cross-regional, differentiated, and fair-yet-efficient cultivated land ecological compensation mechanisms.

title: Integrating DNA-based microbial profiling and organic matter chemistry into soil monitoring: Insights from archived Swedish soils
abstract: Soil provides critical ecosystem services, yet anthropogenic pressures have accelerated degradation, prompting the implementation of an EU-wide soil monitoring law aiming to improve all soils by 2050. Despite recent methodological advances that make high-throughput data collection feasible, biological indicators remain underrepresented in most national soil monitoring programmes. Data from DNA-based metabarcoding of soil microorganisms is increasingly highlighted as important to include. Here, we evaluated the potential of integrating DNA-based microbial community data and spectroscopic analyses into soil monitoring using 75 archived samples representing agricultural soils from southern Sweden with a wide range of organic matter contents. Fungal and prokaryotic communities were strongly correlated, and their compositions were also related to the spectroscopy data. Contrary to common assumptions, indices of fungal and prokaryotic diversity were not positively related to soil organic carbon content. Instead, links were detected only when the chemical composition of organic matter was taken into consideration. Specifically, fungal diversity was positively correlated with the abundance of alkyl-C, which is indicative of more decomposed organic matter. We highlight data on microbial community and data from mid-IR spectroscopy as particularly interesting candidates for inclusion in soil monitoring programmes. However, it may be more informative to focus on analysing community composition and potential functioning rather than species richness.

title: Coupling coordination evolution and scenario simulation of the flow–sediment transport, eco-environment, and socio-economy system in the Yellow River Basin under interregional transmission
abstract: Regulated sediment-laden river basins face multiple pressures from water-resource constraints, water–sediment regulation, ecological maintenance, and socioeconomic development. Although system dynamics and composite evaluation models are increasingly used for dynamic basin assessment, the effects of section-to-section water–sediment transmission and representative hydrological boundary conditions on subsystem coordination remain insufficiently quantified. Building on previous flood–sediment concepts, this study defines flow–sediment transport (FS) as a functional subsystem representing water–sediment supply, regulation, and in-channel transport capacity, thereby linking basin-scale water availability and reservoir regulation with in-channel flow/flood conveyance and sediment transport. An indicator-based dynamic assessment framework was developed for the FS, eco-environment, and socio-economy (FES) system in the Yellow River Basin. Multi-source datasets for 2000–2023 were used to construct and validate an annual system dynamics model for the upstream, midstream, and downstream sections. Representative wet, normal, and dry hydrological boundary years were selected from the natural runoff series at Huayuankou station, and four development scenarios were designed for 2024–2030. The model represents stepwise interregional water–sediment transmission through key cross-sectional outputs and is coupled with composite evaluation and coupling coordination analysis. Results show that hydrological boundary conditions strongly shape system constraint intensity, with development level and coupling coordination generally following wet > normal > dry. In the downstream section, the 2030 baseline coupling coordination degree without interregional transmission was 0.89, 0.78, and 0.71 under wet, normal, and dry boundary conditions, respectively. Under downstream dry boundary conditions, incorporating interregional transmission changed the 2030 coupling coordination degrees across the four development scenarios from 0.71–0.74 to 0.69–0.76. Ecological and integrated scenarios generally outperformed the economic-growth scenario, indicating that efficiency improvement and ecological constraints are more favorable than socioeconomic expansion alone under limited water availability. The framework provides a dynamic indicator-based approach that incorporates water–sediment transmission and hydrological boundary effects for adaptive governance of regulated sediment-laden basins.

title: Driving mechanisms and regulation of neighborhood-scale urban forest carbon storage in New York City, USA
abstract: This study looks at the differences in urban forest carbon storage not only in New York City (NYC), but also in the neighborhoods. It combines information from literature, remote sensing, and LiDAR, and employs Pearson correlation analysis and boosted regression tree modelling. The results reveal that carbon storage vary widely across NYC space. The area of Staten Island has the most significant carbon storage, where over 40% of the neighborhoods are more than 20,000 T C of carbon. Also, on the other end of the spectrum is Manhattan with over 90% of neighborhoods containing less than 1,000 T C of carbon. Further: The total carbon storage (r = 0.96) strongly correlates to tree number and canopy cover area. The forest metric Treecanopy Percentage of Landscape (T_PLAND) strongly associated with carbon density (r > 0.5), while canopy height is the major factor for per-tree carbon storage (r = 0.46). Variables in the landscape explain 99.7% of the variation in total carbon storage, and tree number is the main driver. Soil nitrogen and canopy cover of a forest showed positive correlation with carbon storage, while GDP and Roads Percentage of Landscape (R_PLAND) showed negative correlation. This study argues that increasing green space, modifying the built-up and vegetation ratio, and altering spatial configuration can enhance neighborhood-level carbon storage. It gives a scientific basis for urban forest engineering and carbon sink improvement.

title: The varied impacts of urbanization on ecosystem services under spatial zoning policy: a case study in the Middle Reaches of Yangtze River Urban Agglomeration, China
abstract: Understanding how urbanization affects ecosystem services (ES) across different spatial planning zones is essential for sustainable land management. In China, the Major Function Zone (MFZ) framework provides a unique lens to examine these interactions, yet the spatial heterogeneity of urbanization–ES dynamics under this system remains underexplored. Focusing on the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River Urban Agglomeration (MRYRUA), this study integrates the InVEST model, coupling coordination degree (CCD) model, and PLUS land-use simulation to assess historical trends (2000−2020) and project future trajectories (2020–2035) under Shared Socioeconomic Pathways-Representative Concentration Pathways (SSP-RCP). Results show that urbanization increased steadily across all MFZs, with National Key Development Zones experiencing the highest growth. ES trends diverged: water yield and soil conservation rose, while habitat quality, carbon sequestration, and water purification declined. The CCD between urbanization and ES improved modestly (0.18–0.38), shifting from moderate to mild disorder, but remained low overall. The spatial pattern of the urbanization–ES relationship clearly reflects the hierarchy of the MFZ. Spatially, CCD was highest in National Key Development Zones and lowest in National Key Ecological Functional Zones. Future scenario projections identify SSP119 as optimal for balancing urban development with ecological protection, aligning best with long-term sustainability objectives. These findings underscore the critical role of MFZ planning in mediating urban–ecological trade–offs and provide actionable insights for aligning regional development with global sustainability goals.

title: Ecological niche position and functional traits jointly shape abundance-occupancy patterns of stream fishes in the Dabie Mountains, China
abstract: Abundance-occupancy relationship (AOR) is central to explaining why some species are both locally abundant and regionally widespread, yet the mechanisms underlying this pattern in freshwater fishes remain poorly understood. Here, we examined AOR in stream fish assemblages from the Dabie Mountains, China, based on 40 species surveyed across 230 sites, and evaluated how ecological niche properties and functional traits jointly influence species abundance, occupancy and their coupling. Realized niches and functional strategies were quantified to evaluate the relative contributions of niche position, niche breadth and functional traits to AOR within a hierarchical analytical framework. Fish assemblages exhibited a clear positive AOR (R 2 = 0.844), while retaining a measurable degree of interspecific variation around the overall pattern. Niche position emerged as the primary constraint on both local abundance and regional occupancy, whereas niche breadth showed weak and inconsistent effects. Composite functional traits related to swimming, feeding, and spatial positioning exerted little direct influence on either abundance or occupancy, but significantly modified the AOR, such that species characterized by a strong swimming-related component attained higher occupancy at comparable levels of abundance. Structural equation modelling further indicated that niche position influenced occupancy mainly through its effect on abundance, while this composite functional dimension primarily regulated how variation in abundance was translated into spatial occupancy. Our results demonstrate that abundance-occupancy patterns in mountain stream fishes arise from the combined effects of strong environmental filtering and trait-mediated processes, highlighting complementary roles of niche properties and functional traits in shaping species distributions within spatially constrained river networks.

title: Associations between urbanization-driven watershed landscape pattern shifts and seasonal riverine environmental-ecological responses
abstract: Rapid urbanization reshapes land use, water quality, and sediment conditions in river basins, yet their combined effects on phytoplankton remain inadequately understood. In particular, whether intensified landscape fragmentation during flood periods can decouple phytoplankton communities from their usual dependence on water quality remains an unresolved question. This study investigated spatio-temporal variations of land use, water quality, sediment, and phytoplankton (structure, biomass, diversity, resource use efficiency) in the Tuojiang River's Chengdu section to clarify their relationships and impact pathways. Redundancy analysis, variance partitioning analysis, Mantel test, and Partial least squares path model were used to quantify relationships and impact pathways. Results showed water quality was the dominant driver of phytoplankton, while land use (e.g., cropland proportion, patch density) became significantly more important during floods periods (explanation rate increased from 6.0% to 11.5%). Spatially, from upstream (forest-dominated, low fragmentation) to downstream (cropland-dominated, high fragmentation), phytoplankton richness and diversity rose, but evenness and RUE declined potentially associated with the increased dominance of Bacillariophyta (diatoms, >90% proportion), which may have altered community balance under eutrophic and hydrologically disturbed conditions. PLS-PM revealed period-specific pathways: land use exhibited stronger statistical associations with phytoplankton communities during the flood period, potentially decoupling communities from their usual dependence on water quality, whereas the phytoplankton community during the dry period was primarily associated with changes in water quality. Thus, priority should be given to internal pollution mitigation during dry periods, while controlling land use types and runoff during flood periods. These findings suggest a seasonal shift from internal river regulation toward watershed-scale landscape correlational modulation under hydrological disturbance, though further validation is needed to indicate causal mechanisms.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors of net carbon intensity in arid cropland systems: An explainable machine learning study in the Hexi corridor
abstract: Arid and semi-arid cropland systems play an important role in food production and terrestrial carbon cycling, but their high dependence on agricultural inputs may intensify trade-offs between productivity and carbon mitigation. This study developed a net carbon intensity (NCI) assessment framework for cropland systems in the Hexi Corridor, a typical arid region of northwestern China, and analyzed the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving factors of county-level NCI from 2001 to 2022. By integrating carbon emissions from agricultural inputs and management activities with crop carbon sequestration, we quantified cropland NCI using multi-source statistical data from 20 counties (cities and districts). Spatial analysis and an explainable machine learning framework (XGBoost–SHAP) were further applied to identify key drivers and their nonlinear effects. Results showed that cropland systems in the Hexi Corridor maintained a stable net carbon sink during the study period, while NCI exhibited an overall fluctuating upward trend (4.28–5.57 t C·ha −1 ). Spatial disparities among counties gradually decreased, accompanied by an expansion of high-NCI areas in oasis agricultural regions. Diesel input intensity (DII), cropland labor density (CLD), and the multiple cropping index (MCI) were identified as the dominant drivers of NCI. SHAP analysis revealed pronounced threshold effects and nonlinear interactions among these factors, suggesting that cropland carbon performance is governed by the coordinated effects of agricultural inputs, production systems, and environmental constraints rather than by individual drivers in isolation. These findings provide scientific support for region-specific low-carbon agricultural management and agricultural decarbonization in arid regions.

title: Corrigendum to “Understanding multi-hazard risk dynamics between land use, climate extremes and water quality leveraging artificial intelligence” [Ecol. Indic. 182 (2026) 114494]
From ecological indicators to photovoltaic planning: A graded suitability framework and long-term potential on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau
abstract: The Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau (QTP) is one of China's most resource-rich regions for utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) development, but abundant solar radiation alone is insufficient for defining rational development priorities in this ecologically fragile and topographically complex region. Existing studies often rely on static resource indicators, binary ecological exclusions, or suitability mapping that is weakly linked to long-term development potential. To address these limitations, this study develops an ecologically constrained, integrated and reproducible framework for utility-scale PV planning on the QTP. The framework integrates five dimensions—climate resource endowment, construction and operation suitability, ecosystem importance, ecological sensitivity, and socio-economic suitability—and combines hierarchical Bayesian estimation of global horizontal irradiation, stability analysis of irradiation supply, entropy-based weighting, and fuzzy Gamma aggregation. Long-term PV development potential is then estimated as an ecologically constrained technical potential under two nested planning scenarios. The results show that PV suitability on the QTP is highly spatially differentiated and cannot be inferred from radiation conditions alone. High-grade suitable land is concentrated mainly in Qinghai and Xizang, whereas the southern and southeastern Plateau are more strongly constrained by ecological sensitivity, land-use conflict, and complex terrain. Under the conservative scenario, the retained PV potential is 6.39 TW of installable capacity and 11.86 PWh·yr −1 of annual generation; under the long-term scenario, these expand to 18.61 TW and 33.95 PWh·yr −1 . Qinghai and Xizang together account for over 87% of both scenarios, indicating a clear two-tier structure in which a spatially concentrated near-term core is complemented by a broader high-suitability long-term reserve. These estimates should be interpreted as ecologically constrained upper bounds rather than deployment targets. The framework provides a transparent and policy-relevant basis for phased PV development on the QTP.

title: Comprehensive impacts of national park construction from the multi-dimensional perspective of ecological-production-living functions: a case study of Qilian Mountains grassland ecosystem, China
abstract: National parks are widely recognized for their crucial roles in protecting biodiversity, maintaining grassland ecosystem functions, and ensuring ecological security. However, these protective effects are not always immediate or consistent across regions because they depend on resource resilience, spatial heterogeneity, climatic conditions, policy implementation, and functional interactions. Understanding the impact of national parks on grassland functions is essential for guiding the effective design and management of protected areas. We evaluated the impact of national park construction in the Qilian Mountains (QLM) on grasslands, considering ecological, production, and living functions (EPLFs). We applied spatial analysis, trend analysis, and self-organizing mapping to examine the spatiotemporal dynamics of the grassland EPLFs in the QLM. Regression analysis was also employed to determine the comprehensive impact of national parks on grassland EPLFs. From 2012 to 2022, grassland EPLFs in the QLM showed a stable but heterogeneous spatial pattern with an overall decreasing trend. Ecological functions were generally stronger than production and living functions, which declined more inside the national park. Grassland EPLF bundles were mainly dominated by ecological-living and ecological-production-living types, showing a clear shift toward the latter. This indicates that national park construction makes grassland EPLFs more integrated. Overall, areas outside the park were more strongly impacted. We propose strategies to balance ecological protection and human needs for sustainable grassland management in the QLM. These findings provide theoretical support for national park construction and grassland management optimization.

title: A process-oriented framework integrating DPSR and NESH for spatially explicit urban flood resilience assessment
abstract: Urban flooding increasingly threatens human safety, infrastructure, and socio-economic systems due to rapid urbanization and climate change. Accurately assessing urban flood resilience is critical for informing disaster prevention, mitigation, and adaptation strategies. This study develops a process-oriented framework integrating the Driving force–Pressure–State–Response (DPSR)model and Natural–Economic–Social–Hazard (NESH) models to evaluate urban flood resilience across multiple rainfall scenarios, incorporating spatially explicit and dynamically weighted indicators for fine-grained sub-regional assessment. Applied to the central urban area of Zhengzhou City, China, the framework identifies spatial resilience patterns, key influencing indicators, and vulnerable zones. Results show that driving force resilience is moderate with lower values in central districts; pressure resilience declines systematically with increasing rainfall intensity; state resilience exhibits a ring-shaped spatial structure; and response resilience is concentrated in the urban core. Overall urban flood resilience decreases from 0.592 under moderate rainfall to 0.538 under extreme events. Simulation of grey-green infrastructure interventions, including stormwater pipe dredging and increased vegetation coverage, demonstrates substantial flood risk reduction under moderate rainfall but diminished effectiveness under extreme events. This framework provides a scientifically rigorous and actionable tool for urban flood resilience assessment, enabling identification of vulnerable zones and guiding targeted mitigation and urban planning strategies.

title: Using single-date airborne LiDAR features to map tree mortality timing in central european forests
abstract: Mapping tree mortality timing is essential for understanding forest disturbance dynamics and supporting management decisions under changing climatic conditions, particularly in regions affected by bark beetle outbreaks and increased wildfire risk. This study proposes a framework to estimate tree mortality timing using single-date airborne LiDAR data combined with an area-based approach. The method was applied in Bohemian Switzerland National Park (Czech Republic), where extensive Norway spruce mortality occurred between 2018 and 2021. Geometric and radiometric LiDAR features were extracted and used in three classification scenarios: (i) individual mortality years (2018–2021), (ii) grouped mortality classes (2018–2019 vs. 2020–2021), and (iii) contrasting mortality years (2018 vs. 2021). Spatial dependence was accounted for using spatial-block cross-validation, and Global Random Forest and Spatially Localized Random Forest models were compared, showing only minor differences in performance. Classification accuracy increased with the temporal contrast between classes. Scenario (i) showed limited performance (OA = 0.50), reflecting the difficulty of distinguishing adjacent years due to gradual structural and radiometric changes. Grouping mortality years (scenario ii) improved results (OA = 0.72), while the highest accuracy was achieved with scenario (iii), when contrasting temporally distant mortality years (OA = 0.81). Feature importance and ALE analysis indicated that geometric variables captured subtle structural differences, whereas radiometric features provided stronger discrimination for more distinct mortality conditions. Although precise annual dating from a single acquisition remains challenging, the proposed framework enables scalable mapping of mortality timing across large areas, supporting fire risk assessment and forest management.

title: Shifting urban baselines limit the abundance-based resolution of a classical lichen indicator
abstract: Most urban lichen bioindication frameworks were developed under the substantially higher industrial and traffic-related pollution levels that characterised many European cities in previous decades. In many European cities, however, nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) concentrations have declined substantially over recent decades alongside ongoing climatic warming, raising the question of whether classical indicator species still track present-day pollution gradients. We evaluated the abundance-based indicator performance of the widely used lichen bioindicator Xanthoria parietina across complementary temporal (10 sites monitored from 2015 to 2025) and spatial (63 sites, 2023–2025) gradients in Vienna (Austria), combining repeated field surveys with year-specific spatially resolved NO₂ and climate data. During the study period, NO₂ concentrations declined markedly while air temperature increased. Across both datasets and modelling approaches, estimated NO₂ effects on lichen abundance were small, with confidence intervals overlapping zero and providing limited support for strong abundance responses within the observed NO₂ range. Contemporary NO₂ concentrations spanned a narrow and comparatively low range relative to historical urban conditions, suggesting that present-day exposure may lie largely below the species' effective abundance–response range. Accordingly, Xanthoria parietina provided little abundance-based resolution of current urban NO₂ gradients. These findings suggest that the diagnostic value of individual bioindicator species may decline when pollution levels fall below their effective response range, highlighting the importance of periodically reassessing indicator performance under shifting urban environmental baselines.

title: Can desertification reversal alleviate carbon balance pressure in energy-dominated regions? Evidence from asynchronous dynamics between ecological restoration and energy-related carbon emissions
abstract: Ecological restoration in global drylands is expected to reverse land degradation and enhance vegetation-based carbon uptake, yet its interaction with expanding energy systems remains insufficiently quantified. Using the Mu Us Sandy Land as a case study, we integrated multi-source gridded datasets from 2000 to 2020 to assess desertification reversal, NPP-based ecological buffering, energy-related CO₂ emissions, and the CO₂-oriented carbon balance pressure index (CBPI). An SPEI-informed spatial Durbin model was used to account for spatial dependence and examine associations and spillover patterns among hydroclimatic variability, desertification dynamics, socioeconomic factors, and CBPI. Results show that 59.78% of the region underwent a nonlinear transition from severe to mild desertification, with widespread non-climatic restoration signals after accounting for hydroclimatic variability. However, ecological buffering and emissions became increasingly decoupled: emissions increased more than ninefold, whereas the increase in vegetation carbon uptake potential accounted for only 31% of concurrent emission growth, indicating a shift toward an emission-dominated carbon-pressure regime. Spatial econometric results indicate that higher desertification intensity was positively associated with local CBPI, while CBPI exhibited strong spatial dependence. In energy-dominated regions, the local association between desertification reversal and CBPI was weakened, whereas spillover associations with adjacent areas were amplified. Overall, desertification reversal enhanced NPP-based ecological buffering but did not keep pace with energy-related CO₂ emissions. Ecological restoration should therefore be interpreted as carbon-pressure risk regulation—reducing exposure to persistent high-CBPI states through landscape stabilization and NPP-based buffering—rather than complete carbon-balance restoration, verified carbon offsetting, or a substitute for emission-side mitigation.

title: Enhancing satellite-based turbidity monitoring in drinking water source lakes using optical classification–guided machine learning
abstract: Turbidity is a key indicator of inland water quality and a critical parameter for the management of drinking water source lakes. In optically complex lakes, pronounced spatial heterogeneity in water optical properties often limits the reliability of conventional remote sensing–based turbidity retrieval methods, constraining their application in regional water source management. This study proposes an optical classification–guided remote sensing framework integrating machine learning to improve turbidity estimation in heterogeneous drinking water source lakes. Waters are first classified into algae dominated water, transitional water, and suspended particulate matter dominated water using K-means++ clustering based on optical characteristics, enabling water type–specific model calibration. Model evaluation shows that eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), BP neural network (BP), and random forest (RF) achieve optimal performance for algae-dominated (MAPE = 13.8%), transitional water (MAPE = 19.7%), and suspended particulate matter–dominated (MAPE = 13.7%) water, respectively. Application of the framework to three large regional drinking water source lakes reveals strong spatial heterogeneity in turbidity and consistent seasonal patterns, with higher turbidity in autumn and lower levels in spring. Mean turbidity ranges from 36.1 to 62.5 NTU across the lakes, indicating substantial variability in regional source water quality. Further analysis indicates that meteorological forcing is the dominant control on turbidity variability, explaining 88%–91% of the observed changes. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust and transferable approach for regional-scale turbidity monitoring in optically complex lakes and supports drinking water source protection and adaptive water quality management.

title: Phytoplankton community metrics and physiological ratios as indicators of light limitation and fragmentation in a dammed, sediment-laden river
abstract: Phytoplankton are primary bio-indicators of riverine ecosystem functioning, however, their robustness in turbid, fragmented systems remains poorly characterized. This study investigates spatiotemporal dynamics of phytoplankton community composition, biomass, and diversity in the Upper Red River, China, a system defined by sediment overloads and cascading dams. Seasonal field campaigns aim to evaluate the influence of hydro-physical filters (temperature, discharge and turbidity) alongside nutrient forcing. Results reveal a seasonal pattern in phytoplankton biomass, with higher levels during the dry season of lower temperatures. This is likely driven by increased water retention time and hydrological stability in dammed reaches, which appears to facilitate biomass accumulation despite lower nutrient concentrations. During the wet season, extreme turbidity and elevated flow suggest that light limitation and hydraulic flushing may override nutrient availability as primary regulators of biological metrics. Under these conditions, phytoplankton exhibit shifts in Chl-a/biomass ratios consistent with physiological strategies maximizing light-harvesting efficiency in low-light environments. We suggest that metrics like Chl-a can be unreliable indicators of total biomass in turbid environments, as their correlation is affected by community compositional shifts and potential physiological pigment adjustments. Observations indicate that the wet-season flood pulse enhances longitudinal homogenization, acting as a potential reset mechanism temporarily restoring the riverine continuum and mitigating serial discontinuity due to cascading dams. These findings point toward the flow regime as a major determinant of ecological structure in sediment-laden rivers. Effective monitoring of fragmented corridors may benefit from hydro-ecologically integrated indicators like pigment-to-biomass ratios and hydrology-based metrics, rather than over-reliance on nutrient-biomass paradigms.

title: Navigating ecological constraints in governance: The transformation of regional division as a pathway to county economic development
abstract: This study treats the designation of national key ecological function areas (NKEFA) as a quasi-natural experiment, we examine the impact of NKEFA policy on regional economic performance. The main findings are as follows: Firstly, the economic development index demonstrates a sustained upward trend over the study period, with higher levels concentrated in southeastern coastal regions as well as parts of western Inner Mongolia and Gansu. Secondly, the establishment of NKEFA significantly promotes county economic development, raising the economic development index by an average of 2.86% compared to the control group. This positive effect strengthens over time with continued policy implementation. Thirdly, this location-oriented policy primarily promotes county-level economic development by fostering technological innovation, stimulating entrepreneurial vitality, and enhancing industrial structure. It demonstrates more pronounced effects in counties located in eastern China and those with lower urbanization rates. Additionally, the policy exhibits a spatial influence on the economic development indices of neighboring counties.

title: A framework for effective long-term conservation in a changing climate
abstract: The effectiveness of many existing conservation strategies is at risk of being diminished, as they were designed and/or implemented under the assumption of a stationary rather than a changing climate. Continued support for these strategies could divert resources from alternative strategies that are more sustainable over the long term. We introduce the “longevity of existing conservation strategies” (LECS) decision-support framework for proactively assessing and adaptively managing existing strategies to enhance future conservation capacity. The framework, which is based on the concept of climate change refugia, was applied to two prototype conservation strategies, namely the reintroduction of captive-bred giant pandas into historical geographic ranges and the establishment of the Giant Panda National Park (GPNP). Long-term effectiveness was evaluated based on the potential for in situ and ex situ refugia for a phenologically-diverse bamboo food supply. Application of the LECS framework, using climate scenarios for 2061–2080 under a high emissions trajectory, suggests that 1) panda reintroduction likely would only serve as a near-term strategy except within the current range and portions of the historical range along the Tibetan Plateau, and 2) proactive management of the GPNP is needed that anticipates potential reductions in a diverse bamboo food supply in the northern GPNP and takes advantage of a projected sustained food supply in the central and southern GPNP. These two applications of the LECS framework highlight that ongoing assessment of the long-term effectiveness of existing strategies needs to become a routine component of conservation practice to reduce climate change maladaptation and misplaced conservation.

title: A multi-source data fusion approach for high-resolution mapping of forest structure and carbon storage
abstract: Accurate estimation of forest carbon storage is essential for implementing nature-based climate solutions and achieving carbon-neutrality goals, particularly in China, which has the world's largest afforestation efforts. Although remote sensing offers powerful tools, accurately quantifying carbon in heterogeneous forest landscapes remains challenging due to the complex vertical structure and the difficulty of scaling plot-level measurements. This study presents a multi-source data fusion framework that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle LiDAR, airborne LiDAR, Sentinel-1/2 satellite imagery, and ground inventory data to produce a high-resolution map of forest carbon storage in the Tongshan District of Xuzhou City. The key lies in stratifying forests into single- and multi-layer types using canopy entropy (CE)—a metric derived from LiDAR point clouds that quantifies structural complexity. Separate random forest models were then developed for each forest type, with input features optimized using SHAP analysis. This stratified modeling approach significantly improves prediction accuracy (RMSE%: 6.23% for single-layer and 8.61% for multi-layer forests) compared to a unified model (RMSE% = 10.23%). The resulting carbon map estimates the total forest carbon storage in Tongshan at 1.30 Tg, revealing substantial carbon sequestration potential in rehabilitated mining areas associated with ecological restoration projects. This method demonstrates that incorporating structural stratification based on CE can effectively reduce estimation errors caused by forest heterogeneity, providing robust technical support for regional high-precision carbon monitoring.

title: Characterizing “production-living-ecological” space conflicts in China's ecologically fragile regions: the case of the floodplain of the Lower Yellow River
abstract: This study examines the interactive evolution of production-living-ecological (PLE) spaces and the spatiotemporal variations in spatial conflicts across the Lower Yellow River Floodplain. The Markov land-use transition matrix, spatial conflict comprehensive index (SCCI), kernel density estimation, and spatial autocorrelation analysis were employed to characterize spatiotemporal patterns. Multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) and Geodetector models were used to quantify core drivers behind PLE spatial conflict changes. The main findings are as follows: (1) During the study period, the study area experienced remarkable spatial restructuring, showing a decrease in production and living spaces and an expansion of ecological space. Agricultural production and rural living spaces shrunk continuously, whereas aquatic ecological spaces expanded rapidly and dominated overall ecological space growth. (2) Spatial conflict intensity first increased and then decreased. The SCCI value rose from 0.32 in 2000 to 0.35 in 2018, before a slight drop to 0.34 in 2020, closely tied to regional land-use restructuring and spatial governance practices. (3) PLE spatial conflicts showed substantial spatial unevenness, with low-low (L-L) clustering as the dominant pattern. The Henan reach and the Kenli section of Shandong Province remained relatively stable low-conflict zones. (4) Both natural and socioeconomic factors shaped the evolutionary changes of these conflicts. Population density (PD), land-use intensity (LUI), and road density (RD) showed relatively strong explanatory effects on spatial conflict variability. Factor interactions consistently outperformed individual factors, pointing to clear synergy among multiple drivers. These findings strengthen the empirical understanding of PLE conflict evolution in floodplain areas and provide useful evidence for formulating differentiated spatial governance schemes.

title: Spatially divergent cropland disturbance and driving mechanisms in the transboundary Heilongjiang River basin, 1990–2021
abstract: Cropland disturbance monitoring is essential for sustainable agriculture and ecosystem conservation, yet remains challenging over large areas due to the complexity of land use change processes. This study developed a cost-effective framework to monitor cropland disturbance and analyze its driving forces in the Heilongjiang River Basin (HRB), a transboundary basin spanning China, Mongolia, and Russia. The framework integrated Landsat time-series imagery, machine learning, change-detection algorithms, and decision tree models. We processed 36,027 Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI images and used the random forest classifiers trained with annual cropland samples and spectral-temporal features to estimate annual cropland probability (1990–2021). The LandTrendr algorithm segmented the cropland probability time series to determine the spatiotemporal distribution and intensity of cropland disturbance. A decision tree model quantified contributions of different disturbance drivers. The framework enables a more comprehensive assessment of cropland stability through the integration of disturbance detection and driver attribution. Our results reveal that 128.9 × 10 4 ha of cropland were disturbed between 1990 and 2021, of which 762,900 ha (59%) were classified as severely disturbed, indicating sustained pressure on regional agroecosystems. Agricultural activities and cropland fallow accounted for for 47% and 22%of total disturbances, reflecting dominant human influences across the transboundary region. On the Chinese side (Heilongjiang and Jilin), disturbances were primarily driven by urban expansion and agricultural activities, whereas cropland fallow and abandonment dominated in the Russian side (Zabaykal'ye). These spatial divergences underscore that cropland disturbances emerge from the interplay between natural environmental conditions and region-specific policy contexts. This study clarifies the mechanisms driving cropland change in transboundary basin regions and provides a scientific basis for region-specific land management and coordinated ecological conservation to support sustainable agricultural development.

title: Spatial patterns of cultural ecosystem services and their associated landscape factors in a coastal wetland park: A case study of Minjiang River estuary Wetland Park, China
abstract: Cultural ecosystem services (CES) are an important link between ecological conservation and human well-being. However, their identification and quantification are often constrained by insufficient attention to local cultural contexts and limited understanding of associated landscape factors, which restricts the development of targeted site management strategies. Using the Fujian Changle Minjiang River Estuary National Wetland Park as a case study, this study integrated social media texts, on-site questionnaire data, and field-measured landscape data to develop a localized CES assessment framework and to identify the spatial distribution and associated landscape factors of CES. Evaluation indicators were derived through text mining and semantic mapping, and factor analysis was used to identify CES dimensions. Kernel density estimation, correlation analysis, one-way ANOVA, and stepwise regression were then applied for integrated analysis. The results showed that: Bi et al. (2024) ( Bi et al., 2024 ) CES in the study area comprised five dimensions, namely physical and mental restoration, sense of identity, capacity enhancement, connection to nature and inspiration, and spiritual significance; Busch et al. (2024) ( Busch et al., 2024 ) waterbody type and bird activity were significantly associated with differences in the overall CES score, whereas resting facilities showed significant associations only with specific dimensions; and ( Calcagni et al., 2022 ( Calcagni et al., 2022 )) waterbody type, spatial type, and shaded area jointly explained 36.0% of the variance in total CES scores; and ( Cao et al., 2022 ( Cao et al., 2022 )) sea water scene, spatial type, and shaded area formed the main direct statistical associations with CES perception. These findings indicate that CES in the Minjiang River Estuary Wetland Park arise from the combined influences of ecological elements, spatial organization, and local cultural practices. This study provides case-based evidence for understanding the perception and spatial variation of CES in the Minjiang River Estuary Wetland Park, and offers references for cultural resource conservation, public space optimization, and refined management in similar coastal wetland parks.

title: Few-shot transfer learning for endemic and data-scarce species: A scalable framework for bioacoustic analysis and monitoring
abstract: Acoustic communication pervades the animal kingdom, spanning taxa from insects to whales, with many species employing structured sequences of acoustic elements for interaction. Bioacoustics, the study of sound production, transmission, and reception in animals, plays a critical role in understanding wildlife behavior, communication, and ecological dynamics. Many endemic species are elusive, nocturnal, or inhabit remote regions, and some are acoustically active only during limited temporal windows. These factors make large-scale labeled data collection challenging. Furthermore, many deep learning studies exclude species with fewer than 50 annotated recordings during dataset curation, thereby limiting representation of rare and low-resource taxa. This highlights the need for data-efficient learning strategies capable of operating under severe data scarcity. In this study, we investigate episodic meta-learning using PANN-derived embeddings and Prototypical Networks for Few-shot species classification under low-resource conditions. Using the BirdCLEF 2024 dataset as a benchmark, we evaluate the proposed framework across varying N-way and K-shot settings to assess generalization to Novel species. Experimental results demonstrate that metric-based meta-learning enables robust adaptation to unseen and underrepresented species with minimal supervision. Under the Base versus Novel generalization evaluation, the proposed network achieves Novel species classification accuracies of 61.1 ± 2.13%, 47.7 ± 1.89%, and 38.0 ± 1.93% under 3-way, 5-way, and 8-way evaluation settings respectively with only five support samples per species, all substantially exceeding their corresponding random chance baselines of 33.3%, 20%, and 12.5%. Compared to a transfer learning baseline that utilizes the same PANN embedding backbone but relies on episode-level fine-tuning rather than episodic meta-learning, the proposed FSL model consistently outperforms across all settings, achieving improvements of +6.8%, +9.3%, and +10.3% at 3-way, 5-way, and 8-way respectively, with all differences statistically significant at p < 0 . 001 and Cohen’s d increasing from 0.42 to 1.08 across settings. The model additionally demonstrates substantial computational efficiency, completing inference over 500 episodes approximately 6 × , 5 × , and 4 × faster than the transfer learning baseline at 3-way, 5-way, and 8-way settings respectively, while achieving superior classification accuracy across all evaluation settings. These results collectively demonstrate that the proposed framework generalizes effectively to previously unseen species with minimal supervision, offering a taxonomically and computationally scalable solution for long-tail biodiversity monitoring. By emphasizing performance in data-constrained scenarios, this work contributes to the development of efficient, ecologically meaningful automated acoustic monitoring systems.

title: Detailed photovoltaic mapping and multidimensional analysis based on deep learning: a case study in Jiangsu Province, China
abstract: Solar photovoltaics (PV) constitute a key component of renewable energy, and accurately mapping their spatial distribution and assessing their environmental benefits are crucial for energy planning and sustainable development. Focusing on Jiangsu Province, China, this study employs deep learning techniques to develop a semantic segmentation network named PV-AssNet for the precise extraction of PV distributions from high-resolution remote sensing imagery. Building on this, a systematic analysis is conducted to investigate their spatial patterns, land use preferences, and carbon reduction benefits. The results show that PV-AssNet enhances PV identification performance, achieving an overall mapping accuracy of over 98% and outperforming other comparative models. The total PV area in Jiangsu Province in 2020 was 142.01 km 2 , exhibiting significant spatial heterogeneity, with high-density clusters mainly concentrated in cities of Yancheng, Suqian, and Huai'an. Water surfaces (primarily reservoirs and ponds) were the dominant land use type for PV deployment, accounting for 45.71% of the total area, followed by cropland and construction land. The carbon payback period for PV systems was approximately 2.19 years, achieving considerable net carbon emission reduction benefits over its lifecycle, with the pace of carbon benefit realization showing minimal variation across different land types. The findings provide a scientific basis for PV resource planning and territorial spatial policy formulation in Jiangsu Province, as well as a reference for coordinating regional renewable energy layout and land use optimization.

title: Ensemble-based estimation of fractional vegetation cover in arid and semi-arid regions
abstract: Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) is a key biophysical parameter for characterizing vegetation dynamics and ecosystem functioning, and is essential for ecological monitoring in arid and semi-arid regions. However, sparse vegetation and strong soil background effects in these regions lead to substantial variability in the applicability and stability of different inversion models, thereby limiting further improvements in FVC estimation accuracy. To address these challenges, this study applied three FVC inversion models—Random Forest (RF), Fully Constrained Least Squares (FCLS), and the Dimidiate Pixel Model (DPM)—to Sentinel-2 data, and further proposed a consistency-constrained ensemble approach. The results show that the three models exhibit pronounced discrepancies in both spatial patterns and value ranges. Specifically, RF performs better in high-coverage areas, whereas FCLS is more sensitive to soil background effects under low-coverage conditions. The proposed ensemble approach effectively integrates the strengths of individual models, improving overall accuracy by approximately 2.1% and reducing estimation uncertainty relative to individual models. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves FVC estimation in arid and semi-arid regions and provides a robust framework for large-scale quantitative vegetation monitoring using remote sensing.

title: Identifying algal indicators for streamflow duration assessment methods in forested headwater streams
abstract: Streamflow duration assessment methods (SDAMs) are rapid tools for reach-scale streamflow duration classification. SDAMs use single-visit indicator data as surrogates because direct measurement of long-term flow duration is resource intensive. Algae (diatoms and soft-bodied algae) are potentially strong indicators of streamflow-duration class (SDC) because of geographical ubiquity and biodiversity across moisture gradients. Algal cover and algal assemblage data (presence/absence, density, and biovolume) at species- and genus-levels were analyzed from 508 samples across 22 ephemeral, 37 intermittent, and 51 perennial reaches distributed along 31 forested headwater streams within 4 ecoregions in the contiguous United States. Random forest models using species- and genus-level datasets to predict SDCs had classification accuracy ranging from 69.5% – 88.4%, with accuracy being highest for density, intermediate for presence/absence, lowest for biovolume data. Species-level models had 0.6% – 5.9% higher accuracy for density and presence/absence datasets than genus-level models. Based on their median ranks of minimum node depth among random forest models, season (wet vs dry) was a more important factor than habitat sampled (erosional vs depositional) when distinguishing ephemeral, intermittent and perennial but habitat was more important when distinguishing ephemeral from non-ephemeral reaches. Algal cover index (categorical visual-tactile assessment) was the most important indicator of SDC. Except for the red alga, Audouinella , the identified indicator taxa were diatoms. Our findings support epilithic algal cover as an SDAM indicator for forested headwater streams. Until taxonomic tools are available for field identifications, algal cover index and abundance of soft-bodied algae and live diatoms may be candidate indicators for regional SDAMs.

title: Dominant role of CO₂ in the decoupling of structural and functional resilience indicators in the Yellow River Basin
abstract: Ecosystem resilience is essential for maintaining the structural and functional stability of terrestrial ecosystems under ongoing climate change and human disturbances. However, the long-term coupled evolutionary relationships between vegetation structural and multi-dimensional functional resilience remain poorly understood, restricting comprehensive resilience assessment of watershed ecosystems. Here, we employed first-order lag autoregressive coefficients (AR(1)) of leaf area index (LAI), water use efficiency (WUE), gross primary productivity (GPP), and evapotranspiration (ET) to quantify vegetation structural resilience and multiple key functional resilience dimensions across the Yellow River Basin during 1982–2018. We systematically explored their spatiotemporal dynamics, phase-dependent coupling patterns, and zonal differentiation across three climatic zones, and further identified dominant driving factors using interpretable machine learning (XGBoost-SHAP). The evolution of structure–function coupled resilience experienced a transition from weak coupling before 2000 to strong coupling in the 2000s, followed by a pronounced decoupling in the 2010s, with the humid and semi-humid zones exhibiting the most dramatic interdecadal shifts. Notably, the most prominent decoupling was observed between WUE resilience and LAI resilience in the plateau cold zone, while the resilience of GPP and ET maintained favorable coordination with LAI resilience. Driving mechanism analysis indicated that atmospheric CO₂ acted as the dominant factor regulating spatiotemporal variations in structural and functional resilience. In arid and humid zones, rising CO₂ increasingly inhibited LAI structural resilience while imposing weaker constraints on WUE functional resilience. Nevertheless, the plateau cold zone showed a unique response, with intensified CO₂-induced suppression on both structural and functional resilience. These findings emphasize the necessity of integrating structural and functional resilience dimensions in ecosystem assessments and highlight the importance of region-specific strategies for large-scale ecological restoration and adaptive management under global change.

title: Forest origin reorganizes environmental control of soil microbial diversity across natural and planted forests
abstract: Soil microbial diversity is a key foundation of forest ecosystem functioning, yet it remains unclear whether forest origin alters both its diversity level and the environmental controls that regulate it. Using a global geo-referenced dataset comprising 610 observations from natural and planted forests, we compared soil microbial Shannon diversity between forest origins and examined the associated environmental driver hierarchy. Microbial diversity was lower in planted forests than in natural forests, and this difference remained after accounting for climate, stand structure, topography, soil properties and study-level clustering. The decline was evident in both bacterial and fungal datasets, with no significant forest origin × microbial group interaction. Natural and planted forests occupied partially distinct environmental space, but the diversity contrast persisted after environmental adjustment, indicating that the plantation effect was not explained by background site conditions alone. Random-forest models showed that dominant predictors differed between forest origins: microbial diversity in natural forests was more closely associated with stand attributes and soil texture, whereas that in planted forests was more strongly linked to elevation, soil carbon and phosphorus availability. Sensitivity analysis excluding forest age broadly retained the main predictor-domain structure. Nonlinear analyses further showed distinct response curves of microbial diversity to major predictors across forest origins. Path analysis showed that climate influenced microbial diversity mainly through stand- and soil-mediated pathways, while topography and soil texture imposed stronger constraints in planted forests. Together, these results show that forest origin not only reduces soil microbial diversity, but also reorganizes the hierarchy and pathways of environmental control. These findings provide a global perspective on belowground biodiversity change under afforestation and suggest that recovery of microbial diversity in planted forests depends on rebuilding stand continuity and soil habitat heterogeneity, rather than increasing tree cover alone.

title: Analyzing spatio-temporal patterns of crown dieback and dead forest trees detected by AI and aerial RGB imagery
abstract: Monitoring the quantity and spatial distribution of dead and dieback trees is essential for tracking forest health and understanding drivers of decline. However, individual-tree level assessments remain temporally and spatially discontinuous due to financial constraints. Regularly collected aerial and drone imagery, combined with deep learning algorithms, now offer new opportunities for spatially continuous monitoring of tree health, enabling the identification of spatiotemporal decline patterns valuable for forest management. Here, we used UltraCam-Xp aerial images (2014, 2016) and UAV images (2025) to detect dieback and dead trees in the Alang Darreh Forest, Iran, using a hybrid YOLO11s-SAM model across three time points. Spatial patterns of detected trees were analyzed using Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi statistics to identify hot and cold spots of tree decline. The identified health decline patterns were then related to topographic variables and the distance from roads using Gi Z -score values, Spearman coefficients and a relative effect analysis to understand the reasons for the observed tree decline. To further understand the drivers of these patterns, we employed multiple regression with two-way interaction terms to also assess the combined effects of slope, elevation, aspect, and road distance on forest decline. Accuracy assessment results showed that the hybrid deep learning model detected dieback and dead trees with overall accuracies of 95.55–98.51% (Kappa coefficients of 0.93–0.97) and 84.79–88.76% (Kappa of 0.74–0.82), at point and polygon levels, respectively. Spatial pattern analyses revealed clustered patterns for dead trees in all years, while dieback trees showed a random distribution in 2014 and a clustered distribution in 2016 and 2025. Spearman correlations revealed significant negative relationships of tree health decline with elevation and slope, and varying positive correlations with aspect across years. Distance from park roads showed mostly negative correlations with tree decline, except for dead trees in 2016. Multiple regression further revealed that road distance was the strongest predictor of forest decline, while significant two-way interactions among road distance, elevation, and aspect confirmed that environmental factors act in combination rather than independently. Relative effect analyses highlighted higher densities of dieback and dead trees at elevations of 400–450 m, slopes below 50%, northeastern to southeastern aspects, and within 150 m of forest roads. In summary, this research demonstrates how high-resolution RGB imagery in combination with the YOLO11s-SAM hybrid deep learning approach provides reliable information for spatio-temporal monitoring of forest decline at individual tree level that among others can serve as a valuable step to guide the sampling procedures of subsequent studies seeking to identify mechanistic reasons for forest health decline. Our approach can be easily adapted for other forest types and regions where high resolution RGB imagery is available.

title: Research on the ecological network and resilience of Yantai based on circuit theory and robustness modeling
abstract: Research on ecological network resilience is key to understanding how ecosystems maintain their structure and function in response to external disturbances. This study evaluates the resilience of ecological networks by employing circuit theory and robustness models. Circuit theory serves as a tool for quantifying energy flow and analyzing system stability by analogizing ecological sources, corridors, and species interactions in an ecological network to nodes and connections in an electrical circuit. The robustness model, on the other hand, further assesses the recovery capacity of an ecological network when facing node or connection failures. By simulating different disturbance scenarios—random corridor failures versus targeted disruptions to critical corridors—this study examines changes in ecological functionality under environmental shifts, analyzing the vulnerability and connectivity of the ecological network. The results indicate that over the past two decades, Yantai City has experienced no significant changes in habitat quality or carbon storage, suggesting overall ecological stability. The structural integrity of the ecological network hinges on the protection and optimization of ecological pinch points and barrier points, while the number of ecological corridors determines network stability. Additionally, redundancy in the ecological network contributes positively to stability—highly connected networks exhibit strong resilience against random disturbances but remain vulnerable to targeted attacks on critical nodes.By analyzing structural changes in the ecological network and simulating corridor disruptions via robustness modeling.

title: Phosphorus speciation and its coupling with organic matter in the water–sediment system of Lake Dian, southwestern China
abstract: The distribution characteristics, concentration dynamics, and organic matter (OM) interactions of different phosphorus (P) species in lake sediments are fundamental to understanding P cycling and release mechanisms. This study investigated P speciation, concentrations, and their associations with OM in the sediments and pore water of Lake Dian, with a focus on spatial heterogeneity and centennial-scale evolution. Results showed that sedimentary P was predominantly retained in relatively stable fractions, namely NaOH-rP, HCl-P, and Res P. Pore-water dissolved organic matter (DOM) was dominated by authigenic, protein-like components, whereas sedimentary OM originated from mixed sources, including aquatic macrophytes, algae, and sewage inputs. Centennial sediment records indicated that increases in P and OM concentrations coincide with the intensification of watershed anthropogenic activities. The spatial co-distribution of OM and P suggested that OM enhanced internal P mobilization by regulating redox conditions and promoting the transformation of labile P fractions (e.g., BD-P). The sediment–water P cycle was governed by coupled physical transport and OM-driven biogeochemical processes. Notably, the degradation of algal-derived OM was identified as a key driver of internal P loading, as it stimulated microbial activity and oxygen consumption, thereby facilitating P release. These findings indicate that effective lake management should integrate external nutrient load reduction with strategies targeting OM-mediated internal P cycling to achieve sustainable water quality improvement in Lake Dian.

title: Multitaxon assessment reveals inconsistent biodiversity responses to forest structural complexity in Flemish forests
abstract: Abstract Increasing forest structural complexity is a key objective of future-proof forest management, with potential benefits for biodiversity. However, empirical evidence for consistent biodiversity-structure relationships across taxa is still limited. We investigated whether structurally more complex forests support greater species richness and higher multidiversity across taxonomic and functional groups in 19 mature forest plots in Flanders, Belgium. As one of the most densely populated and urbanized regions in Europe, with limited and highly fragmented forest cover, Flanders provides a particularly informative and policy-relevant context to test structure–biodiversity relationships. Its forests, often dominated by a few tree species and subject to long-term anthropogenic pressures and management, represent a realistic gradient of structural complexity. Structural complexity was quantified using a Structural Complexity Index (SCI), and biodiversity was assessed using a multidiversity index integrating scaled species richness across five taxonomic and seven arthropod functional groups. Using mixed-effects models and multivariate Bayesian analyses, we tested both direct effects of SCI on biodiversity and the covariation in species richness among groups. Contrary to expectations, SCI was not a consistent predictor of multidiversity, and most groups showed weak or inconsistent responses. These findings might suggest that structural complexity alone may be insufficient to enhance biodiversity in simplified forests. Highlights Forest structural complexity does not consistently predict biodiversity. Responses vary among taxonomic and functional groups. Cross-taxon congruence in diversity is limited and scale-dependent. Keywords: Forest structural complexity; Multidiversity, Species richness; Functional groups; Sustainable forest management

title: Conservation prioritization of macrobenthic communities in subtropical bays: Insights from multidimensional beta diversity and community assembly processes
abstract: Understanding the spatial patterns of biodiversity and the underlying mechanisms of community assembly provides a scientific basis for the conservation and management of coastal ecosystems. Using macrobenthic communities from three subtropical bays and adjacent open waters in China, we assessed taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic beta diversity (βsor) and partitioned it into turnover (βsim) and nestedness (βnes) components. We employed variation partitioning (VPA), local contributions to beta diversity (LCBD), species contributions to beta diversity (SCBD), neutral community modeling (NCM), and the modified stochasticity ratio (MST) to identify key drivers of community differentiation and the relative roles of deterministic versus stochastic assembly processes. Results showed that βsim dominated βsor across all diversity dimensions. Spatial factors generally outperformed environmental variables in explaining beta diversity. Bay areas exhibited significantly higher ecological uniqueness in functional and phylogenetic composition, with deterministic processes dominating their community assembly, whereas stochastic processes prevailed in open waters. This study highlights that bay communities, shaped by environmental filtering, harbor unique functional trait combinations and evolutionary histories and should be assigned higher conservation priority. Integrating multidimensional beta diversity with community assembly mechanisms provides a quantifiable scientific framework for guiding conservation planning and marine protected area design in coastal ecosystems.

title: Contrasting wildlife detection trends without occupancy change: interpreting long-term camera-trap indicators in a protected woodland
abstract: Human recreation is increasingly widespread in protected landscapes, raising concern about its potential effects on wildlife. At the same time, long-term camera-trap networks are becoming central tools for biodiversity monitoring, yet detection-based indices integrate abundance, movement and behavioural activity, complicating interpretation. Long duration, standardised datasets therefore offer valuable opportunities to distinguish behavioural disturbance from broader ecological change. We analysed 16 years of camera-trap data from five fixed woodland locations within a protected landscape to evaluate long-term wildlife trends and assess whether detection-based indicators reflect recreational disturbance or broader ecological dynamics. Species-specific temporal trends were estimated using generalised additive mixed models accounting for sampling effort and location. Dynamic occupancy models were used to distinguish changes in site use from changes in detection or behaviour, and short term disturbance models tested behavioural responses to daily variation in recreation. Wildlife detection trajectories differed among species. Deer species showed overall declines, whereas mesopredators and small mammals were stable or increased. Despite these contrasting detection trends, occupancy probabilities remained stable. Recreational activity also varied among user types: cyclist and dog-related detections increased, while detections of people without dogs or bicycles showed little long-term change. Short-term disturbance effects were weak and inconsistent, and strong diel segregation between humans and wildlife persisted across recreation levels. These findings suggest routine recreation alone is unlikely to explain long-term changes in wildlife detections. Long-term camera-trap monitoring can reveal shifts in wildlife activity patterns and community structure, but detection-based indicators require cautious interpretation alongside occupancy estimates and broader ecological context.

title: Moss biocrusts enhance soil carbon stabilization via microbial necromass accumulation in the karst rocky desertification region of eastern Yunnan, China
abstract: Karst ecosystems are globally important carbon sinks, yet the escalating severity of rocky desertification is causing continuous losses of soil carbon stocks. As a key biological component of karst rocky desertification environment, moss biocrusts play crucial ecological roles, but their impacts on the accumulation of soil microbial necromass and organic carbon remain largely unexplored. In the present study, soils covered by moss biocrusts were collected from rocky desertification sites with different degrees of degradation in Zhanyi District, Qujing City, Yunnan Province, China, at both the biocrust layer (0–1 cm) and the underlying sub-layer (1–5 cm). Soil physicochemical properties, microbial biomass, enzyme activities, and amino sugar content were quantified, and the contribution of microbial necromass carbon to soil organic carbon formation was assessed. The results showed that: (1) with increasing rocky desertification intensity, habitats covered by moss biocrusts exhibited pronounced resource island effects, thereby improving soil physicochemical properties and further promoting the accumulation of microbial necromass carbon and soil organic carbon. (2) fungal necromass carbon accounted for a larger proportion of total microbial necromass carbon than bacterial necromass carbon. Meanwhile, the formation of microbial necromass carbon in the biocrust layer was primarily driven by nutrient supply capacity, microbial activities, and nitrogen cycling processes, whereas its accumulation in the sub-layer was strongly regulated by soil moisture conditions, nutrient availability, and substrate decomposition processes.
