For fragmentation, the dominant process shifted from subdivision at low elevations to shrinkage, whereas perforation became increasingly frequent toward higher elevations, revealing clear altitudinal variations in forest configuration. This study provides a spatially explicit characterization of long-term forest pattern dynamics derived from the CLCD dataset and offers a useful spatial perspective for interpreting forest restoration patterns in fragile karst landscapes.

title: Ecosystem carbon fluxes represent a key mechanism underlying the precipitation-dependent pattern of ecosystem multifunctionality
abstract: Precipitation plays a fundamental role in shaping ecosystem functions, yet ongoing global warming is substantially altering regional precipitation patterns with profound implications for ecosystem multifunctionality ( EMF ). Despite its importance, precipitation-dependent patterns of EMF and their underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood at regional scales. We systematically examined ecosystems (grasslands, shrublands, and forests) spanning precipitation gradients to characterize how EMF varies with precipitation, quantify its sensitivity to precipitation changes, and elucidate the mechanistic role of ecosystem carbon fluxes in mediating these relationships. We identified a pronounced threshold effect in the precipitation- EMF relationship, with EMF peaking at 600–800 mm of annual precipitation. Both water limitation (<200 mm) and excess (>1000 mm) suppressed EMF , demonstrating that moderate precipitation optimizes the simultaneous expression of multiple ecosystem functions. Across semi-humid and semi-arid regions, each 100 mm increase in precipitation elevated EMF by 0.273, 0.483, and 0.187 units in grasslands, shrublands, and forests, respectively, revealing substantial potential for EMF enhancement through moderate precipitation increases in these transitional zones. Importantly, climatic and edaphic factors modulated EMF across vegetation types via distinct carbon flux pathways: elevated ecosystem respiration ( RE ) emerged as the primary driver of grassland EMF , while net ecosystem productivity ( NEP ) played a more critical role in shrublands. Forest EMF responded predominantly to plant species richness and gross primary productivity ( GPP ), though excessive moisture imposed significant constraints. Notably, soil texture and pH consistently predicted EMF across all three ecosystem types. Our results demonstrate that ecosystem carbon fluxes constitute a key mechanistic pathway through which climatic and edaphic factors shape EMF , advancing our understanding of how climate-productivity interactions govern multifunctionality in terrestrial ecosystems.

title: Effect of soil and water conservation measures on the water–sediment relationships at different time scales in the Loess Plateau, China
abstract: The increasing prevalence of extreme rainfall events has further complicated the water–sediment relationship. Understanding the multiscale evolution of this relationship and its response to extreme rainfall is critical for effective sediment regulation. In this study, we employed multiple methods, including change point detection, percentile-based thresholds, and water–sediment rating curves, to examine changes in extreme rainfall across the Loess Plateau (LP)from 1961 to 2020. We studied the evolution and driving mechanisms of the water–sediment relationship at multiple temporal scales in the multi spatial scale watersheds of the middle reaches of the Yellow River (YRB). The results showed the following: From 1961 to 2020, the LP experienced increased spatial extent, higher frequency, and greater intensity of extreme rainfall events. Although the period 2001–2020 recorded the highest values of these indices over the 60-year period, our event-scale analysis, based on flood events grouped by comparable areal rainfall depths, reveals that since 2000, mean flood runoff under such comparable conditions decreased by 69% relative to pre-1980 levels, while sediment transport per event declined by 87%. After 2000, at the interannual scale, the rainfall-sediment correlation weakened considerably, exhibiting varying degrees of negative correlation in the Kuye, Huangfuchuan, and Wuding River Basins, as conservation measures altered underlying surface conditions, reduced runoff erosion and caused structural decoupling between sediment production and transport. At the event scale, extreme rainfall intensified the nonlinear water–sediment relationship, increasing the risk of high-sediment flood events. Soil and water conservation measures, however, substantially prolonged flood durations, attenuated peak discharges, and dissipated energy, which resulted in an approximately 70% reduction in sediment yield. In conclusion, frequent extreme rainfall events are progressively reshaping water and sediment dynamics on the LP. Although soil and water conservation measures have markedly reduced sediment loads, their marginal returns are diminishing. These findings provide a scientific foundation to optimizing soil and water conservation strategies in the YRB.

title: Altitudinal shifts of mining disturbances: linking operational impacts of high-altitude tailings ponds to soil microbial functional regulation
abstract: High-altitude mining has become an emerging ecological concern, yet its impacts remain less studied than those in mid-to-high altitude regions. By integrating soil physicochemical properties, heavy metal factors, and metagenomic data from a total of 45 sampling sites around tailings ponds (average altitude >3700 m) on the Tibet Plateau in China, this study elucidated the two potential explanatory factors (tailings ponds operation and rising altitude) on soil microbial communities in high-altitude regions, and how microbial community response strategies shifted under different habitat stresses. The results showed that the environmental changes induced by rising altitude may affect the impact of anthropogenic disturbance from the operation of tailings pond, as certain soil heavy metal factors tend to influence microbial community structure synergistically with the altitudinal gradient. Microbial communities significantly enhanced the abundance of functional genes related to metal resistance and biogeochemical cycling in response to operational disturbances. However, the relative abundance of these functional genes decreased as the relative abundance of high contributing species decreased at higher altitudes. The metal resistance response might be primarily sustained by the remaining abundant species, and the long-term retention of nutrients indicated the nutrient enrichment of candidate archaea. This study fills a critical gap in understanding the ecological impacts of mining activities at high altitudes and provides new insights into the adaptive mechanisms of high-altitude soil ecosystems under the dual pressures of anthropogenic disturbance and natural stress.

title: Balancing hydrological trade-offs through land-use regulation in a semi-arid watershed
abstract: Effective land-use regulation is a key policy instrument for shaping watershed hydrology and promoting sustainable regional development. However, current land-use policies often rely on uniform, single-objective that overlook spatial heterogeneity and integrated hydrological trade-offs. Here, we selected the Yanhe River Basin on the Loess Plateau, China, as a case study, where rapid land-use transitions have intensified water-resource constraints. SWAT model was applied to simulate hydrological responses under 15 slope-based land-use scenarios reflecting various policy options. An ecological indicator-based evaluation framework incorporating evapotranspiration (ET), water yield (WYLD), and soil moisture (SM) was developed to identify optimal subbasin-level regulation schemes and to assess their resilience under future climate scenarios. Results show that both ET and WYLD increased basin-wide from 2000 to 2022. Afforestation elevated ET and reduced SM, particularly in downstream areas, whereas grassland restoration moderated ET increases and enhanced WYLD. The most effective land-use strategy involves protecting existing cropland and converting slopes >15° in the upper–middle basin and > 5° in the middle-lower basin to grassland. This spatially differentiated strategy simultaneously reduces ET, while maintains SM and increases WYLD, offering the largest hydrological benefits both historically and under future climate conditions. The highest benefits were observed under SSP126 (WYLD +4.19%; ET −8.93 mm), followed by SSP585 (WYLD +3.96%; ET −8.69 mm). By translating hydrological trade-offs into slope- and subbasin-specific regulation rules, this study provides actionable policy guidance for optimizing land-use planning, improving water security, and aligning ecological restoration programs with hydrological constraints in the Loess Plateau.

title: Hierarchical contributions of ontogeny, species identity, stand competition, and local environment to biomass allocation in subtropical coniferous and broadleaved tree species
abstract: How ontogeny, species identity, stand competition, and local environment jointly shape biomass allocation in subtropical trees—and differ between conifers and broadleaves — remains unresolved. We destructively sampled 730 trees from five dominant subtropical species in Hunan, China ( Cunninghamia lanceolata , Pinus massoniana , Populus deltoides , Quercus glauca , and Camphora officinarum ), during 2023–2024 across plantations and natural secondary forests. Drivers of root, stem wood, bark, branch, and leaf biomass were partitioned with linear mixed-effects models including plot and species random effects. Individual size was the dominant driver, with standardised effects of 0.49–0.69 exceeding all other predictors by an order of magnitude and explaining 55–99% of variance in organ biomass (marginal R 2 = 0.55–0.99). Species identity contributed a substantial secondary signal, accounting for 15–33% of variance and producing significant random intercepts for all organs and size slopes for all above-ground organs ( P ≤ 0.007); conifer–broadleaf divergence was strongest in bark and branch–leaf scaling, with broadleaves coordinating branch–leaf investment ( r = 0.54) and conifers prioritising stems. After controlling for ontogeny and species, stand density selectively reduced bark allocation ( P = 0.007–0.008) without affecting other organs. Abiotic effects were weak and organ-specific: slope and soil depth marginally influenced leaf and bark allocation, whereas regional climate variables (PET, CWD) at ∼1 km 2 resolution explained no additional variation once size, species, plot and local factors were accounted for, consistent with scale mismatch against plot-level measurements. Allocation in these species therefore reflects mainly individual size and species identity, with stand competition and local habitat contributing organ-specific secondary effects relevant to regional carbon accounting.

title: Estimation of canopy bulk density for modeling fire behavior in boreal forest of Northeastern China using forest inventory and multisource satellite remote sensing data
abstract: Canopy bulk density (CBD) data is essential for modeling the behavior of crown fires. Few studies generated spatially continuous CBD maps at landscape scale in China. This study developed a framework to estimate CBD using Chinese forest inventory data and multisource remote sensing imagery. We devised an indirect method for calculating plot level CBD based on the load-over-depth concept, integrating Chinese National Forest Inventory plots data and species-specific allometric equations. Pearson correlation and recursive feature elimination were used to identify optimal predictors for ensemble learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting. RF demonstrated the highest performance among these algorithms. The R 2 for the model were 0.67 and 0.57, respectively, and the RMSE values were 0.0219 kg/m 3 and 0.0269 kg/m 3 . The final 10-m resolution CBD map generated by the RF model for the study area, which revealed values ranging from 0.0180 to 0.1476 kg/m 3 , with a mean of 0.0808 kg/m 3 . Pixel-level uncertainty in spatial extrapolation was also quantified based on the RMSE and rRMSE. Additionally, explainable analysis identified the contribution of each selected feature. The accuracy of the resulting maps can serve as a baseline for the Chinese boreal forest.

title: Soundscape preferences at Mount Kilimanjaro reveal differing perceptions of non-material nature's contributions between residents and tourists
abstract: Soundscapes allow people to experience nature and associated non-material Nature's Contributions to People (NCP), such as restorative or aesthetic experiences. However, little research has investigated the relationship between specific acoustic characteristics and perceived non-material NCP, and whether these associations differ between social groups. To this end, we assessed the preferences of residents and tourists for soundscapes at Mount Kilimanjaro (Tanzania), representing seven acoustically distinct habitats at both dawn and dusk times of the day. Specifically, we examined how both groups related eleven context-specific non-material NCP to their preferred soundscapes. To identify factors, including seven acoustic indices as measures of acoustic characteristics, associated with NCP selection, we applied generalized linear mixed models. Overall, dawn soundscapes were preferred over dusk, likely due to the dominance and variability of bird vocalizations compared to the louder, insect driven dusk soundscapes. However, preferred soundscapes originated from different habitats; for example, subalpine habitats were favored by tourists but strongly disliked by residents. The acoustic characteristics of preferred soundscapes differed between residents and tourists, and so did the associated non-material NCP, potentially reflecting residents' cultural ties to the region (e.g., cultural heritage) and tourists' demands for natural areas (e.g., therapeutic experiences). Seven non-material NCP were correlated with specific acoustic indices, demonstrating how these indices can serve as valuable tools for identifying both culturally and ecologically important areas for conservation. Importantly, we show that perceptions of NCP, together with soundscape preferences, differ with socio-cultural background, highlighting the importance of integrating diverse preferences into conservation and landscape management approaches.

title: Multi-scale, multi-region, and multi-stage dynamics and drivers of landscape ecological risk in source areas of global mega Inter-Basin water transfer projects
abstract: Under the dual pressures of global climate change and human activities, the cascading effects of large-scale inter-basin water transfer projects on the landscape patterns and ecological risk of water source areas urgently require systematic evaluation. Taking Nanyang City, the water source area of the South-to-North Water Diversion Middle Route Project (SNWDP-MR), as the study area, this research divided the period 1995–2024 into three stages—the pre-construction phase, the construction phase, and the operation phase—based on land-use data. Considering the functional differences among Nanyang, the Middle Route Water Source Area, and the Canal Buffer Zone, multi-scale, multi-region, and multi-stage landscape ecological risk index (ERI) assessments were conducted using grid scales of 2 km × 2 km, 3 km × 3 km, and 0.5 km × 0.5 km, respectively. The results showed that: (1) land-use change was driven by the triple forces of “urbanization–engineering–ecology”, with dominant drivers dynamically shifting across stages and regions; (2) low-risk areas continuously expanded while high-risk areas retreated and fragmented, with forest restoration and strict construction land control significantly reducing risk; (3) ecological risk in Nanyang was jointly controlled by land use, topography, and climate, while being primarily driven by the synergistic coupling of climatic conditions and topography in the Middle Route Water Source Area, and constrained by land use and topography in the Canal Buffer Zone. This study provides theoretical and methodological references for ecological impact assessment and sustainable management of similar projects worldwide.

title: Future food security risks driven by crop production and water scarcity in China's Yangtze River Delta under SSP–RCP scenarios
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and socioeconomic transition, the coupled dynamics of crop production and water scarcity have posed severe challenges to regional food security. Focusing on the Yangtze River Delta (YRD), this study conducts a comprehensively assessment of future food security risks constrained by water resource limitations and shifting grain supply–demand dynamics, under two combined SSP-RCP scenarios (SSP1–2.6 and SSP3–7.0) across two future time horizons (the 2050s and 2070s), by projecting grain supply and demand that incorporate SSP-driven changes in population structure, dietary preferences, crop sown area, and unit-area yield. Based on the Pressure-Exposure-Resilience (P- E -R) framework, we constructed a Food Security Risk Index (FSRPS) comprising three components—Water Scarcity Index ( WSI , pressure), Proportion of Irrigated Grain Production ( P Ir , exposure), and Grain Self-sufficiency Rate ( RATE , resilience). This index was then applied to analyze the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of food security risks in the YRD. The results indicate that in the 2017 baseline year, the spatial distribution of food security risks exhibited a distinct north-higher-than-south pattern. Across future scenarios, regional risk will increase significantly compared with the baseline, accompanied by growing spatial heterogeneity. Notably, driven by intensifying water scarcity and high irrigation dependence, the overall risk under the low-emission pathway (SSP1–2.6) — reaching 4.63 in 2050 and 4.12 in 2070 — is higher than that under SSP3–7.0 (4.04 and 3.87, respectively). Spatially, central and northern Jiangsu, Shanghai, and northern Anhui are the core sensitive regions (maximum risk index variation >0.3), whereas Zhejiang and the mountainous areas of southern Anhui remain relatively stable (variation generally below 0.01). Accordingly, two targeted regulation strategies are proposed: under SSP1–2.6, coordinate grain production with water resource carrying capacity; under SSP3–7.0, enhance agricultural climate resilience and implement differentiated zonal governance. This study provides a scientific reference for climate-adaptive food security and water resource management policies in the YRD.

title: Ecological indicators of carbon storage across tree, litter and soil compartments in semi-arid Zagros oak forests, Western Iran: a multi-compartment assessment
abstract: Forest carbon indicators derived from vegetation, litter, and soil components provide critical insights into ecosystem functioning, particularly in semi-arid regions. This study evaluated key indicators of carbon storage across tree biomass, forest floor litter, and soil compartments in oak-dominated forests of the Zagros Mountains, western Iran. Carbon stocks were quantified for different tree growth forms (standard vs. coppice), dominant woody species, litter fractions (fine and coarse), and soil properties over three consecutive years (2019–2021) across two forest stands. Standard (seed-origin) Quercus brantii trees exhibited dramatically higher biomass and carbon stocks than coppice-origin individuals, highlighting growth form as a primary structural indicator of aboveground carbon storage. Oak trees stored significantly more carbon than associated shrub species. Fine litter represented the dominant litter carbon pool and showed pronounced interannual variability, reflecting sensitivity to climatic conditions. Soil organic carbon constituted the largest ecosystem carbon reservoir but declined from 65.3 to 34.6 t ha −1 over the study period. Soil organic carbon showed significant positive correlations with total nitrogen (r ≈ 0.65, p < 0.05) and microbial respiration, indicating strong coupling between soil carbon and biological activity. Overall, the integration of structural, biochemical, and biological indicators revealed that forest degradation and climatic variability jointly constrain carbon sequestration in semi-arid oak ecosystems. These findings support the use of multi-compartment carbon indicators for guiding forest management and climate mitigation strategies in dryland forests.

title: Evaluation of minimal local recalibration for reducing transfer error in Sentinel-2 chlorophyll a estimation across heterogeneous waterbodies
abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl a ) is a commonly used indicator of phytoplankton biomass, trophic status, and eutrophication risk in inland waters. Sentinel-2 satellite imagery can scale up spatiotemporal chlorophyll monitoring, but transferability of retrieval models across heterogeneous waterbodies remains a challenge for operational use. This study evaluated a local bias recalibration approach for Sentinel-2-based Chl a estimation in heterogeneous inland waters. The study covered 28 lakes and reservoirs in eastern Poland and included 203 field-satellite match-ups after quality control. Six modelling approaches were evaluated: 2 linear models, 2 generalized additive models, Elastic Net, and Random Forest. Transferability was assessed using leave-one-cluster-out cross-validation. A minimal recalibration of the bias component was tested using 0–3 reference samples. Transfer prediction errors were characterised using bias-scatter analysis. Without recalibration, generalized additive models and Random Forest showed the best transfer performance, with median RMSE of 0.270–0.274 and FAC2 of 69.05–71.43%. A single calibration sample significantly reduced transfer bias. For Linear (MCI), RMSE decreased from 0.377 to 0.190 and FAC2 increased from 35.42% to 85.71% from k = 0 to k = 1. The largest improvements were observed for simple linear models, while more complex models showed comparatively smaller gains. Recalibration mainly corrected systematic bias, with minimal effect on residual scatter. With 1–3 calibration points, simple models approached the performance of more complex models. Minimal local bias recalibration can effectively support Chl a monitoring in heterogeneous inland waters, particularly in systems that already rely on periodic in situ sampling.

title: Ecological restoration reorganizes climate–runoff pathways in the Yellow River Basin
abstract: Vegetation restoration is reshaping dryland river basins, yet its hydrological consequences remain uncertain because greening can both enhance land-surface water retention and increase biological water consumption. This uncertainty is particularly relevant for the Yellow River Basin, where large-scale ecological restoration has coincided with marked changes in climate and runoff. Here we examine naturalized runoff, climate variability and vegetation greenness across the basin from 1982 to 2018 to determine whether post-restoration greening was associated with altered climate–runoff relationships. Natural runoff changed from a broad decline during 1982–2000 to a post-2000 recovery, although the recovery was not spatially uniform. Precipitation remained the primary positive predictor of runoff, while NDVI emerged as the most important secondary predictor. Temperature and solar radiation showed weaker and generally negative associations. Statistical pathway decomposition further indicated that vegetation greenness modified how climatic signals were associated with runoff. The area where NDVI-mediated pathways reinforced precipitation effects increased from 54.19% to 61.47%, and the area where they partly offset negative temperature associations increased from 33.41% to 47.83%. These results suggest that vegetation recovery did not produce a uniform hydrological response, but was linked to a reorganization of climate–vegetation–runoff associations. Restoration assessments in dryland basins should therefore consider not only vegetation gains, but also how greening changes runoff sensitivity to climate.

title: Multidimensional diversity patterns and community assembly of birds across heterogeneous habitats in an urban wetland
abstract: Urban wetlands are increasingly recognized as important refuges for biodiversity within rapidly urbanizing landscapes, yet the mechanisms by which habitat heterogeneity shapes bird communities remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we conducted monthly bird surveys from 2023 to 2025 across four habitat types (wetland, forest, farmland, and impervious areas) in Longpao Wetland, eastern China. We quantified taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic diversity, and assessed community assembly processes using standardized effect sizes of phylogenetic structure. A total of 183 bird species were recorded, including five National Class I and 29 Class II protected species, representing 47% of Nanjing's avifauna despite covering only 0.41% of the city's land area. Species richness and total abundance did not differ significantly among habitats, whereas functional richness (FRic) and phylogenetic diversity (PD) varied markedly, with wetlands (FRic = 9.61 ± 4.34; PD = 1019.70 ± 357.74) and forests supporting the highest values and impervious areas the lowest (FRic = 2.28 ± 0.90; PD = 529.51 ± 201.90). Indicator species analysis identified 82 habitat-specific species, with wetlands dominated by waterbirds including threatened taxa. SES analyses revealed significant phylogenetic clustering in forests and impervious habitats, indicating strong environmental filtering, whereas wetlands and farmland communities were random. These results demonstrate that habitat types contribute unequally to multidimensional biodiversity and community assembly, and that small urban wetlands can harbor disproportionately high bird diversity, including multiple conservation priority species. Maintaining habitat heterogeneity and connectivity is therefore essential for urban biodiversity conservation and ecological resilience.

title: Integrated effects of land-use change and human–environment interactions on habitat quality in the Chengdu–Chongqing urban agglomeration: Insights from explainable machine learning and structural equation modeling
abstract: The Chengdu–Chongqing urban agglomeration is a vital area in China's regional development plan and also plays an important role in protecting the environment. As the local economy expands rapidly, the ecosystem in this region is under growing pressure. However, limited research has examined the detailed evaluation of habitat quality (HQ) and the mechanisms underlying its evolution. This study applied the InVEST model, contribution index, and spatial autocorrelation analysis, combined with XGBoost–SHAP and a structural equation model (SEM), to systematically examine the spatiotemporal variations of HQ in the Chengdu–Chongqing region and its influencing factors. The findings indicate that: (1) Between 2000 and 2020, the HQ value in this region dropped from 0.615 to 0.606, indicating a small overall downward trend. (2) Ya'an and Leshan were important high-quality habitats, while Nanchong, Ziyang, Chengdu, and the main urban area of Chongqing were representative low-level habitats; spatially, low-level habitats in the central region gradually became fragmented, and high-quality habitats expanded eastward. (3) The ranking of the main influencing factors by their contribution was slope > temperature > cropland fragmentation > forestland fragmentation > vegetation greenness > nighttime illumination > population density. During the study period, urban expansion, cropland conversion, and changes in forest land configuration jointly altered the contribution of land-use structure to modeled HQ. (4) The SEM-based path analysis further showed that slope was linked to modeled HQ through vegetation greenness and land-use configuration. This study provides an extensive analysis of how climate, vegetation, landscape and human activities work together to affect HQ amid changes in land use. The findings provide practical evidence to help balance urban growth and ecological conservation as the Chengdu–Chongqing region undergoes rapid urbanization.

title: Time-series inversion of heavy metal and non-heavy metal water quality parameters and reveal their driving mechanisms using CNN-BiLSTM-Attention and PLS-SEM
abstract: Monitoring heavy metals and other pollution in drinking water sources is protecting public health, ensuring social stability, and promoting sustainable ecological development. Traditional fixed-point sampling approaches suffers from insufficient spatial coverage, weak remote sensing signals for heavy metals, and considerable challenges in achieving robust long-term inversion. To address these limitations, this study develops a multi-dimensional time-series feature fusion model (CNN-BiLSTM-Attention) for water quality parameter inversion. This model integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN), a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM), and an attention mechanism to enable monthly inversion of eight indicators, including dissolved oxygen (DO), chemical oxygen demand (COD), ammonia nitrogen (NH₃-N), fluoride (F − ), permanganate (COD M n ), zinc (Zn), selenium (Se), and mercury (Hg). This paper investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of both heavy metal and non-heavy metal water quality parameters during normal, dry and flood seasons. A partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) is constructed to quantify the direct and indirect effects of climate, human activities, and hydrological characteristics on the dynamic changes of the eight water quality parameters, thereby identifying their dominant drivers. The results showed that the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model substantially improves inversion performance by capturing nonlinear spatiotemporal relationships among water quality parameters (mean R 2 = 0.791), representing a 32.05% increase over the conventional CNN-LSTM model (mean R 2 = 0.599). From 2018 to 2024, the overall water quality exhibited an improving trend, with notable decreases in Hg, Zn, Se, and COD concentrations (maximum reduction of 68.3%), while DO and NH 3 -N increased slightly. Spatially, pollutants accumulated at the reservoir edge and tributary confluences during the dry season and migrated toward the reservoir center in the flood season. Notably, the low-DO area largely overlapped with the peak COD Mn and COD region in the southwestern tributary of the reservoir. PLS-SEM revealed that the organic pollution load (COD Mn , COD) serves as the central hub driving heavy metal evolution, exhibiting a strong positive correlation with heavy metal indicators (Hg, Se; β = 0.946, P < 0.001). Human activities exert a direct negative effect on oxygen-consuming pollutants (DO, NH₃-N; β = −0.359, P < 0.01) and indirectly modulate heavy metal dynamics through the organic pollution load pathway ( β = −0.432, P < 0.05). Climatic factors (primarily rainfall, β = 0.534, P < 0.1) and water temperature ( β = −0.562, P < 0.05) constitute the dynamic basis of heavy metal evolution. The proposed time-series inversion and driving mechanism analysis method enables both temporal monitoring and attribution analysis of heavy metals and non-heavy metals in water bodies, providing reliable scientific support for water quality management in drinking water sources.

title: Assessing the cross-scale spillover effect of urban Heat Island (UHI): an indicator-based approach in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region
abstract: Due to rapid urbanization, urban heat island (UHI) effects have expanded from city-level phenomena to continuous cross-city UHI belts, posing challenges to regional ecological security and public health. However, a critical research gap remains: the spatial structure, formation mechanisms, and cross-scale transmission processes of continuous UHI belts are insufficiently quantified, primarily due to a reliance on isolated, single-scale analyses. In this study, an indicator-based, multiscale analytical framework was developed at the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region, city, and 1-km grid scales. Landscape metrics, a coupled random forest-geographic SHAP (RF-GeoSHAP) model, and generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) were used to investigate the hierarchical transmission pathways of continuous UHI belts. Our results show that these belts emerge as structurally connected regional heat sources once heat island dominance (HID) surpasses a nonlinear threshold of approximately 7%. At the agglomeration scale, HID, along with climatic and ecological backgrounds (PRE, NDVI, TMP), are identified as the dominant thermal predictors, while at the fine grid scale, local thermal accumulation is substantially amplified by building height (BH) and sky view factor (SVF) under structural forcing. Crucially, the influence of these key driving indicators exhibits clear threshold effects that are nonlinearly amplified by regional UHI connectivity. Overall, this study enhances the understanding of UHI dynamics across scales and offers valuable insights for indicator-guided UHI mitigation strategies at the urban agglomeration scale.

title: Improving ecological indicators of mangrove canopy height and aboveground biomass through multi-source data fusion on the Amazon coast
abstract: Reliable ecological indicators of mangrove structure and carbon storage are essential for monitoring coastal ecosystem conditions, yet their accuracy remains uncertain in tall, structurally heterogeneous forests, where Earth observation products differ in sensor physics, spatial resolution, and acquisition dates. Here, we present a multi-scale framework to evaluate, calibrate, and improve two widely used ecological indicators of mangrove condition—canopy height and aboveground biomass (AGB)—across approximately 7000 ha of mangroves in the Marapanim estuary, northern Brazil. The framework integrates UAV photogrammetry, radar-derived digital elevation models (TanDEM-X and SRTM), and field measurements to quantify cross-scale discrepancies and identify the main sources of uncertainty affecting indicator retrieval. High-resolution UAV canopy-height models revealed exceptionally tall Avicennia forests reaching up to 53 m, among the tallest mangroves reported globally. At the local scale, mean AGB reached approximately 648 Mg ha −1 in the southern Avicennia -dominated sector and 430 Mg ha −1 in the northern mixed Rhizophora–Avicennia sector, with local maxima of ∼800 Mg ha −1 . In contrast, radar-derived products yielded substantially lower estimates of canopy height and biomass, with height differences of 8–10 m in tall and structurally heterogeneous stands. These discrepancies reflect the combined effects of sensor-dependent canopy representation, spatial averaging, and temporal mismatch between historical radar acquisitions and recent UAV observations. To improve the ecological interpretation of these products, we implemented a calibration strategy linking field and UAV measurements to satellite observations and complemented it with UAV-based three-dimensional volumetric reconstruction of individual trees as an independent structural check on allometric biomass estimates. Our results show that canopy height and AGB derived from coarse-resolution radar products can systematically underestimate mangrove structural condition and carbon storage in tall forests unless locally calibrated. Beyond documenting exceptionally tall and carbon-dense Amazonian mangroves, this study provides a transferable framework for evaluating and improving ecological indicators of forest structure and biomass in complex coastal ecosystems.

title: Quantifying hydrological niche segregation and water use divergence among coexisting desert plants in an extreme arid environment
abstract: Understanding the coexistence mechanisms of multiple plant species in extreme arid environments is a crucial challenge in dryland ecology. Hydrological niche segregation (HNS) has been recognized as a key driver of plant coexistence; however, its linkage with intrinsic water use efficiency (WUE i ) remains poorly understood. In this study, we combined stable isotopes (δ 2 H, δ 18 O, δ 13 C) with MixSIAR and NicheROVER models to investigate water uptake strategies (WUS), hydrological niches, and WUE i of four coexisting plant species ( Populus euphratica : Pe , Haloxylon ammodendron : Ha , Alhagi sparsifolia : As , and Halimodendron halodendron : Hh ) in the Ebinur Lake Basin, northwest China. Results showed that Pe , Ha , and As relied predominantly on groundwater (46–69%) and deep soil water (26–42%), while Hh exhibited greater flexibility, obtaining 58 ± 17% of its water from deep soil layers. In particular, Ha exhibited the highest WUEᵢ and a relatively narrow niche breadth (2.15), while As showed the narrowest niche breadth (1.93) and low WUEᵢ, coupled with a strong reliance on groundwater. In contrast, Hh possessed the broadest hydrological niche (3.40) and a moderately high WUEᵢ, whereas Pe exhibited the lowest WUEᵢ and a broad niche (3.26). Pairwise niche overlap was highly asymmetric: Pe overlapped with Hh by 55.3%, while the reciprocal overlap was only 34.5%, indicating directional competitive asymmetry. This differentiation appears to facilitate species coexistence through divergent strategies: the high WUEᵢ species ( Ha ) maintained a narrow hydrological niche, whereas Pe and Hh achieved coexistence through broader hydrological niches, and As relied on stable groundwater despite low WUEᵢ and a narrow niche. These findings enhance our understanding of the relationship between WUEᵢ and hydrological niche segregation in desert ecosystems and provide practical guidance for adaptive vegetation management in arid regions.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamic evolution and driving factors of eco-efficiency in China's Grand Canal:A county-level study
abstract: As a large-scale linear heritage integrating heritage, economic, cultural, historical, and ecological dimensions, the Grand Canal's eco-efficiency (EE) holds substantial practical value for advancing the sustainable development of heritage spaces. Based on desirable output theory, this study evaluated the EE of 150 county-level administrative units within the Grand Canal core area from 2012 to 2023, systematically analyzing the key factors influencing EE and their spatiotemporal heterogeneity by employing the XGBoost-SHAP and the GTWR. The main findings are as follows: (1) EE exhibits a notable “polarization” trend, with an increase in the number of both high-value (EE > 0.8) and low-value (EE < 0.3) areas and a decline in medium-efficiency zones. High-value areas are predominantly concentrated in the southern section of the canal. (2) EE demonstrates spatial autocorrelation, with the Moran's I index showing a “W”-shaped fluctuation, indicating clear club convergence characterised by “high-high” and “low-low” agglomerations. (3) Regional disparity analysis reveals the following ranking of Gini coefficients across provinces and municipalities: Shandong > Hebei > Anhui > Jiangsu > Henan > Zhejiang > Tianjin > Beijing. Interregional differences have become the primary source of overall disparity. (4) EE is nonlinearly driven by multiple factors. Population size, vegetation coverage, and urbanization rate exert positive effects, whereas consumption level, urban–canal relationship, industrial structure, and government regulation show negative impacts, with significant spatial heterogeneity observed in the influence of each factor. This study provides a scientific basis for promoting ecological coordinated governance and differentiated policy design along the Grand Canal. Accordingly, this study advocates a differentiated development strategy tailored to regional EE levels along the Grand Canal. Specifically, high-efficiency regions should leverage their advantages to foster high-value-added green industries, such as cultural creativity and ecotourism. Transitional zones require bolstered technological innovation and policy incentives to propel them toward higher efficiency tiers. Low-efficiency areas must prioritize ecological restoration and stringent pollution control. Furthermore, establishing a cross-regional big data platform is recommended to facilitate collaborative governance.

title: Spatially non-stationary and threshold-dependent drivers of cropland productivity in humid subtropical China revealed by explainable machine learning
abstract: Understanding spatially heterogeneous controls on cropland productivity is critical for improving agroecosystem sustainability under increasing climatic variability and anthropogenic pressure. However, the nonlinear and spatially non-stationary relationships between productivity and its drivers remain difficult to quantify using conventional approaches. Using multi-source remote sensing and ancillary datasets, this study applied an interpretable machine-learning approach to investigate the spatial controls of cropland net primary productivity (NPP) across humid subtropical China based on two representative periods (2010 and 2020). Results showed that cropland NPP increased by 4.7% during the study period, although substantial spatial heterogeneity persisted. Climatic factors, particularly potential evapotranspiration and mean annual temperature, showed the strongest contributions to spatial variations in NPP, with their contribution patterns exhibiting pronounced spatial reversals along hydroclimatic gradients. Soil pH acted as a conditional regulator within a narrow optimal range (5.5–6.0), whereas nitrogen fertilizer input and population density imposed increasingly negative effects beyond critical thresholds. Clustering of pixel-level SHAP vectors identified four functional zones characterized by distinct combinations of dominant drivers and constraint regimes, linking regional productivity gains with localized vulnerability risks. The results further reveal that cropland productivity exhibits multiple interacting constraint domains, where productivity responses depend on whether local conditions remain within effective threshold ranges. By integrating remote sensing observations with explainable machine learning, this study provides a spatially explicit framework for understanding productivity–ecological environment relationships and supporting adaptive cropland management under climate change.

title: Multitrophic indicators reveal replacement-driven community reassembly in urban-dominated and mountainous river systems of Beijing, China
abstract: Urban expansion and hydrological disturbance are reshaping river ecosystems worldwide, yet their relevance for ecological indicators across trophic levels remains insufficiently resolved. We compared phytoplankton, benthic macroinvertebrate, and fish communities between urban-dominated and mountainous river systems in northern Beijing during spring and autumn 2025. By integrating community composition, beta-diversity partitioning, fish functional diversity, and environment–community analyses, we examined how multitrophic community patterns differed between contrasting river contexts and how autumn patterns were expressed following a major regional flood. Community responses were trophic-specific: phytoplankton showed pronounced seasonal turnover, fish showed a weak autumn tendency toward urban–mountain differentiation, and benthic macroinvertebrates displayed more context-dependent seasonal responses. Across all trophic levels, urban–mountain differentiation was dominated by turnover rather than nestedness, indicating that urban-dominated communities were not simply species-poor subsets of mountainous communities but assemblages characterized mainly by species replacement. Fish communities in urban-dominated reaches also showed reduced functional richness, suggesting a narrower range of ecological strategies in these river contexts. The autumn survey followed the Haihe “25·7” regional flood, which affected the Chaobai River basin and the Bai River flowing through Yanqing. In this post-flood autumn context, within-group heterogeneity was higher in some urban-dominated assemblages, whereas measured nutrient variables explained only a limited proportion of multitrophic community variation. These patterns are consistent with possible disturbance-related reorganization superimposed on longer-term differences between river contexts, but they should not be interpreted as direct evidence of flood causation or as a strict causal test of urbanization. Overall, our results show that taxonomic, beta-diversity, and functional metrics provide complementary indicators for assessing river ecosystem reorganization under interacting urban and hydrological pressures. These findings support multitrophic, multi-season, and context-aware biomonitoring, and highlight the importance of conserving mountainous headwaters while restoring habitat complexity, ecological flow, and longitudinal connectivity in urban-dominated rivers.

title: Long-term ecological health assessment of the yellow river estuary (2003−2022) using an EQR-standardized PSR framework with entropy weighting
abstract: Estuaries are highly valuable but increasingly engineered ecosystems, where apparent recovery may reflect direct management inputs rather than autonomous ecological improvement. Existing PSR- and DPSIR-type assessments rarely separate these signals, potentially inflating recovery diagnoses. Therefore, we developed a management-adjusted Pressure-State-Response and Ecological Quality Ratio (PSR-EQR) framework for the Yellow River Estuary (YRE) using a continuous 2003–2022 monitoring record. The 24-indicator framework partitions the Response domain into management-response indicators, such as ecological water supplementation and wetland-protection effort, and biotic-response indicators, such as fish early-life-stage and benthic-community metrics. Each indicator was transformed to a 0–1 EQR using cost-, benefit-, or optimum-type functions against auditable benchmarks, weighted with the Entropy Weight Method, and examined with exploratory PCA after correlation-guided block aggregation. The results showed that the full PSR trajectory was inverted-N-shaped, declining from 0.685 in 2003 to 0.428 in 2016 and rebounding to 0.715 in 2022. The 2016 minimum coincided with severe summer hypoxia (DO = 2.1 mg/L) and opportunistic benthic dominance. After 2019, State and biotic-response indicators improved, but management-response indicators reached benchmark conditions earlier. The ecological-core diagnosis therefore indicated slower intrinsic recovery than the full score, highlighting continuing management dependence. The framework provides a transferable approach for highly engineered estuaries by separating ecological condition from direct management inputs while preserving PSR-EQR comparability.

title: Corrigendum to “Land-use-associated carbon storage variation in the Dashanbao Alpine wetland region: An InVEST-based assessment with soil profile interpretation” [Ecol. Indic. 189 (2026) 115150]
abstract: The authors regret that the graphical abstract and Figure 1 in the original article were not presented optimally.To improve the clarity and readability of the graphical abstract, the left-side part of the first section of the graphical abstract has been removed, and the right-side map has been enlarged.In Figure 1, the inset map of the study area (Dashanbao).The corrected versions are provided below.This correction does not affect the results, interpretations, or conclusions of the original article.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors of landscape ecological risk in the major sugarcane-producing region: an assessment from Guangxi, China (2000–2023)
abstract: Rapid urbanization and intensive human activities substantially reshape land use patterns and ecosystem functions across ecologically fragile regions, thereby inducing widespread landscape ecological risks (LER). Landscape ecological risk assessment is essential for effective ecological governance and sustainable land management in vulnerable karst agricultural areas. As a core sugarcane-producing region located in the typical karst terrain of southern China, Guangxi sustains national sugar security, while its spatiotemporal dynamics of landscape ecological risks remain poorly understood. Based on land use datasets spanning 2000 to 2023, a landscape ecological risk assessment framework integrating multiple landscape metrics and the Geodetector model was applied to reveal grid- and county-level LER variations and their underlying driving mechanisms. The results show that (1) The study area experienced drastic land use changes, with continuous forestland growth, fragmented cultivated land loss, and a 102.89% built-up land expansion. Noticeable land use conflicts existed among ecological restoration, farmland protection and urban sprawl. Regional ecological risk stably presented a spatial pattern of low in the north and high in the south, fluctuating upward before a persistent decline after 2015, which indicated continuous ecological improvement. (2) Topographic slope dominated the spatial differentiation of ecological risk. Nighttime light-indexed urbanization showed increasing explanatory capacity for risk changes, while the expansion of sugarcane cultivation scale has a relatively limited impact. (3) Agricultural cultivation and terrain factors exhibited significant nonlinear interactive enhancement. Sloping farmland was identified as the key ecologically sensitive area requiring targeted governance. The results demonstrate that landscape ecological risk variations are jointly driven by natural constraints and urban anthropogenic disturbances, rather than single agricultural activities. This study provides scientific support for coordinating crop industry development, cultivated land conservation and ecological security in global karst regions.

title: Multiple driving effects and causal transmission mechanisms of watershed runoff variations based on a three-level attribution framework
abstract: Runoff variations in large connected basins are jointly affected by climate variability, human activities, reservoir regulation, and upstream–downstream hydrological connectivity. This makes cascading runoff transmission among sub-basins highly complex. Therefore, this study focuses on 11 controlled sub-basins (S1–S11) in the Yangtze River Basin and uses meteorological and hydrological data from 1965 to 2019. We developed a three-level coupled attribution framework that integrates the Mann–Kendall change-point test, interval runoff contribution identification, Budyko-based attribution, and PCMCI+ causal analysis. The results show that two main runoff change points occurred in the Yangtze River Basin, in 1985 and 2002. The mean interval runoff contribution decreased from 152.7 m 3 s −1 in the reference period (1965–1985) to 138.9 m 3 s −1 in Change Period 1 (1986–2002). It then recovered to 158.4 m 3 s −1 in Change Period 2 (2003–2019). Compared with Change Period 1, the contribution rate of human activities in the middle reaches decreased from 60.5% to 44.7% after Change Period 2. In terms of sub-basin function and transmission, S1–S2 served as upstream runoff supply zones, S3, S5, and S7 were the main midstream runoff attenuation units, and S8–S11 acted as downstream convergence recovery zones. These findings improve the understanding of runoff variation mechanisms, spatial transmission relationships, and functional differentiation in large basin–sub-basin systems. They also provide theoretical support and decision-making references for optimized water resource allocation and differentiated basin management.

title: Spatial suitability and expansion potential of ratoon rice for nature-based climate-resilient farming in Fujian Province, Southeast China under climate warming
abstract: CONTEXT: Ratoon rice offers a nature-based solution for agricultural sustainable intensification by utilizing in situ biological processes to improve resource-use efficiency without proportionally increasing external inputs. However, the spatial suitability and expansion potential of ratoon rice under climate changeparticularly concerning safe growth periods and accumulated temperatureremain insufficiently quantified. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop an integrated assessment framework to evaluate the spatial suitability and expansion potential of ratoon rice in Southeast China under changing climatic conditions from 1990 to 2024, with a focused case study on Fujian Province as a representative monsoonal region. METHODSs: We combined a 35-year climate dataset with soil indicators (microbial biomass carbon and erosion risk) and irrigation capacity. The data were analyzed using SenMannKendall trend analysis, the CatBoost algorithm, and multi-criteria decision-making methods. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The analysis reveals: (1) a safe growth period ranging from 87 to 234 days; (2) significant warming trends (0.03670.6423°C per decade), with a warm-wet pattern in the northwest and a warm-dry trend in the southeast; (3) identification of 18 suitability subzones based on transplanting mode (GC, greenhouse seedling culture-transplanting mode /FC, field seedling culture-transplanting mode) and maturity type, totaling 737.78 × 10 hm² of suitable area, and average climate and soil production potentials of 19,190.39 kg·hm² and 12,566.96 kg·hm², respectively; and (4) a northward and upward expansion of 33.00 × 10 hm² since 19901999, indicating clear climate-driven expansion potential. Within existing cultivated land, 410,167.50 hm² (62.55%) is suitable, including 214,187.07 hm² under GC and 195,980.43 hm² under FC. SIGNIFICANCE: Ratoon rice represents a scalable, nature-based pathway for climate-resilient agriculture in Southeast China. The delineated suitability subzones provide a scientific basis for spatial planning and the allocation of adapted rice varieties tailored to specific local conditions. Strategic scalingsupported by such adapted varieties and targeted policiescan significantly enhance regional food security and deliver substantial eco-economic benefits in the context of ongoing climate change.

title: An integrated interpretable framework for multiscale drivers and nonlinear responses of ecosystem services in karst regions
abstract: Karst ecosystem services (ESs) are characterized by strong spatial heterogeneity, scale dependence, and nonlinear responses to environmental and anthropogenic change. However, existing studies often rely on fixed spatial scales and linear analytical approaches, which limits the identification of multiscale controls, interaction and coupling effects, and ecologically meaningful nonlinear response ranges. To address this gap, this study developed an integrated and interpretable framework to investigate the multiscale drivers and nonlinear responses of ecosystem services in the Lijiang River Basin, a representative karst watershed in China. Carbon storage (CS) and water yield (WY) were estimated using the InVEST and SWAT models, respectively. The Optimal Multivariate-Stratification Geographical Detector (OMGD) was then used to identify scale-dependent drivers and their interaction/coupling effects, while XGBoost-SHAP was applied to quantify factor contributions and interpret nonlinear response patterns. The results revealed marked scale-dependent differences between ecological and hydrological controls. CS was primarily associated with mid-scale processes (1000–2000 m) related to vegetation growth, water availability, and human management, following a “water regulation–vegetation response” pathway. By contrast, WY was mainly associated with large-scale processes (2000–4000 m) related to terrain structure, slope-driven runoff generation, and surface–subsurface connectivity, exhibiting a “terrain-dominated–surface-modulated” pattern. In addition, CS showed strong nonlinear sensitivity to irrigation intensity and vegetation cover, whereas WY displayed regime-specific nonlinear responses, with distinct nonlinear response ranges associated with slope gradients and land-use types. By integrating multiscale detection with interpretable nonlinear analysis, this study demonstrates the value of interpretable modelling for revealing the coupled driving pathways and nonlinear response patterns of ecosystem services in highly heterogeneous karst landscapes. The proposed framework is transferable to other complex socio-ecological systems and can support more targeted ecological assessment and spatial management.

title: The use of long-term commercial fisheries data as a background for development of fish-based ecological status assessment system of transitional waters
abstract: The development of fish-based methods for assessment of the ecological status of transitional waters is challenging due to their unique hydrology, limited reliable historical data, and complex anthropogenic pressures. Nevertheless, long-term commercial fish catch records may serve as a proxy for tracking ecological change. This study analysed commercial catch records from 1953 to 2023. Significant trends of both deterioration and recovery were detected in fish metrics, and the recovery trend was strongly related to declining total phosphorus concentrations in the lagoon, documented since standardized water-quality monitoring began in 1993. Reference values and good/moderate (G/M) status thresholds were defined using metric values from periods preceding and during ecological deterioration. Based on these, an index derived from commercial catch data was developed to assess the lagoon's ecological status. Total phosphorus concentrations corresponding to the reference and GM thresholds were calculated based on the relationship established with the index. These concentrations were then used to calculate the reference and G/M threshold values for the monitoring of fish metrics that were related to total phosphorus, and a monitoring-data-based fish index was developed. Though based on different data sources and metrics, the two indexes significantly correlate ( R = 0.74; P < 0.001). This confirms that fisheries data can help identify long-term trends related to changes in fish communities, can reflect conditions prior to the intensification of human activity, can be linked to monitoring data collected in recent decades, and can serve as a starting point for developing a fish-based method for assessing the ecological status of the lagoon.

title: Spatiotemporal monitoring of small and Micro wetlands for urban ecological security assessment: A case study of Linyi City, China
abstract: Small and micro wetlands (SMWs) have critical ecological value. However, they are frequently neglected in urban ecological security assessments due to the challenges in large-scale mapping, leading to a potential overestimation of security levels. Utilizing long-term Landsat imagery (2001−2020), this study developed a robust method to extract SMWs in Linyi City, which is a typical semi-humid region in China. The minimum mapping unit was 0.09 ha. Our findings revealed that SMWs total area decreased by 36.58 ha (−0.80%) from 2001 to 2020, while patch number increased by 279 (+5.07%). Over the study period, SMWs area experienced an initial sharp decline from 2001 to 2006 (decreasing by 33.9%), followed by a gradual recovery and eventual stabilization after 2010. And the SMWs centroid migrated 13.25 km from urban centers to peripheral mountainous areas, reflecting intense urbanization pressure. The Geodetector model identified GDP (q = 0.118) and precipitation (q = 0.115) as the dominant drivers of SMWs changes. Crucially, by incorporating the landscape metrics of SMWs into the Pressure-State-Response assessment frame-work, we demonstrated that SMWs act as sensitive ecological indicators. In years with abundant precipitation (e.g. 2020), the inclusion of SMWs reduced Comprehensive Ecological Security Index by 12.1% (from 0.672 to 0.591), changing the city's status from “Relatively Safe” to “Warning”. The risk signal was obscured when only large and medium-sized wetlands were considered. This study reveals the mechanism of SMWs as sensitive ecological indicators, emphasizes the necessity of integrating SMWs data for accurate evaluation of urban ecological security, and provides a scientific basis for precise protection of SMWs and sustainable urban management.

title: Dual perspective: Pelagic and benthic communities as biological and functional indicators in riverine ecosystems
abstract: Microbial communities are widely recognised as rapid and sensitive indicators of environmental change, yet they remain underutilised in biomonitoring despite their potential to complement or surpass traditional bioindicators. Conventional biomonitoring approaches in freshwater ecosystems typically rely on fish, macroinvertebrates or plants, each constrained by practical and ecological limitations that restrict when, where and how they can be used to assess ecosystems. In contrast, microbial communities provide both taxonomic and functional signals that reflect a wide range of processes, including direct links to water chemistry. Here, we evaluate microbial communities as environmental indicators of river ecosystem health. We sampled both pelagic and benthic microbial communities across space and time, integrating community composition and ecosystem function. Microbial assemblages differed significantly between the sampled fractions (pelagic vs benthic) and seasonally. Using threshold indicator analyses, we identified a broad set of genera with association to water chemistry and ecosystem function. However, there was no consistent indicator taxa based on these environmental gradients or ecosystem function across sample fraction or season. This highlights the high responsiveness of microbial communities to environmental gradients and temporal change. While context-specific indicators show clear potential, developing robust microbial metrics will require accounting for benthic and pelagic habitats and seasonal variability inherent in riverine ecosystems.

title: Integrating multi-source data and GeoDetector–GTWR to identify desertification-prone areas and quantify spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms: A case study of the three-river-source region
abstract: Desertification is one of the primary threats facing the ecologically fragile Three-River Source region (TRSR). Previous studies have often relied on single vegetation indices or station-based moisture metrics, which suffer from saturation and spatial heterogeneity, limiting accurate characterization of desertification's spatiotemporal heterogeneity—especially inadequate consideration of topographic constraints and nonlinear vegetation responses in alpine regions. To address these gaps, this study improved the wetness index model by integrating Kernel Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (KNDVI) and topographic factors to identify potential desertification areas. Building on this, by combining optimal indices (Modified Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index (MSAVI), Land Surface Temperature (LST)) with the Classification and Regression Trees (CART) decision tree model, we analyzed the spatiotemporal dynamics of desertification from 2000 to 2020. Additionally, the GeoDetector and Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) models were employed to quantitatively examine the driving mechanisms. The results show that the potential desertification area in the study region ranges from 337,008 km 2 to 361,436 km 2 , accounting for more than 80% of the entire region. From 2000 to 2020, the desertification status in this region exhibited an overall improving trend. The proportion of non-desertified areas increased from 63.30% to 71.26%, representing a total increase of 30,534 km 2 . Meanwhile, the area of severely and extremely desertified regions decreased by 14,231 km 2 . Over the 20-year period, the area of restored regions was 60,346 km 2 , accounting for 15.72%, while the area of degraded regions was 11,659 km 2 , accounting for 3.04%. However, the migration of the desertification gravity center was predominantly characterized by localized fluctuating shifts rather than simple linear changes. Analysis of driving mechanisms indicated that desertification in Three-River Source Region is driven by both natural and anthropogenic factors, but the direction and intensity of their impacts exhibit significant spatiotemporal variations. Therefore, formulating reasonable land use and grassland management policies based on different regions is crucial for desertification control efforts.

title: The role of lichens in biomonitoring of pollution, climate change and sea level rise in tropics: Insights from India and beyond
abstract: s Tropical coastal ecosystems are facing rapid environmental change resulting from global climate switch, sea level rise, change in weather and anthropogenic pressures. In this context, reliable ecological indicators are critical for assessing ecosystem response and susceptibility. Lichens with their extreme sensitivity to microclimatic-macroclimatic variation and atmospheric stress have been used as bioindicators in terrestrial ecosystems for a long time. Their ability as coastal climate change indicators, especially in tropical areas, remains insufficiently explored. This paper examines the present knowledge on coastal diversity of lichens in relation to changing precipitation patterns, increasing sea levels and salinity changes. Based on international case studies and literature inventories along Indian coastal areas, it emphasizes how particular lichen species react to climate induced coastal change and address issues using lichens to monitoring climate and sea level in data- scarce tropical areas. The findings highlight the need to incorporate lichen monitoring in coastal vulnerability assessment and restoration strategies immediately.

title: Examination of the evolution and influencing factors of flow and sediment processes in an inland river basin of agro-pastoral ecotone amidst environmental changes
abstract: Elucidating the spatiotemporal dynamics and primary controls of flow and sediment processes (FSP) is essential for sustainable water-soil resource management in inland river basins within agro-pastoral ecotones (IRB-APE). This study refined the Soil and Water Assessment Tool with a time-segmented dynamic parameter adjustment strategy to simulate runoff and sediment dynamics under varying radiative forcing scenarios in the Tabu River basin, northern China. The model achieved robust performance (R 2 > 0.83, NSE > 0.83, |Re| < 16%) across baseline (1982–2000) and changing (2001−2023) periods. During 2001–2023, runoff and sediment transport rates declined by 0.19 m 3 /s and 0.26 kg/s, respectively, attributable to intensified soil drought and vegetation recovery. Under future scenarios (2030−2100), runoff exhibited differential responses: insignificant trends under SSP126/SSP245 but significant increases under SSP370/SSP585 ( P < 0.01), with annual runoff consistently highest under SSP585 across all time horizons. This divergence arises from compound effects of pronounced warming and intensified precipitation under high radiative forcing, accelerating soil saturation and reducing infiltration. Spatially, runoff depth showed a decreasing-then-increasing pattern along the upstream-downstream gradient, with lowest values (≤ 0.84 mm) in middle-reach subbasins with thick permeable soils and highest values (≥ 9.34 mm) in upstream subbasins with steep topography and low-permeability soils. A strong nonlinear runoff-sediment relationship emerged under future scenarios, driven by intensifying extreme precipitation and heightened soil erodibility. Temperature dominated runoff variation across all scenarios, while sediment discharge showed a transition from anthropogenic dominance (SSP126/SSP245) to thermal forcing dominance (SSP370/SSP585), with a critical threshold between SSP245 and SSP370 marking the shift from vegetation protection to climate forcing control. These findings necessitate differentiated strategies: vegetation restoration and water retention infrastructure under low forcing scenarios versus high-efficiency irrigation and climate-responsive land use planning under high forcing conditions.

title: The seasonal dominance mechanism of temperature and runoff on the carbon residence time and the dynamic imbalance of carbon cycle in the Pearl River Basin
abstract: The seasonal dynamics of carbon residence time (CRT) and its regulatory mechanisms under climate change remain insufficiently quantified, particularly regarding the interactions between temperature and runoff on CRT. This study systematically quantified the seasonal dynamics of CRT in vegetation-litter-soil continuum ecosystems across spring, summer, and winter in the Pearl River Basin, China. An integrated approach combining structural equation modeling, threshold detection, and scenario prediction analysis was used. The associations among monthly average temperature (AMT), surface runoff (SFR), ecosystem CRT, net ecosystem productivity (NEP), and ecosystem carbon use efficiency (CUEe) were evaluated to examine a potential pathway linking hydrothermal variability with carbon-cycle disequilibrium. The results reveal how seasonal CRT variation is associated with changes in NEP and CUEe, providing evidence that carbon-cycle disequilibrium in the Pearl River Basin is organized by season-specific hydrothermal conditions rather than representing a simple input-output mismatch. Scenario simulations indicated season-dependent CRT responses under future hydrothermal changes, with the strongest increase projected in winter. Winter carbon loss was markedly intensified under RCP8.5, as indicated by a NEP decline of more than 5.58%. A 23%–29.7% increase in CRT was associated with a 4.13%–5.51% higher probability of NEP transitioning from carbon source to sink, whereas high-CRT scenarios were associated with a 36.1%–58.7% reduction in CUEe.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and scenario simulation of ecological resilience in major grain producing areas: a case study of the northeast plain, China
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and intensified human activities, the stability of regional ecosystems is subject to multiple pressures. Taking the Northeast Plain as a case study, this research analyzes the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and optimization pathways of ecological resilience from 2000 to 2024. The results indicate that: (1) ecological resilience has generally increased, exhibiting a spatial pattern characterized by “higher in mountainous areas and lower in plains,” with significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I ≈ 0.79—0.81) and a northward shift of the center of gravity; (2) the driving mechanism has shifted from natural dominance to a coupled natural–social system, with temperature as the dominant factor (q ≈ 0.28), followed by road network density (q ≈ 0.23), and a pronounced threshold effect is observed; (3) land-use conflict plays a critical mediating role, leading to the formation of control zones (59.5%), coordination zones (32.1%), risk zones (5.8%), and potential zones (2.6%); (4) multi-scenario simulations show that urban development reduces resilience, ecological protection enhances connectivity, and the coordinated development scenario yields the most favorable outcomes. Overall, ecological resilience is jointly shaped by natural constraints and human activities, and its enhancement requires the optimization of land use and zoning regulation to achieve coordinated improvements in ecological integrity and development.

title: Corrigendum to “Construction and optimization of a land–sea integrated ecological network based on complex network theory: A case study of Dalian, China” [Ecol. Indic. 189 (2026) 115172]
Monitoring quality thresholds change the Living Planet Index through shifts in representation, not systematic bias in population trends
abstract: Quantifying biodiversity change using indicators is a crucial part of evaluating progress towards internationally agreed biodiversity targets. Many indicators rely on publicly available species monitoring data which is characterised by uneven geographic and taxonomic representation. The Living Planet Index (LPI) is a global biodiversity indicator which inherits these data biases, resulting in well-documented gaps in population data coverage. However, the relationship between taxonomic and geographic representation and the length and completeness of population abundance time series, a measure of data quality, has not been assessed. Given that LPI outcomes can be influenced by these factors, we explore how temporal data quality varies across taxa and regions and whether it relates to the direction of population abundance trends. We also examine relationships between temporal data quality and covariates: system, region, species range size and a proxy for species interest. We find that removing temporally lower quality data produced less negative aggregated trends but showed no relationship between temporal data quality and average population abundance change. Temporally lower quality data is concentrated in herptiles, particularly in Latin America and the Caribbean and is also related to: range size for amphibians; range size and region for mammals; and region for birds and reptiles. Whilst removing data with lower temporal quality changes the global LPI trend, it simultaneously increases existing geographic and taxonomic biases. Groups which are more likely to be in decline are also more likely to be removed from the LPI when temporal quality thresholds are applied. This highlights the inherent complexity of using species monitoring data in aggregated indicators and that both representation and temporal quality should be considered in data exclusion decisions.

title: Nonlinear attribution and precision governance of urban resilience in Henan: An integrated machine learning and Geographically Weighted Random Forest approach
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of urban resilience (UR) and the explanatory contributions of related indicators is critical for resilience-oriented regional governance, particularly in less-developed inland regions. Using panel data from 18 prefecture-level cities in Henan during 2014–2023, this paper constructs a multidimensional evaluation framework including Ecology, Economy, Society, Infrastructure, Institutions and Technological Innovation (EESIIT), explicitly incorporating technological innovation as an additional dimension to extend traditional five-dimensional UR assessment frameworks. UR was first quantified using the GIPPM-EWM-CWGT method; then GBDT, GWRF, and PDPs were integrated to screen key explanatory indicators, examine their spatially heterogeneous explanatory contributions, and explore nonlinear marginal response patterns. Multi-scenario simulations and the IRPU index were further used to assess future UR trajectories and city-specific marginal intervention efficiency. Key findings: (1) Henan’s UR exhibited clear inter-city differentiation, regional imbalance, and temporal fluctuation, with most cities improving before 2019 and declining or fluctuating after 2020. Zhengzhou and Luoyang formed the main high-value centers, while spatial autocorrelation weakened over time but local differentiation persisted. (2) Local government general budget revenue, the number of R&D personnel, urban population density, and the public safety expenditure ratio were identified as the four key explanatory indicators, accounting for 66% of total feature importance. Their local importance varied across space, and PDPs further showed that fiscal capacity and R&D personnel had stepwise marginal responses, population density exhibited earlier responses followed by stabilization in some cities, and public safety expenditure showed a gradual cumulative response, (3) Scenario simulations for 2024–2035 showed that higher intervention intensities generally generated larger UR improvements, whereas IRPU analysis revealed substantial differences in marginal efficiency across cities. These findings suggest that UR governance should adopt spatially differentiated and city-specific strategies based on local resilience constraints and marginal response characteristics.

title: Land-use legacies drive post-disturbance responses of plant diversity and habitat conservation status in Alpine dry grasslands
abstract: Semi-natural grasslands are biodiversity hotspots of high conservation concern in Europe, recognized under the EU Habitats Directive 92/43/EEC. Their occurrence depended on historical low-intensity agro-pastoral management, which maintained open vegetation structures hosting habitat-typical plant species. In the Alps, widespread land abandonment represents the main threat for these habitats. This study focused on semi-natural dry grasslands within Susa Valley (NW Italian Alps), an area historically shaped by agro-pastoral practices abandoned since the 1950s, involved in a grazing reintroduction project in 2014 and later affected by a severe wildfire in autumn 2017. Here, we investigated the effects of historical and recent landscape structure and the short-term drivers of post-disturbance (i.e., grazing intensity and fire severity) responses in vegetation diversity and habitat conservation status. We detected land-cover changes through classifications of historical (1954) and recent (2015) aerial images, and characterized grassland communities before and after disturbance events through field surveys. Results revealed substantial grassland loss and fragmentation due to dense forest expansion. Current dry grassland biodiversity and conservation status are strongly associated with historical landscape structure: sites embedded in formerly long-standing and extensive open areas host more diverse and better preserved communities. Post-fire responses differed markedly according to pre-disturbance conditions — degraded grasslands exhibited significant increases in habitat-typical species, whereas well-preserved grasslands showed limited compositional changes, indicating higher resistance to disturbance. These findings highlight the importance of landscape and vegetation legacies in shaping grassland dynamics. Management strategies should integrate historical landscape knowledge with current vegetation conditions to effectively maintain these high conservation value habitats.

title: Long-term multi-source remote sensing reveals region-specific driving mechanisms of forest fire spatiotemporal patterns across floristic sub-regions in mountainous Yunnan, China
abstract: Sharp gradients in floristic composition, fuel productivity, hydrothermal conditions and human accessibility can reshape forest fire disturbance in mountain regions, but administrative analyses may obscure ecological differences among vegetation regions.
