Using Yunnan Province, this study integrated Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer Terra thermal-anomaly product (MOD14A1), Fire Climate Change Initiative version 5.1 (FireCCI51), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), Landsat and Sentinel-2 data for 2006–2025. A Simple Non-Iterative Clustering–Random Forest (SNIC–RF) framework mapped burned areas at 30 m resolution. Burned-area maps were summarised across eight floristic sub-regions using a four-dimensional fire-disturbance indicator matrix, including fire timing, burned area, fire-event number and reburned extent. Climatic, vegetation, topographic and human-activity variables were analysed using 5 km × 5 km grids and eXtreme Gradient Boosting–SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost–SHAP). The SNIC–RF framework showed stable performance, with mean Overall Accuracy (OA) and burned-class F1-score values of 91.391% and 85.391%. Forest fires fluctuated strongly, with burned area peaking in 2010 and reaching a secondary high in 2023. Fire-event numbers were high in 2010, 2012–2014 and 2023, but were not synchronised with burned area, indicating joint controls from occurrence pressure and fire-spread size. Single-burn disturbances dominated, whereas Regions I, VII and VIII had more dispersed burn-frequency structures. At the provincial scale, mean temperature (TEM) was the strongest driver, followed by soil moisture (SM) and wind speed (VS). Across floristic sub-regions, TEM remained the common control, while gross primary productivity (GPP), digital elevation model (DEM), VS and SM acted as regional modifiers, and precipitation (PRE), population density (PD) and topographic wetness index (TWI) showed local enhancement. These findings indicate that floristic sub-regions are ecologically meaningful units for explaining regional fire heterogeneity and mechanism reorganisation, and can support the construction of sub-region-based fire-disturbance indicators, the identification of reburning-prone areas, differentiated fire-risk zoning and post-fire restoration prioritisation in mountain landscapes.

title: Advancing ecological network resilience early warning in alpine source regions: A machine learning and multi-scale diagnostic framework
abstract: Alpine source regions sustain the water security of billions downstream, yet existing resilience assessments of their ecological networks fundamentally conflate expansion in patch area and corridor count with genuine resilience recovery, a distinction critical to determining whether conservation investment has truly secured a system against critical-state degradation. Here, using the Sanjiangyuan region across three decades (1990–2023) as a case study, we develop and validate a resilience early-warning framework coupling a machine-learning pipeline with multi-scale network diagnostics. The framework introduces the Resilience Early-Warning Index, which integrates network potential resilience with cascading failure-derived loss risk into a unified supply–demand system, shifting the evaluative focus from how much ecological function has already been lost to how far the network remains from systemic collapse. Despite a 48% reduction in cascading loss risk over thirty years of conservation investment, the index oscillated repeatedly across the critical threshold between 2010 and 2015 without stabilizing, revealing that loss reduction is a necessary but insufficient condition for genuine resilience improvement. Node-level diagnostics further expose a persistent structural contradiction: northwestern marginal zones remained trapped in low-resilience states throughout all study periods, while southeastern core hubs, though structurally indispensable, harbored concentrated cascading risk such that removing a relatively small fraction of high-degree nodes was sufficient to reduce network function by half, a vulnerability that persisted throughout the study period. These results indicate that the dominant ecological challenge in Sanjiangyuan has shifted from network scale deficit to structural imbalance, requiring a management transition from corridor expansion toward cultivating secondary hubs and fostering a polycentric network topology. This study provides a quantitative foundation for evaluating thirty years of conservation practice and advances a transferable early-warning methodology for ecological network management in ecologically fragile regions worldwide.

title: A novel integrated framework for water-energy-food system efficiency evaluation and multi-scenario simulation incorporating water footprint accounting
abstract: Traditional water–energy–food (WEF) efficiency assessments predominantly rely on water withdrawal statistics, which do not accurately represent the water consumption and pollution characteristics of production activities, potentially leading to a systematic underestimation of water scarcity risks and misdirection of resource management policies. This study introduces the water footprint method, utilizing blue water and green water as inputs and gray water as an undesirable output, to establish a refined assessment system. Combining GDIM decomposition and Monte Carlo simulation, this study develops three scenarios are developed to forecast the evolution of WEF efficiency in nine provinces of the Yellow River Basin from 2024 to 2035. The results show that: (1) From 2005 to Li et al., 2023, comprehensive efficiency increased from 0.61 to 0.95, but inter-provincial differentiation is significant, with Sichuan being the only province displaying “high efficiency-low pressure-high coordination.” (2) The blue water stress index is decoupled from efficiency; major grain-producing areas experience blue water overload without exhibiting low efficiency, indicating that the efficiency indicator cannot accurately reflect the relationship between absolute consumption and carrying capacity. (3) Scenario simulations reveal three response modes: constant efficiency type (Inner Mongolia, Sichuan), synchronous improvement type (Shanxi, Henan), and lagging type (Shaanxi). (4) Policy marginal benefits diminish; the general control scenario already achieves most water-saving benefits (e.g., a 29% reduction in agricultural water footprint in Shanxi), while the additional reduction under the enhanced control scenario narrows to 6%–12%. This study provides a scientific basis for refined WEF management in the Yellow River Basin.

title: Global shrub encroachment: cross-system impacts on natural spheres and socio-economy
abstract: Shrub encroachment is a widespread global ecological process that has intensified under the combined influences of climate change and human activities. Although its impacts have been widely documented, their integrated effects across natural and socio-economic systems remain insufficiently understood. By synthesizing 130 empirical studies published worldwide over the past two decades, this review examines the effects of shrub encroachment on atmospheric, hydrological, pedospheric, biological and socio-economic systems. Shrub encroachment reshapes carbon cycling, hydrological processes and nutrient dynamics through changes in vegetation structure, generating both ecological benefits and potential risks. While it may enhance carbon sequestration and soil stability under certain conditions, it can also affect water availability, modify biodiversity patterns and lower rangeland productivity, with potential implications for pastoral livelihoods. These divergent responses are influenced by climatic conditions, soil properties, shrub functional traits and ecosystem characteristics, resulting in pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Overall, shrub encroachment should not be simply categorized as ecosystem degradation or restoration, as its effects are highly context-dependent. Understanding these context-dependent responses is critical for developing tailored management strategies under global environmental change.

title: Quantifying Process Carrying Capacity (PCC) as a threshold indicator for the resource-process-function nexus
abstract: Sustainable resource use requires anticipating ecological degradation before functional losses occur, yet current approaches remain largely reactive. This study develops a process-based framework by integrating the Resource-Process-Function (RPF) nexus with Process Carrying Capacity (PCC), defined as the threshold beyond which ecological processes cannot sustain stable ecosystem services. By conceptualizing resource systems as cascading interactions among resource use, processes, and functions, the framework identifies nonlinear responses and tipping points. Using a cold-temperate forest system, PCC thresholds were quantified for species composition (40–60% larch), precipitation (<520 mm), and elevation (<400 m). Exceeding these limits causes process–function decoupling and rapid declines in carbon sequestration and water regulation. The framework supports source-oriented, adaptive management to maintain processes within safe operating spaces, providing a transferable approach for aligning resource use with ecological sustainability and resilience.

title: Synergizing ground-based and satellite observations for Forest fire prediction: seasonal drivers and model-derived thresholds in the greater Khingan Mountains
abstract: Forest fires represent a critical disturbance regime in cold temperate ecosystems. To address the limitations of single-source monitoring, this study integrated long-term (2001–2024) ground-based records with MODIS data to construct a dual-source dataset for the Greater Khingan Mountains. We evaluated the predictive performance of four machine learning models—Boosted Regression Trees (BRT), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)—across the entire fire season and distinct seasonal periods. The SHAP framework was further employed to quantify non-linear responses and factor interactions. Results demonstrate significant spatial complementarity between data sources: while aligned in the eastern agro-forestry ecotone, MODIS filled monitoring gaps in remote western areas, whereas ground records provided superior detail for northern border regions. Among the models, satellite-based ensemble algorithms (specifically XGBoost and BRT) achieved the highest accuracy (AUC > 0.93) and superior spatial generalization. Crucially, SHAP analysis delineated the seasonal evolution of driving mechanisms. The Spring Fire Season was dominated by strong winds and anthropogenic activity, with a daily minimum temperature of -3°C emerging as a critical physical tipping point. In contrast, the Summer Fire Season was governed by hydrothermal balance; here, 15-day cumulative precipitation and NDVI were primary predictors, with a 40 mm precipitation threshold marking a risk inflection point. High-risk zones exhibited marked seasonal migration from the east (Spring/Autumn) to northern pristine forests (Summer). Consequently, we advocate for a dual-source fusion monitoring system with differentiated strategies: prioritizing anthropogenic prevention in the East during Spring/Autumn, and lightning fire monitoring in the North during Summer.

title: Differentiated industrial transition for typical Chinese cities based on spatiotemporal heterogeneity analysis of ecological resources
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of urban ecological resources is crucial for differentiated urban transition and regional sustainable development. This study developed a Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity analysis framework for Urban Ecological Resources (SHUER) to analyze the evolution and effect mechanisms of ecological resources in Chinese cities, which integrated ecological resource assessment, vulnerable subsystem identification, spatiotemporal heterogeneity analysis, and influencing mechanisms exploration. Based on Pressure-State-Response model, SHUER evaluates urban ecological resource status ( I ERS ) across ecological resources, environment, and socio-economic (2E1S) dimensions. The Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD) model was then used to assess the coordination heterogeneity within the complex system, and used spatial autocorrelation and Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression to identify spatial clustering patterns and the heterogeneous effects of industrial transition. The framework was applied to 60 cities across two ecologically contrasting regions from 2013 to 2022: the Coal Triangle (CT) and the Sichuan-Chongqing (CY) regions. The results showed the CT exhibits significantly lower I ERS and a persistent “high-pressure, weak-response” system imbalance. 2E1S system coupling coordination strengthened over time, yet CT showed emerging phased socio-economic constraints, while CY displayed more persistent ecological resources vulnerability. CT cities exhibited weak spatial correlation, whereas CY shifted from spatial agglomeration towards dispersion. Secondary industry transition exerted the most significant and spatially consistent negative association in CT, and tertiary upgrading leading coordinated improvement in CY. Based on the integrated analysis, typical cities were classified into four differentiated transition pathways, providing targeted implications for sustainable urban governance and maximizing the advantages of the urban ecological resources.

title: The impact of extreme climate events on carbon and water fluxes in grassland ecosystems on the Qinghai-Xizang plateau
abstract: The Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP) plays a crucial role in regulating terrestrial carbon and water exchanges. However, the impacts of increasingly frequent extreme climate events on ecosystem carbon and water fluxes remain insufficiently understood. Here, machine learning models using multi-source datasets were applied to simulate gross primary productivity (GPP) and evapotranspiration (ET) across QXP grassland ecosystems from 1958 to 2024 and to quantify their responses to extreme climate events. Results showed that: (1) the random forest model outperformed other models and revealed significant increasing trends in both GPP and ET; (2) carbon and water fluxes were generally positively correlated with warm extremes, negatively correlated with cold extremes, and showed predominantly negative responses to precipitation-related extremes; and (3) cold compound events (cold/dry and cold/wet) posed the greatest risk to carbon-water cycling, whereas hot compound events exerted weaker impacts on GPP but increased water consumption. Overall, QXP grassland carbon and water fluxes were most vulnerable to cold compound events. These findings improve understanding of alpine grassland responses to climate extremes and provide a scientific basis for ecosystem management under future climate change.

title: Integrated watershed condition score for assessing watershed condition and water quality-related vulnerability
abstract: To address watershed degradation in Taiwan, a nontraditional security (NTS) concern, this study developed an Integrated Watershed Condition Score (IWCS) framework and derived a composite index to assess vulnerability in the Zhuoshui and Danshui River basins using remote sensing and GIS techniques. The IWCS quantifies watershed vulnerability by integrating natural and socio-economic factors through multiple dimensions and measurable indicators. This research utilized datasets including Digital Elevation Model (DEM), soil maps, land use land cover (LULC), rainfall, and lithology, which were collected and processed for watershed assessment. Landsat 8 imagery provided vegetation and moisture indices (NDVI, EVI, NDWI, NDLI) and LULC classifications. In-situ water quality records (2010−2023) from local monitoring stations served as ground-truth validation. DEM-based analysis delineated watershed boundaries, extracted geomorphological parameters, and characterized stream networks. Both the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) identified similar spatial patterns of watershed vulnerability. The majority of sub-catchments exhibit low to moderate vulnerability, indicating stable water security conditions, while localized hotspots highlight the need for targeted management. Field observation at Linnei No. 2 Intake (September 29, 2024) confirmed low IWCS and favorable conditions. AHP and PCA converged on core indicators (population density, drainage characteristics, soil properties) as fundamental drivers of vulnerability, while divergences in slope weighting, resource pressure, and economic indicators revealed complementary strengths of expert-driven and data-driven perspectives. IWCS showed moderate correlations with water quality parameters, particularly ammonia nitrogen ( r = 0.53) and River Pollution Index ( r = 0.43), confirming its effectiveness. This multidimensional framework provides a robust basis for adaptive watershed management and conservation strategies that address NTS threats to water resources. Based on these findings, priority recommendations include controlling urban expansion in the vulnerable Danshui River Basin sub-catchments, managing agricultural non-point source pollution in western Zhuoshui River Basin areas, strengthening water quality monitoring networks, and integrating IWCS into watershed planning and restoration programs, supporting more resilient and sustainable water resource systems in Taiwan's river basins.

title: Fine-scale estimation of urban tree carbon storage by integrating biological attributes and environmental characteristics
abstract: With the growing importance of urban ecosystem services and carbon neutrality, accurately estimating carbon stocks in urban trees has become essential for low-carbon urban transformation and enhanced carbon-sink capacity. However, existing studies mainly rely on tree structural parameters or remote-sensing features, with limited attention to the joint effects of biological attributes, environmental context, and spatial neighborhood relationships at the individual-tree scale. To address this gap, this study proposes a fine-grained urban tree carbon-stock estimation method that integrates biological, environmental, and spatial topological features. Biological variables include species, tree height, DBH, and canopy structure, while local habitat features incorporate vegetation activity, background productivity, land-use condition, and topographic context. Spatial proximity and bio-environment interaction topology are further modeled using a Graph Attention Network (GAT) for cross-channel feature aggregation and carbon-stock regression. Results from approximately 140,000 trees in Shenzhen Bay Park show that the Bio + Env + Spatial model achieves the best performance at a 15 m radius and 2-hop propagation (RMSE = 0.3443, MAE = 0.1927, R 2 = 0.8360), improving R 2 by over 0.21 relative to the biology-only baseline. SHAP results indicate that biological structural traits dominate prediction, while local habitat and spatial features provide complementary refinements by correcting estimation deviations associated with neighborhood competition, habitat heterogeneity, and spatial context.

title: Digital-real integration networks and pollution-carbon reduction efficiency: a co-evolution analysis for Chinese cities
abstract: This study investigates the spatial correlation network of digital-real integration and its co-evolution with pollution‑carbon reduction using panel data from 300 Chinese cities (2013−2023). Prior work often employs gravity models that miss implicit intercity ties. This paper gauge digital-real integration via entropy-weighted TOPSIS, refine the network with a Bayesian latent spatial model, estimate pollution‑carbon efficiency through a super-efficiency SBM-GML model, and assess co-evolution via the Haken model. Findings reveal China's digital-real spatial correlation climbs from 0.171 (2013) to 0.188 (2023), exhibiting an “east-high, west-low, central catching up, northeast steady” pattern. The Bayesian approach captures latent linkages, with three urban agglomerations displaying distinct network structures. Pollution‑carbon efficiency shows static fluctuation yet dynamic growth, with SBM values of 0.149–0.633 and GML values of 1.239–5.533, surging post-2020. Digital-real integration emerges as the order parameter, with synergy ranging 16.788–16.989 (a 1.18% decline over the study period) and elevated levels in core cities and eastern areas. Policy implications are discussed.

title: Comprehensive assessment of ecosystem health in the Dongting Lake Basin from the perspectives of natural ecosystem and socioeconomic system
abstract: As complex socio-ecological ecosystems, watersheds require sound ecosystem health (EH) as a fundamental prerequisite for balancing ecological conservation and socioeconomic development. Although previous studies have developed refined EH assessment frameworks focusing on ecosystem natural health (ENH), human demand for ecosystem services has often been neglected. In this study, we developed an integrated EH assessment framework that incorporates interactions between natural systems and human society, encompassing ENH and ecosystem service supply-demand relationship (ESDR). The framework was applied to the Dongting Lake Basin, China. Using the CRITIC-entropy weighting method and the Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition method, we further analyzed the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of EH and its sources from 2000 to 2020. The results show that: (1) EH remained at Level III, with a spatial pattern characterized by higher values in the west and south and lower values in the east and north. ENH remained relatively stable, whereas the imbalance in ESDR intensified over time. (2) The spatial mosaic pattern and gradient transitions of EH jointly shaped the scale and intensity of spatial differentiation. (3) Spatial heterogeneity of EH was significant, with regional disparities continuously widening, primarily driven by inter-subregional transvariation intensity. This study enriches EH assessment methodology, and the related findings provide scientific references for formulating differentiated zoning management strategies.

title: Research on attribution and prediction of runoff changes in loess gully areas based on SWAT and machine learning models
abstract: Runoff evolution is a key issue affecting regional ecological security and the sustainable utilization of water and soil resources in loess gully regions. The Rui River Basin (RRB) was selected as the study area, and a research framework of trend testing, model coupling, attribution analysis and scenario prediction was constructed, and temporal evolution pattern of runoff was systematically revealed. Based on the SWAT model and its output data, an XGBoost quantile regression (XGBoost-QR) model was developed for runoff simulation comparison, demonstrating the advantages of integrating physical mechanisms with machine learning models, and the contribution of climate change and human activities to runoff changes were quantified using the scenario separation method. Finally, integrating the CMIP6 (BCC-CSM2-MR) climate scenarios and predictions of land use and land cover change (LUCC) patterns were incorporated into the SWAT model, runoff trends from 2022 to 2040 were predicted. The results showed that: (1) Precipitation at Huating (HT), Ankou (AK), and Yuanjiaan (YJA) increased (6.60–10.50 mm/10a), whereas annual runoff generally decreased (0.004–0.04 × 10 8 m 3 /10a), with abrupt changes occurring in 1990 and 2009. (2) The coupling model enhanced the overall simulation accuracy, human interventions were generally the dominant factor driving runoff changes, contributing 42.86% ∼ 73.69%, while the contribution rate of LUCC was between 16.67% and 45.71%. (3) From 2022 to 2040, annual runoff shows an increasing trend (0.01–0.44 m 3 /s·10a) under SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5. Through multi-model integration and multi-scenario analysis, this study provides a scientific basis for the coordinated regulation of water and soil resources and ecological adaptive management in loess gully regions.

title: Climate and traits are differentially associated with range extent and range geometry in global butterflies
abstract: Range extent and range geometry describe complementary dimensions of species distributions, but their associations with climate and functional traits remain poorly resolved at global scale. We rebuilt occurrence-derived alpha-hull range footprints for global butterflies from 66.9 million selected GBIF records using occurrence cleaning, 10-km thinning and sampling-support diagnostics, yielding 6929 species with range metrics. We combined range metrics with footprint-level climate axes, trait axes and a Grafen topology-derived phylogeny in a phylogeny-linked multi-response path model for 5010 species. Climate axes showed stronger conditional associations with range extent, whereas trait axes showed stronger associations with range-shape elongation, with model comparison supporting the selected decomposition but not a causally identified path structure. Sampling, grid-threshold, PM-denominator, CTC/IND, climate-zone and nonlinearity diagnostics supported bounded interpretation while retaining explicit caveats for occurrence-derived footprints, model structure and uneven zonal sample sizes. These results distinguish climate-associated range extent from trait-associated range geometry in occurrence-derived butterfly footprints and may help generate hypotheses and prioritise independent validation or monitoring of range geometry under global change.

title: Selective fishing of top predators further promotes the recovery of riverine fish resources
abstract: The decline of freshwater fish resources has become a global crisis, severely threatening food security and biodiversity in low-income regions. In response, China implemented a “ten-year fishing ban” across the entire Yangtze River Basin, making it one of the world's strictest conservation plans. However, the cascading effects of the ban on fish communities and food webs remain poorly understood, and the restoration outcomes for fish populations remain uncertain, with a lack of assessments regarding the potential impacts of fishing resumption. This study developed an Ecopath model for a typical river section under ban management and used the Ecosim model to simulate the dynamic changes in fish community and food web structure under different fishing strategies. The results show that the rapid increase in top predators after the ban triggers a trophic cascade detrimental to fish resource recovery, primarily through increased predation mortality, which leads to the decline of prey functional groups and limits the recovery of other functional groups. These findings contribute to the understanding and prediction of the impacts of fishing bans on community composition and food web processes. Furthermore, the prediction indicates that different fishing strategies after the ban result in distinct changes in fish communities and food web structures. Only the strategy of selectively fishing top predator functional groups can achieve further fish resource recovery, accompanied by increased food web stability. These results provide key insights for management aimed at restoring fishery resources.

title: Long-term vegetation restoration elevates soil and litter nutrient concentrations of Pinus massoniana plantations in southern China
abstract: Vegetation restoration (VR) is essential for degraded ecosystems by enhancing surface cover and improving soil properties, particularly soil nutrients and water retention in eroded and degraded land. However, long-term studies evaluating the interactive effects of VR on soil properties, plant-soil feedbacks, and nutrient cycling remain limited. This study examined how VR years (8, 11, 14, 17, and 20 years) influenced soil physical characteristics, water regulation, nutrient concentrations across soil depths (0–5, 5–20, 20–40, and 40–60 cm), litter yield and nutrient contents in eroded and degraded Pinus massoniana plantations (CK). Results showed that restoration treatment, restoration years (RY), and soil depth significantly affected soil physical properties, water regulation capacity (represented by soil porosity and soil water content), and nutrient availability. Compared to CK, VR reduced soil hardness (by 1.360–15.25 kg cm −2 ) and bulk density (by 0.118–0.800 g cm −3 ), but increased water content (by −6.126–25.18%), porosity (by 1.597–25.23%), organic carbon (by 0.910–21.70 g kg −1 ), total nitrogen (by 0.190–0.780 g kg −1 ), and total phosphorus (by −0.013–0.210 g kg −1 ), with these improvements intensifying over RY. These improvements of the 0–5 cm were more significant, evidenced by a higher R 2 value. Under VR treatment, RY significantly altered soil texture and litter dynamics, evidenced by decreased sand content but increased clay content and increased litter yield and nutrient concentrations ( P < 0.001). Strong correlations were observed between soil and litter properties, with RY driving increases in litter and soil nutrients through enhanced litter production and improved soil water regulation. Moreover, soil porosity and soil water content were the dominant drivers of soil organic carbon ( R 2 = 76.81%), total nitrogen ( R 2 = 86.19%), and total phosphorus ( R 2 = 92.12%). These findings elucidate the mechanisms by which VR influences soil-litter interactions and nutrient cycling in degraded Pinus massoniana forests, offering a scientific basis for sustainable forest management.

title: Epiphytic foraminiferal community change suggests environmental deterioration of coastal coral reefs
abstract: Benthic protists within Atlantic marine ecosystems play a pivotal role in biogeochemical cycles, particularly through calcium carbonate production, which shapes habitat structure and dynamics. Highly sensitive to anthropogenic perturbations, including nutrient enrichment, these organisms often are more responsive than metazoan taxa, underpinning the FoRAM Index as a robust bioindicator and early warning system for ecological stress. This study evaluates the efficacy of these microbenthic sentinels across the Pinaúnas Reef (Itaparica Island, Bahia, Brazil). Samples were collected during dry and wet seasons across three discrete years (2000, 2010, and 2022) to assess temporal dynamics alongside comprehensive physico-chemical measurements. Univariate and multivariate analyses revealed minimal seasonal variability but a pronounced temporal change in Foraminifera by 2022. Notably, FoRAM Indices declined markedly in the most recent sampling period, driven by a relative reduction in symbiont-bearing taxa (especially Amphistegina spp.) and a concurrent increase in opportunistic species ( Elphidium spp. and Ammonia beccarii ). Elevated nitrate and phosphate levels correlated significantly with these assemblage alterations (positively with taxonomic diversity, but negatively with the FoRAM Index), most likely stemming from burgeoning human population pressures and inadequate effluent management. Although the limited number of sampling years limits the extrapolation to continuous temporal trends, the data clearly indicate a functional transition towards a degraded state. Ultimately, these microorganisms appear to prove far more sensitive than conventional water-quality metrics. By integrating cumulative pollution effects over time, they offer an essential early alert to habitat decline.

title: Incorporating regional characteristics into nitrogen footprint assessment: Development of a watershed scale virtual nitrogen factor calculation method using SWAT
abstract: The conventional nitrogen (N) footprint (NF) calculation approach, known as the N-Calculator method, estimates virtual N factors (VNFs) for food categories primarily from national-scale statistics, which limits its ability to represent regional characteristics and distinct reactive N (Nr) load pathways. To address these limitations, we developed an improved VNF calculation method by integrating a new VNF calculation framework with the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) at the watershed scale. Its application to the Ikushunbetsu River watershed in Japan demonstrated that SWAT effectively captures the complex N dynamics in upland fields. The new framework resolves physically impossible negative Nr loads arising from soil N depletion by explicitly incorporating soil N change as a pool input. Disaggregation of Nr loads by individual load pathways enabled crop-specific identification of mitigation priorities: leaching suppression for onion and wheat, and recovery of soil N stocks for rice and soybean. These advances go beyond conventional watershed-scale N analyses using SWAT by enabling Nr loads to be interpreted within a consumption-based NF framework. Spatial analysis revealed that VNF determinants are inherently crop-specific: wheat VNF showed statistically significant positive and negative correlations with slope and solar radiation, respectively, whereas onion VNF was governed by management intensity. The intra-watershed VNF variation for wheat was comparable in magnitude to inter-country variation reported in previous studies. Because the framework can be implemented with outputs from other process-based models and SWAT is widely applied in data-scarce regions, it supports the extension of spatially explicit, crop-specific NF assessments beyond a single case study.

title: Regional actual evapotranspiration estimation and spatiotemporal evolution pattern in Northwest China
abstract: Quantifying actual evapotranspiration ( ET c ), its components, and ecosystem water use efficiency ( WUE e ) is critical for predicting ecosystem responses within the carbon-water-energy cycle and for informing climate change mitigation and water resource strategies. This study focused on the arid region of Xinjiang, using the Shuttleworth-Wallace-Hu (SWH) model with Monte Carlo algorithms to quantify daily ET c for the period 2003–2021. The spatiotemporal characteristics of ET c , transpiration ratio ( T/ET c ), and WUE e were also analyzed. Based on these results, a simplified WUE e chain framework was constructed using two intermediate processes (photosynthetic transpiration efficiency (GPP/T) and T/ET c ) to investigate the core driving mechanisms of WUE e at the monthly scale. The SWH model performed well, with simulated values close to field observations and spatiotemporal dynamics captured accurately. The multi-year daily averages for the region were 1.94 mm day −1 for soil evaporation ( E ), 1.79 mm day −1 for vegetation transpiration ( T ), 3.73 mm day −1 for ET c , 48% for T/ET c , and 1.40 g C kg −1 H 2 O for WUE e . The values were higher in the north, correlating to higher vegetation cover. Temporally, ET c and T increased, while E was relatively stable. The trends of WUE e were spatially divergent, decreasing in the north and increasing in the south. Changes in water consumption and WUE e were jointly controlled by environmental and vegetation factors. Among these, GPP/T is the primary process driving monthly-scale variations in WUE e , and temperature ( T a ) and net radiation ( R n ) are the main controlling factors of WUE e . This component-based analysis deepened our understanding of ecohydrological processes in arid regions, providing critical support for optimizing water management and climate adaptation strategies.

title: Ecosystem service–development benefit imbalance and governance thresholds for arid salt-lake lithium development
abstract: Arid salt-lake lithium development has become an important upstream component of the low-carbon transition, yet its localized ecosystem-service consequences and development-benefit trade-offs remain insufficiently quantified at fine spatial scales. Taking Golmud in the Qaidam Basin as a representative salt-lake lithium development region, this study examines how lithium-related development reshaped the spatial balance between ecosystem service value and development economic performance from 2005 to 2025. We integrate multi-source remote sensing, land-use, socioeconomic and environmental data to delineate lithium-related development, estimate ecosystem service value and development economic performance, construct a synergy imbalance indicator (SI), and identify drivers and thresholds using XGBoost with Shapley additive explanations. Lithium-related development expanded from 332.85 to 1060.14 km 2 , with most expansion occurring between 2005 and 2015. Stage-based SI analysis shows that non-mining areas remained dominated by very-high-synergy cells, accounting for 93.74% in 2005–2015 and 92.67% in 2015–2025. Mining areas showed a more heterogeneous structure: very-high-synergy cells increased from 25.79% to 39.81%, while very-low-synergy cells still accounted for 16.73% and 12.99% in the two stages, respectively. Model attribution suggests a transition from expansion- and proximity-related imbalance in 2005–2015 to a combined association with elevation, economic growth, road density and existing development stock in 2015–2025. Threshold analysis further shows higher imbalance risks below approximately 2800 m and above 4500 m and accelerating risks where new expansion and road density intensify. The findings translate ecosystem-service accounting and development benefits into management-relevant early-warning information for zoning, infrastructure-density control and sensitive-area monitoring in salt-lake lithium basins.

title: High-resolution projections of carbon neutrality in China: implications for low-carbon territorial space utilization
abstract: Formulating low-carbon optimization strategies for territorial space is crucial for achieving carbon neutrality and addressing climate change. This study employed the STIRPAT model and CMIP6 ESMs to simulate China's carbon emissions and carbon sinks from 2020 to 2060 under SSP-RCP scenarios, with carbon sinks measured using NEP, and explored the viability of achieving carbon neutrality by 2060. It further analyzed the NEP-based carbon sink carrying capacity of different land use/cover types and the spatiotemporal patterns of net carbon emissions at high spatial resolution. Results indicate that carbon emissions peak in 2026 under SSP1–2.6 and in 2036 under SSP5–8.5. Under all scenarios, carbon sink capacity increases slightly, with forest, cropland, and grassland as the main contributors. Forest accounts for an average of 46.53% of carbon sink capacity. The greatest carbon neutrality potential occurs under SSP1–2.6, where carbon sinks can offset up to 46.66% of anthropogenic emissions by 2060. Most provinces will remain net emitters, except for several northwestern provinces. Provinces near southeastern coastal urban agglomerations constitute the core emission zones, especially those adjacent to the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Shandong Peninsula, Yangtze River Delta, and Pearl River Delta urban agglomerations. Therefore, the development of low-carbon territorial space is a key task for China's future. These findings highlight the importance of low-carbon territorial space optimization for supporting China's “dual carbon” goals and sustainable territorial space utilization.

title: A remote sensing-based tree mortality indicator for biodiversity monitoring using multispectral UAV and lidar in the Arctic region, Finland
abstract: Deadwood is a recognised ecological indicator for forest biodiversity. Both the UN Convention on Biological Diversity and the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030 mandates inventorying and reporting deadwood. However, monitoring tree mortality, the source of deadwood, remains challenging, especially in Arctic and sub-Arctic regions. Boreal forests in this region face increasing climate-driven stressors: droughts, pest outbreaks, and snow damage. These stressors accelerate tree mortality and threaten biodiversity. Deep learning-based semantic segmentation offers a scalable solution for monitoring standing tree mortality using remote sensing data such as multispectral UAV imagery and lidar-derived canopy height models. In this study, we (1) evaluated a U-Net model for detecting tree mortality across 208 ha of Picea abies , Pinus sylvestris , and deciduous dominated forests, and (2) produced a wall-to-wall mortality map to identify spatial patterns and potential drivers in Northern Lapland, Finland. The training dataset included 411 tiles containing 4380 manually delineated tree crowns. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.92, with a recall and F1-score for dead trees 0.82 and 0.57, for alive trees 0.93 and 0.96. The performance is sufficient for identifying spatial patterns despite false positive detections. Mortality hotspots were concentrated in Picea abies dominated areas at higher elevations where older trees were located, suggesting a link to snow damage besides natural mortality. These results demonstrate the potential of UAV based deep learning workflows for large-scale exploratory monitoring of tree mortality patterns in northern boreal forests in Arctic and sub-Arctic region and supports biodiversity reporting and restoration monitoring through spatial forest-health assessment.

title: Differential causal responses of four grassland types to hydrothermal drivers on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
abstract: Grasslands on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) are sensitive to climate change, but their causal responses to hydrothermal drivers and the dominance of temperature or water remain unclear. Combining 2000–2023 MODIS NDVI, evapotranspiration (ET), soil moisture (SM), monthly precipitation (PRE), and monthly mean (TMP), maximum (TMAX), and minimum (TMIN) temperatures, we applied Mann-Kendall trend analysis, generalized linear model (GLM), and convergent cross-mapping (CCM) with false nearest neighbors optimization to examine responses of alpine meadow, alpine grassland, temperate grassland, and desert grassland. The results show that (1) growing-season NDVI rose across the QTP, with a clear type-specific: desert grassland (60.29%) > temperate grassland (39.18%) > alpine grassland (28.51%) > alpine meadow (15.24%). (2) GLM (pseudo-R 2 > 0.5 over about 74% of the area) revealed type-specific response patterns. ET and PRE were positive on alpine and desert grassland (>51% of pixels) but negative on alpine meadow and temperate grassland (>50%); SM was broadly positive except in desert grassland; TMAX was negative across types, while TMIN was positive in all four. These reversals confirm that the four grassland types differ systematically in their response directions to hydrothermal drivers. (3) CCM showed temperature as a dominant region-wide driver (>93% of pixels), while the dominant water driver differed by types: SM for alpine meadow (91.79%) and temperate grassland (93.38%), PRE for alpine grassland (84.39%), and ET for desert grassland (74.97%). These findings clarify temperature drives overall QTP grassland changes, while water's dominant effect varies by type, supporting type-specific conservation and adaptive management under rapid climate change.

title: Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence reveals a functional recovery lag behind canopy structural recovery after flash drought on the North China plain
abstract: Increasing flash drought frequency poses a serious threat to ecosystem stability. Traditional greenness-based remote sensing methods are slow to detect early suppression of photosynthetic physiology and its recovery. While the earlier response of Solar-Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence (SIF) to drought stress is well documented, the asymmetry between functional and structural recovery after drought termination has not been systematically quantified. Here we address this gap by comparing SIF and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) within a unified resistance-resilience framework during the 2015 flash drought on the North China Plain. SIF showed strong spatiotemporal consistency with gross primary productivity (GPP, R 2 = 0.95). Quantitative assessment revealed, for the first time, that recovery times differed markedly among indicators (SIF 30.7 d, NDVI 20.3 d, GPP 40.0 d). This ordering, with NDVI fastest, SIF intermediate, and GPP slowest, reflects a hierarchical recovery cascade. Structural re-greening occurs first, followed by photochemical efficiency restoration as captured by SIF, and finally full re-establishment of carbon assimilation metabolism as represented by GPP. Both functional recoveries, SIF and GPP, thus lag behind structural recovery. Both also showed high spatial consistency, identifying ecologically fragile areas such as the sandy lands of the Yellow River floodplain. Air temperature was the primary environmental predictor associated with SIF variations. These findings suggest that SIF enables early detection of photosynthetic decline and, more importantly, provides the first quantitative evidence that functional recovery lags behind structural recovery, a critical insight for post-drought ecological assessment.

title: From methodological divides to planning priorities: a goal-scale framework for selecting connectivity methods in ecological network planning
abstract: Connectivity assessment is central to ecological network construction, yet different methods generate distinct forms of planning evidence, and guidance for selecting them according to the planning question remains limited. To address this gap, this study develops a planning-oriented goal–scale framework for connectivity method selection and illustrates its planning relevance through a comparative analysis in Shenzhen, China. A shared ecological source system was derived using morphological spatial pattern analysis (MSPA), and two analytical pathways were compared: minimum cumulative resistance (MCR)-based cost connectivity and graph-theoretic connectivity represented by the integral index of connectivity (IIC) and probability of connectivity (PC). The cost-connectivity pathway identified accessible ecological service patches and low-resistance corridors, mainly in eastern and southeastern mountain areas and reservoir-associated ecological spaces. IIC/PC emphasized mountain-reservoir backbones, central structural patches, and bridge-like links supporting network coherence. Coupling coordination analysis showed substantial divergence: antagonistic areas accounted for 60.82% of patches and 44.73% of corridors, while high-level coupling coordination areas accounted for 5.22% and 8.04%, respectively. High-coordination areas were concentrated in ecological anchors where cost accessibility and structural importance coincided. Geographical detector analysis showed that patch-level differentiation was mainly associated with land class, distance to the urban core, road density, and point-of-interest (POI) density, whereas corridor-level differentiation was weakly associated with individual urban-context variables. The findings indicate that MCR and IIC/PC provide complementary but non-interchangeable evidence: graph-theoretic indices foreground network structural prioritization, whereas cost connectivity provides spatially explicit evidence for corridor routing and implementation-oriented intervention.

title: Corrigendum to “Nonlinear thresholds of landscape indicators regulating net ecosystem productivity in a subtropical region: An interpretable XGBoost–SHAP approach” [Ecol. Indic. 189 (2026) 115087]
abstract: This correction relates solely to the visual presentation of the conceptual schematic and does not affect the scientific content, data, analyses, results, interpretations, or conclusions of the article.

title: Indicators and predictive frameworks for microbial regime shifts in aquatic ecosystems: From collapse detection to recovery prediction
abstract: Microbial communities regulate essential biogeochemical processes in aquatic ecosystems and play a central role in maintaining ecosystem stability. But the increase in environmental pressures resulting from climate change, eutrophication, pollution, and hydrological alteration has intensified interest in predicting microbial community collapse before irreversible ecological change occurs. This review examines the current knowledge on the prediction of microbial community collapse in aquatic ecosystems through four interconnected areas, including multi-omics-based early-warning indicators, quantitative network and functional thresholds, computational frameworks for predicting collapse and recovery, and emerging spatio-temporal network approaches. The current evidence shows that the integration of metagenomics, meta transcriptomics, metabolomics, ecological network analysis, and mechanistic modeling has substantially improved understanding of microbial instability and resilience. Functional perturbations often precede detectable taxonomic changes, while recovery trajectories frequently involve restoration of ecosystem function without complete recovery of community composition. Constraint-based metabolic models, machine-learning approaches, and dynamic ecological models each provide complementary predictive capabilities but differ in their mechanistic interpretability, data requirements, and applicability across spatial and temporal scales. Likewise, spatio-temporal network frameworks provide an increasingly comprehensive representation of microbial ecosystem dynamics but remain limited by high computational demands and the scarcity of high-resolution environmental observations. Despite these advances, operational prediction of microbial collapse remains constrained by limited long-term monitoring datasets, insufficient validation of proposed ecological thresholds across ecosystem types, incomplete integration of environmental drivers into predictive models, and persistent uncertainty associated with nonlinear ecological regime shifts. Future progress will require standardized monitoring protocols, systematic cross-ecosystem validation of predictive indicators, integration of multi-omics with mechanistic and data-driven modeling, and adaptive validation frameworks capable of quantifying predictive uncertainty.

title: Assessing climate-driven ecohydrological effects on altitudinal vegetation belt dynamics in the Bogda natural world heritage site, northwestern China
abstract: Climate change is profoundly altering altitudinal vegetation belt regimes in global mountain ecosystems, yet the ecohydrological mechanisms underlying these alterations remain poorly quantified. The Bogda Natural World Heritage Site on the Tianshan Mountains in northwestern China, preserves a complete altitudinal vegetation belt spectrum from desert steppe to alpine meadow, offering an ideal natural experimental area to disentangle climate-driven ecohydrological controls and consequences across elevation gradients. Here, using field comprehensive measurements in conjunction with stochastic ecohydrological modelling approaches, we find that soil and river properties shift nonlinearly along the elevation gradient. Soil moisture increases and soil temperature decreases with elevation, while soil pH and electrical conductivity each follow unimodal distributions peaking at the montane coniferous forest belt. River pH and electrical conductivity decrease with elevation, whereas dissolved oxygen peaks in the desert grassland zone, and suspended solids and turbidity spike at the subalpine alpine meadow transition. Aboveground biomass is controlled primarily by temperature and precipitation, whereas belowground biomass is governed mainly by soil properties. Critically, water‑carbon coupling shifts across vegetation belts, with desert and montane grasslands being water-limited, whereas coniferous forest, subalpine and alpine meadows are energy-limited. Increased rainfall frequency enhances soil moisture stability, while greater rainfall intensity promotes effective water replenishment; their combined effect elevates mean effective soil moisture and enhances carbon assimilation capacity. Accordingly, altitudinal vegetation belts do not respond linearly to climate forcing but instead shift between distinct ecohydrological regimes. These findings offer critical insights for strengthening ecosystem resilience, protecting biodiversity, and enhancing carbon sinks in global mountain systems facing climate change.

title: High spatiotemporal resolution process-based model revealed an aggravated nitrogen legacy-related water pollution risk in a large basin: spatio-seasonal patterns, drivers, and management opportunities
abstract: Legacy nitrogen, i.e., long-term nitrogen storage in landscapes, poses a formidable water environmental management challenge due to its ongoing threats to surface water quality, considerable magnitude, and dispersed spatial distribution. A comprehensive understanding of legacy nitrogen and its impacts on water quality at broader, finer spatiotemporal scales is crucial for legacy-related water pollution control and eco-environment sustainable development. Here, we developed a process-based model system with high spatiotemporal resolution to generate seasonal maps of legacy nitrogen in soils ( N leg _ soi ) and groundwater ( N leg _ gr ) for the Songhuajiang River basin during 1978–2020. The model revealed an upswing in seasonal legacy nitrogen storage, with increases of approximately 1.4- to 3.6-fold. Legacy hotspots covering 10% of the basin area contributed approximately 38–67% of total legacy nitrogen storage, implying markedly uneven spatial distribution of legacy nitrogen. N leg _ soi showed higher sensitivity to anthropic factors, while N leg _ gr was more sensitive to natural factors. With increasing legacy effects over time, legacy nitrogen was responsible for approximately 48–73% of seasonal riverine nitrogen loading. A combination of livestock-crop-human coupled system, fossil fuel use reduction, and soil and manure management can effectively abate legacy-related water pollution.

title: Revealing the alterations of social-ecological system networks by China's national parks: Evidence from the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China
abstract: National parks are pivotal instruments for advancing biodiversity conservation and fostering regional sustainable development. Yet, against the backdrop of intensifying climate change and growing anthropogenic pressures, the mechanisms by which national park governance reshapes coupled social-ecological systems (SES) remain insufficiently elucidated. Taking Qinghai Province, China, as a case study, this research integrates multi-source data to systematically investigate county-level ecological dynamics from 2005 to 2023. We employed a mixed-methods framework combining social network analysis (SNA), machine learning, and partial least squares structural equation modeling to quantify spatiotemporal variations in ecological importance, trace the dynamic evolution of SES linkage networks, and disentangle the direct and indirect pathways through which natural and anthropogenic factors drive SES dynamics. The results indicate that the evolution of SES shows a general trend of growing connectivity and stronger coupling. The linkage between economic and ecological components is positively shaped by a topography-soil-vegetation cascade, with standardized path coefficients of 0.72, 0.73, and 0.90, respectively. Compared with non-park areas, national park areas showed enhanced network structural cohesion, with policy-induced increases of 40% in network density, 35.16% in average clustering coefficient, and 70.89% in average weighted degree. Meanwhile, natural processes contribute to a more notable rise in coupling intensity. These findings advance the theoretical understanding of the socio-ecological impacts of protected area governance and provide a rigorous scientific basis for guiding the sustainable transition toward integrated ecological protection and socio-economic development at the regional scale.

title: Corrigendum to “Integrated risk assessment of sediment-bound heavy metals using macroinvertebrate indicators in South Korea’s major river basins” [Ecol. Indic. 181 (2025) 114380]
An interpretable–causal learning framework for identifying the drivers of surface urban Heat Island intensity: evidence from 527 urban clusters in China
abstract: Under the combined effects of global warming and rapid urbanization, urban morphology has emerged as an important factor associated with variations in surface urban heat island intensity (SUHII) through its influence on surface physical properties and urban energy balance. Ho，wever, existing studies have largely relied on statistical correlation analyses and often lack standardized definitions of reference zones or sufficient control of confounding variables, making it challenging to disentangle environmental disturbances and identify the underlying drivers of SUHII and their spatial variability. To address these limitations, this study employs the Google Earth Engine platform to construct a multi-constraint framework for quantifying SUHII across 527 urban clusters in China and integrates LightGBM-SHAP with Double Machine Learning (DML) to establish an analytical framework that combines correlation analysis, causal inference, and mechanism interpretation. The results indicate pronounced spatial heterogeneity in summer daytime SUHII across China, with generally higher values observed in eastern and southern regions than in western and northern regions. Correlation analysis identifies impervious surface fraction (ISF) and tree canopy cover (PT) as the dominant statistical predictors. However, causal inference suggests that ISF (ATE = 0.374), largest patch index (LPI, ATE = 0.253), and water body proportion (PW, ATE = −0.240) exhibit relatively robust average estimated effects within the causal inference framework at the national scale. By contrast, PT, building height (BH), and patch density (PD) display substantial contextual dependence, with their thermal regulation effects varying across different climatic conditions, which may explain their inconsistent significance within the causal framework. By integrating correlation-based identification with causal validation, this study helps clarify the scope and limitations of urban morphological influences on SUHII and provides scientific support for the development of differentiated and evidence-informed urban planning strategies aimed at improving climate resilience.

title: The use of acoustic doppler current profiler acoustic backscatter to develop a regional zooplankton indicator for temperate marine ecosystems
abstract: Zooplankton are important prey in ocean food webs, linking primary producers to higher trophic levels; understanding their biomass is important to understanding ecosystem state and managing commercial fisheries accordingly. Due to expense and necessary processing time, there are limited indicators of zooplankton that can be produced timely enough to be useful for real-time management needs. We analyzed and compared an 18-year dataset of zooplankton biomass of 21 different species/taxa groups from net samples and acoustic backscatter from Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCPs) deployed on underwater gliders in the California Current System. Results show positive linear relationships across multiple spatial and temporal scales with greater than 50% of the variance of the total zooplankton biomass explained by the acoustic backscatter when samples were collected within 24 h and 1 km of each other. Copepod species usually dominated the total net haul biomass and there were similar relationships between copepod biomass and a) acoustic backscatter and b) total net biomass. An analysis of cross-shelf transects of the acoustic backscatter data was used to create a Glider Acoustic Backscatter Index (GAZI). The indicator shows consistent low values during El Niño periods and consistently high values during La Niña periods, conforming to our understanding of general productivity in the California Current during El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events. These results provide a zooplankton indicator that can be rapidly produced on a sub-monthly time frame and a pathway to potentially using autonomous underwater gliders with ADCPs to monitor zooplankton in other oceanic environments.

title: Total suspended matter dynamics in the Songhua River over four decades: evidence of anthropogenic decoupling between soil erosion and in-stream regulation
abstract: Human activities have profoundly altered suspended-sediment dynamics in large rivers; however, long-term, spatially explicit records that disentangle basin-wide forcing from reach-specific engineering impacts remain scarce. Here, we develop a Random Forest (RF) retrieval model based on Landsat top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance and 542 in situ samples to reconstruct annual Total Suspended Matter (TSM) concentrations along the main stem of the Songhua River from 1984 to 2023. The resulting four-decade record reveals a basin-wide decline beginning in the early 1990s, accompanied by pronounced spatial heterogeneity among river reaches. At the basin scale, the relationship between watershed soil erosion (RUSLE-based dataset, 1990–2022) and riverine TSM is weak at the annual timescale. This weaken the linkage is most evident in the SRH–FRH reach downstream of the Dadingzishan hydro-junction, where in-stream regulation may override upstream erosion signals. Breakpoint analysis, using 2008 as the full-impoundment year, indicates a marked acceleration in TSM decline within SRH–FRH, from −0.22 mg L −1 yr −1 during 1984–2008 to −0.78 mg L −1 yr −1 during 2009–2023. A reach-to-reach quasi-experimental comparison further demonstrates a significant post-2008 divergence between SRH–FRH and a downstream control reach (ANOVA: F = 13.045, p = 0.0001), reinforcing the interpretation that reservoir regulation exerted a dominant, reach-specific influence on suspended sediment dynamics after impoundment. Together, these findings indicate that in heavily managed basins, in-stream engineering can reorganize sediment connectivity and partially weaken the linkage between downstream suspended sediment from basin-scale erosion signals. This process underscores the need to explicitly incorporate reservoir operation into sediment management and water-quality governance frameworks.

title: Mining intensifies connectivity vulnerability in a function-state-structure ecological security network on the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau
abstract: Coordinating intensive mineral extraction with ecological sustainability in fragile mountain regions remains a critical challenge. On the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, where karst fragility, plateau lakes, and clustered mining activities intersect, apparent vegetation recovery may not coincide with ecosystem service recovery or network resilience. However, conventional ecological security pattern (ESP) workflows may insufficiently capture this mismatch because they often rely on static land-cover classes, greenness-dominated ecological indices, or single ecosystem service metrics. To address this gap, we developed a function–state–structure framework that integrates ecosystem service supply, terrestrial and aquatic ecological status, patch-level connectivity importance, and mining-modified resistance. A Comprehensive Ecological Index (CEI) was used to identify candidate source areas where ecosystem function and ecological condition coincided, while delta Probability of Connectivity (dPC) retained patches that were topologically indispensable to the regional network. A Mining Disturbance Index (MDI), derived from the current mining inventory, was embedded in the mining-sensitive resistance surface to diagnose extraction-related impedance to ecological flows. From 2001 to 2023, the mean CEI increased from 0.44 to 0.47, and the share of Good and Excellent ecological-quality classes remained close to 40% after 2013. This apparent improvement masked a growing structural vulnerability: ecological source patches increased from 119 to 166, but larger sources fragmented, barriers expanded after 2013, and connectivity became increasingly dependent on a small number of pinch points. Partial least-squares structural equation modelling further showed that human pressure strengthened its negative effect on CEI from −0.268 in 2001 to −0.437 in 2023, whereas climatic and topo-edaphic controls mainly defined the natural baseline. Local diagnostics revealed two mining-driven failure modes: direct severance of pinch points and formation of high-resistance mining matrices that force ecological flows to detour. These findings support a targeted spatial optimization strategy of “one ring, two wings, two belts, and multiple points,” offering an adaptable methodological reference and regional-scale evidence for coordinating ecological restoration and mineral-resource governance in fragile karst mountain regions.

title: Temporal dynamics and drivers of soil organic carbon following ecological restoration on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
abstract: Investigating soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamic and its controlling factors is essential for improving soil carbon sequestration in ecological restoration areas. However, the temporal variations in SOC content and composition in alpine ecological restoration areas remain poorly understood. In this study, soil physicochemical properties (pH, aggregates, total and available nitrogen, total and available phosphorus, and available potassium), enzyme activity (sucrase, cellulase, alkaline protease, and alkaline phosphatase), microbial characteristics, and SOC composition were analysed to investigate the temporal changes in SOC content and its major controlling factors in alpine ecological restoration areas. Results showed that SOC content continuously increased following ecological restoration. Lignin and phenols were more abundant following ecological restoration, whereas the relative abundances of aromatic hydrocarbons, alkanes and alkenes exhibited the opposite trend, indicating a shift from microbially derived to plant-derived SOC inputs following ecological restoration. Soil enzyme activities and microbial community characteristics responded significantly to restoration, and the relative importance of stochastic processes in bacterial community assembly increased with restoration time. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) revealed that restoration time was the dominant factor associated with SOC dynamics through both direct and indirect effects mediated by soil properties, SOC composition, and microbial communities. Correlation analysis further identified soil total nitrogen (TN) as the factor most strongly associated with SOC content. These findings provide mechanistic insights into SOC accumulation following restoration and offer a scientific basis for enhancing carbon sequestration in degraded alpine ecosystem.

title: Are Mongolian rangelands overgrazed? Estimating grassland utilisation and sustainable stocking rates with a vegetation model
abstract: Mongolian grasslands are vulnerable systems, prone to degradation, as low precipitation and poor soil fertility limit biomass production, while increasing livestock numbers intensify pressure on rangelands. Although reducing livestock numbers is proposed to relieve pressure, quantitative tools to project forage availability, grassland utilisation, and potential livestock densities over time remain limited. In this study, we applied the LPJ-GUESS dynamic global vegetation model, enhanced with a custom livestock submodule, to simulate historical grassland dynamics (1970–2023, 9 × 9 km) while explicitly accounting for vegetation-livestock interactions. The coupled model was used to analyse spatial patterns of forage availability and grassland utilisation via the Human Appropriation of Net Primary Production (HANPP) framework and to estimate potential livestock densities using a novel optimality approach. The model exhibited reasonable to good spatial and temporal agreement with remotely sensed GPP and NPP. Agreement was strongest in the eastern steppe, where the model also successfully reproduced satellite-based above-ground biomass estimates, which were calibrated with local field data. According to the simulations, HANPP increased from an average of 6% in 1970 to 21% in 2018 across Mongolia's grazing areas. At the same time, livestock reduced NPP by about 9% on average. Model-estimated potential livestock densities were broadly consistent with established methods, demonstrating the approach's potential for application. Reported livestock densities exceeded model-estimated potential densities in 33% of grazing areas in 2019, an estimate subject to substantial uncertainty in desert and desert steppe, where NPP may be underestimated or satellite reference data are lacking. Applied with future climate projections, this method can help policymakers and land managers maintain the ecological balance and productivity of Eurasian grasslands under future climate and grazing scenarios.

title: Occurrence, characteristics, and multiple ecological risks of microplastics in surface water-sediment system of the Yangtze River basin, China
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution poses a significant threat to large river basins, yet a systematic assessment within the water-sediment system of the Yangtze River Basin (YRB) has been lacking. This work systematically analyzed and assessed the occurrence, distribution, and risks of MPs across four media within the YRB based on synthesized published data, employing both deterministic index and uncertainty probability methods: river water (RSW), lake/reservoir water (LRSW), and their corresponding sediments (RS and LRS). The average abundance was 2203.17 items/m 3 in surface water and 437.04 items/kg in sediments, showing correlated yet spatially heterogeneous patterns, with the Chengdu section of the Minjiang River and lakes in the middle and lower reaches of the YRB identified as significant pollution zones. Dominant MPs were small-sized (75.56%), transparent (39.75%), fibrous (57.75%) particles composed mainly of PP (37.25%) and PE (23.75%). Correlation analyses between influencing factors and MPs characteristics revealed that human activities distinctly affected MPs characteristics in each medium. Deterministic ecological risk assessment (DERA) indicated low pollution load and potential risk, but high polymer hazards. In contrast, the probabilistic ecological risk assessment (PERA) indicated that the overall probability of ecological risk in the YRB is relatively low, with high-hazard polymers contributing significantly to MPs risks, while also reducing the uncertainty associated with the DERA. This study systematically and scientifically revealed the ecological risk status of MPs in the YRB, providing the scientific basis for targeted management measures.

title: A spatial pattern identification method for Forest fire risk based on multi-model weight fusion: A case study of Liangshan prefecture, Sichuan Province, China
abstract: Forest fire risk identification in mountainous regions is affected by strong spatial heterogeneity, nonlinear interactions among driving factors, and the difficulty of transforming regional risk results into practical prevention units. This study proposes a spatial pattern identification method for forest fire risk based on multi-model weight fusion, with Liangshan Prefecture, Sichuan Province, China, as the regional study area. Using 1165 historical forest fire records and multi-source environmental factors standardized at the prefecture scale, a Forest Fire Risk Identification Model (FFRIM) was constructed. Entropy-weighted TOPSIS was used to determine objective weights for basic indicators, Random Forest was introduced to evaluate the relative contribution of driving factor groups, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process was used to maintain the structural consistency and interpretability of the hierarchical weighting system. The prefecture-scale results were analyzed at grid, county, and village levels to reveal the spatial differentiation of forest fire risk in Liangshan Prefecture. The results show that fire risk is jointly influenced by drought duration, terrain variation, fuel conditions, and human fire-use activities. High-risk areas are more evident at the grid scale, while village-level aggregation reveals localized prevention units that may be obscured by county-level averages. Therefore, multi-scale expression is necessary for connecting regional risk identification with grassroots fire prevention. Muli County was further selected as a typical mountainous case area for prevention-oriented safety pattern analysis. Its selection was not based on the highest county-level average risk, but on its complex terrain, extensive forest resources, historical major fire events, and practical prevention needs. Importantly, the Muli County analysis was not a higher-precision downscaling of the prefecture-scale model. Because the available county-level environmental data differ from, and are not necessarily more precise than, the prefecture-scale data, this stage was designed to examine how regional risk identification results can be interpreted under different spatial scales, data precisions, and management objectives. Based on available county-scale data and forest sub-compartment management units, SOM clustering, spatial autocorrelation analysis, minimum-cost corridor extraction, and circuit theory were used to identify prevention function zones, risk corridors, vulnerable nodes, and key intervention areas. This study provides a regional-to-local framework that links forest fire risk identification with village-level prevention zoning and typical mountainous case interpretation. The framework offers a methodological reference for transforming forest fire risk assessment into spatially explicit prevention strategies under heterogeneous data conditions. • A regional-to-local framework was proposed for forest fire risk identification in mountainous regions. • FFRIM integrated entropy-weighted TOPSIS, Random Forest and AHP in a hierarchical weighting system. • Forest fire risk was evaluated across grid, county and village management scales in Liangshan Prefecture. • Muli County was used to interpret prevention-oriented safety patterns under heterogeneous data conditions. • SOM, spatial autocorrelation and circuit theory supported functional zoning and prevention connectivity diagnosis.

title: Threshold-governed nonlinearities and configurational interactions of development activities on cultural landscape resilience in karst traditional villages
abstract: In mountainous regions, traditional villages face deepening tensions between cultural landscape conservation and economic development. Various development activities' impacts on Cultural Landscape Resilience (CLR) exhibit complex nonlinearities and uncharted configurational effects. This study examines 636 village-year observations from 106 karst traditional villages in Southwest China (2020–2025), using gradient boosting regression trees and configurational analysis. Results demonstrate threshold-governed nonlinearities in individual activities: tourism investment, infrastructure improvement, road expansion, public service facilities investment, and agricultural facilities investment emerge as high-importance predictors, following four distinct patterns, optimal-intensity saturation, dual-critical-point transition, discrete-threshold activation, and path-dependent lock-in. For combinational effects, tourism and infrastructure investments serve as primary interaction hubs, capable of forming strong interactions with multiple development activities and influencing CLR. Moderate-intensity configurations (M-M, M-L, L-M) generate positive CLR outcomes through synergistic mechanisms, whereas extreme configurations ( L − L , H − L , L − H ) produce antagonistic effects. These findings advance a precision governance framework grounded in dynamic intensity thresholds and evidence-based synergy strategies.

title: Quantifying driving mechanisms and spatial optimization of water supply-demand dynamics in humid subtropical regions: Evidence from a typical hilly region of southern China (1996–2023)
abstract: Humid regions, traditionally regarded as relatively water-abundant, are increasingly facing localized water scarcity and spatial mismatches between water supply and demand under the combined pressures of rapid urbanization, industrial agglomeration, and climate change. This study focused on Jiangxi Province, a representative humid subtropical region in China. We developed an integrated analytical framework by coupling the InVEST model, bivariate spatial autocorrelation analysis, and XGBoost-SHAP interpretable machine learning. This framework was used to systematically examine the spatiotemporal dynamics of regional water supply (WS) and water demand (WD) from 1996 to 2023, identify spatial clustering patterns, quantify key influencing factors and their spatially heterogeneous model-based contributions, and delineate differentiated water-resource management zones. The results showed that: (1) Jiangxi Province generally remained in a water-surplus condition during 1996–2023, with a mean water security index (WSI) of 0.36; however, WD increased by 21.57%, far exceeding the increase in WS of 2.21%. The spatial distributions of regional water supply and demand exhibited a relatively stable pattern characterized by long-term supply–demand surplus in mountainous areas and intensifying imbalance in the northern plain. (2) based on a two-dimensional zoning framework integrating WSI surplus–deficit status and spatial clustering patterns, the study area was divided into five functional zones, and corresponding management strategies were proposed for each zone. (3) gross domestic product (GDP) and precipitation (PRE) were the most important contributing factors associated with WSI. The negative contribution of GDP was most pronounced in the urban agglomerations of the northern plain, whereas the positive contributions of PRE, slope, and plant available water content (PAWC) were concentrated in the eastern and southern mountainous areas, highlighting the spatially heterogeneous associations of natural endowments and human activities with WSI. This study provides a transferable methodological reference for identifying water supply–demand mismatches, diagnosing WSI, formulating differentiated management strategies, and the understanding of driving mechanisms in humid subtropical regions

title: Life-history type-based functional indicators mediate avian community responses to airport-associated disturbance gradients
abstract: Anthropogenic environmental changes can reshape animal spatial distribution at both species and community levels, yet how individual behavioral responses scale up to influence community-level succession remains unclear. To address this question, we propose the “disturbance gradient filtering” hypothesis, which posits that anthropogenic disturbance gradients act as an ecological filter for species with distinct life-history types, and test it using avian community data around three airports (Zhongchuan, Lintao, and Wuwei) with different bird repellency histories and frequencies. Two conventional diversity indices (Shannon and Simpson) and one life-history type-based index (AWM_PC1, abundance-weighted mean position of the first principal component of life-history traits along the fast-slow continuum) were calculated and regressed against the distance from airport across different airports and habitat types.
