To address these limitations, we developed a modified remote sensing ecological index (MRSEI) specifically tailored to the RRB. The MRSEI integrates the Soil-adjusted vegetation index (SAVI) and desertification monitoring index (DMI) to mitigate background radiation and capture surface sand exposure. Using Landsat time-series imagery from 2000 to 2025, combined with Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall trends tests, and OPGD, we quantified the long-term evolution of EEQ and analyzed its spatial coupling with 131 national-level traditional villages in the basin. Our results reveal three main findings. First, EEQ followed a V-shaped evolution trajectory, with the mean MRSEI declining from 0.45 (2000) to 0.42 (2010) before recovering to 0.58 (2025). driven by the transition from intensive agricultural expansion to ecological restoration policies. Second, we observed a significant spatial coupling exists between high-density village clusters and superior ecological zones (MRSEI >0.6), supporting the concept of “habitat-optimized” site selection rooted in traditional ecological knowledge. Third, natural factors, specifically slope and precipitation (q > 0.3), defined the ecological baseline, whereas the synergistic interaction between urbanization and gross domestic product (GDP; q = 0.43) emerged as the dominant anthropogenic stressor. Collectively, these findings clarify the biophysical basis of vernacular settlement adaptation and offer a quantitative framework for the integrated preservation of ecological security and cultural heritage in complex river systems worldwide.

title: Accounting for noise improves the generalization of acoustic indices when estimating biodiversity
abstract: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) is increasingly adopted as a tool for monitoring biodiversity, as the availability of cheap long-term recorders now allows us to collect acoustical recordings over extended temporal and spatial gradients. The use of PAM for estimating biodiversity often requires the use of acoustic indices that summarize the acoustic properties of the recordings. Although acoustic indices have been shown to successfully track biodiversity in limited contexts, the recurrent failure of acoustic indices generalization across domains has raised doubts regarding the reliability and scalability of PAM. Variation across ecological communities is often cited as a principal limit to the generalizability of acoustic indices-based biodiversity estimation, while background environmental noise variability is often overlooked. Background noise can change between recordings because of environmental (e.g., wind) and system (e.g., microphone) differences that make noise equalization across studies difficult. In this study, we use both synthetic soundscapes and field recordings to assess the effects of background noise on acoustic index generalization. We reveal a dramatic effect of background noise on the ability of acoustic indices to generalize biodiversity estimates across datasets. We demonstrate that careful selection of noise-invariant acoustic indices, accounting for the signal-to-noise ratio, training across noise types and segmentation of the recordings all improve acoustic index-based biodiversity generalization. We also demonstrate the potential use of acoustic simulation training for acoustic index-based biodiversity estimations and generalization. We conclude that acoustic indices extracted from PAM have untapped potential as a simple and cost-effective biodiversity monitoring tool and highlight several possibilities for mitigating background noise variability during training to improve generalization.

title: Interactive effects of precipitation, temperature, and grazing pressure on the net ecosystem carbon balance of grazing lands across the continental United States
abstract: Grazing lands cover approximately one-third of the contiguous United States, support much of the nation's beef production, and are an important component of the U.S. terrestrial carbon budget. In this study, we quantified net ecosystem carbon balance ( NECB ), the net status of grazing lands as a carbon sink (C-sink) or source (C-source) and a key determinant of soil health and productivity. Our primary objective was to synthesize multiple years of annual NECB across heterogeneous grazing lands across the continental U.S and evaluate annual NECB against physical drivers (mean annual precipitation ( MAP ), mean annual temperature ( MAT ), vegetation, and moisture condition) and management practices (grazing pressure index ( GPI ) and fertilization history). We hypothesized that (1) NECB is higher in mesic and fertilized grasslands; (2) NECB increases with MAP and MAT but decreases with GPI ; and (3) interactive effects exist among MAP , MAT , and GPI . Using carbon fluxes measured by eddy covariance towers and methane emissions including both enteric methane and manure derived from stocking rates across seven USDA Long-term Agroecosystem Research Network sites, we found: (1) grazing lands were a C-sink or carbon neutral at most sites; (2) vegetation type, moisture conditions, or fertilization had no significant effect on NECB ; (3) NECB increased with MAP and MAT, but decreased with a higher GPI ; and (4) MAT had a significant positive effect on NECB when MAP exceeded 750 mm (greater water availability). The effect of GPI on NECB was significantly negative when MAP was below 1000 mm, significantly negative when MAT < 12 °C and significantly positive when MAT > 16 °C. Thus, most grazing lands in our study acted as C-sinks unless water deficit, low temperature, or heavy grazing were interactively present. Understanding how climate and management influence NECB of grazing lands is key to maintaining resilient agroecosystems that secure beef production and sustain rural prosperity.

title: Response characteristics and threshold identification of desert steppe degradation to multiscalar drought in Yinshanbeilu
abstract: Under ongoing climate change, drought-induced grassland degradation has become a major threat to dryland ecosystem stability. However, the nonlinear response of grassland degradation to drought across different temporal scales and the associated ecological thresholds remain insufficiently quantified. Taking the Yinshanbeilu desert steppe of Inner Mongolia as a case study, we integrated long-term remote-sensing and meteorological data from 1985 to 2024 to construct a Grassland Degradation Index (GDI) and multi-scale Standardized Precipitation Indices (SPI). Generalized Additive Models and piecewise regression were used to identify scale-dependent drought responses and critical thresholds. The results showed that six-month cumulative drought was the dominant climatic driver of degradation, explaining 67.4% of the variation in GDI, which was higher than the explanatory power of one-, three-, and twelve-month drought indices. Threshold analysis identified an early-warning threshold of approximately −0.26 to −0.28 and a degradation-acceleration threshold of −0.42 for SPI-6. A reverse GDI threshold of 0.51 indicated a transition from a drought-resistant to a drought-promoting state. Recovery showed strong hysteresis, as highly improved grassland required much wetter conditions, with SPI-6 values ranging from 1.0 to 2.2. These findings demonstrate that the coupled degradation–drought threshold framework can serve as an ecological indicator for detecting early-warning signals, identifying tipping points, and guiding adaptive restoration in arid and semi-arid grasslands.

title: Urbanization and afforestation are associated with competing carbon stock dynamics in Xiong ’an New Area: A decade of evidence from multi-temporal land cover mapping
abstract: The temporal sequence of annual land-cover change and carbon storage is a useful ecological indicator for tracking carbon-sink function in rapidly urbanizing areas. Existing studies, however, rely on medium- to low-resolution products and static single-date estimates, which cannot capture how carbon-sink function evolves over time. The period during which newly planted trees are spectrally hard to distinguish overlaps with the early stage of carbon accumulation, so misclassification can systematically underestimate carbon-sink areas. Xiong’an New Area, where rapid urbanization and large-scale afforestation occur together, is a suitable case for studying this problem. We propose TS-Carbon-Framework, which combines a three-frame semantic segmentation network (TriFuseNet), the InVEST carbon-storage model, and error-propagation analysis into a processing chain that turns multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery into annual carbon-storage indicators. TriFuseNet separates newly planted vegetation from cropland using the cumulative spectral difference between a historical frame taken before planting and the current frame. On the 8-class segmentation dataset for Xiong’an New Area, the mIoU reached 45.33%, 2.44 percentage points higher than the best comparison method, and the Trees IoU reached 35.21%, 6.99 percentage points higher than the best single-frame comparison method (SegFormer-B4). Total carbon storage ranged from 1.938 × 1 0 7 to 2.658 × 1 0 7 Mg C. The systematic bias of TriFuseNet was − 2.43 % , and after correction the carbon storage of the Trees class was 10.32% higher than the pixel-count estimate. This updatable indicator system can serve as a reference for regional ecological monitoring and carbon-sink management.

title: Impacts of snow cover on net primary productivity across Forest–grassland ecological zones: Hydrothermal and Phenological pathways in the greater Khingan range
abstract: Against the backdrop of climate change, variations in snow processes in cold temperate ecotones and the mechanisms by which they affect vegetation productivity remain insufficiently understood. Taking the western slope of the Greater Khingan Range in Inner Mongolia as the study area, this study integrates multi-source remote sensing and reanalysis data for the 2000–2024 hydrological years. Using trend analysis, correlation and partial correlation analyses, lagged correlation analysis, and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), we systematically investigate the response of vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) to snow cover changes across forest, forest–grassland ecotone, and grassland zones, as well as the underlying spring hydrothermal and phenological mechanisms. The results showed that: (1) during the study period, the cumulative number of effective snow-covered days in the study area generally decreased, with snow cover days (SCD) declining at a rate of −0.40 d yr −1 . The snow onset date advanced overall, whereas changes in the snow end date were relatively weak. Meanwhile, NPP exhibited pronounced seasonal differentiation: in spring, areas with increasing NPP dominated, accounting for 95.5% of the total study area; in summer, areas with decreasing NPP predominated, accounting for 78.8%. These findings indicate a clear stage-specific pattern in vegetation productivity dynamics across the study area. (2) The snow–NPP relationships exhibited ecological-zone-dependent and cross-seasonal patterns. In the forest zone, a later snow cover melt date and a longer snow cover duration were closely associated with reduced spring NPP, with correlation coefficients of −0.59 between SCM and spring NPP and − 0.50 between SCD and spring NPP. In the grassland zone, antecedent snow accumulation was positively associated with subsequent productivity, with spring SWE showing correlation coefficients of 0.24 and 0.19 with summer NPP and growing-season NPP, respectively. (3) The PLS-SEM results indicated that the direct association between snow cover and NPP was relatively weak, and that snow-related effects were mainly reflected through potential pathways involving spring soil hydrothermal conditions and NDVI-derived monthly-scale phenological indicators. Across the three ecological zones, the path coefficients from snow cover to spring soil moisture ranged from 0.15 to 0.57, while those to soil temperature ranged from −0.31 to −0.50, indicating that snow cover was associated with both water-retention and cooling effects. Specifically, in the grassland zone, the dominant pathway was the positive snow cover–soil moisture–NPP linkage, whereas in the forest zone and the forest–grassland ecotone, snow-related cooling was more closely associated with monthly-scale phenological indicators and reduced early-season productivity. Overall, the snow–NPP relationships in the ecotonal region on the western slope of the Greater Khingan Range exhibited ecological-zone-dependent patterns, reflecting differences among ecosystems in the relative importance of thermal limitation and snowmelt water supply.

title: Vegetation resilience to compound drought and heatwave events in China: Spatiotemporal patterns, drivers, and future risk
abstract: Compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events are intensifying under global warming and pose growing threats to the stability of terrestrial ecosystems. However, vegetation resilience to CDHWs, its underlying drivers, and its future trajectory remain poorly understood across China. Here, we developed a Standardized Compound Drought and Heatwave Index (SCDHI) by coupling the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) and Standardized Temperature Index (STI), identified CDHW events using run theory, and quantified resistance and recovery of eight vegetation types based on MOD17A2H gross primary productivity (GPP). We then used an interpretable XGBoost-SHAP framework to identify dominant drivers and projected future resilience risk under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5 using bias-corrected CMIP6 data. Since the beginning of the 21st century, CDHW intensity, severity, peak magnitude, frequency, and duration have all increased significantly across China. Resistance showed a pronounced east-high–west-low pattern controlled primarily by event-period maximum temperature, whereas recovery declined from south to north under post-event precipitation control. Resilience also differed substantially among vegetation types: forests were the most resilient, jointly maintaining high resistance and recovery, while shrubland, grassland, and cultivated vegetation were intermediate, and alpine and desert vegetation were the least. Historically, resistance remained broadly stable, whereas recovery declined in most vegetation types. In contrast, future projections indicate widespread declines in resistance, while recovery remains stable or increases slightly. Resistance declines most sharply in the western interior, the principal future vulnerability region. Together, these findings show that the dominant dimension of resilience loss shifts over time, calling for region-specific adaptation pathways under intensifying climate change.

title: Identifying spatio-temporal changes and driving factors of the water-ecology-economy system resilience in the water-receiving area of the Lower Yellow River
abstract: Enhancing the resilience of water-ecology-economy system (WEES) and clarifying improvement pathways are essential for achieving ecological conservation and high-quality development of the Yellow River Basin. Taking 23 cities in the water-receiving area of the Lower Yellow River (LYR) as the research subject, we constructed a WEES resilience evaluation indicator system. The resilience development index (RDI) was assessed utilizing a three-dimensional space vector model. Kernel density estimation and Moran's I methods were employed to explore its spatio-temporal evolution characteristics and spatial correlation levels. Furthermore, social network analysis (SNA) was applied to reveal the interactive relationships among various influencing factors. The results showed that (1) the resilience of the water-receiving area of the LYR exhibited a fluctuating upward trend, with the RDI increased from 0.57 to 0.66. The adaptation dimension presented high resilience levels, ranging from 0.52 to 0.58. Cities with high RDI are primarily clustered within Shandong Province, such as Jinan, Dongying, Tai'an, etc. (2) The overall resilience of the water-receiving area of the LYR exhibited a "main peak shifts to the right" pattern, with rising peak values and gradually narrowing disparities. Regional differences in WEES resilience levels were progressively diminishing year by year. (3) The resilience of WEES in the water-receiving area of the LYR exhibited positive spatial correlation and localized spatial auto-correlation. (4) The water system is the primary factor hindering the WEES resilience in the water-receiving area of the LYR. Key factors include matching coefficient of water and GDP (C27), water resources utilization rate (C25), matching coefficient of water and land (C28), and per capita GDP (C9). In light of the limited water diversion from the Yellow River, local governments ought to place greater emphasis on enhancing water use efficiency. This study provides decision-making references for regional sustainable development.

title: Trophic state modulates congruence between metabarcoding and microscopy in freshwater biomonitoring
abstract: Phytoplankton communities are key indicators of ecosystem health, yet routine monitoring, which relies on the observation of morphology and pigments under light microscopy, requires taxonomic expertise and is resource intensive and taxonomically limited. Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding offers a scalable alternative, but its performance relative to microscopy across trophic gradients remains poorly studied. Here, we combined a full-length 18S and 16S rRNA metabarcoding with light microscopy to characterize microbial communities across a broad trophic gradient in Chautauqua Lake over two sampling seasons. Both approaches were congruent in the taxa they detected, but metabarcoding consistently recovered higher diversity, particularly under hypereutrophic conditions when microscopy's diversity rapidly saturated. While microscopy and 16S rRNA diversity followed a unimodal pattern along the trophic gradient, 18S rRNA richness continued to increase even under intense cyanobacterial blooms. Metabarcoding also revealed diverse microeukaryotes and prokaryotic groups, absent or underrepresented from microscopy observations. Together, these results indicate that no single method is sufficient on its own: microscopy remains necessary for biomass and biovolume metrics, 16S rRNA improves detection of cyanobacterial and bacterial community gradients, and 18S rRNA expands microeukaryotic coverage, particularly under bloom conditions. These patterns indicate that long read sequencing is a promising complement to light microscopy for characterizing microbial communities across trophic gradients driven by decreasing costs, expanding reference databases, improved taxonomic resolution, and simplified bioinformatic workflows. However, integrating this platform into routine or statutory monitoring programs will require further calibration.

title: Engineered freshwater flows promote fish reproduction and stock recovery in the estuarine ecosystem
abstract: Freshwater inflow to estuaries is essential for regulating key biological processes and sustaining critical ecological functions. However, under combined pressures from climate change and anthropogenic activities, freshwater discharge frequently declines below the threshold required to maintain ecosystem health. Currently, the threshold at which river discharge into the sea affects biological production processes in estuaries is unclear; thus, accurate determination of the environmental flow requirements for maintaining estuarine ecosystem health is not possible. This research examines the effects of varying spring freshwater discharge on fish spawning and fishery recovery based on long-term field observations in the Yellow River Estuary (YRE), China. The results revealed a significant positive correlation between spring streamflow and fish egg abundance, while fishery stocks sharply increased within a certain range of spring discharge. From a biological resource perspective, the environmental flow required for the estuarine ecosystem during critical periods was determined at 3.5 billion cubic meters in spring for the YRE. This study advances a transferable framework for temperate estuarine management that illustrates how regulated inflow from large-scale engineering can sustain fisheries and promote ecosystem health, offering a scientific basis for integrated water and ecosystem management globally.

title: Designing resilient ecological networks through topological redundancy in the Sichuan–Yunnan Ecological Barrier Zone
abstract: Ecological barrier zones are increasingly threatened by habitat fragmentation, climate change, and human disturbance. Designing ecological networks that remain functional under disturbance requires the identification of ecological sources and corridors and the optimization of network topology and redundancy. Here, we developed a resilience-oriented ecological security framework for the Sichuan–Yunnan Ecological Barrier Zone by integrating morphological spatial pattern analysis, the minimum cumulative resistance model, circuit theory, and complex network analysis. Using data-driven thresholds, we identified 28 ecological sources totaling 50,919 km 2 , equivalent to 21.51% of the study area, and 93 baseline corridors. The baseline network exhibited dense southern connectivity, a central longitudinal axis, and relatively sparse northern links. Adding 35 cost-constrained corridors increased the number of edges from 93 to 128, equivalent to an edge-count increase of 37.6%. The optimized network reduced the Gini coefficient of composite node importance from 0.381 to 0.249 and maximum node importance from 1.609 to 1.243, while increasing global efficiency from 0.536 to 0.613. Under random node removal, mean relative largest-connected-component size and global efficiency increased by approximately 6.2% and 25.6%, respectively. Under targeted removal, the slope of relative global efficiency over the 0–30% node-removal interval changed from −1.25 to −0.27, and relative efficiency at 30% node loss increased from 60.7% to 90.7%. At 50% targeted node removal, the optimized network retained twice the relative largest-connected-component size of the baseline network, with values of 0.50 and 0.25, respectively. These results show that topology-based corridor optimization can enhance ecological network resilience by increasing alternative pathways and reducing composite hub dependence. The framework provides a quantitative basis for conservation prioritization and spatial planning in complex mountainous ecological barrier zones.

title: Evolution of water pattern in Chagan Lake Basin from 2017 to 2025 using PlanetScope images and a newly developed MS-FCN8s algorithm
abstract: As a typical lake group in Northeast China, the Chagan Lake Basin's water dynamics are crucial for regional water security and ecological protection. High-resolution images have limited spectral information, water indices perform poorly in complex backgrounds, and deep learning models often blur boundaries or miss detections. To solve these problems, this study aims to build a new MS-FCN8s model using PlanetScope images and reveals the basin's spatiotemporal water pattern evolution. Results indicate that MS-FCN8s algorithm can integrate multi-band reflectance and water indices, showing stable and accurate extraction, with overall accuracy (OA) about 2.8% higher than traditional FCN. In addition, it outperforms U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and TransUNet in detecting small water bodies and preserving boundaries. Moreover, water body changes in the Chagan Lake Basin (2017–2025) showed a total area increased by 17.14%, indicating sustained hydrological expansion. Spatially, the pattern shifted decisively from fragmented, isolated patches to a centralized, hydrologically connected system anchored by Chagan Lake. Area growth was overwhelmingly driven by large water bodies (>1 km 2 ), whereas small water bodies (<0.1 km 2 ), though numerically dominant, contributed less than 3.5% to the total areal gain.

title: Bridging field surveys and expert consensus: a delphi approach to developing site-specific KPIs for estuary restoration
abstract: Measuring the success of a nature conservation project, especially one involving multiple habitats and species, requires selecting effective Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). This study is part of the EU REST-COAST estuary restoration initiative, which includes nine pilot projects aimed at developing a precise, repeatable methodology for large-scale coastal restoration. In Israel, the Dalia Stream, a degraded estuarine system on the Mediterranean coast, was chosen as a pilot site for ecological restoration actions focused on two aquatic nature reserves located within the site. The aim is to rehabilitate these reserves, which have been affected by commercial fisheries, and to restore their ecological and hydrological connectivity to the sea. To evaluate project success, we used the Delphi method, a structured expert-consensus approach that integrated field survey data with professional insights to develop actionable KPIs. The process produced ten KPIs aligned with the project's ecological goals. Uniquely, the same experts who conducted field surveys also participated in the Delphi rounds, ensuring strong continuity between empirical data and expert judgment. This design enabled rapid consensus, whereas previous unstructured discussions had failed to achieve it. We recommend adopting this integrated field–Delphi approach in similar initiatives to improve transparency, comparability, and efficiency in evaluating ecological success.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and response quantification of agricultural carbon dynamics and non-point source pollution in Guangdong Province, China
abstract: In the context of global climate governance, agricultural non-point source pollution (ANPSP) and carbon dynamics (CD) are major challenges to agricultural sustainability, particularly in rapidly urbanizing coastal regions worldwide. This study used geographic information system, structural equation model, and SHapley Additive exPlanations to investigate the spatiotemporal heterogeneity and response quantification of ANPSP and CD in Guangdong Province from 1994 to 2023. The results indicated that (1) total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), and chemical oxygen demand (COD) declined stepwise overall, and the relationship between carbon emissions (CE) and carbon uptake (CU) was complex. The hot spots of ANPSP became increasingly concentrated in southwestern Guangdong. (2) Livestock production (LP) showed the strongest associations with TN, TP, and COD. The FAR, CP, and LP had potential indirect pathways. CU was significantly negatively associated with CE. (3) LP features accounted for the largest contribution across ANPSP, with goat husbandry accounting for 17.75%, 38.73%, and 40.61% in TN, TP, and COD, respectively. FAR accounted for the largest contribution to CE (62.68%), while rice (44.77%) and sugarcane (31.11%) accounted for the largest contributions to CU. These results could provide scientific support for quantitative characterization of ANPSP and CD in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

title: Combining citizen-science data with data from a structured monitoring programme for a Swiss butterfly index
abstract: Reliable biodiversity indicators are essential for informed conservation decisions, yet obtaining comprehensive data remains a significant challenge. While structured monitoring programs are considered the gold standard to estimate unbiased species trends, they are resource-intensive and often miss rare species. Conversely, unstructured citizen-science data provide vast spatial and temporal coverage but may be subject to systematic reporting biases. Using adapted site-occupancy models, we were able to estimate reliable temporal trends from the unstructured records of a national faunistic database, which strongly correlated ( r = 0.85 across species) with the trends estimated from the structured data of the Swiss Biodiversity Monitoring (BDM). The multi-species index (MSI) based on the trends of 179 species exhibited a slight decline contrasting with the increasing species richness that was reported using the BDM data. This discrepancy likely occurred because the MSI effectively captured substantial losses in specialized groups—such as cold-adapted and oligotrophic habitat species—whereas species richness was influenced by the rise of few common species. These findings highlight that both datasets complement each other, the structured monitoring data are central to calibrate the Index whereas the unstructured data extend species coverage by reaching out rarer species. The integration of both datasets into one national index facilitates a more representative national index that covers a broader taxonomic range than traditional indicators alone. Such integrated indicators are vital for evaluating biodiversity policies and capturing the complex responses of species communities to environmental change.

title: Capturing microclimates: 30-m downscaled climate dataset reveals fine-scale suitability patterns of invasive pests in karst landscapes
abstract: Karst landscapes are characterized by extreme topographic heterogeneity, which limits the capacity of conventional coarse-resolution climate data to resolve local microclimates, thereby introducing uncertainty into biological invasion risk assessments. This study developed a high-resolution climate downscaling framework integrating dynamic temperature lapse rates and error correction to reconstruct a 30-m climate dataset for the Southwest China Karst. Using both the downscaled 30-m dataset and the original 1-km dataset, optimized MaxEnt models were applied to predict the potential distributions of two invasive pests, Bactrocera dorsalis and Tuta absoluta . The downscaling framework outperformed conventional interpolation, improving accuracy for maximum temperature, minimum temperature, and precipitation by 12.5% (R 2 = 0.984), 15.1% (R 2 = 0.989), and 4.4% (R 2 = 0.918), respectively. The optimized MaxEnt models showed stable discriminatory performance for both species, with final training AUC values of 0.803–0.835 and ENMeval cross-validated validation AUC values of 0.778–0.809. Relative to the 30-m model, the 1-km model showed broader suitability patterns on steep valley walls for B. dorsalis and expansive basin floors for T. absoluta due to spatial averaging. At the 30-m scale, B. dorsalis exhibited dendritic distributions along dry–hot karst river valleys, driven primarily by Annual Mean Temperature (37.2% contribution) and NDVI (23.9%). Conversely, T. absoluta displayed patchy distributions concentrated in flat plateau basins and depressions, associated with Annual Mean Temperature (27.9%) and Tree Canopy Density (23.5%). Differentiated management strategies are proposed, including linear interception at valley gateways for B. dorsalis and grid-based monitoring in flat agricultural zones for T. absoluta . These findings indicate that high-resolution climate data can refine the spatial interpretation of invasion risk in complex terrains and provide a more detailed spatial basis for precision pest management in karst ecosystems.

title: Deciphering riverine CODMn sources: driver identification and carbon cycle impacts
abstract: The large-scale monitoring of riverine organic pollution is of significant practical importance for river basin ecological management and sustainable development to replace the traditional monitoring stations. The development for remote sensing of riverine chemical oxygen demand (COD Mn ) has pressing demand as a low cost and high effective tool for addressing water quality degradation and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) estimation. In this study, we develop remote sensing monitoring models of COD Mn in individual rivers across China using Sentinel-2 images and national cross-section datasets. The performance of R 2 for main rivers in China with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithms could reach over 0.80. The retrieved average COD Mn from 2021 to 2023 were 3.70 mg/L, 3.53 mg/L and 3.33 mg/L respectively, and the COD Mn trends to be decreased significantly ( p < 0.05). The accumulation influences of precipitation to COD Mn in southern rivers was observed while the dilution effect to COD Mn was shown in northern rivers. Areas where crop land and impervious cover are the dominant land types have significantly higher COD Mn for all rivers. Also, the increase in the number of industrial parks did not lead to an increase in riverine COD Mn . With the relationship of COD Mn and DOC, the total DOC flux from river to sea was ranged from 3.71 to 6.30 Tg C. By bridging remote sensing innovation with water quality parameter of COD Mn in rivers, this research advances sustainable river management and carbon cycle strategies.

title: Evolution of water clarity across the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region over the past four decades (1984–2024): Driven by hydrological expansion and anthropogenic intervention
abstract: Given escalating water scarcity and rapid urbanization, characterizing the long-term evolution of surface water environments across the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region is vital for coordinated regional development. Using Landsat imagery spanning 1984–2024, this study quantified Secchi disk depth ( Zsd ) dynamics in 1105 water bodies across the BTH region and identified the dominant drivers through correlation analysis and generalized linear models (GLMs). Results show that water bodies in the BTH region are predominantly small (1.33 ± 10.32 km 2 ) and characterized by a generally low baseline water clarity (mean Zsd = 0.62 ± 0.22 m). Nevertheless, a pervasive long-term clearing trend was detected: 60.0% of water bodies ( N = 663) exhibited significant increases in water clarity over the past four decades, whereas only 4.2% ( N = 46) showed significant declines ( P < 0.05). GLM analysis revealed that water area expansion was the primary driver of Zsd variability, consistently explaining more than 45% of the long-term variations. This expansion was closely linked to precipitation variability in Hebei Province, while in Beijing and Tianjin it was primarily driven by the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. Land-cover transitions acted as secondary drivers, accounting for 27.2% of the observed variance, whereby reductions in barren land and increases in impervious surfaces together with strengthened environmental governance, effectively mitigated sediment loading. In contrast, intensive cropland in certain regions, particularly Hebei, may still exert a localized influence, where agricultural runoff can partially limit improvements in water clarity. Overall, these findings suggest that strategic water diversion and ecological restoration have been associated with improvements in regional surface water quality, while localized agricultural pressures require more targeted management interventions. This study provides new insights into how both natural and anthropogenic drivers interact to shape long-term water clarity dynamics in this highly water-stressed region and offers a robust scientific basis for informed water resource and land-cover management, and sustainable regional development.

title: Coupling of human activity intensity and ecosystem health in Shaanxi: a state-process dual-dimensional evaluation
abstract: Intense human activities pose continuous threats to regional ecological security. However, current assessments of human-ecosystem interactions predominantly build upon static spatial correlations, which inherently fail to capture complex, nonlinear evolutionary trajectories. To fill this research gap, this study constructs an innovative dual-dimensional diagnostic framework named “State-Process”, integrating static and dynamic analytical paradigms. By coupling the Human Footprint Index with the Vigor-Organization-Resilience-Services (VORS) framework, we adopt the four-quadrant method and decoupling model to synthesize spatial mismatch and temporal response elasticity throughout the period 2002–2022. Taking Shaanxi Province as an ideal empirical testbed to validate this methodology, we found that both the ecosystem health index (EHI) and human activity intensity (HAI) rose over the past 20 years and generally exhibited an apparent synchronous upward trend. However, the application of our dual-dimensional approach indicates a potential risk of “pseudo-stable” ecological states, suggesting that seemingly positive short-term indicators might obscure underlying structural vulnerabilities associated with intense human disturbances. Furthermore, distinct regional differences were observed, and the grid scale showed greater sensitivity than the county scale in reflecting these mesoscale nonlinear fluctuations. Specifically, urban and suburban areas exhibited degradation in ecosystem health due to rapid urbanization, while rural areas maintained relatively higher ecological resilience. The heterogeneous changes across different geographical units collectively shape the overall spatial differentiation pattern of EHI, with an expanding trend in regional disparities. This dual-dimensional diagnostic framework establishes an integrated analytical pathway from spatial matching to process responses, more comprehensively revealing the decoupling pathways between human activities and ecological health. By identifying distinctive response characteristics across multiple geographical units, our multi-scale analysis proposes zoned management strategies. Ultimately, this study aims to characterize patterns of ecological security under anthropogenic disturbances, while offering an original theoretical perspective and scientific foundation for targeted regional ecological restoration worldwide.

title: Soil keystone phylotype diversity and plant diversity co-drive ecosystem stability in the Tibetan alpine grasslands
abstract: Soil multitrophic diversity and plant diversity are critical for ecosystem stability, yet their impacts remain poorly understood. Here, we performed an extensive survey across the Tibetan Plateau to examine the impacts of species pool size (γ-diversity), local richness (α-diversity), and species turnover (β-diversity) of soil multitrophic communities and plants on temporal ecosystem stability. Our results showed that the α-diversity of plants and cluster 2, together with the β-diversity of clusters 0 and 1, is positively associated with ecosystem stability. Notably, the stabilizing effect of α-diversity within cluster 2 increased with organism body size and trophic level, being most pronounced in nematodes and protistan consumers. Structural equation models showed that cluster 2 α-diversity and cluster 0 β-diversity enhanced ecosystem stability via direct or plant-mediated pathways. Collectively, this research elucidates the stability effects of above- and below-ground diversity at multiple spatial scales, underscoring the necessity of integrating soil keystone phylotypes and plant diversity into conservation management.

title: Mapping long-term irrigated cropland dynamics in the Yellow River Basin by integrating a nonlinear LST–NDVI feature space with precipitation constraints
abstract: Accurate mapping of actual irrigated cultivated land is essential for understanding the interactions between human agricultural activities and regional agricultural ecosystem, particularly in large basins with strong climatic and ecological heterogeneity. As a typical arid and semi-arid region, the Yellow River Basin (YRB) is facing prominent contradictions between agricultural water use and ecological conservation, making long-term irrigation monitoring a critical indicator of agricultural water use for assessing basin-scale agricultural health and sustainable development. This study developed a basin-scale framework for long-term irrigation monitoring in the YRB from 2002 to 2020 by improving the LST–NDVI feature space and integrating the Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) with precipitation constraints. Quadratic polynomial dry and wet edge equations were constructed for different climatic zones to better represent nonlinear LST–NDVI relationships. Moreover, TVDI derived from MODIS data was then combined with CHIRPS precipitation using a 7-day cumulative precipitation threshold to distinguish irrigation-induced wetting signals from rainfall-driven soil moisture anomalies. Compared with linear dry–wet edge fitting, the quadratic fitting achieved statistically significant improvement ( p < 0.01) in boundary estimation, with an average R 2 rise of 18.6% and overall R 2 above 0.7 across different climatic zones. The extracted irrigated area exhibited strong agreement with prefecture-level statistical records. Basin-wide irrigated area remained relatively stable during 2002–2022, fluctuating between approximately 6500 × 10 3 hm 2 and 7800 × 10 3 hm 2 , while moderate expansion occurred mainly in marginal upstream and midstream regions. The irrigated areas of the Hetao and Qingtongxia Irrigation Districts in the upstream both exhibited a significant, continuous upward trend over the past 20 years, with annual growth rates of 11.37 and 2.08 × 10 3 hm 2 , respectively. The irrigated area of the Weishan Irrigation District in the downstream displayed an upward trend with stronger interannual variability driven by precipitation fluctuations. The proposed framework provides a scalable and physically interpretable approach for long-term irrigation monitoring in large heterogeneous basins. It offers reliable technical support for agricultural water allocation and sustainable water resource management in ecologically fragile basins under climate change.

title: Standardized lake fish community assessment using modified multi-mesh gillnets to minimize fish mortality
abstract: Systems for assessing the ecological status of lakes with respect to fish population are normally based on catches using conventional European Committee for Standardization (CEN) gill nets. A modified gillnet (MOD) design with less small-mesh and more large-mesh panel area , developed to reduce catch and mortality while retaining the information needed for ecological assessment, was previously demonstrated in two large, deep peri-alpine lakes. The present work investigated its utility in smaller water bodies including two natural lakes, two reservoirs, and six excavated lakes, from 2018 through 2022. Compared to CEN nets, MOD nets reduced fish catch/mortality by 42.0 ± 15.94% (range 4.0%–59.4%). Sampling with MOD nets yielded results comparable to CEN nets with respect to number of species detected, community composition, and catch per unit of net area consistently across lakes and sampled years. The net types did not differ with regard to the length-specific catchability of key species. The MOD nets showed a higher rate of species accumulation in the artificial lakes. With respect to Water Framework Directive metrics, which is likely the most important application for ecological fish surveys in Europe, the net types yielded similar data, confirming the novel MOD net as an ecologically beneficial and economical alternative in fish community monitoring.

title: Network correlation characteristics and Core node identification of provincial water-energy-food-economy-ecology five-dimensional coupling coordination in China
abstract: Water, energy, and food constitute fundamental strategic resources for the survival and development of human society. Given the fundamental role of these resources, the water-energy-food nexus has attracted extensive research; however, the emergent spatial network properties of their multi-system coupling at the provincial level remain underexplored. This study moves beyond dimensional expansion to offer a methodological and governance-oriented contribution. We develop a five-dimensional Water-Energy-Food-Economy-Ecology (WEFEE) framework and, for the first time, apply Social Network Analysis (SNA) to the coupling coordination degree (CCD) of all 31 Chinese provinces (2016–2023), revealing the structural logic of inter-provincial synergistic networks. We further introduce a Minimum Administratively Meaningful Difference (MAMD) threshold of 0.004 to translate statistical CCD changes into actionable policy triggers, and classify provinces into four functional blocks according to their network roles: core coordination, secondary synergy, edge conduction, and isolated development. The results show that: (1) The composite indices of each subsystem exhibit a fluctuating upward trend, with water resources scoring highest and economy lowest, indicating distinct regional advantages. (2) Inter-provincial network density increased from 0.48 to 0.51 with no isolated provinces, yet efficiency slightly declined while hierarchy deepened, revealing a tightening but increasingly stratified structure. (3) Hebei emerged as the central hub (degree centrality 80.00), while Qinghai (20.00) and other northwestern provinces remained peripheral, indicating strong core-periphery dynamics. (4) The four functional blocks offer distinct governance logics, with core blocks optimizing cross-sectoral integration, secondary blocks strengthening transmission, edge blocks targeting resource reallocation, and isolated blocks requiring systemic rewiring instead of one-way transfers, providing a network-based diagnostic tool for precision governance of China's regional resource synergy.

title: Risk and resilience of indicator bird species under climate and land-cover change
abstract: Birds are widely recognised as indicators of ecological integrity due to their sensitivity to climate and habitat change. In Luxembourg, rising temperatures and intensified pressures from habitat loss and fragmentation threaten indicator species and their ecological roles. Substantial research exists on climate-driven range shifts. However, the combined influence of high-resolution land-cover constraints and spatially explicit conservation priority assessment remains insufficiently addressed. To address this gap, we modelled current and future ranges for six key bird species using an ensemble of machine-learning algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Support Vector Machine. Habitat predictions were refined using a 30-m species-specific land-cover mask. We then integrated projections for 2021–2040 and 2041–2060 under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5 with Luxembourg's protected-area network. These elements were combined into a normalised composite Conservation Priority Index (CPI). Using this framework, our projections reveal strong contractions in highly suitable habitat classes under SSP5–8.5: Lanius collurio , Oenanthe oenanthe , and Vanellus vanellus show major shifts toward very low suitability classes, while Ficedula hypoleuca and Accipiter gentilis exhibit substantial reductions in environmentally suitable area. In contrast, Lullula arborea shows comparatively lower losses (47.9%). While climatically stable habitats are better represented in protected areas, species dependent on non-forest habitats remain at risk. These disparities underscore the need for targeted conservation measures. These findings show that integrating high-resolution environmental data, land-cover filtering, and multi-criteria conservation priority assessment provides a robust basis for climate-smart conservation planning.

title: The risk of birds' functional diversity loss with climate change uncovered using deep learning hurdle models
abstract: Abstract Climate change and sea-level rise (SLR) pose increasing threats to coastal ecosystems and biodiversity in the Gulf of America. Most efforts to anticipate these threats focus on species counts or range shifts, while changes in species functional diversity remain uncovered. We estimated the impacts of climate change and sea-level rise on hundreds of bird species’ populations and corresponding shifts in functional diversity. We used the generative deep learning method, Variational Gaussian Mixture Autoencoder (GMVAE), and Trait Probability Density analysis to study such impacts. We found that a generative GMVAE model uncovered species’ unobserved ranges, and that climate change reduced coastal ecosystem resilience and caused biodiversity loss across multiple dimensions, including functional richness, redundancy, evenness, and divergence. Surprisingly, the most impacted areas are not the exposed shoreline but the landward coastal transition zones. Specifically, shoreline functional diversity turned out to increase with climate change and sea level rise, whereas uplands showed declining functional diversity and increasing redundancy, indicating contraction of functional trait space. Furthermore, avian biodiversity expanded in coastal protected areas, serving as refugia embedded in a surrounding landscape where unique combinations of species traits are lost.

title: eDNA metabarcoding provides scalable and continuous biodiversity monitoring across the tree of life
abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding has the potential to substantially expand our knowledge of global biodiversity beyond that provided by conventional approaches. However, the degree to which eDNA data provides real ecological insight, rather than primarily reflecting environmental factors that affect eDNA shedding and degradation, remains unclear. Additional uncertainties arise in terms of cost-effectiveness and whether the price is worth any extra biodiversity information that is gleaned. Here, we established a high-resolution, bi-weekly eDNA time-series in Germany across aquatic and riparian habitats to quantify seasonal biodiversity dynamics, to relate eDNA to different potential environmental drivers, and to parametrize cost estimates. Over one year, eDNA metabarcoding detected more than 1,000 species across multiple trophic levels and primarily revealed real, taxon-specific seasonal patterns, in addition to some relationships to water temperature, discharge, and conductivity. Compared to historical records dating back to 1891, year-round eDNA monitoring increased reported species numbers by 2.4-fold for invertebrates, 2.2-fold for mammals, 1.7-fold for diatoms, 1.2-fold for fish and lamprey, and 1.03-fold for birds. Cumulative biodiversity estimates increased strongly with sampling frequency, demonstrating the value of eDNA for high-frequency time-series monitoring. Moreover, eDNA monitoring was highly cost-effective, providing more than twice the biodiversity information of many conventional surveys for one-sixth the cost, enabling scalable, high-resolution freshwater biodiversity assessments.

title: A risk index for fecal contamination of irrigation water during drought
abstract: Groundwater is increasingly relied upon for irrigation water in semi-arid regions, where recurrent droughts and intensive abstraction have intensified pressure on both groundwater quantity and quality. This study developed a risk index for the contamination of groundwater used for irrigation during drought in the Berrechid Plain, Morocco, where irrigation depends almost entirely on groundwater. Groundwater fecal contamination was assessed using in situ tryptophan-like fluorescence (TLF) measurements collected at 84 sites during drought. To identify the dominant factors controlling TLF variability, 12 environmental variables describing contaminant propagation conditions and 5 source-related variables representing anthropogenic pressures were analyzed using principal component analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. Source-related variables structured TLF variability more clearly than environmental factors, with the first two source components explaining 66% of the variance, compared with 31% for the first two environmental components. Correlation and regression analyses identified PC_src1 as the main significant driver of TLF variability, indicating that TLF concentrations increased with proximity to industrial areas, livestock farms, and wastewater treatment plants. The regression model was significant (F = 4.20, p = 0.00398), with PC_src1 as the only significant predictor (β = −2.205, p = 0.001). The selected contamination-pressure gradient was combined with long-term irrigation intensity derived from remote sensing to generate the spatial risk index. Low, moderate, and high-risk areas covered 43%, 54%, and 4% of the aquifer, respectively. The continuous risk index was significantly correlated with measured TLF concentrations (Spearman ρ = 0.443; Pearson r = 0.469; p < 0.05). Unlike conventional vulnerability approaches, this TLF-based risk index integrates anthropogenic pressure and irrigation intensity, providing an operational ecological indicator for assessing irrigation-water contamination risk in drought-affected semi-arid aquifers.

title: Impacts of farmland trees on ecosystem services in intensive agricultural systems
abstract: Farmland trees, defined here as trees outside forests occurring within agricultural landscapes, provide critical ecosystem services in intensive agricultural landscapes, yet their regional distribution and ecological contributions remain poorly quantified because small, linear, and fragmented tree elements are difficult to map with conventional remote sensing. This study focuses on the intensively cultivated plains of Northeast China (∼469,000 km 2 ) and proposes a hierarchical classification framework integrating object-based segmentation and spatial semantics to produce a fine-scale map of farmland trees using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, and to assess their associations with ecosystem services. The framework first generates a vegetation mask based on time-series vegetation-frequency analysis, then performs vegetation-type classification at the object level, and finally refines the identification and separation of farmland trees embedded within forested areas by incorporating morphological features and their adjacency relationships with farmland. The method achieves an overall accuracy of 81% (Kappa = 0.62), estimating total farmland tree area at 2033.62 km 2 . Furthermore, segmented linear regression was used to quantify the nonlinear relationships between farmland-tree density and key ecosystem services. Water yield was positively associated with density up to about 30%, after which the increase weakened. Sandstorm prevention was positively associated with density up to approximately 40%, after which the increase accelerated. Soil retention showed no significant association below approximately 15% density and a declining tendency at higher density levels. Overall, this framework provides methodological support for scalable and interpretable mapping of farmland trees in large-scale, heterogeneous farmland landscapes, and by identifying density thresholds for service responses, it offers a scientific basis for sustainable land management balancing agricultural productivity and ecological benefit.

title: Spatiotemporal memory and nonlinear transitions in forest phenology–active layer relationships in the permafrost region of Northeast China
abstract: Permafrost degradation is closely associated with changes in high-latitude forest phenology, yet the spatial heterogeneity, temporal memory, and nonlinear form of these relationships remain poorly understood because of coarse spatial resolution, reliance on simple linear assumptions, and confounding by long-term climate warming. Focusing on the permafrost region of Northeast China, we integrated multi-source data, machine learning, and physical models to construct a 30-m-resolution dataset of forest phenology and active layer thickness (ALT) from 2000 to 2024. Utilizing detrending, time-lag, and piecewise regression analyses, we quantitatively characterized the spatially differentiated phenological relationships and nonlinear breakpoints related to ALT fluctuations. Over the past 25 years, regional ALT deepened significantly (0.13 cm/yr). Prior to detrending, this regional trend was accompanied by an earlier start of season (SOS, −0.17 days/yr) and an extended length of season (LOS, +0.16 days/yr). After detrending the ALT and phenological time series, the optimal lag-accumulation associations showed a clear north-south contrast. SOS was negatively associated with ALT variability in the northern discontinuous permafrost region but positively associated with it in the southern marginal zone. Phenology in the north was most strongly associated with multi-year cumulative ALT conditions, whereas that in the south was primarily linked to current-year variability. Separately, piecewise regression of mean-centered pixel-year anomalies identified metric-specific nonlinear breakpoints: Approximately 0.4 cm for SOS and LOS and − 0.1 cm for EOS. Across these breakpoints, the SOS–ALT slope shifted from −2.68 to +0.24 days/cm, while the LOS–ALT slope weakened from +2.78 to +0.87 days/cm. At higher ALT anomalies, continued LOS extension was increasingly associated with delayed EOS (+0.93 days/cm). These statistical relationships provide testable hypotheses for future carbon-sequestration assessments using process-based models and carbon-flux observations

title: Function evaluation and simulation optimization of production-living-ecological space in Fuzhou City, China: a multi-source data and multi-model coupling approach
abstract: Rapid urbanization and socioeconomic growth have unprecedentedly driven spatial restructuring and functional conflicts in territorial space. Fine-scale identification, functional assessment, and multi-scenario simulation of production-living-ecological space (PLES) are essential for territorial spatial governance and regional sustainability. In this study, by integrating remote sensing imagery and point-of-interest data, the spatiotemporal distribution of PLES types was mapped by a hierarchical identification strategy in Fuzhou city of China during 2012–2024. The PLES function was quantitatively evaluated using multi-source data and a comprehensive index system, with its driving mechanism examined via the GeoDetector model. Multi-scenario simulations of PLES future development were conducted by employing a coupled multi-model framework integrating artificial neural network (ANN), cellular automaton (CA), and multi-objective programming (MOP). The results indicated that the ecological-dominated space remained dominant and stable, occupying approximately 80% of the study area, while living space expanded significantly by 180.11 km 2 from 2012 to 2024. The comprehensive function of PLES increased by 5.42%, with living and production functions rising by 67.45% and 30.98%, respectively. The functional evolution of PLES was jointly driven by natural and socioeconomic factors, which interact through nonlinear or two-factor enhancement effects. By 2040, the living priority scenario would achieve maximal functional optimization, enhancing the PLES comprehensive function by 37.51% relative to the 2024 level. This study provides a replicable method for fine-scale PLES research and supports evidence-based spatial layout governance and quality-oriented sustainable development.

title: Dynamic local and tele-coupling of ecosystem services supply and demand: Implications for sustainable management zoning in a plateau urban agglomeration
abstract: Rapid urbanization intensifies ecosystem services (ES) supply-demand mismatches. However, traditional local static assessments fail to capture cross-regional flows and dynamic evolutionary trajectories. Focusing on the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration (CYUA), we constructed a “conceptualization-process-pattern-mechanism-management” research framework, integrating multi-source data (2003−2023) with a dynamic local and tele-coupling coordination degree (DLTCCD) model and spatial econometric models to evaluate ES spatiotemporal convergence, and employing the XGBoost-SHAP approach to reveal nonlinear driving mechanisms. Ultimately, we proposed a static-dynamic integrated management zoning strategy. The results indicate: (1) CYUA exhibited significant “local collapse and tele-coupling compensation” characteristics; remote spatial subsidies from peripheral areas effectively repaired global coordination despite local decoupling in polarized cores; (2) Despite an absolute β -convergence, extremely slow convergence rates forewarn of persistent long-term spatial disequilibrium; (3) The dominant driving logic transitioned from early natural constraints to nature-infrastructure-policy synergies; (4) Integrating static baselines with dynamic trajectories delineated six sustainable management zones. These findings provide quantitative evidence for local and tele-coupling mechanisms, offering a transferable reference and potential governance framework for complex plateau urban agglomerations.

title: A systematic review on the advancement of ecohydrological research in India over last two decades (2005–2024)
abstract: Ecohydrology is an interdisciplinary science that integrates ecological and hydrological processes to explain the regulation of vegetation, soil, and climate on water and carbon fluxes. Ecohydrological processes not only regulate water, carbon, and energy fluxes at the ecosystem level but also sustain hydrological services in downstream regions. Therefore, a systematic assessment of ecohydrological studies is essential for understanding the methodological advancement. This study reviews two decades (2005–2024) of peer-reviewed literature to understand the methodological evolution, spatial distribution and thematic orientation of ecohydrological studies in India. A structured bibliographic search was conducted using Boolean combinations of keywords across the Scopus and Google Scholar databases. The distribution of ecohydrological studies remains uneven across physiographic and agro-ecological regions. The analysis showed a strong regional concentration of studies in the Northern Plains (20.33%), Coastal Plains (13.96%), and Deccan Plateau (13.55%), accounting for 47.84% of the total literature, whereas the Western and Eastern Himalayas collectively contribute only 16.53%. Our analysis observed dominance of field-based studies compared to model-based studies during phase-I (2005–2014) of study period, however, the opposite is true for phase-II (2015–2019) and phase-III (2020–2024). Majority of field-based studies were carried out in crop field. Forest ecohydrology accounts for only 9.2% of total studies. Studies in the Indian Himalayan Region are also found to be sparse, i.e., covered only 19.29% of the total literature reviewed. Overall, this paper will provide an outlook towards recent developments in ecohydrology research and its spatial distribution across Indian subcontinent.

title: Interchangeability of structure-from-motion platforms in marine monitoring
abstract: Structure-from-Motion (SfM) photogrammetry has revolutionised marine monitoring, however rapid software evolution challenges long-term data continuity. Across longitudinal datasets, changing reconstruction software may introduce artificial variability into ecologically relevant indicators. Establishing the consistency of 3D structural complexity indices is essential for detecting subtle changes preceding ecosystem collapse, especially in the globally rare chalk reefs of the North Sea (UK), where habitat loss is irreversible. This study evaluates the methodological interchangeability, indicator reproducibility, and computational efficiency of two leading SfM platforms, Agisoft Metashape and 3DF Zephyr , using Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) imagery from the Cromer Shoal Chalk Beds. Three complexity metrics (rugosity, relief, and vector dispersion) were compared across five software configurations representing a gradient of computational effort. Macro-topographical indicators such as rugosity remained statistically identical across platforms (GLMM, p > 0.05), though micro-textural outputs such as vector dispersion were significantly more sensitive to software-specific algorithms. High-resolution configurations converged on statistically similar ecological values at vastly different computational costs. 3DF Zephyr exhibited greater mesh generation efficiency than Agisoft Metashape ( F 4,50 = 4.83, p = 0.002), whereas Agisoft Metashape at High setting generated significantly denser point-clouds than Zephyr Advanced ( F 4,50 = 31.27, p < 0.001) by an average of 3.8 × 10 7 points (Tukey HSD: p < 0.001). These findings demonstrate that broad-scale structural indicators remain robust to software and pipeline changes, ensuring long-term data continuity. Nonetheless, the observed shifts in micro-textural metrics may reflect software artefacts rather than genuine ecological decline, highlighting the need for strict parameter standardisation across multi-year monitoring objectives. For conservation programmes, this methodological consistency enables practical transitions between software platforms to optimise field time and processing budgets.

title: Comparative analysis of the factors explaining spatial patterns of net primary productivity across sandified and desertified areas in northwestern Liaoning, China
abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) is a key indicator of vegetation growth and is highly sensitive to environmental change, especially in ecologically fragile areas. Although many studies have explored the factors associated with NPP in degraded ecosystems, few have systematically identified the main variables associated with spatial patterns of NPP in coexisting sandified and desertified areas under the same regional background, or compared their relative importance and response patterns. To address this gap, we comparatively analyzed spatial patterns of NPP across sandified and desertified areas in northwestern Liaoning, China. Using multisource spatiotemporal datasets from 2016 to 2022 together with field soil sampling data, we organized the variables into four factors: soil, topographic, meteorological, and vegetation structural factors. Random Forest (RF), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Accumulated Local Effects (ALE) were used to identify the main variables associated with NPP in each degradation type and characterize their response patterns. The results showed that vegetation vertical structure was most strongly associated with spatial patterns of NPP in both areas, followed by elevation and surface moisture conditions. These shared variables differed mainly in response strength and range between the two degradation types, with stronger and broader responses in the desertified area. In addition, NPP in the sandified area was more strongly associated with moisture-related variables, whereas NPP in the desertified area was more strongly associated with temperature-related variables. Soil variables other than NDWI had relatively low explanatory power for spatial variation in NPP in both areas. These findings improve understanding of NPP patterns in different degradation types and provide a scientific basis for differentiated ecological restoration in northwestern Liaoning.

title: Cropland abandonment as an emerging indicator of food-production vulnerability: Insights from two decades of land-use trajectories
abstract: Cropland abandonment, driven by urbanization and demographic transitions, is a global land-use change. Although its driving factors, extent, and spatial patterns have been widely documented, spatially explicit and temporally continuous estimates of how abandonment translates into losses of food-production capacity remain scarce, particularly at the national scale. This study aims to develop a remote-sensing method for tracking identified abandonment within the 2001 baseline cropland cohort in mainland China and to systematically quantify its spatiotemporal characteristics as well as its impact on agricultural productivity. A remote-sensing identification approach using land-use trajectories was developed to track abandonment among cropland pixels spanning 2001 to 2020. These records were coupled with a baseline of potential grain production to quantify the impact of persistent cropland abandonment on agricultural productivity. Within the 2001 baseline cropland cohort, the annual area of confirmed abandonment ranged from 36,399.30 to 226,873.77 km 2 , equivalent to 3.64–22.69 Mha, with an average abandonment rate of 8.25%, showing a significant upward trend. Spatially, confirmed abandonment within the baseline cohort followed a gradient pattern of “low in the east, high in the west”, with notable clustering in ecologically fragile regions and traditional agricultural areas in the west. The loss of potential grain production associated with confirmed abandonment within the baseline cropland cohort fluctuated, rising from 10.08 million tons in 2004 to a peak of 67.60 million tons in 2018, with a long-term annual average loss of 5.24%, indicating that the long-term abandonment of existing cropland may damage China's food-production capacity and increase its food-system vulnerability. The identification method and quantitative findings of this study provide empirical evidence and methodological foundation for monitoring persistent cropland abandonment and supporting food security governance.

title: How to design measurable ecological flow in tidal river network?
abstract: This study develops a practical, monitorable ecological flow determination framework to resolve the critical limitation that traditional static flow standards fail to quantify actionable ecological flow under reciprocating stream–tide interactions in tidal river networks. Measurable ecological flow, defined as steady downstream discharge within a stable tidal window that supports direct field monitoring without averaging distortion, is proposed as a targeted regulatory indicator for deltaic watercourses. The Pearl River Delta (PRD), a globally typical complex tidal river network in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, is selected as the research domain. A coupled one-dimensional and two-dimensional hydrodynamic model is built to reconstruct high-temporal-resolution tidal daily flow processes using 50-year (1970–2019) upstream runoff series and offshore tidal boundary data, with model validation achieving Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values of 0.86–0.91 for discharge and 0.85–0.93 for water level. An improved phase-aware dynamic time warping (PDTW) algorithm integrated with hierarchical clustering analysis (HCA) is adopted to classify full-channel tidal flow regimes based on section-specific phase weights derived from tidal phase duration and average discharge. A two-level finite difference method is further applied to identify stable measurable windows by extracting local minima of second-order flow curvature around tidal extrema. Combined with multi-year hydrological frequency analysis at the 90% design guarantee rate, monitorable ecological flow thresholds are quantified for each river section. The results reveal distinct spatial differentiation of tidal daily flow patterns across the PRD, which are grouped into four representative types (I–IV). Type I upstream channels maintain nearly unidirectional stable flow, while Type IV estuarine reaches feature extreme tidal asymmetry; the middle-network Type II and III channels exhibit obvious downstream jumps in measurable ecological flow driven by major ebb drag effects. The major ebb phase contains a continuous 6–8 h steady positive-flow window, which is confirmed as the optimal period for ecological flow measurement and evaluation. Most mainstream control stations attain annual ecological flow assurance rates exceeding 90% except for extreme dry inflow due to strong spring–neap tidal fluctuation. This study establishes a novel multi-scale framework tailored to tidal hydrodynamic characteristics, which eliminates the non-measurability flaw of conventional ecological flow criteria. The proposed measurable window method enhances the operability of in-situ water ecological regulation and provides transferable technical references for other human-disturbed tidal deltas.

title: Advanced buoy phenological extraction methods for highly dynamic Zhejiang coastal waters
abstract: Accurate phenological information on phytoplankton is crucial for understanding energy flow, carbon cycling, and the growth and reproductive rhythms of key species within marine ecosystems. However, in dynamic and variable coastal waters, traditional methods struggle to detect critical phenological phases and trends precisely due to the high temporal and spatial variability. Furthermore, the relative contribution of interacting environmental factors to phenological shifts in coastal waters remains insufficiently understood. This study develops an integrated phenology extraction framework based on Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN), designed to handle nonlinear and non-stationary phytoplankton time series in highly dynamic coastal environments. Using in-situ buoy data, we analyzed phytoplankton phenology characteristics and driving factors in the coastal waters of Zhejiang, China, from 2016 to 2020. The results indicate a significant advancement in bloom onset and peak timing across most areas, with temperature and turbidity identified as the factors most closely associated with these phenological shifts. While empirical rules are still applied for phenological definition, the CEEMDAN-based framework significantly reduces the reliance on fixed global concentration thresholds by providing a denoised, adaptive baseline. This research is the first to apply the EMD (Empirical Mode Decomposition) series of decomposition methods to phenological extraction, demonstrating its practicality in handling nonlinear, non-stationary chlorophyll-a time series from buoy data in highly dynamic, eutrophic coastal waters. By adaptively separating high-frequency disturbances, it reveals temperature- and turbidity-driven shifts in bloom timing, offering insights into phenological responses to environmental stressors like eutrophication and pollution, and informing strategies for pollution mitigation and coastal ecosystem management.

title: Shifting resilience: Trends and predictors of mesic resource productivity in western U.S. rangelands
abstract: Abstract Mesic resources, the late-season herbaceous vegetation found in riparian areas and wet meadows, provide disproportionately important forage and habitat across western U.S. rangelands, yet their response to climatic variability and anthropogenic influences remains poorly understood. Using a 40-year Landsat time series (1984–2024), we quantified trends in late-season productivity (NDVI) across 4.5 million hectares of the sagebrush biome and applied random forest models to distinguish between temporal and spatial predictors of mesic resource productivity. We identified a fundamental shift in how mesic resources respond to drought: from 1984 to 2004, mesic productivity was strongly correlated with drought severity (Palmer Drought Severity Index, R² = 0.92), but this relationship weakened substantially in the next two decades (2005-2024; R² = 0.28), during which time productivity increased despite persistent aridity. Temporal modeling identified rising atmospheric CO 2 concentrations as the strongest predictor of this shift, consistent with enhanced plant water-use efficiency under CO 2 fertilization. Spatially, large agricultural valley floodplains act as anthropogenic refugia, sustaining productive mesic resources through flood irrigation and subsequent groundwater recharge into late summer. These findings suggest that human water management and physiological shifts in vegetation are currently buffering mesic systems against meteorological drought throughout U.S. rangelands. However, this apparent buffering is spatially heterogeneous and may mask vulnerability to groundwater depletion, shifts in precipitation regimes, and woody encroachment. Sustaining these vital ecosystems will require conservation approaches that go beyond climate monitoring to include balanced management considering both agricultural and ecological water needs and constraints.

title: High coupling but low coordination: Climate–vegetation interactions on the Chinese Loess Plateau under rapid greening
abstract: In arid and semi-arid regions, large-scale vegetation restoration is widely implemented to combat land degradation. However, it remains unclear whether human-induced greening is synchronized with climate dynamics for long-term sustainability. The Chinese Loess Plateau, a major ecological restoration region, provides an ideal case study. Using a coupling coordination degree model and multi-source datasets from 1990 to 2020, this study investigated the spatiotemporal interactions between climate and vegetation. Results showed a significant warming–wetting trend accompanied by substantial greening and increased carbon storage. A clear mismatch emerged: the system exhibited high coupling but low coordination (coupling degree >0.80, coordination index <0.15), indicating persistent mild maladjustment (coupling coordination degree <0.35). This suggests a potential systemic risk in dryland restoration, where anthropogenically driven vegetation expansion may outpace climatic feedback. The dominant driver shifted from natural productivity to land-use change and, more recently, to precipitation constraints. These results indicate that water availability is a key constraint on greening and that increased vegetation cover does not necessarily ensure sustainability. Therefore, ecological restoration policies may need to shift from a greening-oriented approach toward a comprehensive assessment-oriented framework, taking into account restoration quality in hotspot areas, ecosystem stability in not significant areas, and hydroclimatic suitability in cold spot areas to support the long-term sustainability of regional ecological restoration.

title: Reconciling landscape multifunctionality and population-based spatial equity under future land-use scenarios in Jingning County
abstract: Rapid land-use change is reshaping both the supply of ecosystem services (ESs) and the spatial distribution of human demand, creating new challenges for equitable landscape management in ecologically sensitive regions. However, how alternative land-management strategies jointly affect landscape multifunctionality (LMF) and population-based spatial equity remains insufficiently understood. This study integrated the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model with ES assessment models to evaluate changes in landscape multifunctionality and population-weighted inequality in Jingning County, China. We calculated the LMF index using a preference-weighted sum approach, with weights empirically derived from a stakeholder survey, to integrate biophysical ES supply with social demand. Population-based spatial equity was quantified using the Gini coefficient of LMF relative to resident population. The results showed that preference-weighted LMF decreased from 0.60 in 2000 to 0.37 in 2020, while the Gini coefficient increased from 0.13 to 0.19, indicating that multifunctionality became less evenly distributed relative to the resident population. Future scenarios revealed distinct trade-offs between overall multifunctionality and its population-weighted distribution.
