More importantly, we emphasized the need to balance multiple cooling objectives, as the existing threshold value of efficiency (TVoE) only considers the maximization of cooling efficiency. Our model revealed that a “small area with high complexity” configuration strategy serves as an effective approach to achieving balance among cooling objectives. The final optimal solution required only 11.8 ha, which is much lower than the traditional efficiency threshold. This work opens up a new avenue for more effective urban heat mitigation and provides scientific support for UGS planning.

title: The ecosystem integrity index: a component indicator in the Kunming-Montreal global biodiversity framework reveals the integrity of terrestrial ecosystems globally
abstract: The Ecosystem Integrity Index (EII), developed by UNEP-WCMC and adopted as a Component Indicator for the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM-GBF), provides a simple and robust framework to assess terrestrial ecosystem integrity globally, for use by governments as well as businesses and financial institutions. Being able to flexibly deploy our EII framework will help global to local users to both assess integrity, but also to measure changes due to conservation interventions by government, business and civil society. It is formed of three components (structural, compositional and functional integrity) and provides a continuous measure of ecosystem integrity from fully degraded to fully pristine. Applying the EII framework, we provide trends in ecosystem integrity globally from 2000 to 2020. This analysis shows that approximately one fifth of all terrestrial ecosystems have lost at least half of their ecosystem integrity. The greatest losses are seen in regions of the world where human population is dense or where development has been intense, whereas least developed regions have more intact scores. The loss of ecosystem integrity at this scale, and ongoing changes in other regions, is likely to have significant consequences for humanity and all life on Earth.

title: A SHAP-VW-BN framework for early warning of ecological damage in hilly mining areas: using interpretable thresholds to optimize variable weight theory and Bayesian networks
abstract: Large-scale coal mining in hilly regions often leads to several environmental problems occurring at the same time and in the same areas. These activities can damage vegetation, accelerate soil erosion, and disrupt local water systems, causing their impacts to overlap and interact across the landscape. In this context, the problems of the unclear contribution of ecological damage and difficult prediction of ecological damage probability in hilly mining areas are particularly significant. To address this problem, this paper innovatively constructs a SHAP-VW-BN early warning model for ecological damage in hilly mining areas. The model uses indicator contribution importance and thresholds derived from SHAP to jointly optimize the variable weight theory and the Bayesian network. Taking the Changping mining area as an example, we analyze the evolutionary patterns, nonlinear indicator contribution, and warning status of ecological damages. The main findings are as follows. (1) The SHAP-VW-BN model improved the theoretical basis for weight adjustment and probabilistic inference. The overall classification accuracy of the model is 87.4%, and the accuracy of the severe damage area is the highest (Recall = 0.885, F1-score = 0.919). (2) During the study period, the ecological damage status in the mining area first worsened, then improved, and finally stabilized. The area of the severe damage category initially increased and then decreased, but remained above the pre-mining level. (3) The key ecological damage contribution indicators in the study area were identified as SEI, NPP, CONTAG, TVDI, and SHDI. The indicator contribution thresholds for ecological improvement were SEI < 2, NPP > 520, CONTAG >55, TVDI <0.6, and SHDI >0.7. (4) In single-scenario early warnings, NPP and CONTAG were the key indicators of ecological damage. Under the scenario of improved ecological conditions, the probability of no damage increased by 30.6% and 14.6%, respectively. Areas with high NPP and low SEI showed the lowest likelihood of ecological damage, reducing the chance of severe damage by 21.5% and increasing the chance of no damage by 31.9%. The ecological damage early warning model developed in this study improves the detection of abrupt changes in key indicators and the accuracy of damage probability of the coupled effects among multiple damage processes. It provides technical support for condition-based reliable ecological damage state probability assessment and restoration in hilly mining areas.

title: Land system evolution from an element–structure–function perspective: A case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
abstract: Understanding the evolution of land systems is essential for supporting sustainable territorial spatial governance. Guided by the Element–Structure–Function theory, this study established an integrated analytical framework to investigate land system evolution in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD). Land systems were classified using Divisive Analysis (DIANA) and random forest (RF) algorithms. A LightGBM model was employed to quantify constituent elements and element structures, land functions were evaluated using a Production–Living–Ecological function evaluation system, and the geo-informatic Tupu method was used to reveal spatiotemporal transition patterns. The results showed that the land systems of the YRD exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity and hierarchical characteristics. Between 2000 and 2020, the settlement system (LS1) expanded from 6024 km 2 to 25,988 km 2 , whereas the cropland system (LS2) maintained the largest spatial extent despite substantial internal restructuring. Human activities became increasingly important in shaping land systems, with cropping intensity (CI) becoming the most influential constituent element in 2020 (20.80%), while the feature importance of impervious surface coverage (ISC) increased from 6.75% to 9.03%. During the study period, LS1, the forest system (LS3), and the grassland system (LS4) showed stable element structures dominated by single landscape element, with feature importance exceeding 70%. In contrast, LS2 was dominated by cropland coverage (CLC), which accounted for more than 50% of total feature importance. Land system transitions were dominated by the conversion from LS2 to LS1 (15,383 km 2 ), while frequent bidirectional transitions within LS2 and between LS3 and the cropland & forestland mosaic system (LS7). Functionally, agricultural production became increasingly concentrated in the Huang–Huai and Yangtze–Huai Plain, the urban living function evolved into a multicentric network centered on Shanghai, and the regional ecological function remained generally stable. The findings comprehensively reveal the integrated characteristics of land systems and provide valuable support for territorial spatial planning and territorial spatial governance.

title: Rethinking shoreline-buffer indicators for assessing directional lake cooling in plateau basin cities
abstract: Urban lakes are widely regarded as effective thermal regulators of outdoor built environments, yet their cooling footprints are often assessed using uniform shoreline buffers that assume isotropic distance decay. This assumption is problematic in morphologically heterogeneous lakeside districts, especially in plateau basin cities where terrain, prevailing winds, and urban form reshape surface thermal patterns. This study examined Dianchi Lake in Kunming, China, using daytime land surface temperature composites for January and May. Directional distance-decay analysis, block-scale Local Climate Zone classification, and XGBoost–SHAP attribution were combined to quantify seasonal changes in lake cooling intensity, cooling distance, and morphological controls. Mean cooling intensity increased from 3.16 °C in January to 7.12 °C in May, whereas mean cooling distance changed only slightly, from 340 to 354 m. This apparent stability masked substantial directional redistribution: cooling reach expanded in some sectors by up to about 150 m but contracted in others by more than 300 m. LCZ analysis showed that natural and open classes developed stronger cooling advantages in May, while compact and industrial classes shifted from near-neutral to pronounced warming. SHAP attribution indicated that surface albedo and wind alignment became more influential in January, whereas sky view factor, vegetation cover, and lake proximity dominated in May. These findings show that plateau-lake cooling is directional rather than uniform, supporting morphology-sensitive lakeside heat mitigation.

title: Anthropogenically driven habitat changes caused a directional reorganization of macrobenthic functional structure
abstract: Coastal habitat transformations, including ecological restoration, biological invasion, and shoreline engineering, have become major drivers of ecological change in intertidal ecosystems worldwide. However, their functional consequences for macrobenthic communities remain insufficiently understood. We investigated macrobenthic communities across six representative intertidal habitats in Yueqing Bay and evaluated functional trait composition, functional diversity, functional beta diversity decomposition, and applied RLQ and fourth-corner analyses to identify the environmental drivers of functional traits. Habitat modification selectively favored distinct ecological strategies and resulted in pronounced functional reorganization of macrobenthic communities. Long-term transplanted mangrove forests were characterized by higher proportions of long-lived and infaunal taxa, accompanied by reduced functional space. In contrast, Spartina alterniflora marshes supported higher proportions of epifauna taxa and maintained the larger functional space and stronger turnover-driven functional replacement. Artificial seawalls similarly favored long-lived and sensitive taxa, whereas natural rocky reefs were dominated by short-lived and herbivorous communities. Sediment texture and nutrient conditions jointly mediated trait-environment coupling. These results indicate that multiple anthropogenic pressures directionally restructure macrobenthic functional organization through distinct environmental filtering pathways, highlighting the importance of considering functional responses when evaluating the ecological consequences of coastal habitat transformation.

title: Where might freshwater species persist in an arid state? Assessing aquatic refugia in New Mexico, U.S.A.
abstract: Climate change is impacting freshwater ecosystems, which contain many species already threatened by anthropogenic activities. To help managers protect imperiled species, we developed a framework for assessing the potential for aquatic refugia within the state of New Mexico, U.S.A. We used literature review and state-generated lists of sensitive species and habitats to develop five taxa-specific habitat groups as targets for assessment (cold-water fish habitat, perennial streams, perennial water amphibian and reptile habitat, ephemeral catchments, and springs). We then selected sets of indicators representing macrorefugia (areas of relative climate stability) and hydrorefugia (local features that protect aquatic ecosystems from changes in temperature and precipitation) for each habitat group. Refugia scores, generated from standardized indicator values, showed considerable variation in refugia potential among habitat groups and geographic locations. In most cases, areas with greatest potential for hydrorefugia were separate from those with greatest potential for macrorefugia. Mountainous regions typically scored highest for potential refugia, highlighting the importance of these areas to a variety of aquatic species. Our results can be used to identify additional areas for conservation and to inform species-specific management plans.

title: Multi-scenario zoning control of land use patterns for enhancing ecosystem services in a semi-arid city: A case study of Baicheng, China
abstract: Ecosystem services (ESs) underpin socioeconomic stability in ecologically fragile regions, where land-use change, climate change, and human activity place increasing pressure on ecosystem functioning. Baicheng City lies in a semi-arid–semi-humid transition region of northeastern China. We quantified windbreak and sand fixation, water conservation, carbon sequestration, and the Comprehensive Ecosystem Service Index (CESI) from 2000 to 2023 and examined their driving factors. Constraint-line analysis identified normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and fractional vegetation cover (FVC) thresholds in relation to CESI and delineated ecological security and restoration zones. The ecological security zone served as a common restriction layer in the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model. Three land-use scenarios were simulated for 2035: natural development (NDS), cropland protection (CPS), and ecological protection (EPS). Their conditional CESI responses were assessed with non-land inputs held at their 2023 levels. From 2000 to 2023, all three ESs and CESI generally increased, with precipitation, NDVI, and FVC emerging as the dominant explanatory factors. The NDVI and FVC thresholds were 0.30 and 0.71, respectively. The corresponding ecological security and restoration zones accounted for 26% and 74% of the study area. Mean CESI values under all three scenarios remained slightly below the 2023 baseline. CPS retained the highest mean CESI among the scenarios, EPS had the smallest area of CESI change, and NDS produced the broadest spatial redistribution and the lowest mean CESI. Unlike previous studies that apply either threshold analysis or scenario simulation separately, this study introduces a novel framework that couples empirically derived vegetation thresholds with PLUS-based scenario simulation to inform spatially differentiated land-use regulation. This approach provides a transferable methodology for linking historical ecosystem service assessment to future land-use planning in water-limited regions.

title: Spatial mismatch in benthic-pelagic habitat heterogeneity reveals overlooked conservation priorities in the global ocean
abstract: Under the “30 × 30” target for ocean conservation and the BBNJ Agreement, a quantitative and science-based identification scheme for conservation priorities is required. The Ecologically or Biologically Significant Marine Areas (EBSAs) provide a crucial foundation but rely heavily on empirical biological data and expert consensus. This makes it susceptible to data deficiencies and spatial biases in deep-sea and high seas, while also lacking cross-regional comparability. Habitat heterogeneity is recognized as a robust surrogate indicator for biodiversity. Utilizing multi-source, high-resolution marine environmental data, this study constructed a Benthic Habitat Heterogeneity Index (BHHI) and a Pelagic Habitat Heterogeneity Index (PHHI) using the Shannon index and the Entropy Weight Method. We analyzed global spatial patterns and evaluated existing EBSAs based on single- and dual-dimensional heterogeneity hotspots. Results demonstrate that the global EBSA network's BHHI (0.38 ± 0.23) and PHHI (0.18 ± 0.12) significantly exceed global ocean averages (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.001), indicating overall prioritization of high-heterogeneity areas. However, 8.06 × 10 6 km 2 (8.4% of existing EBSAs) are dual-dimensional inefficient zones. Conversely, 17.45 × 10 6 km 2 of new high-efficiency zones were identified outside the network, with 54.33% in the high seas. Significant spatial mismatches between benthic and pelagic heterogeneity cause extensive single-dimensional inefficiencies within EBSAs (29.2% and 28.8%, respectively). Furthermore, 73.16 × 10 6 km 2 of benthic and 65.83 × 10 6 km 2 of pelagic high-efficiency zones exist outside the network, with 56.9% and 54.0% in the high seas. The quantitative habitat heterogeneity framework provides a novel tool for evaluating global conservation priorities and offers actionable insights for optimizing the EBSA network.

title: Unveiling the non-linear impact mechanism of multi-factor synergy on habitat quality based on stacking ensemble learning
abstract: Rapid urbanization imposes complex nonlinear constraints on ecological sustainability, while conventional linear models often fail to capture critical turning points in interactions among variables. To address this limitation, we developed an analytical framework integrating the InVEST model, stacking ensemble machine learning (EML), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the spatiotemporal drivers of habitat quality (HQ). Using Jiangxi Province, China, as a case study from 2005 to 2023, we quantified the trade-offs between human activities and ecological integrity. The results revealed a distinct core–periphery degradation pattern, with significant declines in HQ concentrated primarily in urban agglomerations. At the county scale and for the dataset analyzed, the stacking ensemble model achieved strong predictive performance, with a test-set R 2 of 0.995, and outperformed the individual base learners in capturing complex multidimensional interactions. SHAP dependence analysis identified model-conditional ecological response turning points of approximately 0.18 for the construction land proportion and 0.51 for the landscape division index. Beyond these values, the modeled negative responses of HQ became more pronounced. Topographic conditions also exerted an important constraint, with a slope turning point of 9.59° marking a shift in the modeled marginal effect from negative to positive. PLS-SEM further showed that the negative statistical association between anthropogenic pressure and HQ dynamics strengthened over the study period. By 2023, this association exceeded that of natural factors, making anthropogenic pressure the most strongly associated component in the specified path model. These findings provide model-based quantitative references for delineating urban growth boundaries and evidence-based guidance for differentiated spatial management, thereby supporting a balance between urban densification and the conservation of critical ecosystem services.

title: Ecological vulnerability assessment of typical grasslands on the Mongolian Plateau: Abrupt change detection and driving mechanism analysis
abstract: The typical grasslands of the Mongolian Plateau, a key component of the global temperate grassland ecosystem, play an essential role in maintaining regional ecological security and ecosystem stability. However, these grasslands exhibit high ecological sensitivity to climate change and human activities. Based on the sensitivity–resilience–pressure (SRP) model, this study constructs a comprehensive ecological vulnerability assessment indicator system that incorporates both ecosystem conditions and human activity factors. Ecological vulnerability in typical grasslands from 2001 to 2022 was systematically assessed using the spatial principal component analysis (SPCA) method. The results indicate a clear northeast–southwest gradient of increasing ecological vulnerability During 2001–2022, the ecological vulnerability grade index (EVGI) exhibited a slow decreasing trend (Slope = −0.001/a), indicating an overall reduction in ecological vulnerability and relatively stable ecosystem conditions. A significant abrupt change occurred in 2014, after which the area of ecological degradation expanded markedly (approximately 57.58%), primarily in the southern and northeastern parts of the study area. Natural factors were the primary drivers of the synthetic ecological vulnerability index (SEVI), with annual mean temperature, annual mean precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, normalized difference vegetation index, and net primary productivity showing higher explanatory power. Following the abrupt change in 2014, the influence of human activity indicators such as population density and livestock density increased. The SEVI in the northern and eastern regions were mainly controlled by natural factors, whereas the southern and western regions were more affected by human activities. Future predictions suggest that the SEVI in this region will decline over the next decade, indicating a gradual recovery of grassland, which may be attributed to the implementation of protection policies and rational grazing management, thereby mitigating human impacts. These findings provide valuable scientific support for ecological conservation, grazing management, and sustainable development of typical grasslands on the Mongolian Plateau.

title: Diagnosing ecological risks under current land-use configurations in Inner Mongolia
abstract: China's food security strategy is shifting beyond cultivated land-based grain production toward diversified food sources and ecological sustainability. Grasslands play a critical role in this transition, supporting livestock production while providing multiple ecosystem services. However, agricultural intensification and cultivated land–grassland competition increasingly threaten their multifunctionality. Taking Inner Mongolia, a region that epitomizes these challenges, as a case study, this research develops a static ecological risk diagnostic framework under current (2024) land-use, integrating ecosystem service assessment and evaluation of land-use alignment with natural conditions. The results show that medium risk areas dominate Inner Mongolia (82.14%) and are primarily associated with ecosystem service-related risks. Among these, ecosystem services conflict on grasslands represents the largest share (58.97%), where high habitat quality co-occurs with low water yield and soil conservation. In terms of land-use alignment, although cultivated land is theoretically subject to broader natural constraints, a larger proportion of existing grassland lies within highly constrained environments. High risk areas further reveal contrasting risk patterns: cultivated land unsuitability is mainly associated with multiple ecosystem service deficiencies, whereas grassland vulnerability consistently co-occurs with ecosystem services conflict. These risk patterns imply different management priorities. High-risk cultivated land highlights the need for ecological restoration to recover ecosystem functionality, whereas widespread medium-risk grasslands call for landscape-scale enhancement of service synergies through region-specific and multi-stakeholder collaboration. The proposed framework provides a transferable approach for identifying restoration priorities and guiding sustainable land-use planning in Inner Mongolia and other agro-pastoral regions, supporting the coordinated achievement of both ecological and food security.

title: Prioritizing ecological restoration in cold Alpine source regions: A multi-dimensional framework integrating ecosystem services, security, and feasibility
abstract: The source regions of the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers serve as a critical ecological security barrier. In recent years, climate change and intensified human activities, such as overgrazing, have led to ecosystem degradation, threatening regional water resources and global carbon dynamics. This study evaluated four key ecosystem services (ESs): water yield, soil conservation, carbon storage, and habitat quality. Based on the Ecological Security Index (ESI) and Ecological Restoration Feasibility Index (ERFI), priority areas for ecological restoration were identified and classified using index overlay analysis. Furthermore, the Geo-detector method was employed to explore the main drivers of the spatial heterogeneity of ESs, ESI, and ERFI. The four ESs exhibited significant spatial variability, with higher values observed in the Yellow River source region. Areas with high ecosystem service values were mainly concentrated in the central and southeastern parts of the Yellow River source region and the southeastern part of the Yangtze River source region. Precipitation, vegetation cover, slope, and potential evapotranspiration were identified as the primary factors influencing the spatial distribution of ESs. In addition, inter-service relationships revealed both synergies and trade-offs. The mean ESI across the study area was 0.33. Approximately 12.7% of the area, primarily located in the northern and southwestern parts of the Yangtze River source region, had an ESI value below 0.2. The mean ERFI was 0.28, with 79.7% of the region exhibiting low restoration feasibility. Notably, areas characterized by low ESI and high ERFI, indicating high restoration priority, accounted for 22.7% of the total area. The integrated ES–ESI–ERFI framework provides a robust basis for targeted ecological restoration and resource allocation in the source regions of the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers, offering a valuable methodological reference for managing other cold, fragile high-altitude ecosystems.

title: Spatiotemporal assessment of watershed health and vulnerability using integrated VOR–RRV frameworks for enhancing ecosystem sustainability
abstract: This study assesses the watershed health (WH) and vulnerability of the Taleghan watershed using an integrated vigor–organization–resilience (VOR) and reliability–resilience–vulnerability (RRV) framework. The integrated VOR–RRV framework simultaneously assesses ecological health and hydrological vulnerability, enabling sub-watershed prioritization based on a health–vulnerability matrix for sustainable watershed management. Watershed vigor was evaluated based on runoff and soil erosion, while organization and resilience were quantified using landscape metrics for 1995 and 2025. Vulnerability during 1995–2025 was assessed through the RRV model incorporating the standardized precipitation index (SPI). Results showed moderate WH, with a declining trend from 0.49 in 1995 to 0.46 in 2025. Vigor, organization, and resilience indices decreased across most sub-basins. Vulnerability analysis indicated moderate conditions, with mean reliability, resilience, vulnerability, and RRV values of 0.46, 0.50, 0.55, and 0.56, respectively. Integrated VOR–RRV results prioritized sub-basins for immediate restoration (33%), immediate conservation (27%), conservation (23%), and rehabilitation (17%). Statistical analysis confirmed significance at the 5% level, although no significant relationship was found between the VOR and RRV models.

title: Monitoring desertification dynamics and transition patterns through spatial-frequency feature integration of remote sensing data: a case study of the Gurbantunggut Desert, China
abstract: One of the most severe types of land degradation in arid and semi-arid regions is desertification, which poses serious risks to ecological security, sustainable development, and the global climate system. However, long-term remote sensing monitoring is challenged by gradual transitions between different desertification levels and the ambiguity of spatial boundaries, leading to substantial uncertainty in fine-grained identification and quantitative assessment. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Deep Semantic Change Detection Network (DSCD-Net) that integrates spatial and frequency feature representations for fine-grained desertification monitoring using multi-temporal Landsat images acquired from 1990 to 2020. The framework takes bi-temporal multispectral images as inputs and directly predicts pixel-level desertification transition relationships, thereby accurately representing the location, direction, and intensity of changes. The proposed framework was applied to the Gurbantunggut Desert, China, to examine long-term desertification dynamics and transition patterns. Experimental results show that DSCD-Net achieved 92.11% OA, 78.18% mIoU, 74.36% Fscd, and 34.75% SeK, outperforming the comparison methods. Long-term analysis shows that the evolution of desertification in this region exhibits significant nonlinear characteristics and periodic fluctuations, with the moderate desertification state as a key transitional phase. Furthermore, precipitation during the snow accumulation and melting period is identified as the dominant climatic driver regulating desertification dynamics. By explicitly capturing transition pathways and intensity, the proposed framework provides a process-oriented ecological indicator framework for assessing land degradation and offers valuable support for ecological restoration planning and sustainable land management in arid environments.

title: Assessment of cropland soil erosion patterns and driving factors in Northeast China through semi-monthly enhanced modeling
abstract: Soil erosion is thinning the fertile black soil in the croplands of Northeast China. However, the spatial patterns, temporal dynamics, and driving factors of cropland soil erosion under the combined effects of freeze-thaw processes, vegetation cover changes, and rainfall erosivity remain insufficiently quantified. This study constructed the Semi-Monthly Enhanced Chinese Soil Loss Equation (SE-CSLE) by incorporating the Freeze-Thaw Adjustment Factor for Soil Erodibility (Ka) and Composite Tillage Factor (Tc) into the Chinese Soil Loss Equation (CSLE). It was applied to analyze cropland soil erosion patterns in Northeast China from 2003 to 2023. The Random Forest analysis showed that Ka and Tc had relative importance values of 23% and 18% among erosion drivers. Temporal comparison with sediment discharge showed generally consistent variations, although the degree of agreement varied among years. Compared with CSLE and other erosion estimates, SE-CSLE yielded the highest NSE (0.551) and the lowest PBIAS (12.363%) based on runoff plot observations. Spatially, soil erosion was mainly controlled by the topographic factor (LS), with steeper and higher areas experiencing more severe erosion. The annual average erosion rate was 7.78 t ha −1 year −1 , and the average semi-monthly soil erosion rate was 0.32 t ha −1 period −1 . Cropland erosion showed an increasing trend from 2003 to 2023. Within a year, soil erosion increased rapidly from April to May due to sparse vegetation and soil thawing and peaked in late June and early July. From the perspective of reducing erosion risk, maintaining straw cover until mid-May in mountainous areas and adjusting straw removal and sowing timing in other croplands may help support erosion control. These findings highlight the need for soil conservation measures that account for regional conditions and seasonal erosion risks in the croplands of Northeast China.

title: Landscape mosaics: Analysing diversity for ecological and economic insight
abstract: Quantifying and valuing biodiversity remains one of the major challenges for the bioeconomy and nature-based solutions. Emerging biodiversity and ecosystem services credit schemes requires robust, scalable indicators, capable of capturing the ecological integrity and environmental value while ensuring standardization and cross-regional comparability. Conventional biodiversity assessment rely on field surveys, taxonomic expertise, and long-term monitoring, limiting their applicability for large-scale or continuous evaluation. This study proposes a methodological framework using landscape ecology metrics as proxy indicators of biodiversity potential and ecological value. Using COSc2024 Interim Land-Use/Land-Cover Map of Portugal, five indices (Shannon Diversity, Class Richness, Patch Density, Contagion, and Connectivity) were calculated across a 10 × 10 km grid covering mainland Portugal. The objective is to evaluate the applicability of landscape-level metrics as scalable proxies for the national scale classification of territorial units according to biodiversity potential and ecological integrity. Results reveal consistent spatial gradients linking compositional diversity, fragmentation and connectivity, delineating eight distinct landscape typologies. Heterogeneous northern mosaics exhibit higher biodiversity potential and resilience, whereas homogeneous southern agroforestry systems show stronger connectivity but lower diversity. Overall, the findings demonstrate that landscape metrics provide reliable and scalable proxies for ecological integrity and ecosystem functionality. These findings provide a practical basis for identifying priority areas for biodiversity credit schemes and supporting spatially explicit decision-making in nature-based investment strategies. By linking landscape structure to ecological valuation and environmental policy, this research contributes to the development of nature-positive investment frameworks integrating sustainable land management and bioeconomic planning.

title: Unraveling how park environmental indicators shape subjective well-being: Multisensory and nonlinear mechanisms in high-density cities
abstract: In high-density cities, limited land resources have shifted the focus of urban park planning from expanding green space supply to improving the environmental quality of existing parks. Although previous studies have examined park accessibility or single-sensory attributes, fine-scale indicators explaining how multisensory park environments jointly shape subjective well-being (SWB) remain insufficient. To bridge this gap, this study developed a visual-thermal-acoustic multi-sensory analysis framework, integrating machine learning (ML) and shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method. Taking multi-scale parks in Guangzhou, China as cases, quantify park environmental, examine their nonlinear and heterogeneous relationships with SWB. Results show that: (1)The integrated multisensory model outperformed single-sensory models, while ML model effectively captured nonlinear relationships across park types, with GBDT performing best for Type I parks and random forest for Types II and III, and Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET) identified as key factors influencing SWB; (2) in large-scale parks, plant diversity and vegetation exert a positive effect beyond 0.42 and 0.58, respectively, whilst Sky View Factor (SVF) and PET turn negative beyond 0.11 and 30.86 °C, respectively. In small-scale parks, acoustic exposure showed a negative effect above 75 dB(A), indicating that micro-environmental constraints are more pronounced; and (3) With the exception of vegetation and PET, children, middle-aged and older adults exhibit a stronger response to shading, acoustic exposure and SVF, whilst young and middle-aged adults respond more strongly to plant diversity, spatial openness and Canny edges. This study translates multisensory park environments into actionable indicators for green space renewal and differentiated park management.

title: Elevation-dependent divergence of vegetation dynamics over the Anyemaqen Mountain revealed by reconstructed Sentinel-2 time series
abstract: Reliable monitoring of alpine headwater vegetation is constrained by persistent cloud cover, seasonal snow, and complex terrain. This study developed an indicator-oriented framework for the Anyemaqen Mountain in the Yellow River Headwaters using 122 observations of 10-m Sentinel-2 Level-2 A images acquired from 2015 to 2025. After quality screening, continuous Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) trajectories were reconstructed using temporal linear interpolation, spatial neighbourhood filling, and climatological mean replacement. Vegetation and snow-cover dynamics were then evaluated using the Theil–Sen trend estimation, Mann–Kendall test, pixel-wise NDVI–NDSI correlation, three elevation bands (< 3800, 3800–4600, and > 4600 m), and geographically weighted regression with elevation, slope, and aspect as explanatory variables. The results show that significant greening occurred across 7.2% of the study area and was concentrated mainly at high elevations, whereas significant browning affected only 0.1% but was localised in low-elevation valleys and riparian corridors. The remaining 92.7% showed no significant trend. Within the analysed snow-covered domain, 8.3% of pixels showed significant NDSI decline, while pixel-wise NDVI–NDSI correlations were spatially mixed, with a spatial mean r of 0.003; none remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. The geographically weighted model represented spatially varying topographic controls, with local R 2 ranging from 0.001 to 0.752 and a median of 0.162. Together, these results define an elevation-dependent vegetation dipole characterised by significant high-elevation greening and localised low-valley browning. The reconstructed high-resolution framework provides a fine-scale ecological indicator for elevation-specific monitoring and management in alpine headwaters.

title: Three-dimensional habitat suitability index as an ecological indicator for diagnosing dam-regulated fish migration corridor disruption and guiding turbine-level flow management
abstract: Dam operations alter the three-dimensional (3D) hydraulic environment of regulated rivers, yet ecological indicators capable of diagnosing how these alterations disrupt fish migration corridors remain lacking. This study develops a 3D habitat suitability index (HSI) as an integrated ecological indicator, coupling computational fluid dynamics with a multi-parameter fuzzy logic model, to diagnose corridor dynamics and guide turbine-level release management. Applied to the Wudongde high-head dam on the upper Yangtze River, with the endangered endemic Leptobotia elongata as target species, the HSI indicator reveals a two-scale diagnostic structure: at the river-channel scale, intermediate total discharge (∼3935 m 3 /s) maximizes high-suitability corridor extent; at the tailrace scale, HSI near the fish-passing facility entrance is governed by individual turbine configuration rather than total discharge — a distinction that conventional discharge-based ecological flow frameworks cannot resolve. An HSI-guided turbine allocation strategy re-established a spatially continuous high-suitability corridor in the model without structural modification, and field hydroacoustic surveys were consistent with the HSI-predicted preferred release conditions at the facility-entrance scale. These findings support the 3D HSI as a scenario-based diagnostic indicator for corridor disruption in regulated rivers. The framework provides a basis for adaptive, turbine-level release management, with full-corridor biological validation identified as a remaining requirement.

title: Experiential factors associated with subjective well-being in urban waterfront environments: Evidence from social media data in Wuhan, China
abstract: Urban waterfront environments, as important forms of urban blue spaces, are increasingly recognized for their contributions to human health and subjective well-being (SWB). However, previous studies have mainly classified waterfront spaces based on waterbody attributes and examined the relationships between objectively measured environmental characteristics and health outcomes, while how spatial forms and functional attributes are associated with public experiences and how these experiential differences relate to SWB remain underexplored. To address these gaps, this study utilizes large-scale social media data from Wuhan to explore how experiential factors—including perception, cognition, and behavior—are associated with SWB in urban waterfront environments and examines their temporal dynamics and typological disparities. The results reveal pronounced long-term variations and seasonal cycles in SWB across waterfront environments that are associated with social and climatic conditions. Overall, physical activity shows the strongest association with SWB (19.12%), followed by traffic (15.96%) and crowding (9.89%). Distinct patterns emerge across waterfront typologies: riverfronts, characterized by a balanced mix of exercise and leisure, exhibit the highest overall SWB with moderate seasonality; waterfront parks, more strongly associated with accessibility and natural environmental quality, show slightly lower SWB but the greatest year-round stability; and waterfront greenways, characterized by physical activity, display the lowest levels of SWB with the largest seasonal variability. This study highlights general experiential patterns and typology-specific differences associated with SWB in waterfront environments. It provides empirical evidence for understanding the health-related benefits of urban blue spaces and offers practical insights for the design and management of waterfront environments to promote public well-being.

title: Statistical significance of nutrient loading structural effects: An adaptive criterion for lake sub-watershed prioritization
abstract: Eutrophication globally impairs lacustrine ecosystem health. Clarifying trophic state (TS) heterogeneity and its driving mechanisms is key to precise nutrient control. To unravel structural disparities in nutrient loading effects and prioritize sub-watersheds for targeted lacustrine TS regulation, nine Yunnan plateau lakes are selected as typical study area. By integrating path analysis for causal inference, the random forest model for trophic state index (TSI) inversion, and the InVEST model, we systematically explored the nutrient structural impact mechanisms and identified priority sub-watersheds (PSWs) for targeted governance. The main findings are as follows: 1) TSI in nearly 90% lake water area declined during 2019-2024, with more significant trends in high-trophic regions; The TS spatial patterns of the nine lakes have been reshaped by the governance efforts. 2) Exogenous nutrients significantly affect TS in most lakes; lowering TSI by 1.00% requires a 1.15%–4.36% reduction in watershed soil erosion, 1.05%–2.94% in nitrogen load, or 1.34%–2.56% in phosphorus load. 3) TSI is affected by the differentiated structural impacts of exogenous/endogenous nutrients; but the statistical significance, as a notable criterion for watershed prioritization, is not entirely dependent on loading magnitude. 4) Four types of PSWs are identified based on effect significance: integrated-control (24.6%), total-organic-control (4.1%), total-nitrogen-control (2.8%), and total-phosphorus-control (0.8%), with targeted governance schemes proposed for each type. A PSWs identification framework is established based on causal inference to provide both scientific insights for global lake trophic state research and practical tools for shifting lake management to precise control.

title: A matter of time: Optimising bee sampling while limiting bycatch
abstract: Pan traps are an established method for sampling bees across a wide range of habitats and geographical regions, but uncertainty persists to what extent pan-trap characteristics influence sampling results. We therefore investigated how pan-trap exposure time (24 h, 48 h and 72 h) affected sampled bee communities and bycatch (insects without bees) at 23 agricultural sites in Germany, using fluorescent blue, white and yellow pan traps. We assessed abundance (number of bees), biomass of bees, total biomass, and taxon richness of bees and bycatch using DNA metabarcoding. Overall, we collected 4963 bee individuals and found interacting effects of exposure time and temperature on bee abundance, as well as taxon richness of bees, Hymenoptera and bycatch. Exposure time also had an effect on total biomass. Bee abundance was higher at 48 h than at 24 h exposure, and at cooler temperatures, bee taxon richness was also higher at 48 h than at 24 h, while we observed no differences between 48 h and 72 h exposure. Total biomass increased from 48 h to 72 h exposure time and, at warmer temperatures, bycatch taxon richness did so as well. We advocate for a pan-trap exposure time of 48 h to maximize trap efficacy in terms of number of bee individuals and bee taxa, while limiting unnecessary bycatch. A 24 h exposure time may be an alternative option that further reduces bycatch, particularly for studies that focus on taxon diversity and have limited sampling time.

title: Decadal assessment of habitat change, hydrological variability, and waterbird diversity in Moe Yun Gyi Ramsar Wetland, Myanmar
abstract: The Moe Yun Gyi Wetland in Myanmar, a key stopover on the East Asian Australian Flyway, has undergone significant habitat changes between 2014 and 2023. This study aims to assess the impacts of habitat degradation, hydrological shifts, and climate variability on waterbird diversity and abundance. We used a combination of ecological monitoring and geospatial analysis to track these changes. Satellite imagery revealed an overall 46% reduction in flooded vegetation between 2014 and 2023, although a temporary recovery occurred during the intermediate restoration period before declining again in the later years. Water body coverage, which peaked at 38% in 2019, decreased to 31% by 2023. Despite these losses, habitat connectivity improved temporarily between 2017 and 2020 following restoration efforts, resulting in peak waterbird abundance (3450 individuals) and species richness (42 species). However, habitat fragmentation and contraction between 2021 and 2023 led to a 27% decline in waterbird numbers. Water-depth responses were guild-specific: diving birds and large waders responded positively to deeper conditions around 2.5 m, whereas dabbling birds and small waders were favored by shallower conditions around 1.5 m. At the community level, approximately 1.5 m represented the most favorable overall water depth, while deeper conditions benefited particular guilds rather than the entire waterbird community. Bird diversity was positively correlated with flooded vegetation, emphasizing the need for effective water movement management. Climatic factors, especially rainfall, positively influenced waterbird abundance, while higher temperatures reduced species richness over the decade. This study underscores the importance of maintaining habitat complexity and hydrological stability to conserve waterbird biodiversity, offering valuable insights for adaptive wetland restoration in Asia and globally.

title: Ecological and economic effects of banning bottom trawling in Natura 2000 sites and reducing its effort in the western Mediterranean
abstract: In the Mediterranean Sea, several fished stocks remain overexploited and several marine protected areas (MPAs) permit high-impact gears such as bottom trawling. Improving understanding of the effects of stricter MPAs and reductions in fishing effort is essential to progress towards biodiversity and sustainable fisheries targets. Here, we use a marine ecosystem modelling approach to assess the potential ecological and fishery-related economic effects of three management scenarios involving a ban of bottom trawling in Natura 2000 sites designated under the Habitats Directive (hereafter SACs) and reductions of bottom trawling effort in the north-western Mediterranean Sea. Our results indicate that implementing the spatial ban alone can lead to increases in revenue and catch of key demersal species (reflecting potential fisheries spillover) outside SACs, particularly in the buffer zones, while delivering ecological benefits within SACs compared to a business-as-usual scenario. Instead, reducing bottom trawling effort overall can enhance demersal biomass recovery over both short and long-time scales, across the study area. Combining both management actions can deliver ecological benefits for key demersal species over both short and long-time scales within and outside SACs, and potential fisheries spillover in the buffer zones. Our findings underscore the importance of banning bottom trawling within SACs as a key step to support demersal community recovery and advance biodiversity objectives. They also highlight that no single management measure can simultaneously maximize ecological benefits and fisheries catch and revenue: combining spatial protection and effort-based regulation may be required to balance biodiversity and fisheries objectives and ensure long-term sustainability of the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Soil Erosion on the Qinghai-Tibet plateau: Dynamics, drivers, and future risk under land-use change
abstract: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), characterized by complex topography, fragile alpine ecosystems, and cryosphere-related processes, is a critical region for assessing soil erosion risk in cold environments. However, plateau-scale evidence on long-term soil erosion dynamics, nonlinear environmental responses, and future risk under land-use change remains limited. In this study, the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) was used to quantify water erosion modulus across the QTP from 2001 to 2023. An integrated framework combining RUSLE, XGBoost-SHAP, and PLUS was developed to link historical erosion assessment, interpretable driver attribution, and future land-use scenario simulation, thereby improving the interpretability and scenario relevance of soil erosion risk evaluation. The results showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in soil erosion, with a multi-year mean soil erosion modulus of 1.85 t hm −2 a −1 . Slight erosion dominated the central plateau, whereas light and more severe erosion classes were concentrated mainly in the southern, eastern, and western mountainous regions. Soil erosion remained generally stable over time, with localized fluctuations in marginal mountains. NDVI showed the largest relative SHAP contribution, contributing 27.37%, followed by precipitation and slope. SHAP dependence plots indicated model-derived nonlinear response transitions for NDVI, precipitation, slope, and elevation. Scenario simulations indicated increasing future soil erosion risk, with mean soil erosion modulus rising to 5.39 t hm −2 a −1 in 2030 and 7.68 t hm −2 a −1 in 2050. Differences among land-use scenarios were limited in regional means but evident in the spatial reorganization of light-to-severe erosion patches. These findings support soil erosion risk management and ecological conservation in alpine regions.

title: Microeukaryotic communities and habitat-based assessment in a large plateau river system
abstract: Understanding how environmental conditions and anthropogenic activities shape microbial biodiversity is essential for ecological assessment of large river systems. However, the structure, assembly mechanisms, and environmental drivers of eukaryotic microbial communities in the upper Yellow River remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted a basin-scale survey across more than 1,000 km of the upper Yellow River in Gansu Province, sampling both trunk streams and tributaries during wet and dry seasons, and analyzed eukaryotic microbial communities using high-throughput sequencing. Our results show clear spatial and seasonal differentiation in community structure. Natural upstream regions exhibited significantly higher microeukaryotic diversity and more complex co-occurrence networks than downstream anthropogenically influenced areas. Community assembly was predominantly driven by stochastic processes, although the relative contributions of dispersal limitation and environmental selection varied across river sections and seasons. In addition, tributary communities were more strongly associated with habitat quality and land-use patterns than trunk-stream communities, highlighting distinct environmental controls across river types. Importantly, integrating habitat assessment and land-use indicators revealed strong and consistent relationships with microbial community variation, suggesting their potential as practical ecological indicators for microbial biodiversity assessment. These findings improve our understanding of microbial ecological processes in large river systems and provide a potential indicator-based framework for river ecological evaluation and management.

title: Embodied emission linkages and interactions of industrial aquatic heavy metals in the Yangtze River Economic Belt, China: a multi-sector multi-region factorial metabolism analysis
abstract: Heavy metal emissions (HMEs) from industrial wastewater pose risks to ecosystems, public health, and regional development. Understanding the embodied emission linkages and interactions in cross-regional HME flows is essential for mitigation policy design. This study develops a multi-sector multi-region factorial heavy-metal metabolism model (FHMM), in which multiregional input-output analysis quantifies direct and embodied emissions, ecological network analysis diagnoses the structure of the emission network, factorial analysis quantifies the response of the network when the emissions of several metals change together, and K-means clustering groups regions for differentiated management; their integration alone delivers these four capabilities. FHMM is applied to the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), China, covering Pb, Hg, Cd, Cr, and As across 42 sectors and 11 regions. The empirical results are baseline estimates for 2015, describing the system before the principal environmental instruments introduced since then. The results indicate that: (1) Industrial aquatic HMEs exhibit strong spatial heterogeneity, with Hunan accounting for about 34% of the YREB total, approximately 125 t. (2) In Hunan, Hubei, and Jiangxi, indirect HMEs exceed direct HMEs, highlighting supply-chain contributions. (3) Interregional linkages are structurally asymmetric, with upstream regions exerting strong influence and transmission dominated by resource- and heavy-industry sectors. (4) The network synergism index responds most strongly to As in Hunan (57.0% of the total variance), while Cd, Pb, and Hg in Hunan and Cr in Zhejiang account for the remainder, with marked cross-metal interactions. These findings support targeted, region-specific HME management within YREB, with relevance for other regions facing similar challenges.

title: Nonlinear response mechanisms and ecological management zonation of ecosystem health based on XGBoost-SHAP explainable machine learning
abstract: Rapid urbanization has led to habitat fragmentation and the decline of ecological functions in ecologically fragile areas, while existing analyses of the spatiotemporal driving mechanisms of ecosystem health (EH) can hardly capture the nonlinear threshold effects and transmission pathways of multiple factors. Based on the Vigor-Organization-Resilience-Ecosystem Services (VORS) model, this study analyzed the spatiotemporal patterns of EH in the Fujian Delta Region (FDR) from 2000 to 2020, introduced the XGBoost-SHAP model to identify the threshold effects and nonlinear response patterns of driving factors, used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze the direct and indirect transmission pathways of natural and socioeconomic factors, and further explored ecological management zoning and optimization pathways under a “status-trend” dual framework. The results showed that: (1) from 2000 to 2020, the EH level in the FDR declined year by year, exhibiting an overall spatial pattern of “high in the west and low in the east”; (2) over the 20 years, the driving factors of EH shifted from being dominated by ecological factors to a coupled influence of natural and economic factors, with each factor exhibiting distinct nonlinear threshold effects, and this shift should be interpreted with caution; (3) complex cascading transmission mechanisms existed among the driving factors, with vegetation playing a partial mediating role between topography and EH; and (4) the FDR was classified into four major ecological management zones, the Ecological Conservation Zone, the Ecological Balancing Zone, the Ecological Restoration Zone, and the Ecological Reshaping Zone. By coupling the VORS, InVEST, XGBoost-SHAP, and PLS-SEM models, this study systematically revealed the spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear threshold effects of EH in the FDR from 2000 to 2020 and constructed ecological management zones under the “status-trend” dual framework, providing theoretical references for EH assessment and differentiated territorial spatial optimization in ecologically fragile areas along the southeastern coast.

title: Coastal lagoons as active biogeochemical reactors: Anthropogenic nitrogen cascades drive N2O emission patterns from local hotspots to regional heterogeneity
abstract: Coastal lagoons act as critical biogeochemical reactors within the land-ocean aquatic continuum (LOAC), processing anthropogenic nitrogen and releasing nitrous oxide (N 2 O). However, the multi-scale mechanisms driving N 2 O emissions from local hotspots to regional patterns remain poorly constrained. Here, we employ a “local-regional” scale investigation framework to elucidate the spatiotemporal dynamics and drivers of N 2 O emissions in subtropical coastal lagoons of South China. At local scale (Pinqing Lagoon), both the concentrations and fluxes of N 2 O exhibit a consistent land-to-sea decreasing gradient. The N 2 O emissions peak during the early wet season (19.00 μmol m −2 d −1 ). Statistical modeling identifies ammonium (NH 4 + -N), rather than nitrate, as the primary driver, suggesting that N 2 O production in this coastal lagoon is consistent with NH 4 + -associated pathways. At regional scale (20 coastal lagoons), profound spatial heterogeneity in N 2 O fluxes (0.16 to 63.23 μmol m −2 d −1 ) is observed across these lagoons. Hierarchical partitioning reveal that watershed land use and nitrogen nutrients, rather than in-situ physicochemical properties, fundamentally determine these regional emission configurations. Furthermore, a continuous land-to-sea decreasing spatial pattern of N 2 O (Reservoirs > Rivers > Coastal Lagoons > Estuaries > Bays > Continental Shelves) is revealed in the South China region by embedding our dataset into the broader LOAC. These findings empirically substantiate that the anthropogenic nitrogen cascade fundamentally shapes coastal N 2 O emission patterns. We highlight the critical necessity of explicitly differentiating hydrologically restricted coastal lagoons from open estuaries in global greenhouse gas inventories, and emphasize that effective climate mitigation requires source-oriented interventions targeting watershed land use.

title: Cross-species evaluation: Reindeer as an ecological evaluator of a satellite-based lichen cover map
abstract: Accurate maps of resources are important tools in wildlife and animal range management yet validating them across large spatial extents remains a challenge. We leveraged fine-scale GPS tracking of consumers and a strong consumer-resource relationship to perform large-scale validation of a resource map. Our aim was to present the first high-resolution ground lichen cover map for the Sámi reindeer winter grazing area in Sweden, and to complement traditional model validation methods by using 680,000 reindeer GPS relocations and the consumer-resource relationship between reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus) and ground lichens for ecological validation. We expected a successful map to be reflected in the reindeer use of lichen, and that predicted lichen cover would be a significant predictor in habitat selection models. The map was produced using a Generalised Additive Model trained on National Forest Inventory field data with Sentinel-2 imagery, forest variables, and soil type as predictors. The model explained 57.4% of the total variance in lichen cover. Our analyses supported both expectations: hurdle models showed that reindeer-used locations were 44% more likely to have predicted lichen cover and had 15% more predicted lichen cover than available locations. Integrated step-selection analyses confirmed consistent selection for predicted lichen cover, and adding the lichen map outperformed a simpler model including topographic and movement variables (mean ΔAIC = -47.5). Best performance was achieved combining predicted lichen cover with land cover classification (mean ΔAIC = -145.1). Our cross-species validation approach offers a complement to traditional statistical validation, applicable to other systems with strong consumer-resource relationships.

title: Comparison of Sentinel of Seabed and Relative Benthic Status indicators' performance to assess the impact of bottom trawling on the epi-benthic communities in an overexploited Mediterranean basin
abstract: Trawl fishing activities are considered one of the main anthropogenic causes of disturbance and degradation of benthic habitats. Several risk-based indicators have been developed to assess trawling impacts on benthic communities. In this study, the Sentinel of Seabed (SoS) and the Relative Benthic Status (RBS) indicators were applied and compared to evaluate the impact of trawling on mega-epibenthic communities in the Adriatic Sea, one of the basins most impacted by bottom trawling. Biomass data were used to calculate sensitivity indices and then evaluate their responses to fishing pressure. The two risk-based assessments were also compared in terms of habitat sensitivity and impact estimates. Both the Sentinel of Seabed and the Relative Benthic Status declined sharply with increasing trawling pressure. They consistently identified muddy habitats as the most impacted, with an 88% loss of sentinel species and the lowest RBS values. The estimated quality thresholds for both approaches indicated a highly impacted scenario in the Northern Adriatic Sea, underscoring an urgent need to adopt adequate management measures to achieve Good Environmental Status (GES sensu Marine Strategy Directive 2008/56/EC). In addition, when quality thresholds are expressed as pressure thresholds, differences are observed between indicators, showing that SoS is more conservative, identifying lower trawling pressure as causing a shift from good to non-good status. Our findings underscore the importance of adopting integrated approaches that combine multiple indicators to evaluate sea floor integrity and support effective measures for a specific region in compliance with the requirements of the Marine Strategy Framework Directive. Such approach could be further extended to assess the condition of soft sediment habitats in the context of the Nature Restoration Regulation (Reg. EU 2024/1991).

title: Self-sustainability status indicators of vegetation stands and types utilising Potential Natural Vegetation estimations
abstract: Optimising conservation and restoration efforts calls for detailed assessment on the potential self-sustainability of vegetation types. We propose an indicator framework relying on matches and mismatches between predicted distributions of vegetation types and observed distributions. We examined the utility of all combinations of predicted and observed values, however, we introduced a five-rank scale to categorise predictions rather than simple presence/absence outputs. This yielded 10 possible indicator combinations, out of which nine was present in the dataset. We tested the indicators' applicability using countrywide observed vegetation data and potential natural vegetation estimates for Hungary. Indicators were subjected to Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to examine the interrelationships as well as mapped in space habitat-wise and as aggregated (synthetic) maps across vegetation types. Indicators were identified in relation to levels of unsuitability, uncertain presence, levels of potentiality, extinction debt and levels of self-sustainability in existing stands. Each indicator was found to correspond to an individual interpretation in terms of ecological insight (including potentiality and vegetation inertia), conservation and restoration optimisation. PCA results reinforced the finding with the first three components explaining 90% and 80% of the variation for the absolute count and relative count based indices respectively. Map representations proved to be informative on conservation and restoration priorities habitat-wise. Furthermore, our indices supported identification of conservation and restoration hotspots, as well as provided insights about the vulnerability of individual vegetation types. Identification of localities and spatial concentration of areas with predominantly self-sustaining or threatened vegetation has potential to support for conservation and restoration decisions.

title: Atmospheric hydrothermal dynamics influence vegetation drought resistance in the Mu Us Sandy Land
abstract: The Mu Us Sandy Land (MUSL) is a typical ecologically fragile region in northern China. Large-scale ecological restoration projects have improved regional vegetation coverage while potentially modifying hydrological processes, making it necessary to further evaluate the drought characteristics and vegetation responses to drought. In this study, three drought indices were applied to characterize drought variations from 2000 to 2022, and the Standardized Evapotranspiration Deficit Index (SEDI) was identified as the most suitable indicator in MUSL. Moreover, vegetation dynamics were represented using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and gross primary productivity (GPP), which were further used to quantify vegetation drought resistance. The results showed that SEDI significantly increased at a rate of 0.08 per year ( P < 0.05), reflecting a notable wetting trend in the region, which was generally favorable for vegetation growth. However, eight drought years with varying severity were identified during the study period, and vegetation responses to drought exhibited spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Overall, vegetation drought resistance significantly decreased with increasing drought severity ( P < 0.05); however, considerable differences in vegetation responses and drought resistance remained among different years within the same drought severity. Further analyses indicated that atmospheric hydrothermal conditions during the growing season were key factors explaining variations in vegetation drought resistance. The growing-season maximum temperature anomalies (TMXano) emerged as the most significant explanatory factor, accounting for 63.4% of the variance ( P < 0.05). Increased TMXano and potential evapotranspiration anomalies (PETano) diminished vegetation drought resistance, while the positive effects of precipitation anomalies (PREano) and SEDI increases were relatively limited. This study highlights the important role of growing-season hydrothermal conditions in influencing vegetation drought resistance in arid and semiarid sandy regions, providing scientific insights for drought risk assessment and sustainable ecosystem management in future ecological restoration scenarios.

title: Assessing Long-term ecological environment quality dynamics and anthropogenic disturbance in the lower Jinsha River basin (LJRB): Integrating MRSEI with Hurst-based persistence analysis
abstract: The Lower Jinsha River Basin (LJRB) has experienced decades of concurrent cascade hydropower construction, mineral exploitation and large-scale Grain for Green (GFG) restoration. Comprehensive long-term multi-dimensional assessments linking these overlapping human activities to basin ecological sustainability remain limited in existing research. This study develops an integrated evaluation framework built on a 35-year (1991–2025) Modified Remote Sensing Ecological Index (MRSEI) dataset, Hurst exponent persistence analysis, a composite Ecological Stability Index (ESI) developed for this study, and Convergent Cross Mapping (CCM) causal attribution to quantify long-term ecological trajectories and identify the ecological regime shift. Results show sustained basin-wide ecological improvement with the mean MRSEI rising from 0.201 to 0.386, with Sen's slope = 0.0055 yr −1 and Kendall's τ = 0.476 ( p < 0.01). Three phases of uninterrupted MRSEI growth are distinguished throughout the study timeline: slow baseline improvement from 1991 to 2000, moderate steady gains between 2001 and 2012, and notably accelerated ecological recovery after 2012 coinciding with reservoir impoundments where EVI and WET increased markedly after reservoir impoundment, by 0.456 and 0.567, respectively. While 93.08% of the basin presents positive MRSEI trends, only 42.51% corresponds to stable long-term recovery; 45.21% displays anti-persistent trajectories (Hurst <0.5), a latent vulnerability that single-indicator trend analysis may not identify. Mining disturbance follows a clear distance-decay gradient (R 2 = 0.63), with functional ecosystem recovery observable 8–10 km from open-pit mine sites. CCM analysis confirms reservoir impoundment as the primary trigger of post-2012 ecological improvement (ρ = 0.617), with cross-map skill 39.3% stronger than GFG revegetation (ρ = 0.443) and 22.7% greater than the reverse feedback pathway (ρ = 0.503). Geodetector modelling shows the interaction between land cover and evapotranspiration delivers the highest explanatory power (q = 0.534), exceeding all single independent variables and reflecting coupled land-water-climate feedbacks shaping regional ecological conditions. The integrated MRSEI–ESI workflow supports delineation of spatial management zones, including stable conservation areas, mining degradation corridors, and empirical 2 km disturbance buffers around reservoirs and mine sites. This analytical framework may be adapted to assess ecological sustainability in other mountain river basins undergoing rapid anthropogenic transformation.

title: Critical climate thresholds and yield responses vary across wheat agro-climatic systems: Evidence from India
abstract: Assessing climate risks to crops needs understanding how thresholds and interactions vary in different environments. However, most assessments use generalized thresholds, even though crop responses differ by region, growth stage, and climate. This study applied an explainable machine-learning framework to identify region- and stage-specific climatic tipping points, post-tipping-point yield sensitivities, and compound climate interactions governing wheat productivity across contrasting agro-climatic regions.,Results revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in climatic sensitivity. Nighttime temperature during the vegetative and early reproductive stages emerged as the dominant climatic constraint across most regions. Corresponding tipping points ranged from approximately 10.5°C in cool semi-arid systems to approximately 16°C in tropical environments, whereas the highland region exhibited positive yield responses above approximately 8°C, indicating substantial regional differences in thermal adaptation under current climatic conditions. Yield sensitivity beyond these tipping points also varied significantly, with the strongest response observed in the cool semi-arid region (approximately 6% yield loss per °C) and the weakest response in the humid plains (approximately 1% per °C).,Interaction analyses further demonstrated that wheat responses cannot be explained by individual climatic drivers alone. Despite increasingly negative impacts of individual limiting variables beyond tipping points, many compound interactions remained positive, indicating that the continuity of climatic conditions across consecutive growth stages can partially buffer thermal stress. In addition, abrupt transitions across tipping-point boundaries generated strong negative interactions and substantial yield penalties. These findings suggest that wheat productivity is more sensitive to thermal instability than to gradual warming itself.,Overall, the results demonstrate that wheat productivity is governed by region-specific climate tipping points, different post-tipping responses, and climate interactions. Including these spatial climatic limits and responses may enhance climate-risk assessment and help create targeted adaptation strategies amid rising variability and warming.

title: Teinopalpus aureus, an indicator species of Asian montane evergreen broad-leaved forests: a deep learning-based case study on butterfly hilltopping
abstract: Ecological indicator is critical to build a dialogue with ecosystems, and such available tools are shortage for montane forest ecosystem in Asia. The Golden Kaiserihind, Teinopalpus aureus , a flagship butterfly, is widely recognized as a key indicator of forest integrity in Asian montane regions, but the related empirical research remains limited due to its strict habitat requirements and lower encounter rate. This study employed surveillance cameras at mountaintop aggregated sites to record diurnal (05:00-18:00) hilltopping behavior videos. And it also integrated multiple deep learning methodologies, including You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLOv11) for individual detection and localization, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for extracting temporal metadata from sequential frames, and InceptionV3 for species classification, to identify and collect dynamic data on hilltopping activity (date, time, frequency, etc.) for T. aureus and a sympatric butterfly, Graphium cloanthus . The two binary recognition models achieved predicted probabilities of 0.955 and 0.967, respectively. We calculated niche breadth and examined niche differentiation by integrating hilltopping behavior data with site-specific microenvironmental variables (e.g. temperature, relative humidity, and light intensity), alongside an analysis of the key environmental contributors identified by species distribution models (SDMs). Results indicated that T. aureus occupies a significantly narrower ecological niche than G. cloanthus , and its niche was even constricted from the spring to the summer generation. T. aureus initiated hilltopping at 05:30 am, peaking at 06:40 am in summer, 2 hours and 28 minutes earlier than the spring generation. This behavior ceased up to 4 hours before that of G. cloanthus . Furthermore, T. aureus exhibited a strict preference for cool temperatures (18.5-20.3°C) and high relative humidity (>95%), whereas G. cloanthus showed no specific preference and remained active under hot conditions (30-35°C). These findings underscore the high sensitivity of T. aureus to montane environmental fluctuations, indicating that its persistence is highly depended on the stability of montane evergreen broad-leaved forests. We propose incorporating hilltopping and other aggregation behaviors into long-term butterfly monitoring programs. By combining modern surveillance equipment with the developed deep learning models, video streams can be analyzed automatically to generates dynamic data for T. aureus and other highly-sensitive butterfly indicators, thus building a dialogue bridge with the ecosystem and enabling the timely detection of signals related to biodiversity loss or recovery.

title: The dual impact of global urban expansion on soil salinization from 2000 to 2020
abstract: Soil salinization is a major form of land degradation threatening ecosystem sustainability worldwide, yet the independent effects of urban expansion on soil salinity remain poorly understood because they are often confounded by natural climatic variability. To address this issue, this study investigated urban expansion across 1443 major cities worldwide using 1-km resolution global urban expansion and soil salinity datasets from 2000 to 2020. We developed a Salinity Disturbance Index (SDI) by integrating multiple climatic background factors to distinguish the independent salinity aggravation and salinity alleviation of urban expansion on soil salinity. Results showed that global urban expansion exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with larger expansion areas concentrated in temperate and continental regions, whereas faster expansion rates mainly occurred in tropical regions. Overall, urban expansion alleviated soil salinization over 8597 km 2 , substantially exceeding the area where salinization was aggravated (5789 km 2 ). Cities experiencing larger expansion areas and faster expansion rates exhibited markedly stronger soil salinity responses, indicating that increasing urbanization intensity amplified both salinity alleviation and salinity aggravation. Transportation accessibility, vegetation dynamics, soil properties, and climatic factors were identified as the dominant drivers of these dual effects, although their relative importance varied among climate zones. By explicitly separating anthropogenic disturbances from natural environmental variability, this study provides the first global assessment of the dual impacts of urban expansion on soil salinization and offers new insights for sustainable urban planning and salinity management.

title: Multi-objective dynamic optimization of urban water resources in arid regions: Identifying robust efficiency-driven pathways under climate and policy environments
abstract: Water scarcity in arid urban regions is intensifying under the combined impacts of climate change and urbanization. However, few studies have explicitly integrated climate change and policy regulation into a dynamic optimization framework with quantified uncertainty, limiting the capacity to support robust decision-making in arid regions. This study develops a coupled system dynamics (SD) and multi-objective dynamic optimization model for Hami, a typical arid city in Northwest China, driven by both climate change and policy regulation. The model performs dynamic year-by-year optimization of water resource allocation and quantifies the associated interannual uncertainty. Four climate scenarios (baseline, SSP126, SSP245, SSP585) and four policy pathways—business-as-usual (BAU), economic growth (EG), technological advancement (TA), and environmental protection (EP)—are combined into 16 scenarios for systematic evaluation. Results show that the TA pathway, centered on water-saving technology upgrades, exhibits clear efficiency-driven features: it achieves the highest improvement in water supply-demand balance (3.9%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.3%–5.5%) at the lowest cost increase (46.6%, 95%CI 39.2%–54.0%), with the smallest comprehensive uncertainty among the four pathways. In contrast, the EG pathway incurs excessive cost (annual average 0.97 × 10 8 ¥), and the EP pathway suffers from insufficient robustness. A three-dimensional trade-off analysis further confirms that the TA pathway maintains low-cost and high-robustness advantages across multiple climate scenarios, representing the globally optimal strategy under climate change. This study provides a quantifiable framework for adaptive urban water resources management in arid regions.

title: Differences in grassland dynamics and assessment of drought sensitivity and vulnerability in Central Asia
abstract: Although Central Asian grasslands have undergone substantial greening and productivity gains over recent decades under accelerating climate warming, how leaf area index (LAI) and gross primary productivity (GPP) respond to drought across multiple timescales, including cumulative effects, lagged effects, sensitivity, and vulnerability, remains poorly characterized along aridity gradients. Here, integrating multi-source LAI datasets and GPP products spanning 1982–2020, we revealed that Central Asian grassland LAI and GPP increased at rates of 0.002 m 2 m −2 a −1 and 0.66 gC m −2 a −1 , respectively, with semi-arid regions contributing disproportionately (51.97% and 53.09% of total LAI and GPP gains).
