Incorporating within-year temporal structure alongside annual production can improve the characterization of large-scale recovery and the interpretation of multi-product satellite assessments. • Counterfactual 8-day GPP trajectories were reconstructed for 7197 fires in China. • Annual GPP converged faster than within-year production allocation after fire. • Early-phase effects remained lower than core-phase effects across both GPP products. • Absolute GPP effects were product sensitive, unlike within-year pattern direction. • Annual totals alone incompletely characterize post-fire productivity recovery.

title: Forest disturbance dynamics in Bavaria: A novel approach for identifying fragmentation processes based on canopy cover loss and morphological image processing
abstract: Unprecedented canopy loss has become a feature of central European temperate forests in recent years and is expected to continue. Bavaria, the largest and most forested state in Germany lost 146,320 ha from September 2017 – July 2025. To investigate the dynamics of forest disturbance, we classified interior, exterior, and convergent fragmentation processes (perimeter loss, shrinkage, perforation, and bisection) over an 8-year study period by intersecting the Forest Canopy Cover Loss (FCCL) dataset with a spatial classification using morphological image processing of 10 m forest mask rasters. We delineated 762,602 individual clusters of forest canopy loss, ranging in size from 0.01 to 1228 ha. The largest clusters were identified as bisection processes and were initiated early in the study period and contained multiple sub-clusters, suggesting expansion and merging of disturbance events. Fragmentation process labeling was sensitive to the edge depth, however the most robust processes were perforation, which covered 43% of total cluster area and perimeter loss (1.8%). Although nearly 34% of forest core areas transitioned into edge zones due to perforations, perimeters were the most relatively affected zone, whereby >7% of canopy was lost. While the number of small forests (‘Islets’) increased by 167.9%, core forest area declined along with a 12.6% decrease in the number of patches. This pattern suggests perimeter loss and bisection of core forests. Because fragmentation processes precipitate localized canopy restructuring and landscape reconfiguration, which have distinct ecological outcomes, this approach can be further applied both for spatially-explicit modeling of forest disturbance and as an indicator for monitoring habitats and biodiversity.

title: Water allocation leveraging multi-reservoir operation for arid basins with high conveyance losses: Trade-off between efficiency and equity
abstract: Balancing efficiency and equity in water allocation remains a major challenge in water-scarce arid basins, especially due to substantial conveyance losses along natural river channels. A key objective is to ensure equitable water supply between upstream and downstream users while reducing evaporation and seepage losses during long-distance conveyance, thereby improving overall water use efficiency. This study develops a water allocation model that balances efficiency and equity by leveraging multi-reservoir cooperation in arid basins with high conveyance losses. Three water allocation scenarios are designed: efficiency-prioritized, equity-prioritized, and a balanced approach integrating both objectives. The Tarim River Basin, the largest inland river basin in China, is selected as the study area. Results indicate that the efficiency-prioritized scenario yields the lowest annual basin-wide irrigation shortage (6 × 10 8 m 3 ), but suffers from extreme spatial disparities, with shortage rate differences reaching 30.1% among irrigation districts. Conversely, while the equity-prioritized scenario achieves absolute fairness, it increases conveyance losses to 67 × 10 8 m 3 (26% of total basin inflow). This leads to a 69.8% surge in total water shortages compared to the efficiency scenario, signaling a sharp decline in overall efficiency. The balanced approach offers a viable compromise, maintaining a moderate shortage rate difference of 8.6% while keeping conveyance losses at 63.66 × 10 8 m 3 . Based on these results, this study proposes two management recommendations for water allocation in arid basins with high conveyance losses: (i) each user should prioritize water from the nearest river section to reduce conveyance losses, and (ii) for users served by multiple sources, priority should be given to rivers with lower conveyance loss rates. These findings provide a practical framework for water resources management in arid basins affected by high conveyance losses.

title: A comparative study of long-term historical soil erosion in the four major Mollisols regions of the world
abstract: The Mollisols are among the world's most fertile soils but are increasingly threatened by erosion due to intensive cultivation and climate change. Despite their importance for global food production, the long-term dynamics of soil erosion in the four major Mollisols regions of the world as well as their comparisons and the control factors remain poorly understood. The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) was applied to estimate historical soil erosion from the 1900s to the 2020s across the four major global Mollisols regions, including the Mississippi Plain (MSP), the Northeast China Plain (NEC), the Pampas Plain (PP), and the Ukrainian Plain (UP). Scenario analysis, machine learning, and driver separation approaches were combined to quantify the contributions of driving forces to soil erosion during the past over 100 years. The results indicate that soil erosion has intensified across all regions during the past century. The NEC experienced the largest erosion intensity and increase, with mean erosion rates rising from 5 to 18.6 t·ha −1 ·yr −1 and a mean decadal increase of 0.95 t·ha −1 ·yr −1 , followed by the MSP (0.12 t·ha −1 ·yr −1 per decade), UP (0.11 t·ha −1 ·yr −1 per decade), and PP (0.10 t·ha −1 ·yr −1 per decade). Spatially, erosion expansion was widespread for all the four regions, particularly in mountainous and hilly landscapes, and LS-factor explained 35–55% of erosion variability. Scenario analysis indicated that land use change controlled long-term erosion trends in the NEC, climate-driven changes reproduced most of the observed increases in the UP, while both greatly affected erosion dynamics in the PP. In the MSP, erosion trajectories transitioned from land-use dominance in the early 20th century to increasing climate influence after the 1970s. These findings emphasize the urgent need for region-specific strategies to mitigate erosion risks in the four major Mollisols regions, especially for NEC.

title: Comparison of eDNA, bulk-community metabarcoding, and morphological identification approaches for assessing stream macroinvertebrate communities
abstract: High-throughput sequencing enables the parallel sequencing of community samples, including environmental DNA (eDNA), making metabarcoding a widely used tool for biodiversity assessment. However, confounding factors such as molecular techniques and gaps in taxonomic reference databases pose challenges for its application in biomonitoring of benthic macroinvertebrates. In this study, we compared eDNA metabarcoding against bulk-community metabarcoding and morphological identification approach from the collected macroinvertebrates in Shimanto and Niyodo Rivers in Shikoku, Japan. We also evaluated the relationship between benthic macroinvertebrate communities and environmental factors. We reported higher alpha diversity with bulk-community metabarcoding than with morphological identification and eDNA metabarcoding. Dry mass correlated more strongly than abundance with the number of reads in the bulk-community obtained with the metabarcoding approach. Our study highlights bulk-community metabarcoding as a potential tool for macroinvertebrates biodiversity assessment and monitoring.

title: Phosphorus limitation is associated with lower nitrification potential and rhizosphere soil δ15N along an Arid Mountain elevational gradient
abstract: Soil 15 N natural abundance (δ 15 N) has been widely used as an integrative indicator of nitrogen cycling. Although nitrogen dynamics are highly sensitive to aridity, the linkages between microorganisms—as key drivers of nitrogen transformation—and rhizosphere soil δ 15 N in arid ecosystems remain poorly understood. In this study, we conducted a systematic investigation in the Helan Mountains of northwestern China, a typical temperate arid mountain ecosystem. We integrated metagenomics, enzyme activity assays, nitrogen transformation rate measurements, and δ 15 N analyses on rhizosphere soils of 15 dominant plant species distributed along an elevational gradient from 1300 to 2900 m. The results showed that rhizosphere soil δ 15 N and net nitrification potential decreased with increasing elevation. Soil carbon-to‑phosphorus and nitrogen-to‑phosphorus ratios increased, whereas total phosphorus content decreased. Enzyme vector analysis indicated microbial phosphorus limitation across all study sites, intensifying with elevation. Metagenomic analysis revealed higher abundances of phosphorus-acquisition genes, but lower archaeal nitrification gene abundance at higher elevations. Random forest and structural equation modeling analyses identified significant correlations between rhizosphere soil δ 15 N and both net nitrification potential and soil stoichiometric ratios. Partial correlation analysis showed that net nitrification rate was significantly correlated with the bacterial, archaeal, and fungal community composition. Overall, along the elevational gradient, soil δ 15 N, net nitrification rate, stoichiometric ratios, nitrification functional genes, and microbial community composition exhibited coordinated variation patterns. This provides a basis for understanding nitrogen cycling processes and informing future nitrogen management strategies in arid mountain ecosystems.

title: Linking ecological resilience assessment and ecological network structure for landscape optimization in fragile alpine mountain regions: A case study of southeastern Tibet
abstract: In fragile alpine mountain regions, ecological stability depends not only on ecosystem condition but also on the capacity of landscapes to maintain ecological connectivity under complex environmental constraints. Southeastern Tibet, located on the southeastern margin of the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau, provides an ideal case for investigating the relationship between ecological resilience and ecological network structure because of its highly heterogeneous terrain and ecological sensitivity. This study developed an integrated analytical framework linking ecological resilience assessment with ecological network analysis for landscape optimization. A PSR-based ecological resilience proxy was established for 2010, 2015, and 2020 using indicators describing landscape disturbance, landscape structure, and ecosystem services. The 2020 resilience proxy was subsequently integrated with topographic, land-use, vegetation, hydrological, and human-disturbance factors to construct a comprehensive ecological resistance surface, from which core ecological sources, potential structural corridors, and topography-related structural nodes were identified and their relative importance was evaluated. The results showed that ecological pressure remained generally low, with low-pressure zones accounting for more than 81% of all grid cells throughout the study period. Ecological state remained comparatively high, although high-state areas declined in 2015 before partially recovering in 2020. Ecological response remained at medium to high levels, whereas comprehensive ecological resilience continued to be dominated by low- and moderate-resilience classes, with high-resilience areas showing a persistent contraction trend. The identified ecological network comprised 11 core ecological sources, 3686 potential structural corridors, and 768 ecological nodes, including 1322 important corridors and 281 important nodes. By explicitly linking resilience assessment with ecological network identification, this study provides planning-relevant evidence for landscape optimization and ecological planning in fragile alpine mountain regions.

title: Vertical variation of ecosystem services supply-demand relationship: Identifying ecological dynamic pattern in the mountainous area of greater Khingan range region, China
abstract: Under global warming, mountainous areas face widespread degradation of ecosystem services (ES), leading to imbalance between ecosystem services supply and demand (ESSD). Mountainous areas are characterized by vertical variation. However, vertical variation of ESSD in mountainous areas remains unclear, urgently requiring to be investigated. Therefore, this study, taking the Greater Khingan Range Region (GKR region), a typical mountainous area with vertical variation , as the study area, constructed an assessment framework for evaluating the vertical variation of ESSD along the elevation zones divided by tree-ring width from 2000 to 2020. Driving factors of ESs in each elevation zones was analyzed through geographical detector. The ecological dynamic pattern along the elevation zones of ESs was then evaluated based on the assessment of ESSD. The results showed that: the ESSD of the GKR region exhibited vertical variation, with spatial mismatch of water yield and soil conservation reduced as the elevation zones increasing; Precipitation is a key driver for ESSD in each elevation zone and the explanatory power of other drivers exhibits vertical variation; Water yield within high elevation zone showed an improvement characteristic of ecological dynamic pattern, habitat quality within low and mid elevation zones showed a significant deterioration characteristic of ecological dynamic pattern. These findings highlight the importance of formulating management measures along the elevational gradient and offer a novelly vertical perspective for investigating supply-demand relationships of ESs in mountain regions.

title: Organic matter promotes freshwater dinoflagellate blooms by supporting mixotrophic growth
abstract: Trophic-state indicators are widely used to assess phytoplankton bloom risk, but their ability to capture freshwater dinoflagellate blooms remains uncertain. Long-term monitoring of Lake Erhai has shown that trophic state have changed little since 2003, and dinoflagellate biomass began to increase in 2016, which was also the year that organic matter concentrations began to increase significantly. These contrasting patterns indicate that trophic-state metrics alone did not adequately reflect the increasing risk of dinoflagellate blooms. Heterotrophic growth supported by organic matter may be a key trigger of dinoflagellate blooms in Lake Erhai. This study highlights the potential value of organic matter as a complementary indicator alongside conventional trophic-state metrics for assessing freshwater dinoflagellate bloom risk, and suggests that managers should reduce the load of organic matter into the lake to mitigate dinoflagellate bloom risks.

title: Regional stability, local vulnerability: GeoShapley-based diagnosis and planning translation of water retention in Southwest China
abstract: Water retention (WR) is a core hydrologic ecosystem service, but planning-oriented assessment often relies on mean-state maps that obscure local trajectories and explanatory context. We examine modelled WR in Southwest China from 2000 to 2024 by linking annual WR trend diagnosis, GeoShapley-based trend explanation and county translation. Mean WR suggests regional stability, whereas coefficient of variation and raster trend diagnostics reveal strong local heterogeneity in variability, direction and significance. Throughout, we use regional stability for the weakly changing aggregate signal and local vulnerability for counties that combine declining Sen slopes and significant decreasing pixels. GeoShapley values for the WR Sen slope model identify changes in annual precipitation and actual evapotranspiration, saturated hydraulic conductivity and the geographic component as leading contributors to heterogeneity in the modelled WR trend. Continuous county trend-status vectors distinguish maintained or improving and degrading status, while county GeoShapley vectors define four explanatory contexts. Crossing these two axes yields eight county-level management units that keep change status and explanatory setting visible together. The study shows that WR evidence becomes more useful for regional planning when mean state, temporal trajectory and model-based explanatory context are diagnosed separately before being translated to administrative units, especially in complex mountain regions.

title: An evidence-gated multi-taxon framework maps invasion evidence, climate-linked dynamics and surveillance priorities across China
abstract: National invasion assessments combine observation systems whose spatial, temporal and taxonomic structure can be mistaken for ecological signal. We developed an evidence-gated, multi-taxon framework linking candidate screening, route-specific atlas construction, detected expansion, climate-velocity comparison, baseline suitability modelling and surveillance prioritisation across China. Of 120 candidates, 88 species entered a five-group atlas. Evidence occurred in 12,545 of 15,800 25-km land cells, but patterns depended on evidence route and taxonomic composition. Administrative-only support closely matched the union atlas (Spearman ρ = 0.996; top-decile Jaccard = 0.919), whereas point-only agreement was lower (ρ = 0.373; Jaccard = 0.226), and excluding plants reduced cell-level agreement to ρ = 0.256. Observation-context models failed spatially blocked calibration and were rejected. Evidence-qualified subsets retained 43 dynamic, 43 velocity and 40 invasion-detection velocity-ratio (IVR) species; 25- and 50-km IVR rankings remained broadly concordant with native estimates (ρ = 0.801–0.989). Across 45 baseline-model species, accessibility/reporting proxies yielded modest, non-universal gains over climate-only models. A 51-species priority construct (A × E × X × G; 4210 species-grid rows; 2144 ranked cells) produced nested tiers; sensitivity analyses showed broad rank structure was more stable than hotspot membership. Reclassification under S* = 0.90P + 0.10D identified 176 stable-core, 39 newly elevated and 39 relaxed cells. By keeping evidence, suitability proxies and priorities distinct, the framework supports auditable surveillance without equating detected evidence with true arrival, absence, causal spread or realised impact.

title: Integrating UAV-LiDAR derived structural metrics and machine learning to enhance fine-scale occurrence pattern identification of an endangered montane conifer
abstract: Rapid climate warming and intensifying anthropogenic disturbances have created an increasingly urgent need for fine-scale spatial information to support the conservation of endangered montane plant species. Traditional approaches for identifying species occurrence patterns primarily rely on two-dimensional environmental predictors, such as topography, vegetation indices, and soil variables. While these variables characterize broad environmental gradients, they often fail to capture stand-scale structural heterogeneity in complex montane forests. In this study, we focused on Tsuga chinensis var. tchekiangensis , a relict conifer threatened by climate change and habitat fragmentation, to evaluate whether forest structural metrics derived from unmanned aerial vehicle-based light detection and ranging (UAV-LiDAR) data could improve the identification of fine-scale occurrence patterns. We extracted canopy height, canopy relief ratio, gap fraction, and vertical stratification from UAV-LiDAR data and integrated these metrics with terrain, vegetation indices, soil type, and field occurrence records to construct MaxEnt, Random Forest, and XGBoost models. Compared with models based solely on conventional two-dimensional predictors, models incorporating LiDAR-derived structural metrics consistently improved discrimination performance across algorithms, particularly under spatial block validation. MaxEnt showed the most stable performance under spatially independent evaluation, whereas XGBoost exhibited strong nonlinear discrimination ability after integrating LiDAR variables. The XGBoost model with LiDAR-derived structural metrics achieved an AUC of 0.75 ± 0.04 and a TSS of 0.26 ± 0.08 under repeated random validation, while maintaining an AUC of 0.73 ± 0.12 under spatial block validation. SHAP-based interpretation identified canopy height, canopy relief ratio, elevation, and gap fraction as the most influential variables associated with TC occurrence patterns, with response transitions around canopy height > 13 m, canopy relief ratio of 0.4–0.6, elevation >1530 m, and gap fraction <0.2. Spatial analysis further showed that 124 of 140 recorded occurrence points (88.6%) were located within high occurrence-consistency areas. These findings indicate that UAV-LiDAR derived structural metrics provide valuable fine-scale indicators of occurrence-associated forest structural configurations in complex mountain environments, offering useful support for targeted field surveys, monitoring design, and improved understanding of endangered montane conifer occurrence patterns.

title: Uncovering patterns and trait-based mechanisms of vegetation recovery over three time periods after low-impact seismic line construction in boreal uplands of northern Alberta
abstract: Disturbance acts as an important environmental filter determining which species will persist or establish, depending on their functional traits. Examined here is the clearing of overstory vegetation in linear corridors, specifically, narrow low-impact seismic (LIS) lines constructed to locate oil and gas reserves. We investigate the initial changes in the understory plant community through the consideration of both taxonomic and functional trait composition and characterize the successional trajectory as the ecosystem recovers. We sampled vegetation over a ten-year period (three-, eight-, and thirteen-years post-construction) at an upland forest research site in the Swan Hills region in northwestern Alberta. We found phanerophyte shrubs (primarily Rhododendron groenlandicum), chamaephytes (mostly low shrubs), and bryophytes all declined drastically in cover after the disturbance. Over the sampling period, chamaephytes and bryophytes recovered to the levels similar to those in the adjacent forest. Hemicryptophytes and geophytes (mostly herbaceous species), showed no declines in cover on seismic lines compared to the adjacent forest. We found no differences in the interspecific trait composition of the chamaephyte and herbaceous plant communities in all sampling periods between disturbed and forested conditions. However, intraspecific trait variation (ITV) was found. Two dominant understory species, Cornus canadensis and Vaccinium vitis-idaea, had lower specific leaf area (SLA) under the higher light conditions found on the seismic line than in the adjacent forest. This information contributes to a better understanding of the impact of the disturbance caused by LIS construction and the mechanisms underpinning their regeneration processes in an upland forested ecosystem.

title: An integrated remote sensing framework reveals zone-specific ecological response trajectories to open-pit mining on the Qinghai-Tibet plateau
abstract: Rapid mining expansion on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau threatens its fragile alpine and arid ecosystems, with complex and spatially heterogeneous impacts, underscoring the need for long-term quantitative monitoring to support effective management. To address gaps in prior work that either focused on individual mining sites or relied on coarse assessments, we developed an integrated remote sensing framework that combines fractional vegetation cover (FVC), seasonal-trend decomposition of normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), functional principal component analysis (FPCA), landscape metrics, and the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI). The framework was applied to 30 mines distributed across four ecological zones during 2000–2020 to characterize mining-induced ecological changes. The results showed that (1) the mining footprint expanded by more than eightfold, accompanied by significant vegetation degradation and increased landscape fragmentation, while the RSEI declined markedly faster within mines than in climate-matched buffers; (2) mining was the predominant local driver, producing ecozone-specific disturbance radii that were temporally consistent with mining histories. The disturbance radius was smallest in the temperate desert vegetation zone (TDV) and largest in the alpine vegetation zone of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (Alpine), with impacts typically concentrated within 2–8, km; and (3) ecological responses were highly heterogeneous, exhibiting three trajectories: sustained high-load degradation in the subtropical evergreen broadleaf forest zone (SEBF); degradation followed by partial recovery in Alpine and TDV; and high-fragility volatility in the temperate desert zone (TDD). The framework is scalable and interpretable, enabling ecosystem-sensitive tracking of mining impacts and providing a transferable basis for restoration planning, regulatory enforcement, and adaptive management in vulnerable environments.

title: Temporal variation in soil organic carbon stocks under different land-use and land-cover conditions in a semi-arid region
authors: Lady Daiane Costa de Sousa Martins
Alexandre Maniçoba da Rosa Ferraz Jardim
abstract: Land-use and land-cover changes, combined with the variation in water availability may disrupt the balance between organic matter inputs and outputs in seasonally dry forests, potentially leading to reductions in soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. However, how such temporal dynamics manifest across areas with different disturbance intensities remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study investigated temporal variation in SOC stocks across Caatinga areas under different land-use conditions in the Brazilian semi-arid region. We evaluated three areas with distinct vegetation cover: (i) preserved Caatinga; (ii) regenerating area; and (iii) deforested area. Soil samples for the determination of SOC stocks were collected at two depths (0–15 cm and 15–30 cm), along with undisturbed soil samples for the determination of bulk density. Microclimatic conditions were monitored using a micrometeorological station installed in the Caatinga area. Additionally, soil samples were collected during four distinct periods defined according to local water availability: the rainy-to-dry transition, dry period, dry-to-rainy transition, and rainy period. Our results indicated significant differences in SOC stocks among land-use conditions and across sampling periods. The preserved Caatinga (15.95 Mg ha −1 ) and the regenerating area (25.87 Mg ha −1 ) exhibited the highest SOC stocks, whereas the deforested area (8.62 Mg ha −1 ) showed substantially lower values. Temporal fluctuations in SOC stocks were observed across all areas but were more pronounced in the deforested area, which demonstrated greater sensitivity to microclimatic conditions associated with water availability. When the soil depths were analyzed separately, no significant differences in SOC stocks were observed between the evaluated layers. Principal component analysis indicated that land use influenced soil physical and chemical properties, with the deforested area showing higher bulk density and lower clay and organic carbon contents. We conclude that SOC stocks in the Caatinga ecosystems are more strongly influenced by land use history than by temporal variation in water availability, underscoring the critical role of native vegetation conservation and restoration in maintaining soil quality and ecosystem services in semi-arid environments. Therefore, sustainable land use management practices, combined with conservation and restoration efforts, are essential to mitigate SOC losses and promote the recovery of SOC stocks in Caatinga regions.

title: Disentangling, quantifying and visualising ecosystem services and multifunctionality through a radar plot method
abstract: Ecosystem services guide conservation policies, land management strategies, and environmental governance. Yet, quantifying ecosystem multifunctionality, the capacity of ecosystems to simultaneously support diverse services, remains methodologically challenging and difficult to communicate beyond academia. This paper introduces a novel approach, the radar plot method, to quantify ecosystem multifunctionality, without being constrained by the availability of biodiversity metrics and with an intuitive yet informative graphical output. The method quantifies multifunctionality from radar-plot areas in polar coordinates, enabling direct ecosystem comparisons and hierarchical assessments of subservices and services. The resulting index combines the mean of services and associated variance, distinguishing overall functioning from functional balance. The performance of the radar plot method is evaluated against four widely used multifunctionality methods: averaging, single threshold, multiple thresholds and effective multifunctionality (Hill numbers), using a conceptual dataset. Reanalysis of previously published data further demonstrate the utility of the radar plot method . Across both tests, the radar plot method produced results consistent with existing methods while providing an intuitive graphical representation directly linked to multifunctionality as well as its component functions and their strengths. The radar plot method combines simplicity with a hierarchical framework that captures multiple levels of ecosystem functioning while retaining statistical power and clear visual interpretation. It therefore provides an accessible way to quantify and disentangle ecosystem multifunctionality while strengthening communication between ecological research and environmental decision-making.

title: Plant species diversity and functional diversity relations at different levels of salinization in desert-oasis transition zone of the Hexi Corridor
abstract: Soil salinization, a typical form of land degradation in arid regions, poses a serious threat to ecosystem stability. However, systematic understanding of the coupling relationship between species diversity and functional diversity and its underlying mechanisms along salinization gradients remains limited. In this study, we investigated plant community characteristics and soil physicochemical properties along a salinization gradient in the desert-oasis transition zone of the eastern and central Hexi Corridor in northwestern China. By integrating Random Forest (RF), Redundancy Analysis (RDA), and Partial Least Squares Path Modeling (PLS-PM), we examined variations in species and functional diversity, their interrelationships, and their responses to environmental factors during the salinization process. Results showed that the soil environment exhibited clear ion differentiation along the salinization gradient, with the accumulation of Na + , Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , SO₄ 2− , and Cl − serving as key drivers distinguishing salinization levels. As salinization intensified, species richness and community density decreased significantly. Environmental filtering was strongest at the moderate salinization stage, where species diversity was lowest and functional traits were most convergent. Functional diversity, measured by functional dispersion (FDis) and Rao's quadratic entropy (RaoQ), first decreased and then increased with increasing salinization, indicating a shift in plant trait responses from convergence under moderate stress to divergence under severe stress. Accordingly, the coupling relationship between species diversity and functional diversity exhibited a typical “weak–strong–weak” pattern, indicating that the correspondence between taxonomic and functional dimensions of biodiversity was strongest at intermediate salinization levels and weaker at both low and high salinization levels. PLS-PM results further showed that salinization was directly associated with reduced species diversity and indirectly related to both species and functional diversity through soil pH and total soil salt content (TSC). Overall, these findings suggest that increasing salinization may strengthen environmental filtering and be associated with shifts in community assembly processes, from environmental filtering dominance toward differentiation of salt-tolerance strategies, providing scientific support for vegetation restoration and management of saline-alkali lands in arid regions.

title: From ecological health indicators to priority zoning: A threshold-guided assessment framework for Northeast China
abstract: Regional ecosystem health assessment requires composite indicators that capture spatial heterogeneity across land-use and climate gradients, yet many frameworks still rely on fixed-threshold classifications and linear driver analyses that may overlook nonlinear ecological responses. A key gap remains between detecting statistical breakpoints in ecological indicator responses and translating their uncertainty into spatially explicit priority zones for land management. This study develops an arithmetic Vigor–Organization–Resilience (VOR) Ecological Health Index (EHI) for Northeast China (NEC) using multi-source remote-sensing and geospatial data from 2000 to 2020 across Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, and Inner Mongolia. The framework combines LightGBM-based SHAP interpretation following candidate-model comparison and repeated spatial optimization, segmented regression calibrated using a spatial wild-cluster block bootstrap, and a confidence-interval-based zoning scheme defined by breakpoint bounds (α, τ^, β). EHI increased significantly across NEC from 2000 to 2020 (Mann–Kendall τ = 0.543, p < 0.001; Sen's slope = 0.00101 year −1 ). Liaoning recorded the highest mean EHI, while Inner Mongolia showed the most consistent monotonic increase. Land-use intensity showed the largest model contribution at the NEC scale and in Heilongjiang, Jilin, and Inner Mongolia, whereas precipitation was the dominant contributor in Liaoning. Spatially calibrated segmented regression identified significant threshold-like responses for elevation, slope, precipitation, and LUI across multiple spatial units, with considerable regional variation, while temperature showed more limited support. LUI breakpoints ranged from 0.9223 to 0.9375 and were interpreted as statistical warning signals rather than field-verified ecological tipping points. Arithmetic–geometric VOR sensitivity testing showed only small differences in LUI breakpoint locations, indicating that the identified LUI transitions were relatively robust to the choice of aggregation formulation. Additional LULC-control analysis showed uniformly weak residual EHI–LUI correlations after accounting for categorical land-cover class (|r| ≤ 0.068), suggesting that shared land-cover structure contributed to the observed association. Final integrated zoning was dominated by high-priority areas in Jilin (53.0%), Liaoning (52.4%), and Heilongjiang (48.06%), whereas Inner Mongolia was dominated by low- and medium-priority areas, with HP accounting for 15.3% and no VHP areas identified. Because EHI is derived from remote-sensing and modeled indicators, the proposed priority zones should be interpreted as decision-support outputs pending independent field-based ecological validation.

title: Diagnosing ecological quality dynamics in a karst restoration belt: Trajectory instability, response breakpoints, and adaptive restoration implications
abstract: Conventional global attribution models tend to smooth over spatially conflicting ecological signals, thereby limiting the identification of trajectory-dependent association patterns, nonlinear responses, and latent instability in heterogeneous fragile landscapes. To address this limitation, this study developed a diagnostic adaptive assessment framework (DAAF) and applied it to the rocky desertification restoration belt of eastern and southeastern Yunnan, China. Using annual remote sensing ecological index (RSEI) data from 2000 to 2022 as the operational indicator of ecological environmental quality (EEQ), Sen's slope, the Mann–Kendall test, and the Hurst exponent were jointly employed to diagnose EEQ trends, characterize Hurst-based persistence tendencies and potential trajectory instability, and delineate eight dynamic trajectory types. Spatially stratified XGBoost–SHAP analysis, breakpoint detection, and network-assisted mediation analysis were then conducted to identify trajectory-specific environmental associations, response breakpoints, and indirect association patterns. The results showed that 88.29% of the study area exhibited improving EEQ, whereas 34.52% fell within trajectory-instability zones, indicating widespread improvement alongside anti-persistent or fluctuation-prone trajectories. Improving trajectories showed stronger associations with reduced external human pressure, whereas degrading trajectories were associated with weaker vegetation-cover conditions, hydroclimatic stress, and cumulative disturbance patterns. The fitted association between land-use intensity (LUCI) and annual RSEI showed an approximate response breakpoint around 2.09. In addition, FVC and precipitation exhibited separate approximate model-based response breakpoints around 0.63 and 970 mm, respectively, within localized degradation trajectories. Their co-occurring nonlinear patterns were consistent with a process-informed karst rainfall-paradox hypothesis under weakened vegetation protection. Mediation-assisted analysis further identified indirect association patterns linking land-use intensity, cumulative human pressure, and annual RSEI, whereas steep slopes showed terrain-related buffering associations with disturbance patterns. By linking trend diagnosis, stratified attribution, and breakpoint identification, the proposed framework provides a diagnostic workflow for EEQ assessment and spatially differentiated restoration management in fragile landscapes.

title: Flood-driven hydraulic-habitat indicators reveal geomorphic associations and functional complementarity across Contrasting River morphologies
abstract: Riverine topographic diversity is widely associated with spatial and temporal variation in hydraulic habitat under flood disturbance. Yet, most existing habitat assessments remain limited to static or quasi-steady flow conditions, restricting the development of indicators that capture habitat responses across complete flood cycles. This study examined the flood-prone Leshan reach of the Min River, using the round-mouthed copper fish ( Coreius guichenoti ) as the indicator species. A flood-cycle hydraulic-habitat assessment framework was developed by integrating hydrodynamic–habitat coupling with the Regional Integrated Suitability Index ( RII ), Hydraulic-Habitat Stability Index ( ESI ), Short-Term Hydraulic-Habitat Recovery Index ( EI ST ), and geomorphic-complexity indicators. Results show that river morphology is strongly associated with hydraulic-habitat dynamics: mid-channel bar reaches exhibit higher ESI under flood disturbance and a greater capacity to sustain suitable hydraulic habitat over time, whereas single-channel reaches exhibit lower hydraulic-habitat stability during intense flood disturbance but higher EI ST by the common event-end time. These contrasting responses indicate temporal functional complementarity at the hydraulic-habitat level in maintaining suitable hydraulic conditions and achieving short-term recovery. The Mid-Channel Bar Complexity Index ( MBCI ) is positively associated with ESI and captures additional geomorphic information beyond individual metrics under intermediate flood conditions, reflecting the combined contributions of mid-channel bar abundance, local topographic heterogeneity, and effective flow space. Overall, contrasting river morphologies have the potential to provide functionally complementary hydraulic-habitat responses under flood pulses. The framework provides a quantitative basis for identifying reaches with greater potential to maintain or recover spawning-suitable hydraulic conditions in flood-prone mountainous rivers.

title: Corrigendum to “Landscape mosaics: Analysing diversity for ecological and economic insight” [Ecol. Indic. 190 (2026) 115384]
Ensemble fire probability prediction by integrating meteorological AI models with lightweight prediction networks
abstract: Wildfires pose persistent threats to ecosystems and human safety, making timely fire-risk assessment essential for disaster prevention and resource management. However, conventional wildfire early-warning approaches are often constrained by static fire-weather indices or machine-learning models driven by reanalysis data, which cannot exploit future atmospheric fields. We therefore propose and evaluate a decoupled cascade framework that decomposes the problem into (i) an upstream AI weather model (Pangu-Weather) to generate future atmospheric states and (ii) downstream probabilistic fire classifiers. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to systematically compare the performance of three operational forecasting strategies (reanalysis, one-step forecast, and rolling forecast) for fire probability estimation. Using Africa as the study area, with multi-source data from 2014 to 2025, we find that one-step AI forecasts preserve the spatial fire-risk structure nearly as well as reanalysis data. Based on this dataset, we evaluated 11 downstream classifiers within a two-stage fire-occurrence and fire-intensity prediction design, while rolling forecasts suffer from degraded detection due to accumulated meteorological errors, with persistent reliability failure occurring after approximately six weeks. Cross-model consensus based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identifies vegetation, land-surface conditions, and meteorological variables as robust contributors. Our results demonstrate that meteorological foundation models can serve as modular and interchangeable upstream modules for operational wildfire hazard estimation, offering a scalable alternative to end-to-end black-box fire foundation models.

title: Disrupted flow regimes amplify climate-driven variability in cyanobacteria and CH4 dynamics in weir-regulated rivers
abstract: While river impoundment increases the climate vulnerability of cyanobacterial blooms, few studies have explored how weir-disrupted hydrologic connectivity modulates climatic forcing on bloom dynamics and associated CH 4 emissions. To assess the climate vulnerability of coupled cyanobacteria and CH 4 dynamics in weir-regulated rivers, we integrated hydroclimatic controls on cyanobacterial abundance across eight cascade weirs with three-year seasonal field surveys from source to estuary of the NR. These surveys evaluated basin-wide variations in the relative contributions of CH 4 , CO 2 , and N 2 O emissions. Compared to two other less impeded rivers in South Korea, the weir-regulated reaches of the NR emitted more CH 4 and N 2 O, but less CO 2 , particularly during hot, relatively dry summers. Diffusive CH 4 emissions and cyanobacterial abundance increased concurrently within a narrow range of high water temperatures and low flow velocities. Graph attention network (GAT) modeling confirmed these hydroclimatic controls on CH₄ (validation R 2 = 0.72), whereas pH and DO were the strongest drivers of CO 2 (R 2 = 0.54) and N 2 O (R 2 = 0.82) variability, respectively. Concurrent CH 4 peaks during cyanobacterial blooms, combined with rising global emissions from impounded rivers, suggest that flow disruption amplifies the sensitivity of these coupled dynamics to intensifying warming and drought. Restoring natural flow regimes should be integrated into national greenhouse gas inventories and watershed management strategies to mitigate cyanobacterial blooms and CH 4 emissions from rivers disrupted by weirs and other small structures.

title: Disentangling climate and fencing effects reveals aridity-dependent time lags in alpine grassland multifunctionality
abstract: Evaluating the true efficacy of nature-based conservation interventions in climate-sensitive ecosystems is fundamentally confounded by macroclimatic noise. To resolve this, we constructed a counterfactual attribution framework across the Changtang Plateau (2001–2020) to effectively decouple the independent effects of grazing exclusion from climate variability across five core ecosystem functions. Our findings unravel two ecological mechanisms dictating functional recovery. First, fencing benefits are governed by an aridity-dependent time lag, while humid alpine meadows exhibit rapid functional saturation, resource-limited arid steppes require prolonged accumulation to safely surpass intrinsic restoration thresholds. Second, ecosystem functions displayed distinctly asynchronous recovery trajectories. While aboveground primary production initially surged and stabilized, subsequent belowground carbon sequestration systematically attenuated, reflecting delayed vegetation-soil feedbacks. Furthermore, we identified a key intensity-spatial decoupling across the regional landscape. Although fencing acts as an effective local amplifier for biologically driven processes (e.g., productivity and soil retention), its spatial footprint gradually contracts along the aridity gradient. Conversely, hydrological and aerodynamic regulations remained primarily disjointed from fencing interventions, highlighting a critical boundary where localized engineering is structurally insufficient to override broad-scale macroclimatic forcing. Ultimately, conflating these complex spatiotemporal dynamics under traditional static evaluations risks notable climate-driven false positives and protection-driven false negatives. By exposing these evaluation traps, this study underscores the need for an alternative paradigm shift from conventional one-size-fits-all policies toward spatially explicit, climate-adaptive management frameworks, establishing an evidence-based basis for optimizing global protected area networks in fragile cold-arid biomes.

title: Impacts of Climate–Land Use Interactions and Topographic Thresholds on Nitrogen and Phosphorus Export Risks in Mountainous Watersheds: A Case Study in Yunnan, China.
abstract: Elucidating the drivers and risk evolution of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) export is fundamental to non-point source (NPS) pollution management. However, existing research focuses primarily on factor contributions or statistical thresholds, often failing to translate attribution results and thresholds into spatial risk diagnostics. This disconnect between mechanistic understanding and spatially targeted management constitutes a critical knowledge gap. This study addresses this knowledge gap by integrating InVEST-NDR modeling, counterfactual factor decomposition, XGBoost-SHAP interpretation, and segmented regression to quantify the relative contributions, nonlinear responses, and threshold relationships of N and P export drivers in Yunnan Province. An ESI-based spatial risk classification framework—integrating environmental sensitivity, source pressure, and climate–land use interaction increments—was developed to delineate priority management zones. The results indicate that: (1) Land use and land cover (LULC) change contributed most (57.2%) with strong temporal persistence; climate effect (33.5%) showed pronounced interannual variability. (2) Cropland area and precipitation exhibited continuously enhancing responses; distance from rivers (DFR) and elevation (DEM) displayed L-shaped threshold responses, with export sensitivity significantly increasing when DFR < 2.3 km and DEM < 1.9 km. (3) Significant synergistic associations exist between cropland change and environmental conditions; agricultural source pressure overlapping with near-river, low-elevation, and high-precipitation zones amplified N and P export risk. (4) Compound high-risk zones accounted for 6.4% in 2020, concentrated in river corridors and agricultural basins, representing priority areas for NPS control. Projected risk patterns diverge substantially across Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), with high-emission scenarios posing considerably greater adaptive management challenges. This study quantifies the relative contributions of climate and LULC change to N and P export dynamics and identifies spatial risk patterns, providing evidence-based guidance for targeted NPS pollution management in mountainous watersheds under climate change.

title: Graph theory-based framework for Diagnosing River fragmentation and connectivity
abstract: River fragmentation and climate-driven thermal change increasingly threaten freshwater biodiversity, yet basin-scale assessments typically treat connectivity as a purely structural property, measuring whether physical pathways exist between network nodes, without considering whether organisms can realistically traverse thermally unsuitable or barrier-impeded reaches. We developed a graph-theoretic indicator suite that integrates thermal habitat classification, barrier passability, and distance-decay dispersal to quantify functional connectivity, locate confluences of elevated biophysical heterogeneity, delineate thermal refugia, and prioritise barriers for restoration under climate-warming scenarios. Applied to the Upper Colorado River Basin (132,487 nodes; 274 dams; 77,444 natural slope barriers), the framework revealed a pronounced structural–functional divergence. Although the network appeared almost fully connected in structural terms, functional connectivity represented only a minute fraction of its theoretical potential once cumulative passability losses and distance-decay dispersal were incorporated. Coldwater habitat (≤20 °C) encompassed 97% of nodes yet was fragmented into isolated high-elevation patches; two refugia above 2700 m contained approximately 60% of all coldwater nodes. Confluences ranking highest on a composite of network centrality, thermal mixing potential, and confluence degree concentrated within high-elevation coldwater reaches in the central and eastern basin. The composite selects warm-margin confluences at above-chance frequency relative to the basin-wide coldwater fraction, identifying candidate locations for biological survey rather than verified biodiversity hotspots. Because the analysis includes only inventoried dams and natural slope barriers and omits the far more numerous small structures such as culverts, road crossings, and low-head weirs, these estimates are conservative, and the true functional fragmentation of the basin is likely more severe than reported. Uniform warming increments, applied as sensitivity scenarios, indicated a 7.8-percentage-point loss of coldwater habitat under +3 °C warming, concentrated in the mid-elevation corridor connecting high-elevation refugia to downstream reaches, where three chokepoint barriers retained the highest priority under thermal perturbation, although simulated connectivity gain was not monotonic in rank. The spatial convergence of functional isolation, thermal stress, and climate vulnerability emerged only under the integrated framework, indicating that structural connectivity metrics alone do not track ecological accessibility in thermally heterogeneous river networks.

title: Topographic and economic drivers of agricultural–ecological coupling in Gansu Province: spatial differentiation and threshold effects
abstract: Improved understanding of agricultural–ecological coupling is critical for sustainable development in semi-arid regions. This study integrated the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI), Agricultural Green Development Index (AGDI), Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD) model, and XGBoost–SHAP to examine the spatiotemporal evolution and nonlinear drivers of agricultural–ecological coupling in Gansu Province from 2010 to 2023 at the county scale. A four-quadrant framework was applied to identify differentiated management types. Results showed that farmland ecological quality exhibited a stepped north–south pattern, improving during 2010–2018 but declining after 2019. Agricultural green development displayed a “high southeast, low northwest” pattern, increasing by 0.0036 yr −1 ( p < 0.01). The coupling coordination degree increased from 0.57 to 0.63, with significant spatial clustering (Moran's I = 0.438–0.528, p < 0.001), characterized by stable “high–high” clusters in southern Gansu and “low–low” clusters in northern Gansu. Relief amplitude (40.9%) and GDP per capita (36.1%) jointly explained 77.0% of coordination variation. Elevation above 2000 m constrained coordination, whereas GDP per capita between 15,000 and 30,000 CNY promoted green transformation, with diminishing effects beyond 40,000 CNY. Severe drought conditions (SPEI < −1.5) caused agricultural–ecological imbalance. Counties were classified into four management types (H H, L–H, L–L, and H–L), requiring differentiated governance strategies. This study provides quantifiable thresholds for improving agricultural–ecological coupling in semi-arid regions.

title: Beyond regional greening: Nonlinear GPP trajectories and their environmental associations in eastern coastal China
abstract: Coastal ecosystems are highly vulnerable to synergistic environmental pressures, yet traditional linear assessments may hide their short-term dynamic responses. To examine these responses, this study developed an integrated diagnostic framework that combined the Mann–Kendall test, BFAST01, and spatially validated XGBoost–SHAP to characterize GPP trajectories in Shandong Province from 2000 to 2022. The Mann–Kendall analysis showed an extremely significant increasing trend in 69.4% of the pixels. BFAST01 further identified eight trajectory types, among which the monotone increasing trajectory covered 54.5% of the study area. The “Interruption: increasing with negative interruption” type (Type 5) and the “Reversal: from increasing to decreasing” type (Type 7) represented 17.5% and 6.0% of the area, respectively. Approximately 92% of the nonlinear trajectories were significant in at least one segment. Among the Type 5 and Type 7 pixels, the XGBoost classifier achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.87, an average precision of 0.68, and a balanced accuracy of 0.78 in an independent 40-km spatial holdout set. Its classification performance remained stable across repeated spatial partitions and block sizes of 20–60 km. SHAP analysis identified ΔT and ΔP as the leading predictors, with mean absolute SHAP values of 0.74 and 0.73, respectively. Hydroclimatic and topographic variables contributed 60.1% and 24.1% of the summed SHAP importance, while ΔP × ΔT exhibited the strongest pairwise interaction. These findings indicate that regional greening can contain contrasting nonlinear trajectories and that Type 5–Type 7 differentiation is closely associated with coupled hydroclimatic and topographic conditions. The integrated framework provides a spatially robust approach for identifying nonlinear GPP changes and supporting regional vegetation monitoring.

title: Hydrological connectivity drives multi-trophic biodiversity and food-web structure in Yangtze River wetlands: Insights from eDNA metabarcoding
abstract: Hydrological connectivity is a fundamental regulator of the exchange of matter, energy, and organisms across aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, especially within wetlands. Despite this critical role, its ecological effects on communities across multiple trophic levels remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we investigated the responses of biodiversity and food web structure to hydrological connectivity based on aquatic environmental DNA data encompassing fish, invertebrates, protozoa, eukaryotic algae, fungi, and bacteria from the middle reaches of the Yangtze River wetlands. Hydrological connectivity exerted limited and taxon-specific effects on α diversity, but had a strong and nonlinear influence on β diversity. Community compositional heterogeneity peaked at intermediate levels of connectivity. Patterns of community stability, quantified by the average variation degree, indicated that hydrological connectivity was the dominant driver for most taxa. Conversely, local nutrient and physicochemical conditions more strongly controlled lower trophic groups such as bacteria and fungi. Food web patterns revealed pronounced nonlinear responses to hydrological connectivity, with trophic coherence and modularity exhibiting U-shaped relationships and robustness reaching its maximum at intermediate connectivity levels. Our findings underscore the central role of hydrological connectivity in structuring both biodiversity patterns and food-web architecture across trophic levels, and highlight its importance for effective conservation and management of wetland ecosystems under changing hydrological conditions.

title: Strengthening water-energy-food and ecosystem services interactions: Integration in nexus planning and targeted governance
abstract: Synergistic management of the Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus and ecosystem services (ESs) is vital for regional sustainability. Yet existing studies have primarily focused on the impacts of ESs on WEF nexus or vice versa, with limited attention to their interactions. To address this gap, this study developed an integrated WEF-ESs framework to analyze one-way and coupled interactions, and identified key factors associated with synergistic coupling and direct and indirect effects in the Yellow River Basin (YRB) from 2000 to 2020. Results showed that ESs were positively correlated with WEF nexus sustainability, with key ESs exhibiting distinct nonlinear threshold effects. Carbon sequestration and soil conservation had significant positive impacts on WEF nexus sustainability below thresholds of 50.12 t/hm 2 and 63.10 t/hm 2 across the basin, while carbon sequestration in upper reaches of YRB (UYRB) generated benefits when it exceeded 63.10 t/hm 2 . Meanwhile, WEF-ESs coordination improved steadily basin-wide but exhibited strong spatial heterogeneity. Natural factors (e.g., NDVI, precipitation) showed primary positive associations, while water factors (e.g., agricultural water proportion) showed key negative associations across the basin. The UYRB was dominated by natural factors (e.g., precipitation and NDVI). The MYRB showed co-occurrence with natural conditions and was associated with energy activities (e.g., energy consumption per 10,000 yuan GDP) and the DYRB showed associations with both socio-economic factors (e.g., building land proportion) and water-related factors. These findings provide insights into interaction pathways and threshold effects, providing scientific support for threshold-oriented restoration in the UYRB, improving resource efficiency in the MYRB, and integrated land–water management in the DYRB.

title: Dynamics of soil organic carbon pools following afforestation in coastal saline–alkali soils: A model–data fusion study
abstract: Coastal saline–alkali lands are important targets for ecological restoration and coastal carbon management, yet assessing durable soil carbon sequestration requires considering not only SOC recovery but also how carbon is distributed between particulate and mineral-associated pools. Whether and when net SOC accumulation occurs after afforestation, and how POC and MAOC recover across stand ages and soil depths, remain unresolved. Here, we integrated field observations from a 21-year chronosequence of Taxodium hybrid ‘Zhongshanshan’ plantations with Biome-BGC simulations to reconstruct SOC stock dynamics in coastal saline–alkali soils of eastern China. The model-based reconstruction suggested a non-monotonic decline–recovery–accumulation trajectory, characterized by an early SOC deficit followed by delayed recovery and subsequent accumulation. The prolonged early decline suggested that new carbon inputs were initially insufficient to offset SOC losses. POC and MAOC showed distinct stand-age- and depth-dependent responses. POC recovered rapidly in the 0–20 and 20–40 cm layers at later stages of afforestation, whereas MAOC recovered more slowly and remained below the mudflat level in the 40–60 cm layer after 21 years. In mixed-effects models accounting for plot-level non-independence, land-use stage and soil depth, POC remained positively associated with sucrase activity, whereas MAOC and SOC were primarily associated with electrical conductivity. These findings indicate that SOC recovery following afforestation is characterized by asynchronous and depth-dependent changes in particulate and mineral-associated carbon pools, with a rapid but non-monotonic POC response and a more gradual, depth-constrained recovery of MAOC. Assessments of soil carbon sequestration in coastal saline–alkali plantations should therefore distinguish the rapid but non-monotonic response of POC from the slower and more depth-constrained recovery of MAOC, while explicitly accounting for subsoil carbon pools.

title: From online traces to upstream surveillance: Large language models uncover the hidden status of non-native freshwater apex predators in China
abstract: Biological invasions are often recognised only after ecological damage has become visible in the wild, even though the human-mediated processes that drive introductions may already be underway through private rearing, trade, and release. This gap in upstream surveillance is especially consequential for non-native freshwater apex predators, whose impacts can propagate rapidly through recipient food webs. Here, we show that these human-mediated introduction dynamics can be reconstructed from online activities at the national scale. Using China as a test case, we developed a large language model-based pipeline to process and validate 366,210 posts on gars (Lepisosteidae) and snapping turtles (Chelydridae) from ten major online platforms spanning 2006 to 2024. We found that online rearing and trade were taxonomically uneven, platform-specific, and temporally dynamic, with already regulated species remaining dominant but several unregulated taxa also emerging repeatedly across rearing, trade, and sighting records. Wild sightings showed clear spatial and temporal structure and were associated with both socioeconomic and environmental context, indicating that an online trade-to-online sighting signal is detectable at the national scale. Together, these results show that dispersed online traces can be converted into usable ecological evidence for upstream surveillance of human-mediated introduction pathways. More broadly, our study provides a scalable framework for detecting online evidence of introduction pathways that conventional surveillance often misses.

title: Dynamic stability and resilience of water conservation in the three-river headwaters region: Trajectory differentiation and causal mechanisms
abstract: Water conservation is a key ecosystem service of the Three-River Source region, the core area of the “Asian Water Tower”. Current studies on water conservation in alpine regions predominantly focus on static spatial patterns and overall driving analyses, while lacking systematic exploration of multi-scale evolutionary characteristics, dynamic trajectory classification, and differential mechanisms of ecological resilience under dry-wet disturbances. To address these research gaps, this study innovatively constructs a coupled integrated framework of “spatiotemporal quantification–trajectory diagnosis–resilience assessment–typed causal identification”. By integrating wavelet periodic analysis, dynamic trajectory recognition, multi-dimensional resilience quantification, and the optimized GPC causal model, this framework overcomes the limitations of traditional static and homogeneous research, and systematically reveals the dynamic evolution, resilience differentiation, and differentiated driving mechanisms of water conservation in the Three-River Source region from 1990 to 2020. The results indicate that water conservation in the study area exhibits multi-scale fluctuation characteristics with a dominant 22-year low-frequency oscillation and a secondary 5-year periodic variation, presenting a long-term spatial agglomeration pattern of “high in the south and low in the north”. Trajectory statistics show that the neutral trajectory accounts for the largest proportion (60.0%), followed by the positive trajectory (29.8%) and the negative trajectory (10.2%). Specifically, the positive linear trajectory possesses the highest comprehensive resilience, whereas the positive and negative step trajectories show the weakest resilience. This indicates that gradual improvement contributes to the accumulation of ecological resilience, while abrupt succession tends to trigger system vulnerability. Significant trajectory differentiation exists in driving mechanisms: stable areas are constrained by the coupled effects of topography, soil, and climatic natural background factors; improved areas are synergistically driven by climatic humidification and underlying surface regulation; degraded and mutated areas are mainly characterized by eco-hydrological decoupling, combined with local human disturbances that induce degradation risks. The study demonstrates that the water conservation capacity of the Three-River Source region is generally stable, but local areas face potential threshold degradation risks. This research provides significant theoretical and practical implications for ecological conservation and refined water resource management in the Three-River Source National Park.

title: Identifying ecological security patterns across Nanshan National Park and its adjacent counties via an integrated XGBoost-MCR framework
abstract: National parks anchor biodiversity conservation, but ecological connectivity in mountainous regions also depends on surrounding county landscapes, where land-use change, transport infrastructure, and landscape fragmentation may constrain cross-boundary ecological processes. Existing ecological security pattern studies are often confined to protected-area boundaries, while resistance surfaces based on expert scoring or linear weighted overlay may inadequately represent nonlinear relationships between ecological resistance and multiple environmental and anthropogenic factors. We treated the four-county analytical extent centered on Nanshan National Park in Hunan Province, China, as an integrated park–county study area and developed an ecological indicator-based extreme gradient boosting–minimum cumulative resistance (XGBoost–MCR) framework. Multi-source spatial datasets were harmonized to a common 30 m grid, from which 12 natural and anthropogenic resistance indicators were derived. Ecological-source areas were used to define the relatively low-resistance sampling domain, whereas areas in the very-low integrated ecosystem-service importance class were used to define the relatively high-resistance domain for seven binary classifiers. XGBoost probabilities were used as normalized relative ecological resistance. Resistance-derived relative ecological security was subsequently calculated as E S i = 1 − R i and classified into five levels, while the resistance surface served as the MCR cost layer for corridor extraction and subsequent breakpoint identification. Among the seven models, XGBoost achieved the highest testing area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.9985), with a testing accuracy of 0.9837, whereas k-nearest neighbors achieved the highest testing accuracy (0.9865). Because the testing subset was randomly held out rather than spatially blocked, these metrics indicate sample-level discrimination rather than spatially independent predictive performance. Shapley additive explanations identified elevation, distance to roads, and population density as the three most influential predictors, accounting for 31.68%, 27.05%, and 15.24% of the normalized mean absolute SHAP importance, respectively. The framework identified 15 ecological sources covering 1730.45 km 2 (16.54% of the study area), 18 ecological corridors totaling 824.37 km, and 66 merged ecological breakpoints, of which 41 were located outside the national park. The resulting ecological security pattern comprised one core, four zones, four axes, and multiple nodes. By avoiding expert-assigned indicator weights in resistance-surface construction, representing nonlinear resistance relationships, and quantifying predictor contributions, the framework provides a reproducible and interpretable spatial basis for corridor protection, breakpoint mitigation, and cross-county ecological governance in mountainous national park regions.

title: Spatial risk zonation of phosphorus loss in agricultural catchments shaped by phosphorus forms and transport pathways
abstract: Identifying spatial risk zones of phosphorus (P) loss remains difficult in agricultural catchments because P forms differ in source availability, leaching potential, and transport pathways. Existing risk assessment frameworks mainly emphasize surface erosion and runoff, making it difficult to capture form-specific risks associated with subsurface leaching. Here, we developed a spatial risk assessment framework for total phosphorus (TP), particulate phosphorus (PP), colloidal phosphorus (CP), and dissolved phosphorus (DP) by integrating soil-column leaching experiments, random forest modelling, field observations of hydrological pathway partitioning, and Monte Carlo-Sobol sensitivity analysis of weighting parameters. The RF models showed moderate predictive performance for leaching loads (R 2 = 0.612–0.661), with pH, redox potential (Eh), electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, and water-dispersible colloid mass showing relatively high model-based importance. Field observations of TP export showed that surface flow was dominant, while interflow and baseflow made measurable contributions, indicating that non-surface P transfer occurred at the catchment scale. Integrated risk analysis revealed contrasting source-transport sensitivities among P forms: TP and PP risk outputs were more sensitive to transport-related weighting parameters, whereas CP and DP outputs were more sensitive to source-related parameters. For TP, the relative contribution of the leaching-related indicator decreased from 33.1% to 17.5% across risk levels, whereas that of soil P status increased from 23.2% to 31.5%. This framework clarifies how P forms and transport pathways jointly shape spatial risk zonation and supports form-specific, zone-targeted management of agricultural P loss.

title: Nonlinear and lagged associations between active-layer thickness and vegetation greenness in the source reach of the Yangtze River basin from 1990 to 2024
abstract: Permafrost degradation can alter alpine vegetation through changing hydrothermal conditions, but nonlinear relationships between active-layer thickness (ALT) and vegetation and their temporal lags remain poorly quantified on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. We integrated a cross-sensor-calibrated 30-m Landsat normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) time series (1990–2024) with gridded permafrost and environmental data for the Source Reach of the Yangtze River Basin (SRYRB). Segmented regression, cross-correlation analysis, and Geodetector were used to characterize statistical thresholds, lagged associations, and their spatially heterogeneous environmental context. From 1990 to 2024, mean ALT increased by 0.135 m decade −1 , while approximately 65.8% of extremely stable permafrost degraded. NDVI increased by 0.0018 yr −1 overall, with a slightly higher rate in seasonally frozen ground (0.0021 yr −1 ) than in permafrost (0.0017 yr −1 ). The positive NDVI trend weakened when ALT reached approximately 1.45–1.65 m, and pixel-level turning events were most frequently associated with cumulative ALT thickening of 0.3–0.5 m. The strongest ALT–NDVI association occurred at zero lag across 58.0% of the study area and at lags of 1–3 years elsewhere. TEMP had the largest individual q statistic, whereas its pairwise combinations with PRECIP, LULC, ALT, and MAGT showed greater joint explanatory power. Continued permafrost degradation may move more of the SRYRB into ALT ranges associated with weaker greening, providing a basis for monitoring of vegetation–permafrost change in Tibetan Plateau.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and nonlinear drivers of urban eco-efficiency in China's old industrial bases using explainable machine learning
abstract: Against the backdrop of climate change and the accelerating green transition, urban eco-efficiency (UEE) has become an important indicator for assessing the coordination between economic development and environmental sustainability. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on national regions, urban agglomerations, and economically developed areas, while relatively limited attention has been paid to old industrial base cities characterized by strong industrial path dependence, structural transformation constraints, and pronounced regional heterogeneity. Moreover, conventional linear econometric approaches may fail to adequately capture the nonlinear, stage-dependent, and threshold effects underlying UEE dynamics. To address these gaps, this study employs panel data from 95 prefecture-level cities in China's old industrial base regions from 2009 to 2023, and adopts a super-efficiency Slack-Based Measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs to evaluate urban eco-efficiency (UEE). Kernel density estimation, Theil index decomposition, standard deviational ellipse, and spatial autocorrelation analyses are integrated to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution patterns of UEE. The Stacking ensemble machine-learning method is introduced to identify the nonlinear effects of influencing factors. Furthermore, SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) interpretable analysis and the GAM model are adopted to reveal the contributions and threshold effects of key variables. During the study period, the overall urban eco-efficiency in China's old industrial bases exhibited a fluctuating upward trend, with continuously enhanced spatial agglomeration characteristics. Regional disparities gradually shifted from being dominated by interregional differences to intraregional differences, and the spatial centroid migrated from the northeast to the southwest. The driving mechanism analysis revealed that economic level served as the core driver, and all influencing factors displayed evident nonlinear threshold characteristics and significant regional heterogeneity. This study deepens the understanding of eco-efficiency evolution mechanisms from a nonlinear perspective and provides a scientific basis for the green transformation and differentiated governance of old industrial bases.

title: Spatial analysis of urban ecological quality based on urban morphological-functional mapping: a case study of Nanjing, China
abstract: Cities constitute complex socio-ecological systems where built-environment characteristics interact dynamically with human activities to shape ecological patterns. However, identifying key associated factors of urban ecological quality remains challenging due to high spatial heterogeneity—especially when taking urban 3D structure and functional diversity into consideration. To address this, we developed an Urban Morphological-Functional (UMF) zoning framework to assess spatial variations in ecological quality (RSEI) in Nanjing, China. We constructed a multi-dimensional feature system integrating natural, morphological, built-up, and social activity factors, then applied Deep Neural Network modeling coupled with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify feature contributions and interpret their nonlinear mechanisms across UMF zones. Results confirmed framework effectiveness: citywide analysis revealed balanced contributions from elevation, average building height, nighttime lighting, and building density, while zone-specific assessments highlighted distinct associated patterns. For instance, UMF_8f (Sparsely Built Ecological Zone) was predominantly influenced by elevation (natural factors: 43.5%), whereas UMF_6e (Open Mid-Rise Entertainment Zone) exhibited ≈90% combined natural-social dominance, with population density unexpectedly enhancing ecological quality. Critically, these relationships followed nonlinear patterns—including saturation effects, L-shaped anthropogenic degradation thresholds, and U-shaped aspect dependencies—challenging conventional linear assumptions. These insights enable context-sensitive urban design, supporting climate-adaptive and health-oriented planning. By linking morphological-functional zoning with ecological diagnostics, the UMF-RSEI framework advances precision sustainability management, offering actionable pathways for optimizing urban resilience at granular scales.

title: Predicting decay in functional diversity in plant communities under future climates
abstract: Climate change is expected to cause widespread shifts in the composition of plant communities. However, the extent to which these changes will alter the composition and diversity of plant functional traits is less clear. Here, we assess how climate change may reshape the functional diversity of 32,996 plant communities by combining data on their traits and realised climatic niches with future climate projections. We find that under projected climates for the decade centred on 2070, in most plots, over a third of species will experience conditions outside of their current realised climatic niches. Yet, typically, the projected removal of these species from communities represented a decay in functional diversity of 11.6%, indicating some functional redundancy. We found that climate-filtered species removal resulted in a marginally greater loss of functional diversity (+1.69%) compared to random species removal. Patterns of relative functional decay (i.e., projected loss of functional diversity relative to climate-filtered species removal under future climate) were distinct between woody and non-woody species, with woody species being at higher risk of declines in functional diversity. These results highlight the importance of integrating additional metrics, such as functional diversity and functional decay, into conservation and restoration planning to characterise vulnerable communities and growth forms. Using a functional dimension of biodiversity can help conservation practitioners identify areas vulnerable to climate change, inform management actions, and prioritise the restoration of key growth forms to reinstate ecosystem function and identity.

title: Environmental DNA maps estuarine regionalisation, zonation, and water quality impacts
abstract: High throughput metabarcoding sequencing of environmental DNA was applied to analyse estuarine biota, along a latitudinal gradient across three regions, estuarine zones, and water quality types. A total of 4757 detections, in 36 biota groupings were observed. The majority in seven key groups: bacteria (23%), plants (13%), fungi (9%), fish (8%), ciliates (6%), insects (6%), and crustaceans (4%).
