Despite high sample variability, differences were observed in detected biota between region, estuary, estuary zone, and water quality types. Water quality pressures differed in each region; however, at sites with the poorest water quality (highest nutrients, and turbidity), differentiation of detected biota was observed. Biota groups that best characterised these differences comprised primarily lower order groups, bacteria, cryptomonads, and ciliates, photosynthetic groups including green algae, dinoflagellates, diatoms, and one higher order group, crustaceans. Typically, lower diversity and number of total detections were observed at the sites with more impacted water quality, this was to the greatest extent in the most human influenced Central region, at mid-estuary sites. However, this trend was not observed for all biota groups, with higher aggregated counts and diversity detected for bacteria, plants, and archaea at more impacted sites. These data set a baseline across regions and estuaries, subject to a range of water quality impacts. Further study is necessary to establish eDNA as an indicator of estuarine condition, to better characterise the influences of other relevant drivers, both natural and human influenced, and change associated with management interventions.

title: Optimal lag time analysis and relative importance decomposition for insights into ecosystem climate adaptation
abstract: Vegetation dynamics are strongly associated with climate variability, yet large-scale quantification of vegetation's temporal lag responses to climatic drivers remains poorly understood. We use multiple linear regression, relative importance contribution analysis and time-lag correlation analysis to systematically examine the sensitivity and optimal lag times (OLT) of vegetation activity (NDVI) to precipitation, temperature, and solar radiation across China during 2001–2024. The results demonstrate that vegetation responses are primarily governed by short lag effects, with temperature exhibiting the shortest mean lag (0.73 ± 0.80 months), followed by precipitation (0.94 ± 0.92 months) and solar radiation (1.87 ± 0.93 months). Spatial heterogeneity was observed in lag structures and vegetation sensitivity among climatic zones and vegetation functional groups. Temperature acts as the dominant driver and explains most of the NDVI variation, while precipitation and solar radiation exert secondary but region-specific impacts. Compared with synchronous correlation analysis, incorporating lag effects greatly improves the explanatory capacity of climate-vegetation relationships. The results emphasize the essential role of temporal memory in vegetation-climate interactions and provide improved understanding of the mechanisms regulating ecosystem responses to climate change. This study provides a robust analytical framework for enhancing vegetation dynamics models and supports more reliable predictions of ecosystem responses under future climate scenarios.

title: Nonlinear driving mechanisms and spatiotemporal heterogeneity of agricultural resilience in arid regions: A SHAP-GTWR based study of Xinjiang, China
abstract: Amid growing resource constraints, understanding how agricultural resilience evolves across space and time is essential for sustaining food systems in arid regions. This study employs a combined framework integrating a game theory-based weighting–TOPSIS approach, the XGBoost–SHAP model, and geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) to examine the evolution of agricultural resilience and its driving factors across 82 counties in Xinjiang between 2000 and 2020. The results show that: (1) Agricultural resilience in Xinjiang increased gradually over the study period, rising from 0.175 to 0.204 ( p < 0.05) and recording a mean yearly expansion of 0.77%; (2) Agricultural resilience showed significant spatial clustering, with high-value areas mainly distributed in the Ili River Valley and along the northern slopes of the Tianshan Mountains, while low-value areas were concentrated along the southern edge of the Tarim Basin; (3) The XGBoost–SHAP results indicate that agricultural resilience is dually driven by ecological and socioeconomic factors, with NDVI and population density as the dominant drivers. Furthermore, these drivers exhibit pronounced nonlinear threshold effects; (4) The GTWR results reveal significant spatio-temporal heterogeneity, with irrigation water use remained positively associated with agricultural resilience throughout the study period. This study presents a robust analytical framework and provides useful insights into resource allocation, ecological vulnerability reduction, and agricultural sustainability in arid regions.

title: Evolution characteristics and driving mechanisms of production-living-ecological spaces across development gradients: Evidence from typical cities in Jiangsu Province, China
abstract: Uncovering the gradient-differentiated evolution and driving mechanisms of production-living-ecological spaces (PLES) is crucial for differentiated spatial governance. However, existing studies have largely focused on area changes or single-dimensional economic gradients, with limited attention to inter-type spatial conversions. This leaves a critical gap in systematic cross-gradient comparisons that integrate natural endowments, locational conditions, and socioeconomic development. Taking Nanjing, Nantong and Xuzhou, three cities at distinct development gradients, as case studies, this study analyzed the characteristics of PLES evolution from 2000 to 2023 and employed interpretable machine learning models to explore heterogeneity in driving mechanisms. Results show: (1) Production space shrank across all cities, most sharply in Nanjing. Living space expanded fastest in Nantong, while ecological space stability positively correlated with economic development gradient. (2) The dominant conversion was from production to living space, and ecological space underwent internal adjustments and conversion to agricultural land, but expansion directions of various space types varied. Landscape fragmentation of living space decreased, but production space remained highly aggregated with increasing shape complexity. Among these cities, Xuzhou exhibited the most fragmented landscape, whereas Nantong displayed a relatively ordered spatial pattern. (3) XGBoost outperformed alternative machine learning models, and driving mechanisms differed markedly across gradients. PLES evolution in Nanjing showed the strongest associations with population concentration and innovation-oriented economy under rigid natural constraints; in Nantong, it was most strongly associated with locational and economic factors, with climatic conditions playing a regulatory role; in Xuzhou, it was jointly associated with natural-ecological constraints and traditional industrial path dependence. These findings indicate that PLES evolution is deeply coupled with development gradient, underscoring the need for tailored spatial governance strategies to foster coordinated regional development.

title: Indicators used by EU policies do not sufficiently match those needed to expand agroecology
abstract: Agroecology is key for developing more sustainable food systems. Yet, the ability of public policies to support the expansion of agroecology remains uncertain. This is partly because assessing this ability requires multiple indicators, adequately covering all dimensions of agroecology. Here, we focus on four dimensions of agroecology: biodiversity, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and farm socio-economic performance. We use the scientific literature on agroecology indicators to identify all relevant themes within each dimension. For each theme, we then compare indicators used for the monitoring of the main agricultural and environmental policies in the European Union (EU) and indicators considered most relevant by agroecology practitioners across 11 European living laboratories. We identified a theme mismatch for 8 of the 28 themes, policy indicators covering 25 themes while practitioner indicators covered 21 themes, with 20 themes being covered by both. Among these 20 themes, 18 were covered through different indicators by policies and practitioners (i.e. indicator mismatch), 15 were covered using similar indicators but with different definitions (i.e. definition mismatch), and 17 were covered using similar indicators but measured at different scales (i.e. scale mismatch). These results show that indicators currently used in EU policies inadequately cover the multiple dimensions of agroecology. We recommend the addition of 16 new policy indicators and the revision of five existing indicators based on available data and methods to enhance the ability of EU policies to support the expansion of agroecology.

title: From habitat prediction to cost-effective intervention: A spatial modelling and connectivity framework for firefly conservation planning
abstract: Firefly habitats are increasingly threatened by rapid urbanisation, while encounters with wild fireflies have become ever rarer, fuelling growing interest in firefly watching and increasing pressure on vulnerable populations. Existing conservation research has largely focused on broad-scale habitat assessment, leaving a disconnect between habitat modelling and practical conservation action. To bridge this gap, we developed an integrated conservation framework using the terrestrial firefly Emeia pseudosauteri as the focal species. We compared random forest (RF), boosted regression trees (BRT), and generalized additive models (GAM), and found that a two-stage spatial hurdle model showed the best out-of-sample performance among the frameworks compared, particularly for conditional abundance under spatially independent validation. By modelling occurrence and conditional abundance separately while accounting for spatial dependence, the model accommodated zero-inflated, spatially clustered firefly counts. We integrated Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-derived life stage based seasonal canopy information, anthropogenic variables, circuit-theoretic connectivity analysis, and grid-level cost-effectiveness evaluation to prioritise conservation interventions. Summer canopy cover and water-edge cost distance emerged as the principal determinants of distribution, while fine-scale sub-canopy analysis indicated that local plant associations explained observed aggregations better than structural complexity alone. The framework identified cost-effective priorities for improving habitat connectivity while informing visitor management to reduce ecological disturbance. By linking spatial habitat modelling, connectivity analysis, and cost-effectiveness optimisation, this study provides a transferable planning framework for prioritising habitat management under increasing human disturbance.

title: Scale invariance in the high-frequency marine soundscape: diel oscillations as a proxy for ecosystem state
abstract: Life generated in the oceans. Human activities rapidly and drastically altered marine environments. Scientists are struggling in defining an effective strategy to assess the anthropogenic impacts into seas and oceans. In fact, marine ecosystems are complex systems, with a multitude of interconnected aspects that makes the understanding of its functioning a challenge. Acoustic waves are the most efficient mechanism for long-range energy transport and communication in the marine environment. Consequently, the marine soundscape integrates information from multiple biological and physical processes and offers a promising framework for ecosystem monitoring. However, most acoustic studies have focused on low-frequency signals associated with anthropogenic noise or species-specific acoustic activity. In this study, we analyse the spectral properties of underwater soundscapes recorded using different instruments and across diverse seasonal conditions in the Adriatic Sea. The analysis focuses on the power-law behaviour of acoustic spectra between 13 and 37 kHz and on the temporal evolution of their spectral slopes. By concentrating on the dynamics of the spectral slopes rather than absolute sound-pressure levels, the proposed approach provides an indicator that is independent of hydrophone calibration and instrument sensitivity offsets. For the first time, we report a persistent diel oscillation in the spectral slope of high-frequency acoustic spectra, consistently observed across winter and late-spring deployments. Statistical analyses demonstrate that day-night differences are robust and reproducible across daily cycles. Comparisons with environmental variables, including irradiance, temperature, tides, and wave dynamics, suggest that the observed oscillation cannot be explained solely by physical forcing. We therefore hypothesize that the diel modulation may reflect temporal variations in the biological component of the ecosystem, potentially associated with collective biological rhythms rather than isolated species-specific acoustic emissions. These results suggest that high-frequency spectral slopes may constitute a novel calibration-independent acoustic indicator for marine ecosystem monitoring. The recurring diel oscillation further indicates that this indicator may provide information on the temporal organization and state of biological activity within marine ecosystems, opening new perspectives for passive-acoustic assessment of ecosystem dynamics.

title: Past flow intermittence duration influences microbial and invertebrate community structure and ecological processes after flow resumption
abstract: Intermittent streams represent over half of the global river network and are becoming increasingly prevalent due to climate change and water abstraction. Despite their importance, knowledge of their functioning remains limited, especially in temperate regions. Here, we assessed the effects of past flow intermittence duration on functional processes during the flowing period in two temperate streams of northeastern France, using functional indicators (i.e., organic matter decomposition and primary production) and monitoring aquatic fungal and invertebrate communities. Indicators were deployed at 12 stations distributed along an intermittence gradient in two contrasting watersheds. We tested whether (1) past drying duration influences functional processes during the flowing phase, (2) drying effects differ between the two streams, and (3) functional indicators are relevant to intermittent stream systems and discriminant enough for assessing drying duration stress. Our results revealed contrasting functional responses between the two systems despite comparable flow intermittence duration. In Orge stream, organic matter decomposition, fungal activity and macroinvertebrate diversity varied along the flow intermittence gradient, exhibiting higher levels for intermediate flow intermittence, whereas the Ormançon stream maintained high and invariable ecological processes intensity regardless of variations in flow intermittence. Effects of drying on macroinvertebrates functional diversity were observed in the Orge, where highly intermittent stations selected traits adapted to flow intermittence. Functional indicators demonstrated their relevance for characterizing the impact of flow intermittence gradients, supplementing conventional taxonomic indicators. Studies covering a larger number of intermittent streams are needed not only to better characterize and understand their functioning, but also to define reference values that will help improve the environmental management of this ecosystem type that is rapidly increasing in proportion.

title: Do soils recover after invasive plant removal? A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Removing invasive plants is commonly assumed to restore soils, yet a soil may change without recovering. We synthesised evidence from 17 papers and meta-analysed upper-soil data from 13 using multilevel models that accounted for dependent effect sizes and shared controls. Recovery was evaluated separately against invaded and reference soils. Relative to invaded soils, removal reduced soil moisture by 2.93 percentage points and exchangeable Ca and Mg by 39.0% and 51.8%, respectively. Exchangeable K also declined in the primary model, but this effect was not retained in sensitivity analyses accounting for multiple observations from the same paper; exchangeable Na showed no detectable change. Soil moisture and exchangeable Ca, Mg and K did not differ detectably from reference soils, indicating that the robust declines in moisture, Ca and Mg were more consistent with reversal of invasion-associated states than degradation. By contrast, post-removal pH remained 0.43 units above reference soils while remaining similar to invaded soils, identifying a persistent chemical legacy. Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus pools showed no common directional response; broad management categories produced no general recovery pattern; and 0.62–15 years since removal did not predict systematic convergence toward reference conditions. Invasive-plant removal therefore selectively resets some soil properties, but neither erases all below-ground legacies nor guarantees continued recovery. By distinguishing treatment response from reference attainment, this study provides a comparator-aware framework in which recovery is demonstrated by sustained, multidimensional movement into ecosystem-specific reference ranges, rather than inferred from invader absence, treatment type or elapsed time.

title: Species-specific responses of zooplankton to intermittent seawater intrusion in a re-opened estuarine system
abstract: This study evaluated zooplankton community dynamics under an intermittent seawater intrusion regime following the partial re-opening of the Nakdong River Estuary Barrage, South Korea from 2022 to 2024. Environmental variables and zooplankton distributions were monitored across vertical water layers (surface, middle, and bottom) at five upstream and three downstream sites relative to the barrage. Linear Mixed-Effects model (LMM) and Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) revealed that salinity was the primary driver of broad-scale differences in community composition between upstream and downstream regions. However, its influence was largely confined to the study site adjacent to the estuarine barrage, where water temperature, pH, and spatiotemporal variables had stronger effects on community composition. Piecewise Structural Equation Modeling (PiecewiseSEM) and Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) further demonstrated species-specific responses associated with seawater intrusion volume; specifically, intrusion was negatively associated with the abundance of the rotifer Polyarthra vulgaris , whereas it was positively associated with the occurrence of the cladoceran Daphnia galeata . These findings suggest that under intermittent seawater pulses, the ecological impact of salinity is largely indirect and mediated by hydrodynamic dynamics rather than direct salinity stress. Consequently, relying solely on community-level and diversity indices may obscure subtle ecological changes, highlighting the necessity of establishing a species-level biological monitoring strategy. To reconcile ecological restoration with the protection of upstream freshwater resources, this study proposes an integrated estuarine management framework featuring adaptive gate-operation guidelines based on empirical benchmarks (approximately 500,000 m 3 of seawater inflow maintaining a 7-day bottom-layer salinity pulse within 1 km upstream) alongside event-aligned monitoring strategies.

title: Morphology-dependent decoupling of heat and air pollution regulation by urban green space in Chengdu
abstract: Urban heat and air pollution increasingly co-occur in urbanizing regions, yet existing green-space studies remain dominated by vegetation-quantity metrics and single-outcome assessments. It remains unclear whether green-space configurations contribute beyond vegetation quantity to LST, PM2.5, and O₃ regulation across seasons. This study examines associations between green space morphology and land surface temperature (LST), fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and ozone (O₃) in Chengdu, China, using data from 2000 to 2024. Green spaces were classified into seven morphological types using Morphological Spatial Pattern Analysis, and relationships were assessed using year-blocked analysis of variance, rank correlation, explainable machine learning, and land-use scenario simulation. Continuous types, particularly Core, were associated with the lowest LST and PM2.5, whereas fragmented types such as Islet and Branch showed the highest values, with an inter-type temperature difference exceeding 7 °C. This gradient peaked in summer for LST and winter for PM2.5. Ozone showed a seasonal reversal masked at the annual scale: fragmented types were associated with higher O₃ in summer but lower O₃ in winter, consistent with a shift from photochemical production to nitrogen oxide titration. After controlling for elevation, nighttime light intensity, population density, built-up density, and vegetation abundance, morphology accounted for 12–27% of attributed importance, while the negative Core contribution to PM2.5 was directionally consistent across all years. Scenario simulations showed that land-use change alters environmental outcomes primarily through green-space configuration. These findings demonstrate that urban environmental performance depends on both green-space quantity and configuration, and that no single configuration can optimize all environmental dimensions simultaneously.

title: Optimizing urban ecological networks via human-land synergy: Coupling ecosystem service supply-demand and multi-dimensional resistance
abstract: Urban agglomerations serve as vital economic engines that concurrently produce significant human-land conflicts, necessitating strong ecological networks to alleviate fragmentation resulting from heavy human activity. Conventional construction methods often emphasize supply rather than demand and biological considerations over societal limitations, leading to design strategies that are detached from resident welfare and practical execution. This study presents a “Human-Land Synergy Ecological Network” (HLS-EN) paradigm used in the Dianzhong Urban Agglomeration, integrating ecosystem service supply-demand alignment with composite resistant surfaces. The identification of ecological sources used the InVEST model with the Ecosystem Service Supply-Demand Ratio (ESDR) and Morphological Spatial Pattern Analysis (MSPA) to identify critical locations. The subsequent development of a composite social-ecological resistance surface incorporated human accessibility for local resistance inversion, along with a spatial conflict layer, enabling network formation through circuit theory and optimization via sophisticated network resilience simulations. Analysis indicated a polarized mismatch of “central deficit and peripheral surplus” in ecological services, requiring cross-regional compensation. The constructed network displayed a clear “dense west, sparse east” layout, wherein the urbanized eastern center depended on a precarious linear structure consisting of 696 corridors and 240 sources, interspersed with 257 conflict obstacles. The strategic incorporation of stepping stone nodes and altered passageways facilitated a topological shift from single-core reliance to multi-core support. Structural redundancy methods substantially postponed the key phase transition of network failure during intentional assault simulations by redistributing super hub loads and preserving connections over 70%. The HLS-EN technique adeptly harmonizes ecological security with resident welfare, providing a scientifically substantiated, actionable spatial planning instrument for addressing ecological deficiencies in densely populated urban areas.

title: Mapping of peatland in Mongolia using machine learning
abstract: Mongolia ranks among the top 10 countries by peatland area and represents an important global carbon sink. However, the distribution of its peatlands remains largely unconfirmed. Here, we combine field survey and remote sensing data to improve estimates of peatland distribution by modeling and mapping soil organic carbon content (SOCC). The case study dataset comprises 5400 soil samples from 1242 sites collected between 2000 and 2023, spanning Mongolia's major natural zones. Peat soils were defined using a threshold of >120 g kg −1 SOCC for the upper 0–30 cm of the soil profile. To predict SOCC, we evaluated thirty-five environmental covariates, including climate data, optical and thermal Landsat-8 imagery, vegetation indices, terrain factors, and soil properties. We implemented a random forest model within a spatial prediction framework, training it on the field soil observations. Cross-validation showed that the SOCC model achieved high accuracy ( r = 0.89 ), with the most important predictors being temperature, silt content, vegetation productivity, and moisture availability. We map a peatland area of 47,050 km 2 , equivalent to 2.9% of Mongolia's territory, concentrated in permafrost high-mountain, taiga, and forest-steppe zones of the major northern and western mountain ranges. Unlike previous estimates, which relied on coarse extrapolation or unvalidated inventories, our approach integrates an extensive field dataset with a machine learning method to produce the first detailed, field-validated national peatland map for Mongolia at 250 m resolution. Our work resolves fine-scale spatial patterns of carbon storage while quantifying predictor importance, providing a critical dataset and ecological indicator for evaluating carbon sinks and sources and for conservation planning in this climate-sensitive region.

title: Fusing UAV-LiDAR, yield-table inversion, and Sentinel data for forest aboveground biomass stock and increment mapping with Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation
abstract: Accurate mapping of forest carbon stocks and their future dynamics is critical for carbon cycle assessment, national greenhouse gas reporting, and forest carbon credit verification, yet most remote sensing approaches provide only static snapshots. This study develops a pipeline integrating individual-tree UAV-LiDAR analytics, yield-table inversion, machine learning, and multi-source satellite imagery to produce 10 m resolution maps of aboveground carbon stocks and projected carbon increments across Shikoku Island, Japan. Tree age and site quality were estimated for 132,890 trees by inverting the Local Yield table Construction System (LYCS) using LiDAR-derived height and diameter at breast height (DBH). An XGBoost model incorporating LYCS-derived age, site quality, topography, and species achieved an individual-tree aboveground biomass (AGB) R 2 of 0.86. AGB was converted to carbon stock using a uniform carbon fraction of 0.47 for model extrapolation. Forward age projection generated carbon increment maps at 5-, 10-, and 20-year horizons whose annual increments followed the ecologically expected rise, mid-rotation peak and decline. Satellite upscaling using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and DEM features achieved a stock model R 2 of 0.74 (rRMSE = 25.1%) under random hold-out validation, decreasing to 0.49 and 0.41 under spatial block and leave-one-survey-area-out validation, so the hold-out values describe within-domain performance. Separate carbon change models trained on Sentinel-1/2 features achieved hold-out R 2 of 0.69–0.74 (0.37–0.52 under the spatially independent schemes). Compared with GEDI L4B over a common forest domain, the estimates were higher by +25.8 Mg ha −1 . A Monte Carlo budget following IPCC Approach 1, propagating age and site quality jointly through the biomass model, gave total uncertainties of 48.5, 46.7 and 42.4% for the 5-, 10- and 20-year extrapolated maps. The outputs could support the monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) workflows of Japan's J-Credit Scheme and international voluntary carbon market standards as an exploratory decision-support and spatial-stratification tool.

title: Rethinking pathways of ecological management: Insights from climate-driven ecosystem health
abstract: Translating multidimensional ecosystem-health assessment into climate-sensitive management remains challenging in arid regions. Taking Xinjiang, China, as a representative desert-oasis-mountain system, this study developed a research framework comprising separate modules for VORS-based Ecosystem Health Index (EHI) assessment, LSTM time-series projection, climate-EHI LSTM-SHAP analysis, and management zoning. EHI was assessed at five-year intervals from 1990 to 2020 and projected to 2035 using historical EHI sequences. Model selection employed temporally blocked validation, with 2020 retained as an independent test set. Across five runs, LSTM outperformed linear regression and Random Forest. Spatially, relatively high EHI values were concentrated in the Altay, Tianshan, and Kunlun Mountains, whereas the Junggar and Tarim basins were dominated by low-to-moderate health levels. Historical changes were generally small and spatially heterogeneous, with localized improvement and degradation coexisting across Xinjiang. A separate climate-EHI LSTM-SHAP analysis identified precipitation of the wettest quarter, precipitation of the warmest quarter, and annual precipitation as the most influential climatic variables and revealed nonlinear, variable-specific response ranges. The nine selected climatic variables were used to construct the Ecosystem Climate Sensitivity Index (ECS), which was coupled with EHI to delineate five mutually exclusive management zones. The resulting zoning distinguishes priorities for ecological intervention, climate-sensitive regulation, early warning, functional maintenance, and coordinated conservation and enhancement.

title: Development and application of a fish and benthic macroinvertebrates multimetric index for tropical reservoirs
abstract: Multimetric indices (MMIs) are widely recognized as effective tools for assessing ecological conditions, but their application in tropical reservoirs remains limited. In this study, we developed an MMI by integrating fish and benthic macroinvertebrates to assess ecological condition in tropical hydropower reservoirs. The MMI was developed on samples in the littoral area of the Furnas Reservoir in southeastern Brazil. The index was calibrated using an Integrated Disturbance Index (IDI) to classify sites based on their local ecological conditions. The MMI has nine component metrics, including taxonomic richness, proportions of resistant and sensitive taxa, occurrence of non-native species, community diversity, and the functional and life-cycle characteristics of fish and macroinvertebrates. The MMI showed significant negative correlations with the IDI in both the calibration (ρ = -0.75; p < 0.001) and validation (ρ = -0.70; p < 0.01) datasets, indicating good responsiveness and robustness. When applied to four additional southeastern Brazilian reservoirs, the MMI also showed significant negative relationships with the IDI in three of those reservoirs (ρ ranging from -0.43 to -0.48; p ≤ 0.005), corroborating its transferability to other reservoirs with similar environmental and biogeographical conditions. Overall, this MMI represents a robust, practical, and cost-effective tool for assessing ecological condition, supporting monitoring initiatives, and informing littoral zone rehabilitation efforts.

title: Evolution of the potential suitable habitat of Haloxylon ammodendron in northwestern China under climate change, desert-unit differences, and identification of priority areas for conservation and restoration
abstract: Haloxylon ammodendron is an important dominant species and sand-fixing plant in the desert ecosystems of Northwest China. To assess climate-driven changes in its potentially suitable habitat, we integrated natural occurrence records from field surveys and public databases, developed an ensemble of eight algorithms in biomod2, and projected current and future suitability using three global climate models. The ensemble model achieved mean AUC and TSS values of 0.950 and 0.763, respectively, with precipitation and minimum winter temperature identified as the principal climatic drivers. Currently, potentially suitable habitat accounts for 3.97% of the study area and is projected to increase to 6.36%–11.85%, primarily through an expansion of low-suitability habitat. Responses differed markedly among the eight deserts. Expansion was greatest in the Tengger and Qaidam deserts, whereas the Taklimakan and Kumtag deserts remained predominantly unsuitable. Threshold-sensitivity and environmental-novelty analyses supported the overall expansion trend. Core conservation and priority restoration areas accounted for 0.70% and 3.23% of the study area, respectively. These findings provide a spatial basis for the conservation and climate-adaptive restoration of H. ammodendron across the eight deserts and their surrounding regions.

title: Flow intermittency amplifies temporal instability in macroinvertebrate communities: Insights from directional β-diversity
abstract: Flow intermittency increases temporal variation in taxonomic composition of riverine assemblages, but conventional β-diversity approaches often overlook the direction of compositional change across drying and wetting phases, which is central to intermittency-driven dynamics. Here, we applied a directional β-diversity framework to quantify species gain and loss through time and to examine intermittency-driven compositional change. We compared temporal changes in macroinvertebrate assemblage composition between perennial and intermittent sites within a river network. We analysed presence–absence macroinvertebrate data from 62 sites (15 perennial, 47 intermittent), sampled during 12 seasonal campaigns between 2020 and 2023 in southwestern Hungary, where most sites were historically perennial but have recently become intermittent. Temporal changes in assemblage composition were partitioned into directional β-diversity components (gain, loss, overlap). Assemblages at perennial sites showed high temporal stability, characterised by high overlap and balanced gain and loss components. In contrast, assemblages at intermittent sites had greater temporal variability, with gain- and loss-dominated phases alternating across successive dry and wetted periods. Nestedness components were consistently lower in intermittent sites. Flow intermittency was associated with greater temporal fluctuation and stronger directional imbalance in compositional dynamics. By resolving gain–loss asymmetry, directional β-diversity revealed temporal compositional patterns at intermittent sites that remained undetected by conventional non-directional approaches. Internal cross-validation showed high accuracy (0.919–0.984) in distinguishing perennial and intermittent sites across the three directional β-diversity partitions. These results demonstrate the predictive potential of directional β-diversity as a community-based signal of intermittency, although independent validation is required before operational application in bioassessment and monitoring.

title: Process-explicit ecological sensitivity assessment in Hohhot, China: asynchronous dynamics and spatial clustering
abstract: Ecological sensitivity in semi-arid agro-pastoral cities is jointly shaped by topography, climate, soil properties, land use, and human activities. A single integrated index may obscure whether high-sensitivity areas are driven by soil erosion, desertification, salinization, or human disturbance. Taking Hohhot, northern China, as a case study, this study developed a process-explicit ecological sensitivity assessment framework for 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025. Soil erosion, desertification, salinization, and human disturbance sensitivity were quantified and integrated using pooled normalization, combined weighting, Global Moran’s I, and Getis-Ord Gi* analysis. The four dimensions evolved asynchronously: soil erosion sensitivity was mainly constrained by northern mountainous terrain, desertification sensitivity peaked around 2010 and then declined, salinization sensitivity was concentrated in low-lying agricultural areas, and human disturbance sensitivity increased with urban expansion. From 2000 to 2025, highly and extremely sensitive areas decreased from 24.32% to 8.40%, whereas insensitive areas increased from 26.02% to 54.91%. However, integrated ecological sensitivity showed persistent spatial clustering, with Global Moran’s I ranging from 0.799 to 0.832. After 2015, the hot spot proportion increased from 24.67% to 31.78%, indicating that residual high-sensitivity patches became more locally clustered. These findings show that process-explicit decomposition and residual hot spot diagnosis can separate apparent class-area improvement from persistent spatially clustered ecological constraints, thereby supporting differentiated restoration zoning in semi-arid agro-pastoral cities.

title: JUNIPER: Joint use of nexus indicators for policy and environmental resilience–case study of Greece
abstract: Navigating sustainable development requires integrated modelling to quantify trade-offs between human systems and ecological boundaries. We introduce JUNIPER, a data-driven system dynamics model operationalising the Water, Energy, Food, Transport, Health, and Biodiversity (WEFTHB) nexus. We applied this framework to Greece during the baseline period from 2000 to 2019. JUNIPER's incremental contribution is a reproducible national-scale implementation that builds on an existing Water–Energy–Food (WEF) system-dynamics foundation by explicitly representing transport and linking cross-sector pressures to model-derived health and living-conditions indicators and model-derived, pressure-based biodiversity-risk proxies within a shared annual simulation. This operational integration supports the consistent examination of cross-sector trade-offs and co-benefits. Baseline results reveal a central cross-sector trade-off: a rising renewables share, declining energy-related CO 2 e emissions, and improved simulated longevity coexist with persistent irrigation-dominated water stress and deteriorating model-derived, pressure-based biodiversity-risk proxies. The integrated analysis highlights transport decarbonization and agricultural water/land management as candidate intervention domains for further scenario testing. Under the illustrative transport-transition assumptions, the model produced lower energy use, lower energy-related CO₂e emissions, and a lower model emissions-pressure aggregate, together with directionally favourable changes in the simulated health indicators and biodiversity-risk screening proxies. JUNIPER therefore provides a transparent, internally consistent historical baseline and a platform for conditional cross-sector policy screening under explicitly stated assumptions.

title: Linking landscape structure and resource availability to coastal bird responses under Spartina alterniflora invasion
abstract: The invasion of Spartina alterniflora has profoundly altered habitat composition, landscape patterns, and resource availability in coastal wetlands. However, the large-scale mechanisms through which these changes affect birds with different habitat requirements remain poorly understood. By integrating bird observation data, habitat remote sensing layers, and ecological datasets along the coastal zone of mainland China, this study systematically evaluated how habitat conversion, landscape structure, and resource supply influence mudflat-dependent, vegetation-dependent, and generalist birds under the context of S. alterniflora invasion. Our results demonstrate that S. alterniflora invasion reduces the capacity of coastal wetlands to support bird communities, particularly mudflat-dependent waterbirds. This decline is primarily associated with the loss of open mudflat habitats, which provide essential foraging areas for waterbirds by maintaining unobstructed access to benthic prey resources. Specifically, the conversion of unvegetated mudflats into S. alterniflora saltmarshes substantially weakened habitat support for mudflat-dependent and generalist birds, as dense vegetation altered habitat accessibility and reduced the availability of key foraging spaces. In addition, S. alterniflora invasion modified the landscape configuration of native habitats, influencing bird communities by altering the relationships between landscape structure and resource availability. Our findings highlight that the ecological consequences of S. alterniflora invasion extend beyond habitat area loss, as changes in habitat configuration and resource accessibility can further reduce the functional capacity of coastal wetlands to support bird biodiversity. Consequently, coastal conservation must transition from area-centric restoration toward spatial configuration optimization and quality enhancement to preserve the functional capacity of wetlands in supporting bird biodiversity.

title: Nonlinear controls on nitrogen export across heterogeneous riparian zones in a karst catchment: Insights from an integrated habitat classification framework
abstract: Identifying the spatial heterogeneity of riparian zones and its regulatory mechanisms on nitrogen migration is crucial for the prevention and control of non-point source pollution in watersheds. However, the influence of complex habitat characteristics in karst watersheds on nitrogen migration and its nonlinear “structure-process-function” response mechanism remains unclear. This study, focusing on the riparian zone of the Lianjiang River, constructed a comprehensive classification framework of “land use-geomorphic background-riparian matrix,” and combined in-situ simulated runoff scour experiments and generalized additive model to assess the runoff-infiltration characteristics and nitrogen concentrations driving mechanisms of different riparian types. The results showed significant spatial heterogeneity of the riparian zone in the study area, with agricultural land dominating and significant differences in the physicochemical properties of different soil types. The cumulative infiltration rate was: urban open space > forest land > agricultural land > grassland. With increasing scour events, the concentrations of TN, NH 4 + -N, and NO 3 − -N generally decreased, but the characteristics and driving pathways differed across the various nitrogen forms. NH 4 + -N export concentrations is mainly controlled nonlinearly by the intensity of human activities, explaining 56.9% of the variance. NO 3 − -N export concentrations is mainly driven by surface runoff, explaining 36.5% of the variance. TN export concentrations shows a weak response to a single environmental gradient and is controlled by the coupling of multiple “structure-process” factors. These results highlight the crucial role of complex habitat characteristics in regulating nitrogen migration along riparian zones in karst watersheds and provide a solid scientific foundation for the precise control of non-point source nitrogen pollution at the watershed scale.

title: Identifying ecosystem service drivers to inform land use scenario simulation: An InVEST-PLSR-PLUS framework for the Danjiangkou Reservoir Basin, China
abstract: The Danjiangkou Reservoir Basin is the core water source of the Middle Route of China's South-to-North Water Diversion Project, yet research in this basin has largely focused on static ecosystem service (ES) assessments, leaving the drivers of ES dynamics and their future trajectories poorly understood. This study develops an integrated InVEST–PLSR–PLUS framework that quantifies the spatiotemporal patterns of water yield, soil conservation, and carbon storage, identifies their dominant drivers objectively via Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), and projects land-use dynamics to 2030 using the PLUS model parameterized with PLSR-derived drivers rather than empirical selection. The main findings are as follows. (1) From 2010 to 2020, water yield increased markedly (from 79.22 to 895.38 to 166.69–1000.24 mm year −1 ), soil conservation declined (maximum from 941.60 to 641.91 t ha −1 year −1 ), and carbon storage remained stable (maximum around 20.4 t ha −1 year −1 ); high soil conservation and carbon storage values were concentrated in ecological and economic forests, whereas elevated water yield occurred mainly in farmland, orchards, and built-up land. (2) Vegetation and land-use variables dominated ES dynamics: EVI (VIP = 1.609), NDVI (VIP = 1.583), ecological forest area (VIP = 1.553), economic forest area (VIP = 1.476), and farmland area (VIP = 1.445) exerted strong positive effects; among landscape-pattern metrics, the landscape shape index (LSI; VIP = 1.313) was positively associated with all three services, whereas patch-subdivision metrics (PD, ED, IJI) showed negative associations; climatic and socioeconomic variables contributed only marginally (VIP < 0.8, except GDP at 0.864). (3) Under the natural evolution scenario, ecological forest and orchard areas are projected to decrease by 40.89 km 2 and 20.54 km 2 by 2030, while economic forest (+29.63 km 2 ), water area (+24.10 km 2 ), farmland (+1.68 km 2 ), and built-up land (+5.98 km 2 ) expand. These findings demonstrate that vegetation cover and landscape connectivity fundamentally regulate ES provision, and indicate that ecological forest protection, control landscape fragmentation, and regulate built-up land and orchard expansion to safeguard the ecological security of this strategic water-source region.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and future trends in vegetation productivity in Xinjiang driven by vapor pressure deficit and potential evapotranspiration
abstract: Under climate change, extreme drought events have become increasingly frequent; however, the regulatory mechanisms through which atmospheric drought affects vegetation productivity in arid regions remain unclear. Understanding the spatiotemporal relationships between vegetation productivity, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and potential evapotranspiration (PET) is essential for assessing ecosystem responses to climate change. Using remote-sensing normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), gross primary productivity (GPP), and meteorological VPD and PET data for Xinjiang from 2004 to 2023, this study employed trend analysis, the Hurst exponent, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to investigate vegetation responses to atmospheric drought stress and the persistence of future trends. GPP increased significantly in 22% of the study area and NDVI in 8.9%, mainly along the Tarim Basin margins, whereas localized vegetation degradation occurred in northern Xinjiang. VPD and PET were primary statistical contributors, with substantially higher relative importance than other factors. Temporally, both were negatively correlated with vegetation productivity; spatially, positive correlations occurred in southern oasis regions, whereas negative correlations predominated in northern Xinjiang. Strong temporal persistence in vegetation productivity was observed in only 8.6% of the vegetated areas. GPP is projected to decline after peaking in 2019, reaching approximately 197.62 g C m −2 yr −1 by 2033, while XGBoost achieved relatively high predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.78). Overall, atmospheric drought substantially constrained vegetation productivity and weakened ecosystem stability, highlighting the need for differentiated management strategies in southern and northern Xinjiang to mitigate the risk of regional vegetation productivity decline.

title: Assessment and projection of mangrove blue carbon sink along the Guangdong coastline: integrating remote sensing and modeling techniques
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems along the Guangdong coastline serve as a vital blue carbon sink, yet their carbon sequestration potential under changing climatic conditions requires rigorous assessment and forward-looking evaluation. This study develops an integrated framework combining remote sensing techniques and spatial modeling approaches to quantify historical changes and project future trajectories of mangrove blue carbon stocks in Guangdong Province, China. Time-series satellite imagery was used to quantify changes in mangrove extent and associated carbon storage over the period 1994 to 2024. Field-validated sediment core data, coupled with the InVEST and CA-Markov models, were utilized to assess historical carbon storage and forecast future challenges along the coastline. Our results reveal substantial spatial variability in mangrove carbon storage across Guangdong. A non-significant increase in mangrove area was observed during the first decade of the study period (1994–2004). In contrast, a significant area expansion of 10.71% occurred between 2014 and 2024, with projections indicating a further increase of 19.45% by 2034. The eastern coast of Guangdong exhibited greater potential for mangrove expansion than the western coast. Based on the projected mangrove extent and the adopted carbon-density framework, the InVEST model estimated a potential 24.62% increase in mangrove carbon storage by 2034 relative to 2024. By explicitly integrating spatiotemporal remote sensing analysis with predictive land-use and carbon storage modeling, this study advances a scalable and transferable framework for assessing mangrove blue carbon dynamics under climate and development pressures. The findings provide critical evidence to inform adaptive coastal management, strengthen Guangdong's carbon neutrality goals, and support nature-based solutions for climate mitigation. Overall, this integrated approach provides a robust scientific basis for coastal spatial planning and offers actionable insights for conserving and enhancing mangrove blue carbon resources along this ecologically and economically important coastline.

title: Satellite insights into diatom biomass dynamics and environmental drivers in the eastern China marginal seas
abstract: Diatoms are among the dominant phytoplankton groups in marginal seas and play a pivotal role in marine primary production and biogeochemical cycling. In this study, focusing on the eastern China marginal seas (ECMS), we developed a remote sensing model to retrieve diatom biomass ( C diat ) directly from remote sensing reflectance. Multiple linear regression and machine-learning methods were evaluated using in situ observations and satellite-in situ matchup datasets. Based on its balanced performance across the available evaluation datasets, the stepwise regression model was selected as the final regional model, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.61 and a symmetric mean absolute percentage error of 48.3% in the satellite–in situ matchup validation. Application of this model to a 23–year record (2002–2025) of Aqua–MODIS observations revealed pronounced spatial and temporal patterns of C diat across the ECMS. Spatially, elevated C diat values were concentrated in coastal and estuarine waters and decreased markedly offshore. Strong seasonality was observed in coastal regions, characterized by summer maxima and winter minima. SHAP-based attribution analysis further identified iron, sea surface salinity, mixed layer depth, photosynthetically active radiation, silicon, and sea surface temperature as important environmental factors associated with nonlinear variations in C diat . River discharge was positively associated with C diat in estuarine waters, although these relationships weakened after removal of the seasonal cycle, indicating a substantial contribution from shared seasonal variability. These findings provide satellite-based insights into the multiscale variability of diatom biomass in the ECMS and improve our understanding of coastal ecosystem responses to environmental change.

title: Ecological industry empowers rural industrial revitalization: The practical logic and driving mechanism of karst desertification control
abstract: Ecological industry (EI) for desertification control has become an important pathway for empowering rural industrial revitalization (RIR) and enhancing regional human well-being. However, few studies have explored the driving mechanisms through which EI promote RIR in the context of typical desertification control. Therefore, this study selected three comprehensive desertification control areas—Salaxi, Hongfenghu, and Huajiang—as study areas, evaluated the spatial differences in the levels of EI and RIR based on a unified criterion-layer and structural-layer framework, and revealed their coupling characteristics. Subsequently, a driving network through which EI promotes RIR was constructed based on the modified factor contribution model, and the interactive effects of factors on EI and RIR were examined using the optimal geographic detector. The results showed that: (1) the levels of EI and RIR in the three study areas exhibited consistency: Hongfenghu (EI = 0.5350, RIR = 0.5308) > Salaxi (EI = 0.2375, RIR = 0.2556) > Huajiang (EI = 0.2324, RIR = 0.2550). The coupling coordination level between EI and RIR followed the order of Hongfenghu (0.80) > Huajiang (0.43) > Salaxi (0.40), and villages such as LDS, YQ, and ML villages achieved high-level coupling. (2) The driving effect of EI on RIR was ranked as Hongfenghu (76.38%) > Huajiang (46.31%) > Salaxi (45.78%), with an overall driving effect of 55.48%. Resource dependence and insufficient infrastructure allocation were the key factors constraining the development of EI in Salaxi and Huajiang, whereas EI development in Hongfenghu has shifted from resource dependence to innovation-driven industrial development. (3) Factor interaction analysis indicated that EI-driven RIR is jointly influenced by internal industrial capacity and external environmental conditions, and the synergistic effects of production capacity, industrial benefits, and geographical advantages represent important pathways for promoting RIR. This study provides a scientific basis for consolidating the achievements of desertification control and promoting the healthy and sustainable development of regional ecological economies.

title: Multi-objective optimization of “human-grassland-wild ungulate-livestock” system in a typical nature reserve on the Qinghai-Tibetan plateau
abstract: Nature reserves on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) play crucial roles in supporting ecological security. Achieving the balance of “human-grassland-wild ungulate-livestock” (HGWL) system is important for sustainable development in these nature reserves. This study developed an indicator-based decision-support framework based on machine learning (ML) methods and the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) in the Changtang Nature Reserve on the QTP. An extreme gradient boosting model was employed to quantify the imbalance between aboveground biomass (AGB) and crude protein (CP) required by livestock and wild ungulates and that supplied by grasslands. A multi-objective optimization model of HGWL system aiming to increase the ecological and economic benefits and decrease the grassland pressure was constructed using NSGA-II based on the imbalance of AGB and CP. This model was applied to analyze the optimized cultivated grasslands planting structure, livestock structure and other variables in three scenarios. Ecological benefits decreased by 0.50% in economic development priority scenario, and economic benefits decreased by 16.22% in ecological protection priority scenario. By contrast, ecological benefits and economic benefits increased, and grassland pressure decreased by 5.06%, 5.05%, and 0.74% respectively in ecological economic balance scenario, which was identified as the optimal scenario. More areas of alfalfa, higher sheep slaughter volume and lower goat and yak slaughter volume were recommended to achieve the HGWL balance. The combination of ML and NSGA-II can help achieve the multi-objective optimization of HGWL system, and this framework has potential to be promoted to other nature reserves around the world.

title: Improving multi-factor river water quality prediction using deep learning and large language models with retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Water quality prediction is critical to protect river ecosystems and sustain effective water management under increasing urbanization pressures. Current methods rely on a limited number of influencing factors and lack interpretability, which presents challenges in practical applications. Emerging large language models (LLMs) have strong capabilities for understanding domain knowledge, but require most relevant information for reliability. This study proposed an automated multi-factor river water quality prediction framework by coupling deep learning with LLMs enhanced by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). A multi-dimensional dataset was constructed by integrating water quality with meteorological, socio-economic and hydro-topographic features to fully characterize river dynamics. Then, LLM-guided hybrid deep learning model, combining convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) and attention mechanisms, namely LCLA model, was developed to predict six water quality indicators. Hyperparameters covering model structure and training strategy were efficiently configured through a literature-based knowledge retrieval, achieving optimal MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE of 0.42, 0.96, 0.54, and 0.11, respectively, with improved optimization efficiency. Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley analysis, revealing main contributions of turbidity, domestic water use, and river discharge. Finally, a RAG-enhanced multi-agent system was established to perform water quality grade classification and improvement recommendation generation by integrating domain knowledge and expert experience with LLM reasoning. The case study of Xinwu District demonstrated actionable management guidance consistent with on-site conditions. This study offered a reliable and efficient framework, with advantages in prediction performance and knowledge decision support, for advancing intelligent river water quality prediction and management in complex environments.

title: Spatial patterns and climatic associations of pollination demand, habitat-based supply, and pollination-dependent production in South Korea
abstract: Pollination is a critical ecosystem service for agricultural productivity, yet climate change and intensification increasingly destabilize its delivery. Despite its importance, pollination demand, pollination-dependent production, and habitat-based supply are rarely assessed through an integrated framework. This study develops spatial indicators representing these components across 17 regions in South Korea from 2016 to 2022. The pollination demand indicator and the pollination-dependent production indicator were quantified using linear mixed-effects models relating standardized cultivation area and yield, respectively, to crop-specific pollinator dependence. The habitat-based supply indicator was estimated using the InVEST Crop Pollination model. Relationships among indicators and their associations with regional climatic and geographic variables were examined using Spearman's rank correlation analysis. Results showed a strong but imperfect association between pollination-dependent production and pollination demand indicators ( ρ = 0.87, p < 0.001), indicating that the relative cultivation orientation toward pollinator-dependent crops was not uniformly associated with production responses across regions. Climatic variables were more strongly associated with the pollination-dependent production indicator than with the habitat-based supply indicator. The production indicator showed stronger associations with temperature-related gradients than the pollination demand indicator, with positive correlations with latitude ( ρ = 0.76, p < 0.001) and negative correlations with mean annual temperature ( ρ = −0.71, p < 0.01). Furthermore, the habitat-based supply indicator showed only partial correspondence with the pollination demand indicator ( ρ = 0.54, p < 0.05) and marginal correlation with the pollination-dependent production indicator ( ρ = 0.42, p < 0.1), suggesting that potential habitat-based supply does not fully correspond to regional variation in the pollination-dependent production indicator across latitudinal and temperature gradients. These findings suggest that habitat-based supply alone does not fully correspond to regional variation in the pollination-dependent production indicator, while climatic conditions provide additional explanatory context beyond habitat-based supply potential. This study demonstrates the importance of explicitly distinguishing among the pollination demand indicator, the habitat-based supply indicator, and the pollination-dependent production indicator, and provides an integrated indicator framework for comparative regional assessment under climatic gradients.

title: Assessing plastic-related environmental risk across EU countries of the Danube basin using a composite risk index
abstract: Plastic-related environmental risk in transboundary river systems represents a multidimensional challenge emerging from the interaction between plastic-related pressures, the vulnerability of receiving aquatic environments, and the capacity of circular economy systems to mitigate environmental impacts. This study investigates the structural factors associated with plastic-related environmental risk and the resulting territorial configurations across seven European Union countries of the Danube basin. Using a balanced panel dataset comprising 84 country-year observations for seven European Union countries over the period 2012–2023, the study develops the Danube Plastic-related Pollution Risk Index (DPPRI), a composite indicator that operationalizes plastic-related environmental risk through the integration of plastic-related pressure, organic pollution vulnerability, and circular economy mitigation capacity. The analytical framework combines composite indicator construction, an Ordinary Least Squares benchmark, supervised machine learning, model interpretation, and unsupervised clustering. Random Forest modelling is applied to assess the relative contribution of environmental, economic, and circular-economy indicators to modelled DPPRI variability, while SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis identifies the magnitude and direction of each indicator's contribution to the predicted composite-index values. K-means clustering, supported by an exploratory hierarchical clustering assessment, is further employed to identify structural risk typologies among the 84 country-year observations. The results show that trade-related plastic flows, the operationalized environmental vulnerability dimension, and indicators of circular-economy intensity and decoupling are among the principal factors associated with variability in the composite risk index, while recycling and recovery performance contribute to the mitigation dimension of the framework. The clustering analysis identifies three distinct structural risk profiles among the analysed country-year observations, reflecting different combinations of plastic-related pressure, environmental vulnerability, economic activity, and mitigation capacity. This study contributes an integrated and potentially transferable risk-screening framework for examining structural conditions associated with plastic-related environmental risk in transboundary river systems. Rather than estimating measured macroplastic or microplastic concentrations, the proposed approach integrates structural indicators of anthropogenic pressure, environmental vulnerability, and mitigation capacity to support the prioritization of monitoring needs and coordinated circular-economy and river-basin policy interventions.

title: Unraveling multi-scale associations and nonlinear threshold relationships between urban spatial structure and water quality in cold cities based on interpretable machine learning
abstract: The tension between urban development and water quality improvement is a major challenge for river-basin management, particularly in cold regions characterized by pronounced freeze–thaw processes. Focusing on the Songhua River Basin, this study integrated water quality monitoring and road-network data (2020–2024) with space syntax and the interpretable machine learning framework XGBoost–SHAP to investigate the nonlinear and cross-scale associations between urban spatial structure and river water quality. The overall City Water Quality Index (CWQI) increased by 6.25% during the study period, indicating an overall deterioration in water quality. Water quality was generally better during the ice-covered period than during the snowmelt period. Dissolved oxygen (DO) was the dominant water-quality indicator during the ice-covered and dry periods, whereas permanganate index (COD Mn ) was more influential during the snowmelt and flood periods. Spatially, water quality was highest in the upstream region, followed by the downstream and midstream regions. Space syntax analysis showed that spatial centrality decreased by 2.3%, with the most pronounced decline occurring at the urban scale, forming a “dual-core, dual-node, and multi-point” pattern. By contrast, spatial hierarchy increased by 1.71%, with the largest increase occurring at the block scale, forming a “one-axis, two-belt, and three-corridor” pattern. XGBoost–SHAP analysis revealed nonlinear and scale-dependent associations between spatial structure and predicted CWQI. During the non-freeze–thaw phase, urban-scale NAIN exhibited relatively larger SHAP contributions and stronger associations with predicted CWQI than district-scale and block-scale indicators. During the freeze–thaw phase, these associations became more strongly cross-scale, with the direction and strength of SHAP contributions changing across different indicator-value ranges, indicating threshold-dependent and nonlinear responses.

title: Acoustic indices differ in their sensitivity to biophony, geophony, and temporal ecological dynamics
Adapting the temperature-fluorescence dryness index as a functional ecological indicator for tracking agroecosystem drought in China's winter wheat regions
abstract: Accurate agroecosystem drought monitoring of winter wheat is essential for ensuring food security in China. The traditional Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) relies on structural reflectance metrics and can be affected by delayed vegetation responses and canopy saturation. The study adapted the Temperature-Fluorescence Dryness Index (TFDI), which integrates land surface temperature and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence, for drought monitoring across China's major winter-wheat regions during 2003–2022. After accounting for temporal autocorrelation and controlling the false discovery rate (FDR), TFDI increased the spatial coverage of significant negative correlations with SMCI1.0 soil moisture at 0–10 cm and 10–20 cm by 14.05 and 13.32 percentage points, respectively, relative to TVDI. However, this overall soil-moisture advantage did not extend to NASAR, where TVDI showed stronger associations in both evaluated layers. Coupling with meteorological drought was scale dependent: TFDI retained broader FDR-significant coverage at SPI-1 and SPI-3, but paired correlation magnitudes were comparable at SPI-1 and only modestly stronger at SPI-3; neither index retained FDR-significant coverage at SPI-6. Trend analysis of the annual March–May TFDI series indicated a mean Sen slope of 0.0092 yr − 1, with FDR-significant positive TFDI trends (drying) across 40.37% of the persistent winter-wheat domain. Drying was concentrated in the Huang–Huai–Hai Plain, Middle–Lower Yangtze Plain, Loess Plateau, and Sichuan Basin. Explanatory modeling identified a north–south contrast in environmental associations with TFDI trends: atmospheric evaporative-demand variables had greater model-attributed importance in northern regions, whereas precipitation had greater importance in southern regions. These results support the large-scale application of TFDI as a physiologically informed indicator of agroecosystem drought while defining the statistical and spatial boundaries of its advantage.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and drivers of vegetation net primary productivity in a karst region: Nonlinear responses and spatial-scale effects revealed by XGBoost–SHAP and MGWR
abstract: Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) is a key indicator of vegetation productivity and carbon fixation. This study examined Wenshan and Honghe prefectures in Yunnan Province, a typical karst region of southwestern China. Theil–Sen trend estimation, the Mann–Kendall test, XGBoost–SHAP, and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) were integrated to characterize NPP dynamics during 2001–2020, identify nonlinear NPP responses to major explanatory variables, and assess spatial nonstationarity. Annual mean NPP fluctuated but showed an overall increasing tendency, with an estimated linear rate of 3.05 g C m −2 yr −2 ( p = 0.052). At the pixel scale, increasing trends covered 72.14% of the study area, including 34.82% with significant increases, whereas decreasing trends occurred across 26.42%. XGBoost–SHAP results showed that land use (LU) and the normalized difference built-up and soil index (NDBSI) had the greatest model-based relative importance, followed by elevation (DEM) and precipitation (PRE). The SHAP contributions of NDBSI and PRE changed direction at approximately −0.03 and 1208 mm, respectively. Both candidate response-transition positions were highly reproducible under spatial-block bootstrap resampling within the current model and sampling framework. MGWR revealed marked temporal variation and scale-dependent spatial nonstationarity in the associations between NPP and its explanatory variables. PRE–NPP associations differed among periods, whereas NDBSI was predominantly negatively associated with NPP and operated at a strongly localized spatial scale. These findings indicate that karst-region management should combine regional land-use planning and water-risk management with targeted restoration of locally degraded surface patches. • NPP showed an overall upward tendency in the karst region during 2001–2020. • Land use and NDBSI had the highest model-based importance for NPP. • Stable candidate transitions were identified near NDBSI −0.03 and PRE 1208 mm. • MGWR revealed temporal variation and variable-specific spatial scales. • NDBSI–NPP associations were predominantly negative and strongly localized.

title: Remote sensing retrieval and driving factors of dissolved organic carbon concentration in typical lakes of the middle Yangtze River in China from 2000 to 2023
abstract: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is the largest organic carbon (C) pool in aquatic systems and closely related to lake C emissions. However, long-term monitoring of DOC dynamics and their driving factors remains limited. This study analyzed DOC concentration evolution in five typical lakes of the middle Yangtze River from 2000 to 2023 using remote sensing retrievals, Mann-Kendall trend test, Pearson correlation, and multiple general linear model (GLM). The results showed that (1) The retrieval models performed well, with R 2 values of 0.76, 0.74, 0.80, 0.84, and 0.76 for Daye, Bao'an, Wanghu, Xiandao, and Cihu lakes, respectively. (2) From 2000 to 2023, the DOC concentrations increased by 1.16 and 3.57 mg/L per decade in Daye and Bao'an lakes, respectively; decreased by 1.38 and 4.00 mg/L per decade in Xiandao and Cihu lakes, respectively; but remained relatively stable in Wanghu Lake. (3) The DOC concentration was highest in summer for most lakes, although the decomposition of submerged vegetation litter led to relatively higher DOC concentrations in spring in some years in Bao'an and Xiandao. (4) GLM analysis identified cultivated land, the normalized difference vegetation index, and population as the most significant watershed-scale drivers. These findings underscore the need for non-point source pollution control in this basin. The results of this study provide a new strategy for the large-scale monitoring of DOC concentrations in lake water, which is helpful for providing a deeper understanding of the lake C cycle and aiding lake ecological restoration and management.

title: Nonlinear contributions of spatial structure and functional diversity to ecological resilience: A case study of the upper Yangtze River urban agglomeration
abstract: The upper Yangtze River urban agglomeration (YUUA) serves as a critical ecological barrier, where territorial spatial structural and functional diversity is essential for sustaining ecological resilience (ER). Nevertheless, the underlying relationships and response patterns remain unclear. This study employs multiple methodological approaches, including kernel density analysis, random forest model, and SHAP framework, to systematically explore the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and contribution pattern of ER and territorial spatial structural and functional diversity in the YUUA from 2012 to 2022. The findings are as follows: (1) ER increased steadily, showing a pattern of higher values in the north and lower values in the south, accompanied by a dual pattern of lower-tail convergence and upper-tail polarization. Chongqing and Chengdu exhibited pronounced spatial polarization. (2) Ecological functional diversity (EFD) was identified as the dominant contributing factor closely associated with ER variations. (3) Nonlinear estimation results revealed significant threshold effects. Both EFD and production functional diversity (PFD) exhibit a U-shaped association with ER, with positive marginal contributions after a critical threshold. In contrast, structural diversity (SD) and living functional diversity (LFD) show an inverted U-shaped association with ER, indicating an optimal threshold. (4) EFD showed functional substitution where living functions were inadequate, whereas PFD contributed more to ER in highly open areas; synergies existed between urbanization and LFD, and between green innovation and SD. This study quantitatively characterizes the nonlinear relationship between territorial spatial structural and functional diversity and ER, offering insights to optimize spatial patterns and implement differentiated regulation to enhance ecological resilience.

title: Integrating ecosystem health and land use conflicts for ecological management zoning and driver analysis in China's ecological barrier zones
abstract: Unraveling the interrelationship between ecosystem health (EH) and land-use conflicts (LUC) and implementing zoned management are crucial for ensuring regional ecological security and achieving sustainable development. However, existing studies still have limitations in identifying the dominant factors and key thresholds of ecological zoning, which constrains the formulation of ecological management strategies. Focusing on China's Ecological Barrier Zones (EBZ), this paper quantitatively assessed the spatiotemporal evolution and interrelationships between EH and LUC from 2000 to 2020 by integrating multidimensional indicators and bivariate spatial autocorrelation methods. Subsequently, ecological zones were delineated using a four-quadrant approach, and XGBoost-SHAP and GWR models were employed to elucidate the nonlinear driving mechanisms and spatial heterogeneity of these ecological zones. The results revealed that (1) EH followed a trend of first declining and then rising, with 2010 serving as a turning point, whereas LUC exhibited the opposite trend; (2) LUC exerted a significant inhibitory effect on EH spatially, though the intensity of this effect has relatively weakened; (3) Ecological zones constructed based on the EH–LUC framework exhibited temporal succession and a stepped distribution pattern; (4) At both the EBZ and zonal scales, natural factors (e.g., normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), precipitation, and slope) were key determinants of EH, all of which exhibit distinct nonlinearity, threshold effects, and spatial non-stationarity. In contrast, the interactions among land use intensity, human footprint, and NDVI play a dominant role in the dynamics of LUC. These findings provide a scientific basis for formulating differentiated ecological management strategies to ensure sustainable development within ecological thresholds.

title: Phosphorus-associated constraint on soil seed bank regeneration potential under salinization: Implications for the restoration of formerly cultivated wetlands
abstract: Passive restoration is the primary approach for near-natural recovery of formerly cultivated wetlands in semi-arid regions. Soil salinization, a growing global abiotic stress, degrades wetland structure and function. Although the mechanisms of wetland restoration and salinization effects on plant diversity are well known, how salinization affects the regeneration potential of the soil seed bank (SSB) during formerly cultivated wetland restoration remains unclear. We investigated the composition of SSBs, the structure of plant communities (PCs), and soil properties under four salinity levels in natural wetlands and formerly cultivated wetlands through field surveys and germination experiments. We also explored the effects of salinization on the SSBs and the changes in similarity between SSBs and PCs. Wetland reclamation and soil salinization significantly altered SSB composition, reducing species richness and density, particularly of perennials. The similarity between SSBs and PCs declined with increasing soil salinity. Redundancy analysis identified total phosphorus (P) as a key driver of variations in SSBs. Structural equation modeling further revealed that salinization stress was associated with lower soil organic matter and increased phosphorus retention, indicating a strong P-related constraint that may negatively affect SSBs. Soil salinization thus appears to weaken the SSB regeneration potential during passive restoration of formerly cultivated wetlands, likely through P-associated mechanisms. We recommend alleviating this via hydrological connectivity and active regulation of SSB input–output dynamics. This study advances the understanding of SSB regeneration potential and guides near-natural restoration in semi-arid regions.

title: Climate regulation of carbon uptake is mediated by vegetation state: a case study in Yunnan Province, southwest China
abstract: Approximately 60% of the global variation in photosynthetic efficiency cannot be explained by climatic factors alone, representing a major bottleneck in carbon cycle and vegetation productivity estimation. Vegetation state serves as a critical link between environmental changes and photosynthetic processes, with its trade‐offs and interactions with environmental factors collectively modulating photosynthetic efficiency. Traditional photosynthetic efficiency models, which primarily rely on climatic drivers, fail to accurately capture the differences in physiological regulation mechanisms and ecological strategies among vegetation types.
