Taking Yunnan Province in China as the study area, this research integrates structural equation modeling (SEM) with machine‐learning‐based SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis, using vegetation state as a mediating variable to systematically disentangle the direct and indirect mechanisms through which climate regulates net primary productivity (NPP). The results indicate that: (1) Vegetation state is the primary mediator of climate impacts on productivity, but its mediating role is not fixed; rather, it varies with the vegetation metric employed. (2) Structural indicators (leaf area index, LAI), physiological indicators (solar‐induced chlorophyll fluorescence, SIF), and stress‐related indicators (Temperature‐Vegetation‐Precipitation‐Drought Index, TVPDI) all exhibit balanced mediating effects, providing the most reliable and interpretable mediation models within the biodiversity hotspot of Yunnan. (3) The global importance ranking of factors, expressed as mean absolute SHAP values, is: precipitation (PREC) > LAI > temperature (TEMP) > TVPDI > solar radiation (SRAD) > SIF, with these factors regulating carbon assimilation through different mechanisms. (4) Vegetation physiological status and growth conditions significantly modulate the influence intensity of precipitation, temperature, and solar radiation; the effect of climate on NPP depends on current vegetation structure and stress conditions, and exhibits pronounced nonlinear characteristics and threshold effects. This study holds promise for substantially improving the explanatory power of photosynthetic efficiency models and for providing novel modeling approaches for global vegetation productivity estimation and carbon cycle research.

title: A SAR-derived indicator framework for flood extent, severity, and land-cover vulnerability in a wetland floodplain
abstract: Wetland floodplains require reliable indicators that support flood monitoring and impact assessment under increasing climatic variability. Although satellite remote sensing has improved flood detection, many studies remain focused on binary mapping products, limiting their usefulness for assessing flood magnitude, severity, and land-cover-specific vulnerability. This study develops a satellite-derived indicator framework using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery within a Google Earth Engine environment. A site-specific dry-season land use/land cover (LULC) baseline is derived from Sentinel-2 imagery at 10 m resolution using a Random Forest classifier, achieving 91.10% overall accuracy (κ = 0.880), and serves as a reference condition that reduces misclassification of seasonally inundated agricultural areas. Flood extent is represented as a binary indicator of temporary inundation, obtained by applying change-detection threshold to VV- and VH- polarized SAR backscatter that isolates transient flood signals from permanent water bodies and other stable low-backscatter surfaces. Flood severity is further quantified as an ordinal indicator based on the magnitude of backscatter reduction, distinguishing mild, moderate, and severe inundation. Land-cover-specific vulnerability is assessed as the proportion of each land-cover class affected. Application to the May–June 2022 pre-monsoon flash flood in the haor wetlands of northeastern Bangladesh shows that 1963.45 km 2 (60.41%) of the study area was inundated at peak flooding. Vegetation and cropland accounted for the largest flooded area (1508.25 km 2 ), while bare soil, embankments, and roads exhibited the highest proportional inundation (66.81%). Built-up areas experienced moderate relative exposure (47.74%). Severity analysis indicates that moderate-to-severe inundation dominated the event, with severe flooding concentrated in central wetland basins and major river corridors. The proposed indicators provide a transferable and repeatable framework for flood monitoring, comparative assessment, and management support in wetland-dominated floodplain environments.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution of vulnerability and dynamic transmission among subsystems in the water–energy–food–ecology (WEFE) system of a major grain-producing region: A case study of Henan Province, China
abstract: Abstract Major grain-producing regions are indispensable for national food security, yet they operate under water scarcity, coal-dependent energy use, and ecological stress. Reliable assessment of water-energy-food-ecology (WEFE) system vulnerability requires indicators that can be traced to feedback mechanisms and are not dominated by redundant variables. Focusing on 18 prefecture-level administrative units in Henan Province, this study develops a city-level panel framework for 2010–2023 that links system dynamics (SD)-based feedback identification with random forest (RF)-based importance screening. The selected indicators are then used with the entropy weight-TOPSIS method, spatial autocorrelation analysis, and a panel vector autoregression (PVAR) model to examine changes in WEFE vulnerability and cross-subsystem transmission. The results reveal a province-wide decline in WEFE vulnerability, accompanied by widening inter-city disparities. The mean WEFE vulnerability index decreased from 0.7418 to 0.6571, representing an 11.43% decline, while the inter-city standard deviation increased from 0.0314 to 0.1043. High-vulnerability units were concentrated mainly in northern Henan; however, the global Moran's I test was not significant, indicating that province-wide spatial clustering was not detected. The benchmark PVAR links ecological vulnerability to subsequent changes in other subsystems. Innovations in ecological vulnerability contributed 25.49% and 31.14% to the forecast error variance of the energy and food subsystems, respectively. These estimates identify lagged statistical relationships between ecological vulnerability and the energy and food subsystems; the underlying mechanisms require separate evidence. Governance in Henan should therefore move beyond adjacency-based zoning and target the dominant vulnerability sources of individual cities.

title: Quantifying the nonlinear effects of driving factors on grassland degradation in Inner Mongolia, China
abstract: Revealing nonlinear relationships and identifying high-risk grassland degradation (GD) areas are essential for grassland conservation and sustainable development in arid and semi-arid regions. Nevertheless, existing research mainly emphasize linear relationships, lacking systematic characterization of nonlinear responses, threshold effects and coupled interactions among driving factors. In this study, remote-sensing data were adopted to assess spatial patterns of GD. An interpretable artificial-intelligence framework was further applied to reveal nonlinear relationships, threshold effects and interactions among factors, identify pixel-scale dominant driving factors and conduct GD risk prediction. GD showed a stage-dependent transition from degradation expansion to substantial recovery, with degraded areas spreading mainly from the central grasslands toward the northeast. Negative SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) contributions were dominated by natural factors in the first two stages (40.3% and 44.0%) but by anthropogenic factors in the third stage (44.1%). SHAP interaction analysis revealed that higher population density (PD) strengthened the negative effect of GDP, whereas DEM, relative humidity (RHU), and PD substantially modulated the nonlinear response of average temperature (Avg_TEM) across different temperature ranges. GD risk was predominantly low to moderate (40.7% and 53.5%), while high-risk areas accounted for only 5.7% and were mainly concentrated in parts of Xilingol, Hulunbuir, and Chifeng. This innovative analytical framework effectively interprets inner driving mechanisms of GD and provides scientific basis for region-specific ecological restoration and targeted grassland management.

title: Spatial patterns and environmental associations of plankton communities in the Karst free-flowing Chishui river: Insights from eDNA metabarcoding and network analysis
abstract: Understanding the mechanisms governing plankton community assembly and spatial heterogeneity is fundamental for freshwater ecosystem conservation, yet such knowledge remains scarce for free - flowing rivers in Karst regions facing compounding anthropogenic pressures. Here, we investigated the spatial patterns, community – environment relationships, and co-occurrence network architecture of phytoplankton and zooplankton communities along the mainstem of the Chishui River, the last undammed tributary of the upper Yangtze River and a biodiversity hotspot of global conservation significance. Integrating environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding with ecological network analysis, we quantified the relative contributions of environmental variables and spatial factors to community structuring across 15 sites along the river continuum. Our results revealed striking trophic-level divergence in community-environment relationships: zooplankton showed significantly stronger associations with measured environmental variables (∼22% explained variance) than phytoplankton, which exhibited weak spatial and environmental structuring, However, large unexplained fraction in both groups precludes assigning this differential pattern to deterministic versus stochastic assembly without formal null-model frameworks. Along the longitudinal gradient, we observed a descriptive trend of increasing network modularity and internal connectivity in the downstream reach, where organic pollution indicators (COD and BOD 5 ) were relatively elevated. We tentatively term this pattern of network densification as a hypothesis consistent with observed topology, but its functional implications remain to be empirically tested. Our findings provide a descriptive and hypothesis generating basis for understanding multi-trophic community structuring in Karst free - flowing rivers, and offer empirical reference points for bio-assessment and adaptive management of riverine ecosystems facing combined anthropogenic stressors in comparable systems.

title: Research on landscape pattern zoning management based on the matching of ecosystem cultural service supply and demand
abstract: Spatial mapping of cultural ecosystem services in each rural tourist destination not only provides tourists with more personalized rural tourist routes, but also facilitates better promotion of rural tourist destinations. However, ecosystem cultural services are difficult to be defined and quantified due to their subjectivity and intangibility. In view of this, this study selected the rural tourism area in Datong City, Shanxi Province as the research object, and determined the value of cultural services in Datong City with the help of SolVES model to determine the characteristics of the spatial distribution of the supply capacity of cultural services in Datong City, through the construction of the demand indicators of ecosystem cultural services, spatial mapping of the level of demand for cultural services, combined with the supply and demand of ecosystem services and the clustering effect of the division of the four cultural function zones, to lay a theoretical foundation for the regional rural tourism. The results show that (1) the value of cultural services shows obvious spatial differentiation, and the more clustered the rural tourism sites are and the closer they are to the periphery of the urban area, the higher the value of cultural services, and the further they are from the road and the water body, the lower the value of cultural services. (2) The total demand for rural cultural services in Datong City has gradually shifted to the central area of the city and is almost densely distributed in Pingcheng District, showing its spatial heterogeneity. (3) The ratio of supply and demand for cultural services is 0.287, which shows that cultural services are in a surplus situation, and there is no risk of an imbalance of supply and demand for the time being. (4) According to the match between supply and demand of cultural services and the agglomeration relationship, the rural areas of Datong can be divided into four categories of developed areas, demand areas, potential areas and less-development areas. This study provides a basis for the subsequent comprehensive development planning of cultural services in rural areas.

title: Spatial patterns of carbon storage and carbon sequestration potential in multi-component carbon pools of forest ecosystems in southeastern Xizang
abstract: Forest ecosystem carbon storage and sequestration potential are key components of terrestrial carbon cycle research and are essential for assessing regional carbon sink functions and supporting ecological security. The Qinghai–Xizang Plateau is one of the regions most sensitive to global climate change. Southeastern Xizang, characterized by abundant forest resources and prominent ecological functions, provides an ideal region for investigating carbon storage and sequestration potential in regional forest ecosystems. This study focused on forest ecosystems in southeastern Xizang and, based on field investigation data, systematically estimated the carbon density and carbon storage of multiple ecosystem components, including tree, shrub, herb, litter, and soil layers. Furthermore, under similar ecological environmental conditions, the carbon sequestration potential of forest ecosystems and its spatial distribution patterns were evaluated. The results showed that the carbon density of forest ecosystems in southeastern Xizang was 211.62 Mg C·hm −2 , with a total carbon storage of 1018.55 Tg C. Carbon density and carbon storage varied significantly among regions, with an overall spatial pattern characterized by higher values in the southeast and lower values in the northwest. The distribution patterns of carbon density and carbon storage among ecosystem components were generally consistent, with the highest values observed in the soil layer, followed by the tree layer. Among different forest types in southeastern Xizang, carbon density was highest in evergreen broad-leaved forests and lowest in deciduous broad-leaved forests. The carbon sequestration potential of forest ecosystems in southeastern Xizang exhibited pronounced regional differentiation, showing a spatial pattern characterized by decreasing values from the central–western regions to the northeastern regions. These findings reveal the spatial distribution characteristics and forest-type differences in carbon storage and carbon sequestration potential in forest ecosystems of southeastern Xizang, providing a scientific basis for regional forest carbon sink assessment and the conservation and restoration of forest ecosystems.

title: Corrigendum to “Nonlinear thresholds in agricultural landscape fragmentation: A GWRF-SHAP diagnostic framework for differentiated rural land management” [Ecol. Indic. 191 (2026) 115483]

Corrigendum to “Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and multi-scenario simulation of vegetation carbon sinks under the influence of ecological engineering: a case study in the Three-River Headwaters Region, China” [Ecol. Indic. 191 (2026) 115459]
Predicting cultivation probability to target monitoring in smallholder landscapes: Proof of concept from dispersed medicinal plant cultivation in Taihe County, China
abstract: Dispersed medicinal plant cultivation by smallholder farmers presents a monitoring challenge that differs fundamentally from conventional agricultural monitoring: fragmented fields, mixed spectra, and canopy occlusion make direct detection difficult, while exhaustive field surveys are prohibitively costly. Rather than detecting every plot, we combined Random Forest modeling with geographical detector analysis to predict cultivation probability from environmental covariates, transforming monitoring from an open-ended search into targeted, spatially guided effort. Using Plantago asiatica L. in Taihe County, China, a 300 years of cultivatd species as a model system. Random Forest achieved stable predictive performance under 5-fold cross-validation (AUC = 0.977 ± 0.022; coefficient of variation = 2.3%). Geographical detector analysis revealed a clear interaction hierarchy. Elevation (q = 0.620) and land use (q = 0.464) as the dominant drivers, and elevation functioned as a universal amplifier, producing consistently strong synergistic effects with any co-occurring factor, in contrast to the highly variable interactions among soil physical properties (CV = 2.8% versus 21.3%). Risk detection further delineated optimal environmental ranges for each factor. Cross-validation between geographical detector and Random Forest importance rankings (Spearman's ρ = 0.664) confirmed the robustness of these mechanistic insights. To inform management, we derived a three tier monitoring priority zoning from the probability surface, in which the high-priority zone, occupying only 9.67% of the county yet comprising over 91% cropland and artificial surfaces, serves as the primary monitoring stratum. This design theoretically reduces annual monitoring workload by 80–90% compared to exhaustive surveys. The approach relies on open-access data and open-source software, providing a template potentially adaptable to other crops and regions with long term cultivation histories, though operational validation remains necessary. By resolving the factor interaction hierarchy, this study advances both mechanistic understanding of cultivation patterns and the design of targeted monitoring strategies in smallholder-dominated landscapes.

title: The Genuine Progress Indicator for the transition economies of the Baltic States: reflections on economic welfare and methodological choices
abstract: The Baltic States of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania have experienced rapid Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth since the collapse of the Soviet Union and subsequent transition from planned to market economy, reporting increasing levels of consumption and subjective wellbeing but persistent income inequality, which raises the question of whether economic expansion has translated into genuine welfare improvements. The study provides the first application of an updated Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI) framework to the Baltic States for the period 1995-2023. To assess the robustness of the results, a sensitivity analysis of the components with the greatest influence on GPI values was conducted: valuation of leisure time, the cost of carbon, and the income inequality adjustment. The analysis reveals that economic welfare measured by the GPI has generally exceeded GDP across all three countries in the study period, apart from 2023 in Estonia and Lithuania, offering indications that the welfare returns of additional economic growth might be diminishing. However, the extent to which the GPI exceeds or falls below GDP varies considerably depending on parameter choices. The sensitivity of the GPI to assumptions regarding hourly wages, carbon cost, and inequality baselines highlights methodological challenges that makes cross-country comparisons difficult. These findings caution against uncritical use of the GPI in policy settings and highlight the need for methodological standardisation and clearer valuation guidelines if the metric is to serve as a credible tool for assessing progress beyond GDP.

title: Title or substance? A policy impact evaluation of nature reserves upgrade in China's borderlands
abstract: Nature reserves (NRs) serve as a critical instrument for curbing biodiversity loss, facilitating ecosystem restoration, and safeguarding ecological security in border regions. However, does the “upgrading” of reserve status lead to “substantive” ecological improvements, or is it merely a nominal designation? To address this question, this study treats China's phased reserve upgrades since 2007 as a quasi-natural experiment. Drawing on balanced panel data from 89 NRs across nine border provinces over the period 2000–2022, we employ a Propensity Score Matching combined with Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DID) approach to provide the first empirical evaluation of the policy effects of NR upgrading in China's border regions. Our findings reveal that: (1) The upgrading policy significantly enhances habitat quality in China's border regions, confirming its de facto ecological benefits. (2) However, the policy effects are not homogeneous but exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity—the effects are more pronounced in southern regions than in northern ones, in biodiversity conservation priority areas than in non-priority areas, in ecosystem-type NRs than in species/heritage-type NRs, and in NRs administered by the forestry and grassland authorities, reflecting a path-dependent pattern of “focused reinforcement” under sectoral dominance. (3) These findings call for future policies to move beyond the nominal goal of “upgrading for upgrading's sake” and instead optimize the strategic layout of upgrading, incorporate protection-object and administrative-competence criteria into the approval process, and translate upgrading into tangible effectiveness through differentiated management and institutional refinement. By constructing a quasi-experimental evaluation framework with panel data, this study provides rigorous empirical evidence for disentangling the de jure versus de facto effects of NR policies, and offers China-based evidence for the global conservation debate between “expansion” and “upgrading.”

title: A spatially explicit UAV-based decision support tool to assess the protective effect of lying deadwood on snow avalanche release
abstract: Mountain forests provide essential ecosystem services, including protection against snow avalanches. Severe disturbances such as windthrow and bark beetle outbreaks generate large amounts of lying deadwood, altering forest structure and affecting avalanche protection. Climate change and legacy effects of past land use are increasing the frequency and severity of such disturbances, while management resources remain limited, highlighting the need for objective decision support tools (DSTs) for evidence-based post-disturbance forest management. We present a spatially explicit DST for deriving spatial indicators related to the protective effect of lying deadwood against avalanche release by integrating terrain, forest structure, and deadwood characteristics. Using high-resolution UAV-derived data, the DSTderivesdeadwoodstructure,models winter terrain under increasing snow depths, and identifies critical snow depths at which surface roughness is reduced. Comparisons with snow-on orthophotos confirm the robustness of the modeled winter terrain. Application across different UAV sensor systems, from low-cost photogrammetry to LiDAR, demonstrates the framework’s broad applicability, showing that even low-cost systems provide suffi ciently accurate results. Analyses across multiple Alpine study sites and post-disturbance management strategies reveal that both the amount and spatial configuration of deadwood control the protective effect. Unmanaged areas maintain the highest protection, requiring snow depths exceeding ∼1.6 m for potential avalanche release, with only minor reductions over a six-year period (∼15% in total). Complete deadwood removal considerably reduces protection, whereas partial removal still provides substantial protection under low-snow conditions. Our open-source DST provides a transparent and practitioner-oriented indicator framework for assessing the protective effects of lying deadwood against snow avalanches under changing disturbance regimes.

title: Climate variability, land-use change, and the development of dominant ecosystem services across China
abstract: Accelerating climate change and land use/land cover change (LUCC) heavily alter ecosystem service (ES) dynamics. This study proposes an integrated framework to identify Dominant Ecosystem Services (DES) based on the Comprehensive Ecosystem Service Value (CESV) method, addressing service overlap and management homogenization. Six representative services carbon storage (CS), water yield (WY), sediment delivery ratio (SDR), net primary productivity (NPP), nitrogen retention (NDR N), and phosphorus retention (NDR P) were quantitatively evaluated across China at a 1 km resolution during 1995–2025 using Z -score standardization and the Maximum Value Criterion (MVC). Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) decoupled the direct and indirect drivers of DES evolution. Results reveal a “southern-high and northern-low” spatial pattern with high regional heterogeneity. CS (36.12%) and SDR (22.08%) exhibit the highest ecological dominance. One-Way ANOVA validates a post-2015 structural shift to SDR dominance in Northwest China, driven by severe precipitation surges (234.8 mm; F = 42.15, p < 0.001) that overrode vegetation stabilization thresholds. PLS-SEM path coefficients show that direct climate impacts declined over time, whereas LUCC impacts rose progressively from 0.189 (1995) to 0.666 (2025). Concurrently, Two-Way ANOVA confirms that unified nationwide Z -scores introduce significant systemic bias across specific ecological zones ( F = 34.21, p < 0.001). WY, NDR N, and NDR-P exert the strongest indirect effects on DES formation. This diagnostic DES-CESV framework establishes a rigorous foundation for spatial zoning and environmental governance under future eco-climatic scenarios.

title: A multi-method validation framework for seasonal environmental-indicator forecasting: Demonstrated with the Keetch–Byram Drought Index
abstract: Environmental indicators that capture seasonal dynamics are widely used in wildfire management, vector control, and natural resource monitoring, but operational forecasting requires more than a fitted seasonal model: the candidate structure must be estimable, its seasonal period sufficiently resolved, and its forecasts demonstrably useful out of sample. We develop a forecast-readiness framework for seasonal environmental indicators and demonstrate it with the Keetch–Byram Drought Index (KBDI), a meteorologically derived hazard indicator. Harmonic regression models, with and without preliminary linear detrending, were evaluated using complementary Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO), Rolling Origin (RO), and Rolling Window (RW) validation. RO and RW forecasts used only observations available before each held-out calendar year and covered the entire following year without updating. Seasonal climatology, lagged persistence, and exponential smoothing provided operational benchmarks. Recurring seasonal structure carried most predictive signal, whereas preliminary detrending did not consistently improve forecasts. The harmonics-only formulation was generally more robust under deployment-oriented validation, and exponential smoothing independently favored a no-trend seasonal structure. For the Lee County record, two-year training windows were consistently inadequate; three years was the shortest history showing partial recovery, but longer records did not guarantee positive skill relative to climatology. A seven-county exploratory holdout under the same two-year constraint likewise showed predominantly negative skill. Seasonal climatology remained a strong benchmark, while peak underprediction and phase errors of weeks constrained point-forecast reliability. These results motivate a six-step forecast-readiness protocol that separates algebraic identifiability, period resolution, and demonstrated out-of-sample value before deployment.

title: Industrialization-driven restructuring of ecological networks: A resilience and topology-based assessment framework
abstract: Industrialization reshapes urban landscapes not only through land conversion but also by altering ecological connectivity, network organization, and systemic resilience. However, existing ecological network (EN) planning frameworks rarely integrate industrial spatial dynamics with topology- and resilience-based assessment, limiting their ability to diagnose systemic ecological vulnerability in industrial cities. This study develops a resilience-informed EN framework to examine how sustained industrial pressure restructures ENs and to identify opportunities for structural reinforcement under alternative development pathways. Using Zhuzhou, China, as a representative industrial city, industrial pollution intensity and proximity to production facilities were incorporated into ecological resistance modeling to reconstruct ENs from 2000 to 2020 and simulate their development to 2030 under natural development (ND), urban expansion (UE), and ecological priority (EP) scenarios. Graph theory and weighted complex-network analysis were used to evaluate topological restructuring and multidimensional resilience under random and targeted node removal. From 2000 to 2020, ecological source area declined and connectivity cost increased by 61%, accompanied by reduced diffusion capacity and increasing concentration of structural importance in a limited number of critical nodes and corridors. These changes indicate that industrialization not only intensified habitat fragmentation but also increased network dependence on key ecological components. The 2030 scenarios exhibited distinct trajectories, with UE tending to reinforce structural concentration and vulnerability, whereas EP promoted lower resistance and a more balanced network configuration. Resilience-informed optimization further improved network structure, increasing the α, β, and γ indices by approximately 67, 35, and 34%, respectively. The overall resilience curve under random disturbance increased by approximately 2.4%, with larger improvements under high-intensity node removal. These findings show that ecological-network degradation involves source-area contraction, fragmentation, altered potential connectivity, and increased structural dependence. Integrating network topology and resilience into industrial spatial planning can therefore provide a stronger basis for identifying structural vulnerabilities and supporting sustainable urban transition.

title: Nonlinear responses of ecosystem services to meteorological drought and driving factors analysis
abstract: Quantifying ecosystem service responses to meteorological drought is crucial for enhancing resilience in arid and semi-arid regions. Existing studies have largely focused on linear or static relationships with climatic factors, while lag effects, thresholds, and spatial heterogeneity remain underexplored. This study assessed four ecosystem services-water yield, carbon storage, soil conservation, and sand retention-in Inner Mongolia from 2000 to 2020. Multiple timescales of the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) were employed to determine response times. Response thresholds were identified using constraint line analysis combined with generalized additive models, and driving mechanisms were examined with the XGBoost-SHAP model. The results showed that: (1) From 2000 to 2020, all four services improved overall, with the mean grid-cell values of water yield, sand retention, carbon storage, and soil conservation increasing by 1.29-, 7.86-, 0.15-, and 0.02-fold, respectively. (2) Drought-response timescales varied across services and aridity zones. Regionally, water yield, carbon storage, and soil conservation were most sensitive to 6-month SPEI, whereas sand retention responded to 24-month SPEI. Responses were uniformly rapid in semi-arid regions but diverged in arid regions, where sand retention responded rapidly while the other services showed longer lags. (3) The response threshold was defined as the dimensionless SPEI value at which an ecosystem service achieved its maximum potential supply; negative and positive values indicate drier and wetter conditions than the long-term average, respectively. Carbon storage, soil conservation, and water yield followed convex unimodal constraint patterns, while sand retention exhibited a hump-shaped response, with threshold values of −0.42, −0.13, 0.62, and 0.76, respectively. The threshold for sand retention decreased from 0.69 in semi-humid regions to 0.19 in semi-arid regions and − 0.02 in arid regions, suggesting a reduced moisture requirement for achieving maximum sand retention under increasingly arid conditions. (4) Precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and wind speed were the dominant natural drivers of ecosystem service variation, while historical drought frequency and human activities, including ecological projects, grazing, and road disturbance, further modulated service supply. These results support zonal management tailored to individual ecosystem services by matching drought monitoring windows to response timescales, promoting vegetation restoration with low water demand and strong drought tolerance according to local moisture thresholds, and prioritizing the control of grazing and road disturbance in vulnerable transition zones.

title: The middle route of the south-to-north water diversion project and urban ecological welfare performance: Evidence from water-receiving cities
abstract: The implementation of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project (MRP) has effectively alleviated the severe water shortage in northern China; however, whether and how it produces synergistic effects on the ecological, economic, and social systems of the water-receiving areas remains a key issue requiring in-depth assessment. Using panel data from prefecture-level cities for the period 2006–2023, this study estimates urban ecological welfare performance (EWP) via a global super-efficiency SBM model (GS-SBM). On this basis, the difference-in-differences method is adopted to examine the implementation effects and mechanisms of the Middle Route Project. The results indicate that: (1) The project is significantly correlated with improvements in urban ecological welfare performance in the water-receiving areas; this conclusion remains valid after robustness tests, including the parallel trends test. (2) The results of the mechanism analysis suggest that industrial structure upgrading, technological progress, and human capital accumulation may be potential channels through which the project influences the ecological welfare performance of water-receiving cities. (3) The policy effects are more pronounced in cities with higher administrative levels and higher levels of economic development, whilst they are not yet significant in areas where groundwater over-abstraction is particularly severe. These findings provide empirical evidence at the city level on the relationship between the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project and the ecological welfare performance of water-receiving cities, and offer a theoretical basis for China's ecological civilisation construction and decision-making on cross-regional resource allocation.

title: Nonlinear responses and spatial heterogeneity of water eco-environmental health in the Lixiahe plain: insights from a spatiotemporal XAI framework
abstract: Water exchange in plain river network regions is shaped by topography and managed water operations. Environmental pressures from agricultural and urban activities interact with ecological regulation, complicating the assessment of water eco-environmental health. Composite indices or factor importance rankings alone cannot adequately characterize year-specific and overall contributions, nonlinear responses, and local spatial associations, limiting their application to spatially differentiated management. Using the Lixiahe Plain as a case study, we constructed a Water Eco-environmental Health Index (WEHI) based on the DPSIRM framework and applied an integrated spatiotemporal explainable analysis workflow (ST-XAI) combining XGBoost, SHAP, GAM, and GWR, with independently fitted annual models and a unified model fitted to pooled data across the study period. From 2000 to 2020, regional mean WEHI increased from 0.518 to 0.567 despite fluctuations. Areas with higher health levels expanded into the north-central region, while spatial clustering weakened after 2005. Year-specific models consistently identified the importance of the remote sensing ecological index, soil moisture, and vegetation coverage; the pooled model additionally highlighted the explanatory contributions of wastewater treatment rate, cropland area, and gross domestic product (GDP). As indicator values increased, the model contributions of the remote sensing ecological index and wastewater treatment rate shifted from negative to positive, with slower increases at high values. Cropland area contributions generally declined, whereas GDP contributions followed a negative–positive–negative pattern. The remote sensing ecological index and wastewater treatment rate showed the strongest interaction contribution in the pooled model. Local associations of wastewater treatment rate and GDP with WEHI varied in direction across space. These findings can inform spatially differentiated management and ecological restoration in the Lixiahe Plain and comparable plain river network regions.

title: Climate change and human activities reshape the water-food-ecology nexus and water-economy decoupling in oasis cities of the Hexi corridor, China
abstract: In arid oasis systems, water allocation links agricultural production, ecological stability, and regional economic development, making the water-food-ecology (WFE) nexus highly sensitive to hydroclimatic stress and human activities. Yet county-scale evidence remains limited on how hydroclimatic and socioeconomic changes are associated with WFE interactions and water-economy decoupling in inland oasis cities. Focusing on the Hexi Corridor, we integrate multi-decadal hydroclimatic records, remote sensing ecological indicators, and county-level socioeconomic, water use, and crop data. Tapio decoupling, temporally purged and spatially blocked random-forest validation, Grey relational analysis (GRA), exploratory two-way fixed-effects piecewise path analysis, and scenario-based reliability-resilience-vulnerability assessment were combined to characterize water-economy relationships, crop–water associations, WFE interactions, and management outcomes. During 1981–2024, annual mean 2-m air temperature increased significantly by 0.038 °C/year, annual precipitation showed a weak increase of 0.349 mm/year, and December SPEI-12 decreased significantly by 0.0476/year, indicating a deteriorating climatic water balance under pronounced warming. Strong water-economy decoupling emerged before 2020 and was associated with declining water use intensity, while industrial decoupling showed greater interannual variability during 2020–2022. Random-forest performance was moderate under temporal validation (R 2 = 0.673) and weaker under spatial validation (R 2 = 0.441), indicating stronger temporal generalization than spatial transferability. Crop composition showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity and county-specific similarity with agricultural water use. Piecewise path analysis revealed scale-dependent associations among socioeconomic activity, water use, hydroclimatic conditions, and vegetation. Within counties, land surface temperature (LST) was negatively associated with normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), while surface water use was positively associated with vegetation condition and SPEI-12 was negatively associated with agricultural water use in the primary specification. Scenario results showed that agricultural-demand reduction and coordinated measures improved water-system reliability and resilience, whereas groundwater constraints applied alone increased unmet demand. These findings support differentiated local implementation within basin-scale governance and provide a transferable diagnostic workflow for comparable arid inland basins, although local parameters and management outcomes require region-specific recalibration.

title: Differential responses of algal ecosystems in freshwater and Saline Lakes on the northeastern Tibetan plateau to climate and anthropogenic disturbances
abstract: The responses of lake ecosystems to climate change and anthropogenic disturbances in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau (NETP) have not yet been fully understood. In this study, we investigated differential responses of algal ecosystems to climate and human activities in NETP during the past millennium, based on sedimentary ancient DNA and multiple paleolimnological proxies extracted from freshwater Lake Hurleg and saline Lake Toson located adjacently in NETP. The results show that the temporal patterns of algal communities and variations are different between freshwater and saline lakes in NETP, with higher productivity and algal diversity during the Little Ice Age (LIA: a cold interval) than the Medieval Warm Period (MWP: a warm interval) in saline lakes, but higher productivity during the MWP and lower productivity and biodiversity during the LIA in freshwater lakes. The diverse ecological features further suggest that the freshwater lake ecosystem in NETP is dominated by temperature variations, while that of the saline lake is controlled by changes in precipitation. Both lakes exhibit marked increases in algal diversity and productivity in the Current Warm Period, likely linked to the increased nutrient supply due to enhanced human activities of the recent epoch. Compared to the saline Lake Toson, the freshwater Lake Hurleg was more sensitive to human disturbances. The results of this study suggest that the intensifying human activities in the NETP over recent decades have altered the natural evolution of lake ecosystems, thus highlighting the urgent need to strengthen the management of human-environment interactions to maintain the sustainability of lake ecosystems.

title: Developing a water–soil carbon–nitrogen–productivity synergy index for diagnosing ecological effects in semi-arid dryland agroecosystems
abstract: Semi-arid dryland agroecosystems are jointly constrained by water conditions, soil carbon–nitrogen status, and crop productivity, yet their multidimensional coordination remains poorly understood. Using ERA5-Land, MODIS, SoilGrids, and other datasets, we developed a water–soil carbon–nitrogen–productivity synergy index (WSCP-SI) for the agricultural region along the Great Wall and evaluated its spatial patterns, temporal dynamics, ecological-effect pathways, robustness, and management implications. Across stable-cropland pixels, the mean values of WCI, SCNI, CPI, EEI, and spatial WSCP-SI were 0.4223, 0.4163, 0.4224, 0.5542, and 0.4056, respectively. WSCP-SI rankings remained highly stable under alternative weighting, aggregation, indicator, parameter, and seasonal settings. During 2001–2023, WCI generally declined, although no significant decreasing area remained after false-discovery-rate correction. In contrast, CPI increased across 99.67% of its valid area, including 89.58% with significant increases. Dynamic water–productivity synergy and EEI also increased, but less extensively, indicating that productivity gains outpaced improvements in system coordination. WSCP-SI and EEI were matched across 62.72% of the valid area, while 37.28% remained mismatched. Latent-variable modelling revealed counterbalancing pathways: Water and SoilCN supported Productivity, whereas their conditional direct associations with EEI were negative and partly offset by positive productivity-mediated pathways. These relationships were interpreted as exploratory because of limited model fit and uncertainty in Water-related paths. Water showed opposite directional associations with efficiency and stability, but neither linear nor quadratic effects were statistically robust, and no supported Water threshold was identified. Two-layer zoning classified 20.12% of the area as vulnerable, 52.79% as improvement potential, and 27.09% as high-synergy stable. Overall, WSCP-SI provides a robust framework for distinguishing productivity growth from genuine multidimensional coordination and supporting spatially differentiated management.

title: Threshold delineation of in-situ and ex-situ carbon ecological compensation in mountain-water-forest-farmland-lake-grassland composite ecosystems
abstract: Precisely characterizing the spatial transfer processes of carbon sink services (CSSs) and defining compensation thresholds are essential for improving ecological compensation (EC) mechanisms. Addressing the deficiencies of existing studies that overemphasize static supply and demand while neglecting spatial radiation processes and cross-scale transmission mechanisms, this study constructs an analytical framework of “CSS flow – multi-scale radiation – multi-scale compensation threshold”. Based on the breaking point, HYSPLIT model and other quantitative methods, this study thoroughly reveals the evolutionary characteristics, spatial radiation effects and compensation threshold characteristics of CSSs within the mountain-water-forest-farmland-lake-grassland composite ecosystems. The results reveal that: (1) During 2000–2020, the total flux of CSS flow decreased by 36.79%, and the supply–demand mismatch continued to intensify. (2) In-situ radiation was primarily dominated by the forest subsystem with a contribution of 61.75%, and the grassland subsystem presented a diffusion characteristic of high frequency but low intensity. In terms of ex-situ radiation, the forest subsystem of Chongqing formed obvious radiation corridors along the middle and upper reaches of the Yangtze River. (3) In-situ carbon EC exhibited a spatial pattern of centralized payment in metropolitan areas and dominant compensation reception in ecological functional zones. The forest subsystem occupied the largest proportion of EC (62.98%–74.29%). Under the ex-situ carbon EC, the number of compensation subjects at the municipal scale was 5.5 times that at the provincial scale. The research findings of this study can offer a theoretical basis for establishing a trans-regional horizontal carbon EC mechanism and optimizing regional coordinated development in Chongqing.

title: Integrating alpha, beta and zeta diversity to explore phytoplankton community stability in Mediterranean lakes
abstract: Biodiversity is often associated with ecological stability, yet how biodiversity relates to changes in community dynamics and long-term stability remains unclear, especially for microbial communities. Understanding community dynamics requires metrics that capture both compositional change and long-term persistence. Here, we analysed phytoplankton dynamics in 14 Greek lakes over an eight-year period (2016–2023) using an integrated framework combining alpha, beta, and zeta diversity metrics. Taxonomic richness varied widely among lakes, with shallow polymictic systems supporting significantly higher taxa richness and variability than deep monomictic lakes. Temporal beta diversity revealed moderate to high community dissimilarity across all lakes, driven primarily by species turnover rather than nestedness, indicating that compositional shifts were dominated by species replacement. Lakes with low taxa richness exhibited lower temporal community stability, suggesting reduced buffering capacity against environmental variability. Zeta diversity analysis provided novel insights into long-term persistence, showing a consistent decline in shared taxa with increasing temporal order across all systems. Despite differences in morphology, the rate of zeta decline did not differ significantly between lake types, indicating similar underlying dynamics. However, shallow lakes maintained proportionately larger core communities, reflecting higher annual richness and greater ecological redundancy. Among phytoplankton groups, Chlorophyta and Cyanobacteria were the main components of community structure, turnover, and persistence, whereas Dinophyta exhibited low persistence and high variability, indicating greater sensitivity to environmental fluctuations. These findings demonstrate that integrating alpha, beta, and zeta diversity provides a robust framework for assessing phytoplankton community stability and identifies biodiversity as a sensitive indicator of temporal persistence.

title: Beyond mapped area: Uncertainty-aware DEM screening of vertical deficits in Lithuanian cut-over peatlands
abstract: Cut-over peatlands are typically screened for restoration using mapped area alone, a metric that cannot distinguish a shallow disturbance from a deep vertical loss. We tested whether adding a digital elevation model (DEM) layer changes that screening order, for a national inventory of 162 Lithuanian cut-over peatland polygons (28,981.5 ha). Because no independent, field-surveyed reference elevations were available to validate any single DEM boundary surface, the analysis compares eight plausible reference-surface scenarios directly and reports where they agree or diverge, rather than selecting one as correct. The aim is to establish whether, and for which polygons, a vertical layer changes the priorities an area-only screen would set, not to produce a validated national peat-loss estimate. For each DEM-matched polygon, geometric deficit was calculated as the non-negative difference between mean interior elevation and eight local boundary-reference alternatives: 0.5 m and 2 m rings summarized by the mean, 90th, 95th and 99th percentiles. Computational coverage and a data-derived upper-outlier screen retained 122 polygons (16,911.5 ha); 40 polygons (12,070.0 ha) remained unresolved. Across the direct subset, the eight reference-surface alternatives produced volume-deficit totals of 26.0–444.7 million m 3 . Area and descriptive median-volume ranks were correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.877), but only five polygons overlapped in the two top-ten lists; the median absolute rank change was nine places and the maximum was 89. Thus, vertical information changed the screening order for some polygons, while the strong overall association confirmed continuing area dominance. For unresolved polygons, four area-only scenario models were compared by leave-one-out prediction of the DEM-derived scenario midpoint. The best internal model had a mean absolute error of 0.684 m; this is an internal prediction result, not a test of field accuracy. Combining eight direct-polygon alternatives with three unresolved-polygon alternatives yielded a deterministic national envelope of 193.2–741.8 million m 3 . An algebraic carbon conversion gave 35.4–136.0 Mt. CO₂ stock equivalent, not measured historical emissions or recoverable mitigation. The analysis shows how strongly the result depends on reference-surface choice and when a vertical DEM layer changes an area-based screen. Field-surveyed reference elevations and data on hydrology, biodiversity, feasibility and cost would be needed to move from screening to restoration priorities or a national peat-loss estimate.

title: SWAT-based assessment of spatiotemporal ecological flow deficit in the Yiluo River Basin
abstract: To address the ecological flow deficit caused by intensive human activities in the Yiluo River Basin, this study integrates the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) with a locally modified Tennant method to systematically evaluate the spatiotemporal characteristics of ecological flow requirements and deficit patterns at the sub-basin scale. Two hydrological scenarios were constructed—a natural scenario representing undisturbed runoff processes and a baseline scenario incorporating actual anthropogenic disturbances such as reservoir operations, agricultural irrigation, and inter-basin water transfers—to quantify runoff dynamics and ecological flow thresholds under different ecological standards. The SWAT model produced reliable simulations: for the natural scenario, R 2 was 0.84 and 0.93 during the calibration and validation periods, with NSE of 0.76 and 0.90, respectively; for the baseline scenario, R 2 was 0.94 for both periods, with NSE of 0.92 and 0.94, respectively. The results indicate that: (1) baseline annual runoff decreased by approximately 40% compared with the natural state, with a reduction of up to 80% during the dry season (February–March); even in wet years (e.g., 2018 and 2021), observed runoff remained 35%–42% lower than natural runoff. (2) Ecological flow requirements exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, ranging from a maximum of 30.2 m 3 /s in the wet season and 15.1 m 3 /s in the dry season at the mainstream outlet (Sub-basin 3) to a minimum of only 5.21 m 3 /s in an upstream tributary (Sub-basin 8); wet-season (June–October) demand was approximately 3–5 times that of the dry season (November–May). (3) Under the moderate Tennant standard, about 84% of the basin area met the basic ecological flow requirements; however, Sub-basins 4 and 6 had the highest deficit frequencies (approximately 63%), followed by Sub-basins 8 and 19 (approximately 50%), with deficits mainly concentrated in the wet season. (4) A priority-based ecological water replenishment framework was proposed, recommending targeted replenishment during the wet season (June–October) for high-frequency deficit areas. The target monthly replenishment volumes were: 1555.2 × 10 4 m 3 for the upper Luo River (Sub-basins 8, 10, and 11), 1166.4 × 10 4 m 3 for the upper Yi River (Sub-basins 15 and 19), 777.6 × 10 4 m 3 for the Lan River (Sub-basin 1), 648.0 × 10 4 m 3 for the Yongchang River (Sub-basin 5), and 1036.8 × 10 4 m 3 each for Sub-basins 4 and 6 (all values are theoretical estimates excluding conveyance losses). By coupling hydrological modeling with sub-basin-scale deficit diagnosis, this study provides an operational hydrological pre-screening basis for ecological water replenishment in the basin. However, it should be noted that the ecological flow defined in this study is a hydrological surrogate indicator and awaits biological validation .

title: Coordinated development of urbanization and ecosystem services: A functional positioning and sufficiency-necessity matrix-driven framework
abstract: Coordinating urbanization and ecosystem services is a central issue for achieving sustainable development. However, existing studies have largely overlooked the functional orientation of regional development and have predominantly focused on the sufficiency dimension of influencing factors, while neglecting the necessity perspective. To address this gap, we integrate the Geodetector and necessary condition analysis (NCA) to construct a sufficiency–necessity framework. This framework explores the influencing factors of the coordinated coupling between urbanization and ecosystem services from two logical perspectives, adopting the major function-oriented zoning of Jiangxi Province, China as the study context. The results show that: (1) From 2000 to 2020, the comprehensive urbanization level (CUL) in Jiangxi Province was predominantly low, with high-intensity areas consistently concentrated in urbanized zones (46.15%); meanwhile, the comprehensive ecosystem service (CES) showed an overall declining trend, with the most pronounced decreases observed in ecological functional zones. (2) The dominant coupling coordination types between CUL and CES were marginal and primary coordination, with dysfunctional counties most prevalent in ecological functional zones and least in major agricultural production zones. (3) The spatial differentiation of the coupling coordination degree between CUL and CES was mainly driven by land-use structure, while climatic factors acted as stable necessary conditions in most regions. Factor classification further revealed that precipitation consistently served as sufficient and necessary category in both urbanized and agricultural production zones. In ecological functional zones, cropland (d > 0.19), built-up area (d > 0.18), and population density (d > 0.16) jointly formed sufficient and necessary category. Accordingly, this study contends that policy-making should be guided by the dual principles of zone-specific governance and factor-based management to provide a basis for formulating targeted government policies.

title: Quantifying trade-offs between sampling effort and biodiversity detection to optimize cave monitoring design
abstract: Reliable biodiversity indicators require sampling designs that balance detection performance and feasibility. Subterranean ecosystems are particularly challenging due to inaccessibility and spatial complexity, and quantitative guidance on sampling strategy is limited. We quantified trade-offs between sampling effort and biodiversity detection to optimize cave monitoring design. Using three caves that provide access to the same geologically connected subterranean system in central Slovenia, we established a reference inventory of obligate subterranean species (troglobionts) through year-round spatially and temporally replicated sampling. We then evaluated 2511 alternative sub-sampling schemes derived from the full design to assess how reduced effort affects detection performance. A total of 118 taxa were recorded, including 21 troglobionts. Rarefaction analyses indicate that the regional troglobiont pool was fully captured by the complete sampling design. Sub-sampling analyses show that only a limited number of scheme combinations reliably detected ≥90% of reference troglobiont species. However, high detection performance can be maintained with substantially reduced effort when spatial replication, seasonal coverage, and complementary sampling methods are retained. By explicitly linking sampling effort to detection proportion relative to a reference baseline, this study provides a quantitative framework for evaluating and optimizing biodiversity monitoring designs. The approach is applicable to other spatially fragmented or difficult-to-survey ecosystems where efficient indicator performance is required under logistical constraints.

title: Identifying bark beetle damage predictors in Austria using interpretable machine learning: Thresholds and management implications
abstract: The increasingly severe and frequent forest damage caused by the European spruce bark beetle ( Ips typographus ) has been systematically surveyed across Europe since the early 2000s, yet underlying drivers remain not fully understood. This study aims to identify key predictors and capture spatiotemporal dynamics of bark beetle damage by analysing annual damage time series from 70 Austrian forest districts (2005–2025) using extreme gradient boosting. We quantified the importance of 18 predictors reflecting preceding forest damage, climate, forest composition and topography. The model was evaluated at the national level and for eight regional clusters. Across Austria, it explained 62% of the variance (R 2 ) in cross-validation and identified 64% of true bark beetle outbreaks. Performance was highest in damage hotspots and lower in less affected regions. Preceding bark beetle damage, outbreaks in neighbouring districts and summer climatic water balance were among the strongest predictors. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values revealed clear thresholds at which damage increased: negative summer climatic water balance (< 0 mm), warm spring temperatures (≥ 14.5 °C), and elevated preceding damage by abiotic events (≥ 2 m 3 ha −1 ) and I. typographus (≥ 1 m 3 ha −1 ). Exceeding these thresholds likely amplifies bark beetle damage in previously less affected regions. We conclude that machine learning-based modelling effectively captures the spatiotemporal dynamics and underlying drivers of bark beetle damage at forest district level. Our findings can advance threshold-based risk assessment systems from national to European levels, supporting bark beetle management and the preservation of ecosystem services under a changing climate.

title: Nonlinear amplification of vegetation drought under compound dry–hot extremes across India
abstract: Understanding how vegetation responds to concurrent drought and heat is critical under a warming climate, yet vegetation drought studies in India have largely emphasized individual climatic drivers, correlation-based relationships, or regional analyses. A national-scale assessment that quantifies how rainfall deficits and temperature extremes jointly amplify vegetation drought, and separates the relative contributions of dryness and heat, remains lacking. To address this gap, we applied a meta-Gaussian probabilistic framework across India for 2001–2024 using IMD gridded rainfall and temperature and MODIS NDVI. Conditional probabilities of vegetation drought were estimated under progressively severe rainfall (P30–P10) and temperature (T70–T90) thresholds, together with compound dry–hot conditions and dedicated amplification metrics. Results show that both rainfall deficits and temperature extremes are critical drivers, with rainfall-related vegetation drought probabilities increasing from ∼0.40–0.60 under moderate deficits to ∼0.50–0.70 under extreme deficits, while temperature-related probabilities remain around ∼0.40–0.55. Under compound dry–hot extremes, vegetation drought probability rises sharply to >0.80, demonstrating strong nonlinear amplification. Dryness-driven amplification (CD ≈ 0.6–0.8) exceeds heat-driven amplification (CH ≈ 0.3–0.6), revealing a clear asymmetry in compound effects. Central, northern, western, and peninsular India emerge as high-sensitivity regions, whereas northeastern India and the Western Ghats show relatively lower sensitivity, and the Himalaya exhibits a contrasting temperature-limited response. These findings provide a national-scale basis for incorporating compound hydroclimatic extremes into vegetation drought assessment and climate adaptation planning.

title: Spatial responses of ecosystem services to future climate change across China in the mid-21st century
abstract: Accurately identifying ecosystem-service (ES) responses to future climate change is essential for improving ecological conservation and restoration and for developing targeted adaptation strategies. However, coherent future response zones across multiple regulating services and their associated predictor patterns remain insufficiently understood. In the current study, we established a comprehensive framework based on Shared Socioeconomic Pathway-Representative Concentration Pathway (SSP-RCP) climate scenarios, by using the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model assessments, hotspot analyses, as well as random forest-Shapley additive explanations (RF-SHAP) interpretable machine learning. We assessed water yield, soil conservation, nitrogen retention, and phosphorus retention responses under future SSP-RCP scenarios across China during 2050–2060 relative to a 2000–2020 baseline. Our results revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in China's future ESs. At the provincial scale, the unweighted mean values of water yield and soil conservation increased by 18.1–19.5% and 22.0–25.9%, whereas nitrogen and phosphorus retention decreased by 14.9–18.3% and 11.0–15.7%. Northwestern China formed a consistent positive-response zone for water yield and soil conservation. Conversely, central-eastern China formed a contiguous zone of declining phosphorus retention, while Southern China exhibited minimal response. Strong synergistic coupling was observed among the four ESs, with water-related services displaying highly consistent spatial correlations. RF-SHAP analysis indicated relatively large contributions of climate-change and hydroclimatic predictors within the selected predictor framework for most ES responses. In contrast, nitrogen retention showed broader associations with climatic, topographic, and human-activity conditions. These findings provide a scientific basis for spatially differentiated ecological conservation and climate-resilient governance.

title: The ecosystem health of Tarim river basin: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving forces
abstract: The ecosystem health of inland river basins in arid regions is crucial for maintaining water resource security and oasis stability. To reveal the spatiotemporal evolution patterns and driving mechanisms, this study assessed the ecosystem health of the Tarim River Basin—a typical arid inland river basin in China—from 2000 to 2023 using the Vigor–Organization–Resilience ( VOR ) model within a runoff–generation–runoff–consumption–desert zoning framework, integrating coefficient–of–variation, Hurst–exponent, and GeoDetector analyses. The results showed that: (1) Ecosystem health exhibited a pronounced west–east gradient: high values were concentrated in the runoff generation zone and oasis patches, whereas low values prevailed in the desert hinterland; the basin–wide mean EHI remained low with mild interannual fluctuations and no clear increasing trend. (2) The grade structure was dominated by “Poor” and “Relatively poor” levels, with localized upgrades mainly in the runoff generation zone and parts of the runoff consumption zone, indicating limited ecological recovery against a background of persistent desert degradation. (3) Annual evaporation, annual precipitation, annual mean temperature, altitude, and population density were the factors most strongly associated with the spatial pattern of the EHI , their explanatory power varied markedly over time and among zones, and interaction effects were generally stronger than individual effects. Natural factors exhibited the highest single–factor explanatory power for the macro–scale pattern, whereas human–activity factors contributed mainly through interaction effects in the runoff consumption zone. This study provides a typical case for ecosystem health assessment in arid inland river basins, and the revealed zonal driving mechanisms offer a scientific basis for differentiated ecological protection and adaptive governance.

title: Parcel-level remote sensing evaluation framework for cropland ecological quality in arid oasis regions: A case study of Luopu County, Xinjiang
abstract: Cropland ecological quality evaluation in arid oasis regions faces three challenges: the disconnect between evaluation units and parcel management, the neglect of core-edge ecological gradients by homogeneous methods, and the difficulty in quantifying human management responses. This study constructs a new evaluation framework integrating functional zoning and spatial variable weighting based on remote sensing. Using cropland parcels as the basic evaluation unit, the study divides the area into core irrigation zones, ecological transition zones, and desert edge zones based on geospatial features. Subsequently, a Pressure-State-Response (PSR) evaluation system is built, strengthening indicators related to human management dimensions. Finally, a spatial variable weight model is used to assign differentiated criterion-layer weights to the three functional zones, enabling dynamic evaluation weights adjustment with spatial function. The case in Luopu County, Xinjiang, shows that the Pearson correlation coefficient between the results of this framework and the remote sensing ecological index (RSEI) is 0.867, higher than the 0.858 of the uniform weight model and significantly higher than the 0.814 of the pixel-level method. These results indicate that parcel-level valuation suppresses noise and aligns better with management boundaries than pixel-level valuation, while the spatially variable weighting model responds more sensitively to the dominant driving mechanisms of different functional zones. This study shifts the evaluation unit from pixels to parcels, realizes the differentiated diagnosis of ecological gradients within oases, and provides an operable methodological framework for the refined monitoring and targeted management of cropland ecological quality in arid regions.

title: Multi-scenario simulation of the co-evolution between production-living-ecological space conflict mitigation and carbon balance in Jiangsu province
abstract: Rapid urbanization and industrialization have intensified competition among production, living, and ecological spaces (PLES), leading to escalating land use conflicts and carbon imbalances. However, critical knowledge gaps remain. Existing studies have largely examined spatial conflict and carbon balance in isolation, and multi-scenario simulations have predominantly prioritized single objectives — economic growth or ecological protection — over synergistic pathways that jointly address conflict mitigation and carbon reduction. To address this gap, we developed an integrated analytical framework coupling spatial conflict index (SCI) measurement, carbon balance accounting, and the intPLUS model to analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of PLES conflict and carbon balance in Jiangsu Province, China, from 2000 to 2020, and to simulate four 2030 scenarios: natural development (ND), economic development (ED), ecological protection (EP), and a novel conflict-balanced low-carbon synergy (CBLSC) scenario. A four-quadrant conflict-carbon analysis and Geodetector were used to identify synergies, trade-offs, and driving mechanisms. Results show that from 2000–2020, spatial conflict intensified significantly, with high-conflict areas concentrated in southern Jiangsu and the Yangtze River belt, closely linked to construction land expansion and rising carbon emissions. By 2030, the ED scenario yields the highest spatial conflict (mean SCI = 0.43) and net carbon emissions (117.70 Mt), while the EP scenario minimizes net emissions (81.14 Mt) but limits development flexibility. Notably, the CBLSC scenario achieves the lowest mean conflict value (0.35) and moderate net emissions (87.14 Mt), effectively mitigating high-conflict-high-carbon clusters and demonstrating superior balance between conflict alleviation and low-carbon transition. Geodetector results reveal that socioeconomic factors, particularly nighttime light intensity, GDP, and population, dominate the spatial differentiation of conflict-carbon coupling, with transportation accessibility playing a supporting role. We conclude that embedding conflict mitigation and carbon balance objectives into land use simulation provides a more effective pathway for territorial spatial optimization in developed regions. The CBLSC scenario offers a practical governance strategy for Jiangsu and similar high-density areas to achieve low-conflict, low-carbon, and spatially coordinated development.

title: Key factors and pathways through which photovoltaic arrays mediate changes in microclimate, vegetation, and soil in a rocky desertification ecosystem
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) arrays substantially alter above- and belowground environmental factors as well as ecosystem functionality. However, the intrinsic mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood, particularly in fragile karst ecosystems. The present study examined the impacts of installing photovoltaic arrays on microclimate, vegetation, and soil properties in a rocky desertification ecosystem in southwestern China. Compared with adjacent reference areas, the photovoltaic arrays significantly modified the local microclimate, reducing light intensity by 49.39%–68.03% and wind speed by 76.53%–97.96% across seasons (measured at 60-min intervals with sensors at 1.5–2 m height). A seasonal alternation between “heat island” and “cold island” effects was observed: under the arrays, air temperature increased by 0.54 °C in summer but decreased by 0.23–0.42 °C in spring and winter, while relative humidity consistently increased (0.38%–10.82%) throughout the year. Regarding soil properties, the PV arrays caused a 22.8% to 28.1% increase in soil temperature and moisture during the rainy season but led to significant declines in bulk density, organic carbon, and hydrolyzed nitrogen during the dry season, with reductions ranging from 10% to 55% ( p < 0.05). The observed 15.3%–27.8% declines in carbon and nitrogen represent substantial nutrient losses; bulk density showed seasonal reversals (decreasing in the dry season due to soil shrinkage but increasing in the rainy season due to particle migration) based on repeated sampling at fixed plots. Conversely, available potassium increased by 32% in the dry season ( p < 0.05), attributed to reduced plant uptake and leaching losses under shading. Plant community diversity (Shannon index, Pielou evenness, and richness) significantly increased, while the dominance index decreased ( p < 0.05). This diversity change may be driven by PV shading, which suppresses dominant heliophilous species and promotes shade-tolerant species, thereby redistributing species dominance and creating more equitable resource competition. However, plant root systems became simplified, with a 6.73%–80.40% reduction in root tip number. This simplified root architecture may reduce resource acquisition efficiency from deeper soil layers, yet it does not significantly alter total above- or belowground biomass. This trade-off between aboveground gains (higher diversity) and belowground costs (simpler root structures) may have implications for long-term ecosystem stability and recovery, especially in shallow karst soils. Partial least squares path modeling (GOF = 0.67) revealed direct benefits to microclimate (path coefficient = 0.76) and diversity (0.89) but direct costs to roots (−1.22) and soil (−0.97), representing statistical associations rather than causation. The model accounted for 68%, 86%, 45%, and 82% of the variance in microclimate, plant diversity, root morphology, and soil properties, respectively. Indirectly, microclimate improved soil via plant diversity (∼0.26 path coefficient) and directly via microclimate (∼0.52), totaling approximately 80% of the direct negative effect, partially offsetting direct negative impacts. Mechanistically, PV shading initiates a cascade: altered microclimate reshapes plant communities by reducing heliophilous species and promoting shade-tolerant species, while plants simplify root architecture under low light and soil nutrients decline; these direct costs are partially offset by diversity-mediated feedback to soil properties. This trade-off is particularly acute in shallow karst soils with limited nutrient buffering, cautioning against extrapolation from other ecosystems and highlighting the need for site-specific assessment and long-term monitoring.

title: How many indicators make a good assessment?
abstract: Marine ecosystem assessments use indicators and various integration methods to conclude on ecosystem state. The integration methods vary in their structures, which will influence the number of indicators required. Thus, the choice of an assessment method will have cost consequences, but if the indicator pool is fixed, it is important to select a suitable method to ensure scientific robustness of the results. While science has been hesitant to provide methods for simplifying inherently dynamic ecosystems, the integration of ecosystem indicators is a necessity for answering the demands from policy, societies and wider audience. Some integration methods emphasize the precautionary approach or finding average conditions, some want to include detailed indicator data and some paint with broader brush of ecosystem conditions. In this study, we tested how data-hungry three common integration methods are and how indicator availability impact the robustness of the integrated result. We used real indicators from three European sea regions in five test sites. The results showed that uncertainty in an assessment result increases in more structured integration methods if indicator availability is limited. This should raise warning flags for managers with limited monitoring resources to prioritize indicators or change the integration method.

title: Climate-driven habitat loss of Chinese sturgeon in the Northwestern Pacific and implications for marine protected area design
abstract: The conservation of endangered anadromous fishes depends on understanding their full-lifecycle habitat requirements, yet the marine phase of Chinese sturgeon ( Acipenser sinensis ) remains a critical knowledge gap despite over 90% of its lifespan occurring at sea. We integrated multi-source occurrence data (satellite tagging, bycatch records, environmental DNA, and online databases) and applied an ensemble modeling framework (Biomod2 with eleven algorithms) to predict habitat suitability across the Northwestern Pacific Ocean (100°E–150°E, 10°N–55°N). After collinearity filtering, seven key environmental drivers were retained, among which mean temperature contributed most, followed by maximum pH, total suspended matter and mean silicate. The ensemble model achieved high predictive performance (median TSS = 0.944) and identified the Changjiang Estuary and coastal waters of Zhejiang and Jiangsu provinces as current distribution hotspots. Under the high-emission scenario (SSP5–8.5), suitable habitats are projected to disappear completely by 2100, accompanied by a significant northward contraction. These projections should be regarded as a potential worst-case scenario under high-emission conditions rather than a deterministic forecast. These findings demonstrate that business-as-usual emissions would eliminate viable marine habitat for this critically endangered species. Conservation priorities should therefore focus on (1) protecting benthic prey resources in the Changjiang Estuary and Zhoushan Archipelago as core refugia, and (2) transitioning from static marine protected areas to dynamic, climate-adaptive zoning informed by real-time habitat predictions. The ensemble modeling approach developed here is transferable to other data-limited, endangered marine species facing similar climate threats.

title: Changes in natural forest fragmentation and their driving factors across Japan from 1985 to 2022
abstract: Forest fragmentation reduces biodiversity and ecological function. However, some regions now show signs of defragmentation, a recovery process in which forest cover becomes more continuous. Defragmentation owing to the recovery of natural forests is especially important because natural forests generally support higher biodiversity than planted forests. Despite this, most previous studies into forest defragmentation have not distinguished natural forests from planted forests, leaving natural forest defragmentation insufficiently understood. This study provides the first nationwide assessment of changes in natural forest fragmentation in Japan from 1985 to 2022 and identified the factors promoting fragmentation dynamics. Using annual land cover maps, we quantified long-term changes in landscape metrics and evaluated the effect of site factors and land use factors using Bayesian spatial regression models implemented through INLA-SPDE framework. Across Japan, natural forests became less fragmented, while the proportion of natural forests showed a slight increase. Although the number of small, isolated patches increased after 2000, simultaneous increases in area and spatial aggregation metrics suggest that this trend was consistent with ongoing defragmentation. Bayesian spatial regression analysis showed that defragmentation was promoted by clear-cutting and occurred most readily in remote areas with high elevation, steep slopes, and low population density. In these areas, conversion from planted forests to natural forests following clear-cutting was strongly associated with natural forest defragmentation.
