Within the human activity contribution, 39.00% of the area (with consideration of the lag) exhibited negative effects during 1989–1999; notably, in extremely dry years, the positive regulatory capacity of human activities significantly weakened. The benefits of large-scale ecological projects, represented by the Grain for Green program, entered a period of significant release after 2010, reached a peak of accelerated NDVI increase during 2012–2017, and subsequently decelerated. After the regional average NDVI exceeded approximately 0.40, the combined benefits of climate and human activities on vegetation restoration became increasingly difficult to enhance, indicating the existence of an indicative threshold. These findings provide a direct scientific basis for understanding climate–human interaction mechanisms in the vegetation restoration of the Mu Us Sandy Land, for objectively evaluating the long-term effectiveness of ecological projects, and for optimizing adaptive management strategies.

title: From binary occurrence to continuous space use: A framework for species distribution modelling using high-frequency GPS tracking data
abstract: High-frequency GPS tracking provides fine-scale insight into animal space use, but spatial thinning—routinely used to meet independence assumptions—discards substantial information and can underestimate core habitat quality. Using 65,548 high-frequency GPS fixes from 42 wintering black-necked cranes ( Grus nigricollis ), we developed a framework that converts these fixes into continuous kernel density estimation (KDE) surfaces of space-use intensity and then models these surfaces using random forest (RF) regression. We compared this KDE + RF approach with two thinning-based alternatives: conventional thinning + Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and thinning + RF, across nine environmental variable combinations. The 100 m KDE bandwidth, corresponding to the median step length of the GPS-tracked black-necked cranes, generally outperformed the 500 m bandwidth, particularly for models incorporating remote-sensing variables, and was therefore used in subsequent analyses. For the same predictor combinations, KDE + RF models consistently achieved higher predictive performance than their thinning + RF, with higher area under the curve (AUC) and continuous Boyce index (CBI) across all nine combinations; the CBI gain is particularly relevant because it concerns the ranking of habitat quality rather than the discrimination of presence from absence. For example, under the Clim + LC combination, KDE + RF achieved a higher CBI than thinning + RF (0.989 ± 0.007 vs. 0.947 ± 0.042), and their AUC values were comparable (0.989 ± 0.006 vs. 0.984 ± 0.007). KDE + RF also generally outperformed the conventional thinning + MaxEnt framework across environmental predictor combinations. Independent field validation supported closer correspondence between KDE + RF predictions and observed flock distributions at both wintering sites, with stronger enrichment in the High-quality habitat and a more consistent increase in flock occurrence ratios along predicted habitat-suitability gradients. By preserving space-use intensity information and improving the representation of habitat-suitability gradients, the framework may support more effective conservation prioritisation for black-necked cranes. More broadly, it offers a transferable methodological concept for other species monitored with high-frequency GPS tracking.

title: Effects of snow drought on spring green-up on the Mongolian Plateau
abstract: Snow drought has become a research hotspot due to its widespread impacts on ecosystems and water resources, yet its effects on vegetation phenology remain relatively understudied. Focusing on the Mongolian Plateau, this study used the Snow Water Equivalent Index and the start of growing season (SOS) to assess the associations between snow drought and vegetation green-up and their differences among vegetation types by integrating trend analysis, partial correlation analysis, lagged effect analysis, linear mixed-effects models, and structural equation modelling. Results show that snow drought significantly intensified during 1982–2022 (slope = −0.13, p < 0.05), with this trend predominantly occurring in the central and western Mongolian Plateau and exhibiting greater intensification in typical steppe and desert steppe. SOS advanced overall but exhibited strong spatial differentiation. Positive associations between snow drought and SOS were dominant in the northern and western regions, whereas negative associations were more concentrated in the eastern and southern margins. Relative to non-snow-drought conditions, SOS generally occurred later under snow drought conditions, with the largest difference of 9.49 days observed in desert steppe. Lagged effects were mainly identified for early spring of the current year, with April accounting for the largest proportion, while the sensitive months differed among vegetation types. Snow drought was independently associated with SOS and was also indirectly associated with SOS through soil-mediated hydrothermal pathways. These findings provide scientific support for regional snow drought monitoring and early warning, ecological risk assessment, and adaptive management.

title: Multiscale Hydromorphological impacts of Run-Of-River hydropower cascades: A comparative multi-index assessment framework
abstract: Hydropower plants (HPs) disrupt longitudinal river continuity, impacting sediment transport and, consequently, driving complex hydromorphological adjustments that are rarely addressed in small hydropower cascades. This study assesses the hydromorphological impacts of six small, run-of-river HPs on the Bóbr River in southwestern Poland. The primary objective is to assess potential hydromorphological alterations in upstream and downstream river segments fragmented by HPs, and to analyze the feasibility of different assessment methods. The research evaluated 15 study sections using four distinct European assessment methods: the Hydromorphological Index for Rivers (HIR, Poland), the Riparian Quality Index (QBR, Spain), the Hydroecological Monitoring Method (HEM, Czechia), and the Morphological Quality Index (MQI, Italy). Averaging 67 structural components across the applied methodologies revealed a mean multimetric hydromorphological deterioration of 7.21% in downstream tailwaters relative to upstream impoundments ( n = 6 paired hydropower plants). This value represents a descriptive mean and should be not interpreted as a statistically causal effect. MQI and QBR recording average downstream deteriorations of 11.97% and 13.40%, respectively. In contrast, localized habitat indices such as the HIR and HEM showed only marginal changes—a 2.42% deterioration and a 1.02% improvement in downstream/upstream HPs, respectively—and the four assessment methods produced markedly different responses. Process- and connectivity-oriented methods, specifically MQI and QBR, recorded mean downstream deteriorations of 11.97% and 13.40%, respectively, whereas HIR showed a smaller deterioration of 2.42% and HEM indicated a slight average improvement of 1.02%. These divergent responses suggest that the methods capture different dimensions of hydromorphological condition and that their conceptual and spatial frameworks influence their responsiveness to hydropower-associated alterations. In this case study, physical and structural alterations were more readily detected than changes in conventional physicochemical parameters reported for the same river. However, this observation does not determine the relative ecological importance of hydromorphological and physicochemical impact pathways. Method selection should therefore be aligned with the specific monitoring or management objective, and broader validation across additional rivers and hydropower cascades remains necessary.

title: Multidimensional biodiversity mediates environmental - food web relationships in river - reservoir ecosystems: Evidence from the world's largest hydropower project
abstract: While hydropower development provides clean energy, it also disrupts river continuity, leading to an unprecedented decline in biodiversity. However, most studies have focused on the impact of hydropower development on taxonomic diversity (TD), and there remains a relative lack of research on multidimensional biodiversity, specifically TD, phylogenetic, and functional diversity (PD and FD), and its effects on the stability of aquatic food webs. This study employs eDNA and traditional sampling methods to assess the spatiotemporal variations in biodiversity and food web structure within the Three Gorges Reservoir area (TGR), and examines the evolution of river-reservoir ecosystems from the perspective of “environmental factors—multidimensional biodiversity—food web”. The results indicate that phytoplankton (PP), zooplankton (ZP), and fish (Fish) were identified across 5 kingdoms, 12 phyla, 17 classes, 42 orders, 80 families, and 144 genera; The spatiotemporal patterns of multidimensional biodiversity and food web structure in the TGR show a slight (not significant) increase from the reservoir head to the reservoir tail during the impoundment period, while they decrease significantly during the flood period; Partial least squares structural equation modeling results indicate that changes in food web structural robustness in the TGR primarily mediated by diversity rather than direct environmental factors. Furthermore, the food web in the TGR is dominated by bottom-up effects, with the magnitude of influence ranked as follows: PP_PD > PP_TD > ZP_TD > Fish_TD, among which PD exerts the strongest influence. In summary, these findings emphasize that, in river-reservoir ecosystems such as the TGR, integrating multi-taxa, multidimensional biodiversity and its regulatory mechanisms on food web structural robustness is key to elucidating ecosystem evolution.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and SHAP-derived characteristic points of vegetation resilience across China
abstract: Vegetation resilience reflects the capacity to resist and recover from disturbance, yet its variation across China’s aridity gradient remains poorly understood. Using monthly normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) data for 2000–2024, we constructed a Composite Vegetation Resilience Index (CVRI) integrating resistance, recovery, and stability. We assessed spatial patterns, estimated trends over 2002–2022, and examined environmental associations using XGBoost and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Mean CVRI was 0.486 ± 0.156 (mean ± SD), with higher values in humid and arid zones than in semi-arid and sub-humid zones. Significant increases and decreases occurred over 14.38% and 7.00% of the assessed vegetated area, respectively, and the area-weighted mean Sen slope was ＋0.002108 CVRI units per year. Mean annual precipitation (MAP) and mean annual temperature (MAT) were the leading predictors, while their relative importance varied among climate zones. SHAP-derived characteristic points occurred at approximately 560 mm for MAP, 2 ° C for MAT, 0.65 for the aridity index, and 740 m for elevation. These values summarize features of the fitted dependence curves. Predictor-removal and land-cover sensitivity analyses consistently ranked MAP and MAT first and second. The results identify spatial contrasts in vegetation resilience and highlight the semi-arid–sub-humid transition belt as a priority for drought monitoring and restoration assessment.

title: Spatial lock-in, blue carbon stock contributions, and source-sink mismatches: assessing low-carbon target feasibility on Hainan Island, China
abstract: Tropical islands are often regarded as promising regions for low-carbon transitions because of their coupled terrestrial and coastal ecosystems. However, high ecological endowment does not automatically ensure the feasibility of low-carbon targets, especially where coastal urbanization, land scarcity, and ecological-protection constraints coexist. Taking Hainan Island, China's largest tropical island, as a case study, this study develops a spatial carbon-indicator framework based on land-coastal carbon stock-flow accounting to evaluate the feasibility of low-carbon targets under existing spatial-development trajectories. The framework integrates multi-source carbon-emission inventories, land-use simulation, InVEST-based terrestrial carbon storage assessment, Google Earth Engine (GEE)-based mangrove mapping, seagrass carbon estimation, and trend-regression-based stress testing. Results show that the current-policy spatial-inertia scenario maintains substantial carbon pressure associated with coastal construction-land expansion, whereas the historical-trend Poly2 stress test places the central turning point around 2032 at approximately 11.08 Mt. C. Bootstrap diagnostics indicate substantial uncertainty around the 2030 policy threshold, suggesting a limited safety margin rather than a deterministic delay. Terrestrial carbon storage declined by about 3.32 Mt. C, while coastal blue-carbon storage increased by about 2.355 Mt. C, making a substantial but non-substitutable contribution to the regional carbon-stock balance. County-level carbon stock-flow coupling reveals a spatial mismatch between coastal emission-pressure zones and central ecological carbon-storage zones. These results indicate that assessing the feasibility of low-carbon targets requires moving beyond aggregate emission trajectories to incorporate land-use-driven spatial lock-in, carbon-storage limits, and differentiated territorial responses. The framework provides a spatial carbon-indicator approach for stress-testing low-carbon targets in ecologically constrained island and coastal regions.

title: Spatial supply–demand matching of urban green space cooling services
abstract: The cooling effects of Urban Green Spaces (UGS) have been widely studied, but existing assessments of cooling-service supply–demand matching still insufficiently consider differences among functional UGS types and social demand. This study applies an ecosystem service supply–demand framework to quantify the matching relationship of UGS cooling services. Two key indicators are proposed: the Cooling Supply Index (CSI), which evaluates the cooling contribution and spatial spillover effects of different UGS types, and the Cooling Demand Index (CDI), which integrates both physical and social dimensions. Based on these indices, four-quadrant analysis and bivariate local spatial autocorrelation (BiLISA) are applied to characterize the supply–demand matching of UGS cooling services. The results indicate that: (1) the cooling service capacity of different UGS types varies significantly, following the descending order: regional green space > park green space > affiliated green space > protected green space; (2) both CSI and CDI demonstrate strong discriminative ability and interpretability in characterizing cooling supply and demand; (3) the four-quadrant analysis emphasizes within-unit supply–demand relationships, while BiLISA effectively reveals spatial clustering patterns, making the two approaches complementary; and (4) typical Low-supply–high-demand mismatches are concentrated in core urban districts and should receive priority intervention. This study distinguishes the roles of different UGS types in cooling-service supply and incorporates social factors into cooling-demand assessment, thereby further advancing the analytical framework of ecosystem service supply–demand matching and providing scientific support for refined green space planning and climate-resilient urban governance.

title: From upstream to downstream: Ensemble machine learning uncovers for River Water Quality Prediction
abstract: Water quality in the Khorramabad River has declined over recent decades with population growth, industrialisation, and agricultural activity. This study examined water quality using six months of monthly data (July to December) from six monitoring stations. To address the sample size limitation and produce a daily time series, we used two time-based interpolation methods: linear interpolation and Gaussian Process Regression. These methods generated 1104 daily samples. Three machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost—were used to predict dissolved oxygen (DO), phosphate, and nitrate concentrations, and to analyse their temporal and spatial patterns. Over the study period, DO showed a slight upward trend, which corresponded with decreasing water temperature during the coldest months. Nitrate levels increased steeply from October onward. Phosphate levels decreased over the same period. A clear spatial gradient was present from upstream to downstream. Cross-validation identified the Ensemble model as the most stable for predicting DO (CV R 2 = 0.9957 ± 0.0004). For nitrate, XGBoost performed best (CV R 2 = 0.9831 ± 0.0038). For phosphate, XGBoost also performed best (CV R 2 = 0.9793 ± 0.0058). Feature importance analysis showed parameter-specific patterns. For DO, BOD₅ and calcium were the most influential predictors. For phosphate, calcium and Station_encoded dominated. For nitrate, Station_encoded, turbidity, and EC were the most influential. Station_encoded, as a spatial feature, was highly important for phosphate and nitrate, confirming a distinct spatial gradient along the river. Station F was the most critical point requiring immediate attention.

title: Are greener forests stronger carbon sinks? Rising vapour pressure deficit instigates greening-productivity decoupling in a tropical biodiversity hotspot in India
abstract: Forests across the humid tropics are widely reported to be “greening”, leading to the assumption that they will remain reliable carbon sinks under changing climate. We explored this critically in the forests of North Eastern Region of India (NER), a climatically sensitive biodiversity hotspot containing ∼1/3rd of India's forest carbon. Using 24 years (2001–2024) of satellite-derived canopy structure (LAI), photosynthesis (GPP) and productivity (NPP) data, we designed a divergence framework to evaluate whether increases in vegetation activity translate into sustained carbon gains. Results revealed that despite stable canopy structure and modest increases in GPP (+1.76 g C m -2 yr -1 ), NPP declined across much of the region (-0.83 g C m -2 yr -1 ), suggesting that photosynthetic gains are increasingly decoupled from net carbon gain. Structural-functional divergence (LAI-NPP decoupling) affected ∼40% of forested areas, while photosynthetic-productive divergence (GPP-NPP decoupling) occurred across ∼30% of the area, revealing a progressive weakening of carbon-use efficiency. Breakpoint analysis identified a reorganization of forest carbon functioning beginning in the early 2010s. Coupling between canopy structure and photosynthesis weakened, while the conversion of photosynthetic gains into net carbon accumulation became increasingly constrained. Pixel-wise climatic causal analysis further identified vapour pressure deficit (VPD) as a primary driver of the productivity declines. Our results demonstrate that NER forests are not collapsing structurally but are undergoing a concealed weakening of carbon sink strength. Greenness-based assessments can substantially overestimate sink strength, underscoring the need to incorporate atmospheric stress, carbon-use efficiency, and functional vulnerability into carbon accounting and forest management under a warming climate. Our findings further highlight how biological responses to atmospheric dryness may decouple structural and functional forest carbon dynamics at landscape scale.

title: Beyond the SLOSS dichotomy: Mixed conservation strategies for species diversity in fragmented Karst Mountain landscapes
abstract: The independent effects of habitat fragmentation on biodiversity remain debated, a controversy central to the single large or several small (SLOSS) debate in reserve design. Karst plateaus contain heterogeneous and isolated habitat patches that may favor several small reserves through habitat complementarity and species turnover, whereas area effects and local carrying-capacity constraints may favor a single large reserve. We used 41 nature reserves on the Guizhou Plateau, Southwest China, as study units and combined distribution data for birds, mammals, amphibians and reptiles with the Quinn-Harrison saturation index (SI), a species-area relationship (SAR)-based SLOSS index and generalized additive models. We assessed reserve-network configuration efficiency and its drivers. Most taxa had SI values greater than 1, indicating higher species accumulation rates in several small reserves. In contrast, SLOSS indices were negative for all taxa, suggesting greater theoretical species-holding capacity in a single large reserve. This mismatch indicates that SLOSS patterns are strongly dimension-dependent. Further analyses showed that SAR slope (z value) was the main driver of the SLOSS index, largest patch area had taxon-dependent nonlinear effects on SI, and community nestedness affected the relative benefit of several small reserves by modulating species complementarity. Widespread anti-nestedness in the study region further supported the species-accumulation advantage of several small reserves. Therefore, reserve design in fragmented karst plateau landscapes should combine large reserves that maintain long-term species-holding capacity with well-distributed small reserves that capture habitat heterogeneity and species turnover, thereby balancing species-accumulation efficiency with long-term persistence.

title: A dynamic pricing mechanism for cross-regional water rights trading based on water supply-demand in the Yellow River Basin, China
abstract: A reasonable pricing mechanism is the core of successful water rights trading. Most existing studies adopt static pricing methods, which fail to incorporate the dynamic fluctuations of water supply and demand. Moreover, current methods for inter-region water rights neglect regional heterogeneity and marginal benefits of water use among different sectors. To address these challenges, a dynamic water rights trading mechanism encompassing supply-demand accounting, price formulation, fund collection and allocation was established. Taking the Yellow River Basin (YRB) as study area, the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model was used to quantify water supply. Supply-demand curve theory and sectoral water use data were then employed to establish dynamic water rights trading prices, and both top-down and bottom-up approaches were proposed for the collection and allocation of trading funds. The results show that: (1) the water supply in the YRB fluctuated significantly, ranging from −2.2 to 2.8 times that in 2010 at the provincial level, whereas the water demand exhibited relatively small fluctuations, ranging from −0.4 to 0.4 times. (2) Water rights trading prices change dynamically, reaching a peak in 2015 and a trough in 2021, the average prices is 1.53CNY/m 3 . (3) Qinghai, Sichuan, and Gansu provinces in the upper YRB have consistently been net water rights sellers. These findings can provide systematic guidance for improving water rights pricing in the YRB, as well as methodological references for other river basins.

title: Optimizing urban green space allocation by integrating development propensity as an endogenous objective
abstract: Urban greening is critical for climate change mitigation, sustainable urban development, and urban ecological health. However, the effectiveness of urban greening depends not only on the ecological objectives pursued but also on whether the spatial allocation of green spaces is compatible with the development conditions of candidate areas. Existing urban green space optimization studies typically treat development propensity as a spatial filter that excludes undevelopable areas, assuming homogeneous propensity across the remaining candidate set, overlooking its continuous spatial heterogeneity in highly urbanized environments. Consequently, the trade-offs between development propensity and ecological objectives remain largely uncharacterized. To address this gap, this study proposes modeling development propensity as a continuous spatial indicator derived from land-use transition probabilities and incorporates it alongside carbon-uptake potential and landscape connectivity within an NSGA-II framework. Applied to Suwon City, South Korea, the results reveal trade-offs: the MAX-NPP solution achieved the highest carbon-uptake potential (666.19 tCO₂ yr −1 ) but with comparatively low development propensity (133.63) and low connectivity (68.37 × 10 −9 ), whereas development propensity and connectivity showed only a weak, configuration-dependent compatibility rather than systematic synergy. These trade-off structures, together with the continuous gradient of development propensity across the Pareto front (approximately 117–186), highlight the importance of incorporating development propensity as an endogenous objective into green space planning. This framework provides planners and policymakers with the capacity to explore and evaluate alternative greening scenarios, reconcile competing objectives through quantitative trade-off analysis, and derive evidence-based spatial strategies for advancing sustainable urban development.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity analysis of parameters' sensitivity: A new perspective for evaluating ecological process models
abstract: Ecological process models have become essential tools for studying terrestrial ecosystems. In practical applications, the model selection and evaluation are critical. In this study the concept of spatiotemporal heterogeneity in model parameters' sensitivity was introduced and corresponding quantitative metrics were defined; based on these, a methodology was established to evaluate model applicability through assessment of the Spatiotemporal heterogeneity of overall (or average) parameter sensitivity. Using the Biome-BGC model as a representative ecological process model, the temporal, spatial, and spatiotemporal heterogeneity of model parameters' sensitivity from different observation sites and time periods across three vegetation types were analyzed. The results revealed that model parameters' sensitivity exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity; within the same vegetation type, temporal heterogeneity was lower than spatial heterogeneity; across vegetation types, average spatiotemporal heterogeneity followed: evergreen broad-leaved forest < deciduous broad-leaved forest < C3 grassland. Stronger model simulation capability correlated with lower (average) spatiotemporal heterogeneity of parameter sensitivity. This study provides a novel perspective and methodology for evaluating ecological process models. This methodology can still provide a preliminary assessment for model's simulation capability even when ground-based validation data is limited.

title: From MODIS active-fire detections to dynamic fire regimes: an indicator-based spatiotemporal framework for fire-regime monitoring and modeling
abstract: Understanding how Fire Regimes evolve through time is critical for assessing ecosystem change. However, temporal and spatial fire analyses are typically conducted separately, limiting the ability to link temporal changes in fire activity with their spatial Fire-Regime patterns. This study addresses this gap by developing an indicator-based framework that integrates Fire Frequency and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) as complementary indicators of fire activity, linking their temporal trajectories to spatial Fire-Regime patterns, and evaluating the sensitivity of Fire-Regime delineation and environmental associations to detection-type composition. MODIS Active-Fire detections were analyzed for both Temporal Fire Evidence and spatial–temporal Fire-Regime patterns. Temporal Fire Evidence was evaluated for both 2000–2024 and 2003–2024 using seasonal Fire Frequency, relative seasonal Fire Frequency, and the mean FRP of detections exceeding the 95th percentile. Temporal trends in these indicators were evaluated using the modified Mann–Kendall (MK) test and Sen's slope. For spatial–temporal Fire-Regime analysis, annual Fire Density and FRP for 2003–2024 were independently evaluated using the MK test, and the resulting MK Z values were classified using ±1.96 as the thresholds for significant increasing and decreasing trends, respectively, before cross-classification to derive nine Fire Regimes. The resulting Fire Regimes were modeled using machine-learning classifiers. Two modeling strategies were considered, namely Regime 1, contrasting declining versus increasing Fire Regimes, and Regime 2, contrasting Increasing Fire Frequency versus Intensifying Fire Regimes. Both strategies were modeled independently for the complete retained MODIS detections (All-Type) and for Type 0 detections representing presumed vegetation fires. Spatial Block Cross-Validation was applied to the All-Type models to assess geographic transferability, while the Type 0-only analysis provided a sensitivity assessment of the influence of detection-type composition on Fire-Regime delineation and environmental associations. Temporal Fire Evidence revealed heterogeneous temporal robustness, with the most persistent increase in Fire Frequency occurring in spring and an increase in absolute Fire Frequency also retained in winter. Spatial analysis identified nine Fire Regimes and revealed contrasting trajectories of fire occurrence and energetic intensity, with the Increasing Fire Frequency Regime occupying 17.32% of the mapped All-Type area compared with 0.03% for the Intensifying Fire Regime. Across the All-Type and Type 0-only models, the four principal predictors of Regime 1, namely elevation, Wind speed, population proximity, and rural accessibility, were common to both configurations, although their relative importance was reordered. For Regime 2, topographic position and Wind speed remained prominent in both configurations, while the relative importance of secondary predictors varied. Overall, the results demonstrate that integrating temporal indicators with spatial Fire-Regime trajectories can reveal distinct and spatially structured pathways of changing fire activity, while sensitivity to detection-type composition provides an important basis for interpreting the environmental context of these Fire Regimes. The framework therefore offers a reproducible indicator-based approach for monitoring heterogeneous Fire-Regime dynamics and identifying areas requiring further ecological and environmental assessment.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of ungulate habitats on the Mongolian Plateau: A climate change driven perspective
abstract: Climate change poses a severe threat to biodiversity in ecologically sensitive regions like the Mongolian Plateau. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of habitat suitability for four representative ungulates, Asiatic wild ass ( Equus hemionus ), Mongolian gazelle ( Procapra gutturosa ), wapiti ( Cervus canadensis ), and Siberian roe deer ( Capreolus pygargus ), to provide a scientific basis for conservation planning. Using the MaxEnt model, we projected habitat suitability under historical (1970–2000) and future (2021–2100, SSP1–2.6 and SSP5–8.5) climate scenarios, identified potential climate refugia, and assessed their spatial overlap with existing protected areas (PAs). Results indicate that annual mean temperature (Bio1) and precipitation of the wettest quarter (Bio16) are the dominant environmental drivers of habitat suitability for three of the species, except for the wapiti, which is highly sensitive to topographic factors. Under future climate scenarios, the habitats of the Asiatic wild ass, Mongolian gazelle, and wapiti generally exhibit an expanding trend, whereas the Siberian roe deer shows high vulnerability under the high-emission scenario. We identified stable suitable habitats serving as potential climate refugia, primarily distributed in northern Mongolia and northeastern Inner Mongolia. However, significant spatial mismatches exist between these refugia and the current PA network, with a substantial proportion of refugia remaining inadequately protected. We suggest that priority should be given to the establishment of transboundary ecological corridors and the implementation of adaptive conservation strategies to safeguard ungulate populations against climate change and habitat fragmentation on the Mongolian Plateau.

title: Elevation-dependent greening of grassland vegetation and its driving factors in the Tianshan Mountains, Central Asia
abstract: The Tianshan Mountains constitute the “water tower” and a critical ecological barrier in the arid region of Central Asia, where climate change has significantly affected vegetation dynamics. Owing to elevation gradients, grasslands exhibit pronounced vertical differentiation, yet elevation-dependent changes remain insufficiently understood. Using the PKU GIMMS normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) v1.2 dataset, vegetation greening trends during 1982–2022 were analyzed, grassland NDVI variations across elevation gradients were examined, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was applied to reveal the mechanisms driving NDVI changes. Growing season NDVI exhibited an overall greening trend, with 43.92% of the area showing significant greening and 28.33% browning. Strong seasonal contrasts were observed, with greening predominating in spring and browning in autumn. Interannual NDVI variability increased markedly after the beginning of the 21st century, with this enhancement occurring across 96.01% of the valid vegetated area. Grasslands exhibited stronger differentiation, characterized by weaker greening and more pronounced browning. Both mean NDVI and its trends showed clear elevation dependence, with greening weakening and browning emerging at higher elevations. SEM results indicated that grassland dynamics were primarily controlled by the positive effect of soil moisture (SM) and the negative effect of vapor pressure deficit (VPD). Temperature effects varied seasonally, while precipitation exerted an indirect positive influence via SM. These findings highlight the dominant roles of moisture conditions and hydrothermal processes in shaping grassland dynamics, providing a basis for sustainable management and ecological conservation in arid mountain regions.

title: Spatial identification and resilience optimization of urban cold-heat networks for heat island mitigation
abstract: Global warming and rapid urbanization have significantly intensified the urban heat island (UHI) effect, posing severe challenges to urban sustainability and public health. Previous studies investigated UHI mitigation pathways from a network perspective, encompassing the enhancement of urban cool island (UCI) networks and the disruption of UHI networks. Nevertheless, these studies predominantly concentrated on a single type of UCI or UHI network, neglecting the source–sink linkages between UCI and UHI, which to some extent constrained the comprehensiveness of mitigation strategies. Therefore, this study developed an integrated urban cold-heat network (UCHN) by incorporating morphological spatial pattern analysis, landscape connectivity, and circuit theory, using the main urban area of Xi'an as a case study. Furthermore, robustness analysis was introduced to evaluate the network's resilience. Results revealed that the UCHN comprised 50 UCIs, 59 UHIs, and 291 cold-heat corridors (CHCs). Among these, 47 connectivity pinchpoints (CPs) and 33 connectivity barriers (CBs) were attached to the CHCs; optimizing or removing these problematic nodes could effectively enhance the UCHN connectivity. Resilience assessment showed that under intentional attacks, the progressive failure of UCIs significantly weakened the network structure. However, after adding four potential UCIs based on planning requirements and satellite imagery, the resilience of the UCHN improved during the early stages of attacks. The “network identification – resilience assessment” cascade framework developed in this study was intended to provide guidance for the spatial governance and adaptive planning of urban thermal environments.

title: Effective number of communities reveals extent of biodiversity change – a cross-organism analysis in the Wadden Sea
abstract: Biodiversity changes in ecosystems worldwide, but assessing the true magnitude of this transformation requires the analysis of multiple dimensions of compositional change. Trends in α-diversity only capture the net difference between gains and losses, while year-on-year temporal turnover in composition does not reflect long-term changes in species identity. We used extensive monitoring data from the Wadden Sea UNESCO World Heritage Site as a case to explore the accumulated change over time through presence-absence and dominance-weighted data. Most time series showed significant temporal trends in α-diversity, but increases or decreases occurred in roughly equal proportions, such that average slopes did not differ from zero. Turnover between subsequent years was higher for fast-growing taxa, but showed only subtle signs of acceleration or deceleration over time. Organism groups did not show an overall decrease in spatial turnover, contrasting concerns of biotic homogenization. The full extent of change became visible only when analysing the accumulated turnover of species composition with time as the effective number of communities (ENC temp ), defined as the overall diversity in a time series divided by the median annual diversity. ENC temp increased with time, such that even when focusing strongly on dominant species, 8% (phytoplankton) to 36% (plants) of time series effectively exchanged community composition at least once (depending on organism group and dominance-weight). Implementing ENC temp in biodiversity assessments provides practitioners and scientists with unique information about the addition or loss of rare species as well as shifts in dominance.

title: Coupling minimum cumulative resistance and circuit theory for intangible cultural heritage corridor construction: A case study of the Jin-Shaan gorge
abstract: Intangible Cultural Heritage(ICH) is an important foundation for sustainable cultural development and regional cultural identify. However, ICH resources are often spatially fragmented, and their regional integration receives limited attention. Existing corridor methods also have difficulty representing multiple connectivity pathways and spatial continuity between heritage resources. This study examined 177 designated ICH sites in the Jin–Shaan Gorge section of the Yellow River Basin as the research objects, utilizing integrated Geographic Information Systems, Kernel Density Estimation, the Nearest Neighbor Index, the Analytic Hierarchy Process, the Minimum Cumulative Resistance model, and circuit theory to investigate the spatial distribution characteristics and optimize the ICH corridor network. The results show clear clustering, with large-scale dispersed distribution and small-scale clustered distribution, forming a “three cores and one belt” pattern. The main clusters are located in Suide County, Hancheng, Hejin, and Shuocheng District. Suitability analysis shows that highly suitable and moderately suitable areas for corridor construction account for approximately 74.0% of the study area and are predominantly located in the southern part of the gorge. The coupled Minimum Cumulative Resistance model and circuit theory identify a hierarchical corridor system with 78 primary corridors, 38 secondary corridors, and 9 tertiary corridors, forming a spatially connected and integrated heritage network. This study proposes a multi-scale framework for Intangible Cultural Heritage corridors and provides a scientific basis for the systematic conservation, spatial integration, and sustainable development of intangible cultural heritage in large river-basin regions.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of plastic pollutant emissions from agricultural greenhouses in China
abstract: Greenhouses are increasingly recognized as hotspots of agricultural plastic pollution, yet the spatiotemporal dynamics of their pollutant emissions and the mechanisms by which natural, management, and socio-economic drivers jointly regulate these emissions remain poorly quantified. Thus, we integrated time-series Landsat imagery on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform with a prefecture-city-level emission inventory to quantify emissions of 2 representative phthalate esters (Dibutyl phthalate (DBP) and Bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)) from China's agricultural greenhouses during 2005–2024. We then coupled Random Forest (RF) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation to identify dominant drivers and their key thresholds, and applied partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to decompose the direct, indirect, and total effects of latent drivers (natural conditions, on-site management, agricultural development, and urbanization) on emissions. National emissions increased 2.7-fold over the study period (DEHP: from 24.29 t to 65.50 t; DBP: from 12.37 t to 33.35 t) and were strongly spatially concentrated with East China. Driver importance shifted markedly over time, with slope and rural population gaining prominence. Crucially, PLS-SEM revealed pervasive offsetting pathways: for urbanization in 2015, its direct suppressive effect on emissions (−0.195) was more than cancelled by a positive indirect effect operating through agricultural expansion (0.248), yielding a near-zero net effect (−0.015). Thus, a driver's apparent unimportance can mask large but opposing direct and indirect pathways. We conclude that greenhouse expansion simultaneously secures production and amplifies plastic pollutant emissions through a coupled driver network in which indirect mediation dominates. Because an apparently weak driver may merely be internally offset, interventions targeting a single driver are liable to be neutralized; effective control must instead act on the mediating pathways (e.g., agricultural expansion) and be differentiated by region.

title: Structural thresholds regulate forest demographic processes across plantation and natural forests
abstract: Stand structure regulates forest recovery through demographic processes, yet thresholds controlling growth, recruitment, and mortality remain poorly quantified across forest types. Using long-term observations (1979–2017) from 1369 permanent plots (1225 natural forest plots and 144 plantation plots) in the mountain forest ecosystems of Sichuan, China, we separately analyzed growth, recruitment, and mortality dynamics in natural and plantation forests and identified their structural thresholds in response to stand age and basal area (BA). Plantation forests exhibited higher growth, recruitment, and mortality, with abrupt declines occurring at earlier thresholds than in natural forests (growth drops at 15.0 and 45.0 yr vs. 39.0 and 120.0 yr; recruitment declines at BA 12.0 and 28.0 m 2 ha −1 vs. 23.0 and 50.0 m 2 ha −1 ). Mortality showed contrasting trajectories: it increased at both early and late stages, indicating higher demographic risk in plantations, whereas it declined with age and only rose slightly in late stages in natural forests, reflecting more stable turnover. The influence of BA on demographic rates varied with stand age. In both natural and plantation forests, recruitment showed the highest sensitivity to BA from young to mature stands, whereas mortality became increasingly important in over-mature stands, indicating a general shift from recruitment limitation to competition-driven filtering during forest development. This transition occurred substantially earlier in plantations than in natural forests. These patterns highlight critical windows for intervention: managing stand structure before the onset of threshold declines in growth and recruitment—particularly in young, dense plantations—can accelerate transitions toward stable, resilient forest dynamics and promote more desirable forest recovery trajectories under ongoing restoration.

title: Diagnosing post-fire recovery with satellite-based indicators: divergent trajectories and phase-dependent predictor associations after a boreal megafire in Northeast China
abstract: Wildfire alters forest attributes that may recover at different rates, yet their temporal divergence and phase-dependent associations remain poorly understood. We developed a multi-indicator diagnostic framework to assess two decades of recovery following the 2003 megafire across 1116 km 2 of boreal forest in Northeast China. The framework integrated the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), Leaf Area Index (LAI), and percent tree cover (PTC), representing vegetation greenness, photosynthetic carbon uptake, leaf area, and tree cover, respectively. Long-term trajectories and predictor associations were derived from satellite products; ground-based and drone surveys were used to evaluate the 2023 vegetation classification. Indicator-specific phases were identified from control-corrected data series, and pixel-level mismatch between indicator- and PTC-based recovery was quantified using explicit thresholds. NDVI, GPP, and LAI approached 0.95 of their product-specific pre-fire values within a decade, whereas PTC remained below 0.80 in 2023. Approximately 43–50% of the valid area reached the corresponding NDVI, GPP, or LAI threshold while remaining below the PTC threshold. Predictor importance and model-based associations shifted among phases, with fire severity and climate ranking higher early and pre-fire vegetation conditions becoming more prominent later. Retrogressive transitions were more frequent in higher-severity classes. Divergence among indicator trajectories was consistent across alternative data sources, temporal-processing methods, and spatial resolutions. By integrating explicit thresholds with spatial disagreement among indicators, this framework advances post-fire assessment toward an ecologically explicit diagnosis of vegetation resilience that distinguishes attributes and identifies persistent constraints, thereby directing management attention to where it is most needed.

title: Species-specific phenological indicators reveal topographic–climatic associations with evergreen-tree phenology in subtropical hilly regions
abstract: Evergreen-tree phenology is an important ecological indicator of forest responses to climate change and local environmental heterogeneity. In subtropical hilly regions, frequent cloudy and rainy conditions, complex terrain, and weak seasonal greenness signals hinder species-level phenological retrieval and interpretation. Here, we evaluated the ecological indicator value of the start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), and length of season (LOS) for eight representative evergreen tree species in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China. We reconstructed 8-day, 30-m normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) time series from Landsat 8 and MODIS observations during 2015–2020 using the gap-filling–Savitzky–Golay (GF-SG) method, derived phenological metrics, and analyzed topographic–climatic associations using mixed-effects piecewise structural equation models (SEMs). Independent withheld-Landsat validation of reconstructed NDVI showed R 2 values of 0.581–0.671 during June–August and 0.710–0.770 during other months. SOS and EOS shared a broadly similar coastal–hilly gradient, with earlier dates in southeastern coastal and lowland areas and later dates toward the northwestern hills; LOS generally increased toward the hills. EOS exhibited broader interspecific distributions and greater interannual variability than SOS. For SOS, precipitation-effect estimates were predominantly negative across species, whereas temperature associations varied more strongly in direction and magnitude. For EOS, temperature-effect estimates were positive across all eight species, whereas precipitation associations showed greater interspecific heterogeneity; aspect showed the most directionally consistent topographic association with EOS. These patterns support EOS as a comparatively sensitive ecological indicator of species-level differentiation and late-season environmental variation in subtropical evergreen forests.

title: Assessing and Predicting Ecological Quality Using a Novel Indicator and Machine Learning Framework: A Case Study of Beijing
abstract: Ecological quality is a comprehensive concept that reflects the overall condition of an ecosystem. Understanding its dynamic evolution and future trajectories is essential for sustainable ecosystem management. However, existing studies often rely on single-dimensional perspectives and overlook ecosystem complexity, nonlinear relationships, and interactions among drivers. Therefore, this study developed a novel ecological quality indicator based on a “function–status–disturbance” framework integrating ecosystem services, the Remote Sensing Ecological Index, the Modified Water Area Remote Sensing Ecological Index, and nighttime light intensity. We quantified the spatiotemporal evolution of ecological quality in Beijing from 2000 to 2020. Correlation analysis was used to select ten significant environmental and socioeconomic drivers from eleven candidate variables. A Random Forest model incorporating the ten drivers predicted ecological quality under three representative SSP–RCP scenarios for 2035. Permutation importance based on the percentage increase in mean squared error and partial dependence analysis were used to quantify the relative importance, nonlinear responses, and threshold effects of drivers. The results showed that (1) ecological quality in Beijing exhibited a three-tier concentric gradient pattern, increasing from the urban center to the northwestern mountains. (2) Ecological quality declined overall from 2000 to 2020, particularly during the first decade. (3) The Random Forest model showed high predictive accuracy, with an R 2 of 0.979, an MAE of 0.029 and an RMSE of 0.041. Among the three scenarios in 2035, the ecological protection scenario exhibited the highest ecological quality, followed by the middle path and baseline scenarios, but all remained below the 2020 level. (4) Ecosystem responses varied substantially across scenarios. Natural ecosystems performed best under the ecological protection scenario, whereas cultivated land showed the opposite pattern, with the baseline scenario achieving the highest quality. (5) Annual precipitation and distance to regional centers were the most influential drivers, and most factors exhibited nonlinear and threshold effects. These findings provide scientific support for adaptive ecosystem management and sustainable urban planning.

title: Ecological quality–risk integration reveals spatial management priorities in rapidly urbanizing high-biomass regions
abstract: Rapid urbanization in high-biomass regions has intensified conflicts between ecological conservation and urban expansion, yet conventional assessments may overlook areas where high ecological quality coexists with elevated landscape structural risk. However, the long-term spatial mismatches between ecological quality and landscape ecological risk, together with their nonlinear associations with natural and anthropogenic factors, remain insufficiently understood in rapidly urbanizing high-biomass regions. To address these gaps, this study integrated an improved Remote Sensing Ecological Index (IRSEI) with a Landscape Ecological Risk (LER) model to evaluate ecological quality–risk relationships across Guangdong Province, China. To improve ecological assessment in densely vegetated areas, IRSEI replaced NDVI with the kernel normalized difference vegetation index (kNDVI) and incorporated the abundance index (AI) and net primary productivity (NPP) to represent habitat-support conditions and ecosystem productivity. Standardized IRSEI and LER values were combined through quadrant partitioning, and extreme gradient boosting coupled with SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost–SHAP) was used to examine nonlinear relationships with natural and anthropogenic factors. From 2001 to 2022, ecological quality remained generally stable with a slight upward trend, whereas landscape ecological risk showed substantial spatial changes. The integrated assessment revealed persistent quality–risk mismatches, particularly in areas with relatively high values of both indicators. These Priority Regulation Zones expanded from 6.36% to 8.14% of the study area, suggesting that landscapes with relatively high ecological quality but structural vulnerability may be underestimated by quality-based assessments alone. SHAP results indicated that topographic factors had the strongest associations with both ecological quality and landscape ecological risk, while anthropogenic factors showed nonlinear and stage-dependent relationships. The IRSEI–LER framework thus provides a practical basis for differentiated ecological management in rapidly urbanizing subtropical high-biomass regions.

title: Operational dual-track indicators for dryland greening quality and drought response: A Junggar Basin demonstration
abstract: Dryland greening is often treated as recovery success, yet greenness only describes vegetation state and does not measure the capacity to recover after drought. Treating greenness troughs as drought years, or ignoring the long-term rise in greenness, can overstate recovery and miss meteorological drought. This study develops a practical dual-track monitoring suite for inland oasis–desert landscapes, so greening quality and drought response can be reported separately rather than diagnosed as one global greening–resilience pattern. In the Junggar Basin, long-term greening is combined with a resilience-change metric to separate true-recovery greening from fragile greening. Meteorological drought years are identified independently; greenness is used only to measure impact and recovery time. Fragile greening covers more of the basin (17.8%) than true-recovery greening (11.8%), and more than half of significant greening is fragile. Meteorological drought years and vegetation-trough years seldom coincide. The two tracks are only weakly related, so one cannot be inferred from the other. Greening quality and drought response answer different questions and should be reported together: quadrant shares, a meteorological drought list, and post-drought recovery times, kept separate by oasis and land-use context.

title: Landscape carrying capacity approach: Thematic and methodological patterns
abstract: The challenges of 21st century reguire more sustainable solutions and processes. Spatial planning is one of the most comprehensive process of structuring and directing of human activities on multiple scales. The shift of spatial planning systems toward sustainability has begun over the past few decades. Landscape carrying capacity approach can be a crutial element of sustainable spatial planning. The scientific methods need to be more integrated into the spatial planning practice to ensure sustainability. Studies related to landscape carrying capacity have increased rapidly over the past three decades. The aim of this study is to provide an initial review of the research field of the landscape carrying capacity approach in relation to spatial planning. 701 studies were assessed, and their evaluation was conducted through thematic and methodological clustering. Results show that land suitability assessments; agriculture sector or agriculture-industry-servicies sectors in parallel; all or most of environmental components in parallel are the most frequently researched topics. Several conventionally applied methods (e.g. analytical hierarchy process), several specialized applied methods (e.g. life cycle assessment), and several rarely applied methods (e.g. DPSIR) were identified relation to landscape carrying capacity. These research findings can support the development of a standardized landscape carrying capacity methodology, contribute to more sustainable spatial planning processes, and facilitate the advancement of sustainable sectoral planning approaches. Therefore, this study may serve as an initial step toward promoting the comprehensive integration of scientific methods and tools—while allowing for flexible adaptation—into spatial planning processes.

title: An assessment system integrating FESLM and SDGs for sustainable use of black soil: Quantifying cross-framework objective consistency
abstract: Black soil degradation in Northeast China threatens regional sustainable development. Conducting a scientific assessment of sustainable use of black soil is of great significance. The Food and Agriculture Organization's Framework for Evaluating Sustainable Land Management (FESLM) and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) provide authoritative frameworks for guiding sustainable land use assessment, but there has long been a lack of quantitative evidence regarding the consistency of their objectives. In this study, we first integrated these two frameworks to develop an assessment system for sustainable land use tailored to the Black Soil Region. Second, we employed the unsupervised dimensionality reduction and resynthesis process of canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to quantitatively measure the degree of consistency between the two frameworks. Then, using combined weighting method based on game theory (CWGT), we estimated the levels of sustainable use of black soil across 111 counties and districts from 2010 to 2020, and explored their spatiotemporal evolution patterns. Finally, using root mean square deviation (RMSD), we explored the trade-offs and synergies among different assessment dimensions and SDG targets across counties and districts. The results indicate that (1) the two frameworks exhibited high objective consistency, with the first three canonical correlation coefficients reaching 1.000 and the remaining two reaching 0.983 and 0.671; (2) levels of sustainable use of black soil were generally low, with 107 counties and districts (96.4%) having average scores below 0.4 and high-value clusters concentrated in the Harbin–Changchun Urban Agglomeration; (3) counties and districts with high viability scores generally had advantages in industrial and investment indicators, whereas those with lower viability scores often had advantages in primary-sector output; (4) the degree of synergy among the five FESLM dimensions and among the SDG targets was generally low, with 88.3% and 95.5% of counties and districts, respectively, having average RMSD values above 0.3 during 2010–2020; and (5) high overall scores could coexist with uneven performance across dimensions, while low RMSD values could coexist with low scores across dimensions. These findings support the integration of FESLM and SDGs in assessing sustainable use of black soil and highlight the need to consider overall performance and multidimensional balance together when identifying regional management priorities.

title: Physical environmental indicators of protected area representativeness: a machine-learning approach across 35 Japanese national parks
abstract: Evaluating the physical environmental representativeness of protected area networks requires spatially explicit indicators that are locally calibrated yet nationally comparable. We introduce PhysRep (Physical Representativeness score), a continuous indicator of how closely physical environmental conditions at any location resemble those within a protected area's strictly protected zones. PhysRep is derived from park-specific XGBoost classifiers trained on climatic, topographic, geological and micro-landform variables within an H3 hexagonal grid at approximately 0.1 km 2 resolution, and demonstrated across all 35 Japanese national parks. Spatially grouped nested cross-validation guarded against inflation from spatial autocorrelation, and SHAP values identified the variables driving PhysRep at park and network scales. All 35 park-specific models outperformed label-shuffled negative controls in ROC-AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, median 0.792 versus 0.488; smallest margin 0.113), the metric used for tier assignment because it is invariant to class prevalence (median F1: 0.777). Climatic and topographic variables dominated nationally, while geological and micro-landform features dominated in regionally specific contexts. Nationwide mapping revealed spatially coherent high-representativeness areas extending beyond current park boundaries, but for most parks these occur as many small, scattered patches rather than large contiguous tracts, indicating limited environmental continuity around individual parks. PhysRep surfaces thus make representativeness gaps and redundancies explicit at the park level. We recommend that protected area network planning under area-based frameworks such as 30 × 30 and Other Effective Area based Conservation Measures (OECMs) incorporate park-specific similarity assessments alongside existing biological and connectivity indicators, prioritizing parks with little contiguous environmental continuity nearby and recognizing where such continuity already provides regional-scale redundancy. The indicator is modular and transferable, requiring only spatial boundaries and environmental rasters as inputs.

title: Root-zone moisture governs vegetation recovery after drought across the Mongolian plateau
abstract: Drought is intensifying across dryland ecosystems under climate change, yet the mechanisms controlling post-drought recovery remain unresolved. Satellite observations have produced conflicting evidence on whether photosynthetic activity or canopy greenness recovers first, limiting assessments of ecosystem resilience. Here we analyse 24 years of drought-recovery events across approximately 73,000 grassland pixels of the Mongolian Plateau, using GOSIF and GPP as functional indicators and NDVI and EVI as structural greenness indicators, to test how recovery varies with aridity and soil-water replenishment depth. After screening near-zero fluorescence baselines, canopy greenness and photosynthetic function recovered at broadly similar times, with remaining GOSIF–NDVI differences close to one native GOSIF observation interval. A large apparent driest-quartile reversal, in which greenness appeared to recover approximately 80 days before fluorescence, was predominantly a metric artifact: 57% of driest-quartile fluorescence events had near-zero baselines, and screening collapsed the difference from +80 to +8 days. Root-zone moisture was consistently associated with shorter GOSIF recovery, and this relationship remained consistent in separate tests using SPEI-based drought termination and spatial blocks up to 4°. GPP showed the same directional relationship but with weaker attribution magnitude under independent termination, whereas structural deep-soil coefficients and the aridity-specific recovery ordering were sensitive to the event-termination definition. These results identify a robust GOSIF–root-zone association while showing that broader functional–structural contrasts depend on event definition and spatial scale.

title: Exploring the value of thematic urban ecosystem accounts in Western Balkan countries to inform urban greening actions
abstract: Abstract Urban ecological health is increasingly prioritized in Europe, as reflected in the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030, the Nature Restoration Regulation, and the amendment to the Regulation on Environmental-Economic Accounts. Translating this ambition into greening actions that halt and reverse urban ecological degradation requires standardized, spatially explicit indicators. This study explores the utility of the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting–Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA-EA) framework for developing thematic urban ecosystem accounts as integrated metrics to inform urban greening in the Western Balkans. We constructed pilot accounts for the Western Balkans for 2018, with particular focus on Horizon-funded CROSS-REIS countries, where local accounts were also developed for representative municipalities (Kranj, Rijeka, Niš, Podgorica, Tirana). The accounts quantify ecosystem extent, four condition metrics (imperviousness, green space, tree cover, and PM₁₀ concentration), and the service air filtration using PM₁₀ deposition onto vegetation as a proxy. Results were benchmarked nationally against EU/EFTA/UK countries and locally against Italian municipalities of the National Biodiversity Future Centre project. The analysis reveals that urban ecosystems in the Western Balkans exist on a continuum with other European countries but exhibit a distinct, more homogeneous profile shaped by geography, climate, and policy legacies. The accounts identify ecological degradation hotspots (e.g., high soil sealing) and areas of high service-delivery capacity, supporting translation of spatial diagnosis into targeted greening priorities. Overall, the study shows that thematic urban ecosystem accounts offer a standardized, multi-scale evidence base to inform and monitor urban greening policies, supporting the Western Balkans’ environmental management needs on their path toward EU integration.

title: From early-warning signal to potential risk indicator: Using tree-growth variability to assess climate-related risk in major European tree species
abstract: Variability metrics are the most frequently used early-warning signals across scientific disciplines. Applied to ecological time series, increasing variability is widely interpreted as a signal of reduced system stability. In trees, elevated growth variability has been linked to increased climate sensitivity, but its drivers and continental-scale patterns remain poorly understood. Here, we assess patterns of tree-growth variability under climate change and explore its potential to serve as an indicator of climate-related growth vulnerability. We quantified growth variability using the Gini coefficient applied to a Europe-wide tree-ring width dataset covering seven tree species from 631 sites. Generalized additive models were used to identify climatic and tree-level drivers of growth variability and to project spatio-temporal trends across biogeographical regions under three climate change scenarios from 2011 to 2100. To evaluate the applicability of growth variability as risk indicator, predicted growth variability was translated into species-specific risk classes. High growth variability was consistently associated with higher climate-related risk classes, whereas intermediate and low levels showed a less distinctive and more species-specific signal. Climate and tree variables were identified as key drivers of growth variability, whereby warming consistently increased variability, whereas precipitation reduced it. Growth variability increased in older trees but declined with higher basal area increment. Future projections showed increasing growth variability with scenario severity, particularly in continental parts of species' distribution areas, although responses differed among species and biogeographical regions. Our results suggest that increasing growth variability reflects rising climate sensitivity and may indicate heightened climate-related risk once species-specific thresholds are exceeded. This approach represents a first step towards using growth variability not only as a diagnostic signal, but also as a prospective indicator of climate-related tree risk that may complement existing modelling frameworks for assessments of tree species suitability in the future.

title: Ecological indicators of biodiversity and ecosystem responses to climate change in agroecology and nature-based solutions: a scoping review
abstract: Climate change reshapes biodiversity patterns and ecosystem processes across scales. However, ecological indicators used to track these changes remain uneven in structure and application. This study maps and synthesizes indicators applied in agroecology and nature-based solutions (NbS) for assessing biodiversity and ecosystem responses under climate change. A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, covering literature from 2003 to 2026. From a final dataset of 89 sources, data were extracted through a structured coding framework and synthesized using an Indicator–Scale–Response matrix and an Indicator Application Index. Findings show shared reliance on indicators such as species diversity, ecosystem productivity, carbon dynamics, ecosystem services, and resilience. Differences emerge in how these indicators are applied. Agroecology prioritizes process-based and field-level measurements grounded in local ecological interactions, while NbS emphasizes standardized and scalable metrics linked to monitoring and reporting systems. Cross-scale integration remains uneven, particularly in connecting species-level responses with ecosystem and landscape indicators. Remote sensing and Essential Biodiversity Variables provide emerging pathways for linking scales, though field integration remains partial. Results point to fragmented indicator systems that limit coherent ecological assessment across management contexts. Strengthening alignment between field observations and scalable monitoring approaches could improve comparability and usability of ecological indicators for climate adaptation and ecosystem management in agricultural landscapes.

title: Precipitation legacies reshape clonal demography associated with early productivity recovery in a semi-arid typical steppe
abstract: Altered precipitation can leave persistent legacies after climatic anomalies cease, yet whether these legacies are retained in plant regenerative organs and linked to subsequent productivity recovery remains unclear. Using a long-term precipitation manipulation experiment in a semi-arid typical steppe, we examined aboveground net primary productivity (ANPP), plant community composition, and clonal demographic traits during early recovery following seven years of drought and increased-precipitation treatments. Drought legacies reduced belowground bud and aboveground shoot density, particularly for forbs, and shifted bud bank and shoot composition toward greater relative grass dominance. In contrast, increased-precipitation legacies enhanced forb bud density, promoted forb shoot density in year-specific comparisons, and increased forb dominance, while grass responses were weak or negative. Although the effects of historical precipitation treatments on whole-community ANPP weakened during recovery, functional-group responses and community composition remained associated with precipitation histories. ANPP recovery was positively associated with community-level bud and shoot densities during recovery from drought, whereas these associations were not significant during recovery from increased precipitation. Structural equation modeling further linked soil moisture to ANPP recovery through clonal demography under drought legacy conditions, whereas ANPP recovery following increased precipitation was positively associated with available phosphorus and negatively associated with forb relative biomass. Our findings suggest that belowground bud bank may retain the effects of historical precipitation conditions, with corresponding differences subsequently expressed in aboveground shoots. However, the contribution of this demographic memory to productivity recovery depends on precipitation legacy context, supporting a context-dependent role for clonal demography as a biological link between past precipitation and subsequent productivity recovery.

title: Vegetation structural change and carbon–water functional responses across arid Central Asia: spatiotemporal patterns and environmental associations
abstract: Anthropogenic climate change is intensifying ecological stress in arid Central Asia, where vegetation structure and carbon–water-related functional responses are strongly constrained by water availability and atmospheric demand. Yet structural greening does not necessarily imply parallel changes in carbon–water-related functional dimensions. Here, we examined long-term relationships between leaf area index (LAI) and three complementary indicators of ecosystem carbon–water coupling—precipitation use efficiency (PUE), water use efficiency (WUE), and the transpiration-to-evapotranspiration ratio (TET)—and assessed their associations with climatic and soil-moisture conditions during 1982–2018. Using satellite, reanalysis, land-use, soil-moisture, evapotranspiration and climate records, we combined temporal trends, pixel-wise correlations, land-use transitions and ridge-regression-based relative statistical contributions across aridity gradients. Regional LAI increased only weakly, whereas WUE declined significantly (−0.023 decade −1 , p = 0.047). Spatially, significant greening was more widespread than browning (22.99% versus 11.31%), but declines in PUE, WUE and TET extended across more than half of the study region. Positive LAI–functional associations were concentrated in irrigated oases and cropland-dominated landscapes, whereas weaker or negative relationships occurred across parts of natural grassland and desert vegetation. Environmental associations were indicator-specific: surface soil moisture generally exhibited larger relative statistical contributions to PUE and WUE, whereas root-zone soil moisture showed relatively stronger associations with TET; sensitivity analyses broadly retained these rankings but indicated weaker depth-specific differentiation for WUE. Contribution direction also depended on the temporal trajectory of each environmental factor, with the largest-contribution factor showing trend-consistent signed contributions across 72.53–80.56% of the analyzed area. Along the aridity gradient, associations shifted from stronger soil-moisture dependence in drier environments toward greater temperature importance in wetter environments. These results indicate that, within the integrated dataset framework adopted here, vegetation greenness alone is insufficient to characterize carbon–water-related ecosystem functional responses across the dryland landscapes examined in arid Central Asia and should be interpreted together with hydroclimatic conditions, land use, and aridity context.

title: Attribution of changes in vegetation structure and carbon–water fluxes in the Ji-shaped bend of the Yellow River based on process-guided machine learning
abstract: Arid and semi-arid ecosystems play an important role in the global terrestrial carbon cycle, but the relative contributions of climate change, elevated CO₂, and land-use change (LUCC) to their carbon–water processes remain uncertain. In this study, we developed a process-guided machine learning (PGML) framework integrating Biome-BGC and LightGBM, which achieves synergistic simulation of mechanistic constraints and data-driven modeling through residual learning. PGML significantly improved the pixel-scale simulation accuracy of LAI, GPP, and ET in the Ji-shaped Bend of the Yellow River, a typical arid and semi-arid region of China, with R 2 values of 0.70, 0.95, and 0.91, respectively, and reduced RMSE by 61%–83% compared with the calibrated process model. Full-factorial attribution showed that LAI, GPP, ET, and WUE all increased significantly during the study period, with the growth rate of GPP exceeding that of ET, thereby promoting an increase in WUE. Under the process representations and driving factors considered in the PGML framework, elevated CO₂ was identified as the largest simulated contributor to the increases in LAI, GPP, and ET, with contribution rates of 71.8%, 78.7%, and 75.2%, respectively; climate change contributed approximately 15%, while the direct contribution of LUCC was less than 0.25%. Meanwhile, the regional mean climate–CO₂ interaction effect was negative, indicating that local climatic conditions generally weakened the CO₂ fertilization effect. These results reveal that elevated CO₂ made the largest contribution to the enhancement of vegetation structure and carbon–water fluxes in the Ji-shaped Bend of the Yellow River over the past two decades.

title: Associations among alien fish dominance, biodiversity, and spatial variability of native fish assemblages in Plateau Rivers
abstract: While plateau river environments shape native fish diversity, they inherently constrain species' spatial distribution patterns; however, this equilibrium, forged through long-term evolution, may be disrupted by the introduction of alien species. Integrating spatial distribution survey data of fish communities across six rivers in the Western Sichuan Plateau, China, we applied Piecewise Structural Equation Modeling (PSEM) to disentangle the associations among physical habitats, alien species dominance, biodiversity, and community spatial variability (measured by Abundance Variation Degree, AVD). The results indicated that the rivers with high alien species dominance did not exhibit a direct decline in native diversity; rather, alien species dominance was significantly and positively correlated with native taxonomic diversity (Shannon index), but had no direct effect on functional diversity (Rao's Q). This phenomenon likely occurs because the unique habitats and highly specialized native fish assemblages in plateau rivers leave unsaturated ecological niches, thereby facilitating a temporary sympatric coexistence between alien and native species, while extreme environmental filtering strictly constrains the functional trait space of the communities. PSEM analysis further revealed that high-altitude environments strongly restricted alien species (path coefficient = −0.54), and functional diversity (Rao's Q) did not exhibit any significant association with AVD. Conversely, both alien species dominance (path coefficient = 0.52; P < 0.001) and native taxonomic diversity (Shannon index, path coefficient = 0.31; P < 0.05) were significantly and positively associated with AVD, indicating that spatial turnover in these native assemblages is highly sensitive to taxonomic shifts, whereas functional traits remain highly conserved across the plateau rivers. These findings suggest that in fragile plateau rivers, anomalously elevated diversity indices may obscure the increased spatial variability and altered compositional structure associated with the presence of alien species. Therefore, rather than merely maximizing overall biodiversity indices, conservation strategies for these high-altitude ecosystems should prioritize the spatial reconstruction of native assemblages to proactively fill unsaturated niches, thereby enhancing community resistance to alien species.

title: Belowground ecosystem multifunctionality embodied in China's agricultural imports: Thermal geography, equity trajectory, and a multi-indicator accounting framework
abstract: Belowground ecosystem multifunctionality (BEMF), a composite indicator of soil biological and biogeochemical functioning, underpins agricultural productivity yet is absent from consumption-based environmental indicator frameworks.
