We develop and apply the first annual trade-embodied BEMF indicator system for a national economy, applied to China's agricultural sector (2009–2022), built from a spatially resolved country–sector intensity matrix spanning 2222 cells across 133 nations (93.9% direct pixel-level data), linked to bilateral trade flows from 61 partners. The framework integrates six components: consumption-based accounting, structural decomposition, thermal stress stratification, biocapacity overdraft, planetary equity boundary tracking, and counterfactual analysis. China's consumption-based BEMF expanded 48.2% while import-embodied BEMF grew 161.7%, with import-volume growth contributing 124% of cumulative change and geographic re-sourcing producing no detectable ecological signal over fourteen years. A thermal stress concentration indicator benchmarked against the 16.4 °C suppression threshold shows thermally stressed origins supplied 64.1% of import-embodied BEMF by 2022, with a persistently sub-unity concentration ratio confirming systematic per-ton underperformance of thermally degraded suppliers. A planetary equity boundary exceedance ratio rising from 0.419 to 0.676 projects transgression of the global equal-rights BEMF allocation by approximately 2036 under the full trend, with shorter recent windows placing this later, within 2036–2049. Counterfactual indicators quantify a thermal quality penalty of up to 7.7% of annual consumption-based BEMF, achievable through sourcing geography alone without altering trade volumes or commodity composition. The framework is replicable across any agricultural trading economy, offering an operational tool for integrating belowground indicators into biodiversity monitoring aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and SDG 15.3.

title: A national-scale probabilistic ecological risk indicator for land use change: An improved Sharpe ratio framework with nonlinear driving threshold identification across China
abstract: Global climate change and intensified anthropogenic land use have profoundly altered ecosystem structure and function, resulting in increasingly complex ecological risk (ER) patterns. However, ecological risk induced by land use change (ERLUC) remains constrained by insufficient consideration of land use uncertainty, ecosystem service (ES) trade-offs, and nonlinear mechanisms. This study develops a probability-based ERLUC framework for China by integrating land use simulation (LCM), ecosystem service modeling (InVEST), an improved Sharpe ratio-based risk indicator, and LightGBM-SHAP. The framework quantifies future land use transition probabilities and ecosystem service responses from 2020 to 2035, while identifying dominant drivers and ecological thresholds.ERLUC exhibited significant spatial heterogeneity across China. High-risk areas were mainly concentrated in rapidly urbanizing regions such as the North China Plain, whereas low-risk areas were primarily distributed in the interior Qinghai–Tibet Plateau and arid regions of Northwest China. Under future land use scenarios, ecosystem services showed contrasting responses: carbon sequestration remained stable (−0.02%), water yield increased slightly (+1.16%), while habitat quality and soil conservation declined by 1.46% and 9.58%, respectively. LightGBM-SHAP analysis identified NDVI as the dominant factor controlling ER differentiation, contributing 17.7%, followed by bio15 (13.3%), bio23 (10.9%), and precipitation (10.4%). Nonlinear analysis revealed a clear NDVI threshold effect, with ecological risk decreasing rapidly as vegetation coverage increased and showing predominantly negative responses when NDVI exceeded approximately 0.15–0.20.This study provides a probability- and mechanism-oriented framework for national-scale ERLUC assessment, enhancing understanding of how uncertain land transitions, ecosystem service responses, and nonlinear environmental drivers jointly shape ecological risks. The identified spatial patterns and ecological thresholds support differentiated land management and ecological restoration strategies.

title: Abrupt vegetation shifts and their drivers in Arid Central Asia
abstract: Dryland vegetation responses to environmental change may be nonlinear or abrupt rather than gradual. However, long-term vegetation studies have largely focused on linear trends, leaving abrupt trajectories and their nonlinear environmental associations in Central Asian drylands insufficiently understood. Using 2000–2023 MODIS NDVI, we distinguished linear, curvilinear, and abrupt trajectories through multi-model trajectory diagnosis and used land-cover transition analysis and XGBoost-SHAP to examine abrupt-trajectory patterns and environmental associations. Negative change trajectories were slightly more prevalent, but abrupt trajectories comprised 65.06% of positive and 25.95% of negative change trajectories. Abrupt trajectories accounted for 12.72% of all trajectories, with positive and negative abrupt trajectories accounting for 8.40% and 4.32% of all trajectories, respectively. Positive abrupt trajectories were concentrated at mid-to-high elevations, whereas negative ones occurred patchily along the western and northern margins and around the Aral Sea. Deserts and grasslands had the highest proportions of positive abrupt trajectories; only in shrublands did negative abrupt trajectories outnumber positive ones. Desert-to-grassland transitions were associated with positive abrupt trajectories, whereas grassland-to-desert transitions were associated with negative abrupt trajectories. In the positive abrupt-shift model, trends in soil moisture and atmospheric CO₂ concentration ranked highest, whereas mean temperature and solar radiation ranked highest in the negative abrupt-shift model; SHAP interaction contributions also varied nonlinearly with environmental conditions, and Human Footprint had relatively low SHAP importance in both. These findings improve understanding of nonlinear vegetation dynamics and contrasting abrupt shifts in Central Asian drylands, providing regional information for vegetation monitoring and spatially differentiated management.

title: Asynchronous recovery of grassland ecosystem health in northern China: A three-dimensional assessment of structure, function, and environmental quality
abstract: Assessing ecosystem health under global change remains a central challenge in dryland ecology, as most existing approaches rely on single indices or aggregated metrics that obscure fundamental differences among ecosystem components. Here, we introduce a three-dimensional framework that explicitly separates grassland ecosystem health (GEH) into structural integrity, functional performance, and environmental quality, allowing us to diagnose not only overall trends but also hidden divergences among ecosystem dimensions. Applying this framework to the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China over the period 2000–2023, and combining long-term remote sensing data, ecosystem service modeling, and interpretable machine learning, we uncover a previously underappreciated pattern of ecosystem change. We show that GEH has improved overall, but through strongly asynchronous pathways: structural health and environmental quality increased consistently, whereas functional health exhibited a slight but persistent decline. This result challenges the common assumption that vegetation greening and environmental improvement reflect holistic ecosystem recovery. Instead, our findings demonstrate that ecosystem components respond at different rates and through distinct mechanisms, leading to a decoupling between structure, environment, and function. Precipitation emerged as the dominant driver, interacting nonlinearly with topography, and grazing intensity to regulate ecosystem responses. In particular, climate-driven gains in vegetation structure are partially offset by grazing pressure and soil constraints, which limit the recovery of ecosystem services. By explicitly revealing this multidimensional decoupling, our study advances ecosystem health assessment beyond conventional composite indices and identifies asynchronous recovery as a fundamental feature of dryland ecosystems under global change. Critically, this asynchronous decoupling creates a misleading signal of overall ecosystem stability while substantially lowering long-term grassland resilience against extreme drought and intensified human disturbance, generating hidden ecological vulnerability despite widespread vegetation greening. Our results highlight the need to move from structure-based restoration targets toward function-oriented management strategies. The proposed framework provides a transferable tool for diagnosing ecosystem condition and guiding adaptive management across dryland regions worldwide.

title: Mapping environmental disturbance around China's 5A tourist attractions using CatBoost
abstract: Tourism development generates environmental spillovers beyond attraction boundaries, yet their spatial extent remains difficult to identify because tourism-related signals are often confounded with natural background heterogeneity and other human activities. This study develops a framework for identifying environmental disturbance zones around tourist attractions that integrates an Environmental Disturbance Index (EDI), CatBoost-based baseline prediction, and four-neighbor connectivity analysis to map tourism-associated disturbance zones around 358 National 5A Tourist Attractions in China. The EDI combines landscape disturbance and environmental vulnerability dimensions. Using outer buffer zones (20–40 km) as reference areas, CatBoost models were trained to predict baseline EDI values for inner zones (0–20 km). Annual disturbance-detection thresholds were then defined using the one-sided 95th percentile of prediction residuals derived from the reference areas, and candidate anomalous grid cells spatially connected to attraction boundaries were retained according to the four-neighbor connectivity rule. The results show that environmental disturbance zones were identified around 96, 99, and 96 attractions in 2012, 2017, and 2022, respectively, with maximum disturbance distances of 9.01, 8.27, and 7.30 km. Correlation analyses further indicate that disturbance extent was associated with topographic conditions and road density. In both 2012 and 2017, slope and road density were significantly and positively correlated with disturbance area and maximum disturbance distance, whereas nighttime light intensity and population density did not exhibit consistently significant relationships with either disturbance area or distance across the three study years. Overall, this study provides a new methodological approach for identifying tourism-associated environmental disturbance and improves the spatial precision of large-scale disturbance delineation around tourism destinations.

title: Mapping intermittent river surface water in Arid and Semi-Arid China using Sentinel-2 and a novel seasonal intermittency index
abstract: Intermittent river surface water is a crucial feature in dryland river ecosystems, underpinning biodiversity, nutrient exchange, and hydrological connectivity, yet its spatiotemporal dynamics remain poorly quantified by existing ecological indicators. This study proposes a framework for mapping and quantifying the intermittency of river surface water across the Arid and Semi-Arid China (ASAC) using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2019 to 2024. A Spatial–Temporal Similarity Interpolation (STSI) method was developed to reconstruct a gap-filled monthly river surface water extent dataset at 10-m resolution by recovering observations obscured by cloud cover and topographic shadows, increasing detected river surface water extent by approximately 11% on average. Validation against PlanetScope imagery yielded an overall accuracy of 0.93 and an F1 score of 0.92. To characterize seasonal intermittency, we further developed a Seasonal Intermittency Index ( I s ), a spatially continuous ecological indicator that integrates water occurrence frequency with the seasonal intensity of water–non-water transitions. Using I s combined with water frequency, we found that intermittent river water bodies dominate the ASAC (89.3%), whereas perennial river surface water constitutes only 10.7%. Notably, 52.0% of the total river surface water area experienced interannual regime variability during 2019–2024, with transitions between seasonal and non-seasonal intermittent regimes (18.72%) occurring nearly three times more frequently than transitions between perennial and intermittent regimes (6.71%). These results indicate that hydrological change in the ASAC was primarily characterized by reorganization within intermittent regimes rather than expansion or contraction of perennial river surface water, with the semi-arid sub-region exhibiting the highest level of regime variability. As a spatially continuous, transferable indicator, I s enables consistent monitoring of non-perennial river dynamics and reveals substantial regime variability in dryland river systems, providing spatially explicit information to support ecological assessment, monitoring, and adaptive management.

title: Landscape ecological health assessment of coastal cities: a case study of Weihai
abstract: Landscape Ecological Health (LEH) assessment supports the coordination of ecological conservation, urban development, and resource use in rapidly changing coastal cities. However, existing studies often apply a uniform indicator system and weight vector across the entire study area. This approach does not adequately account for differences in the spatial applicability of terrestrial and marine indicators. Taking Weihai, China, as a case study, this study developed an integrated pressure–structure–process–function framework for citywide LEH assessment at eight observation dates from 1990 to 2025. A 23-indicator system, comprising 15 terrestrial indicators and 8 marine indicators, was established through qualitative screening and quantitative analysis. The marine indicators were applied within a 1.5 km landward coastal belt, whereas the terrestrial indicators were applied to the remaining area. The two domains shared a common normalization baseline but used separate domain-specific weight vectors, which are integrated to generate a continuous citywide LEH surface. The results indicate that: (1) Mean LEH increased from 0.3835 in 1990 to 0.4092 in 2025. The temporal pattern showed gradual improvement, a brief decline around 2010, and renewed growth after 2015. Over the same period, the proportion of the low-LEH class decreased from 59.19% to 45.28%, whereas that of the high-LEH class increased from 0.07% to 3.32%. (2) LEH exhibited persistent and significant positive spatial autocorrelation, with global Moran’s I remaining approximately 0.86–0.90. Higher-value areas gradually expanded in selected coastal sections and mountain–reservoir corridors. Lower-value areas remained concentrated in intensively used plains and urbanized belts. (3) Land use (q = 0.373) and elevation (q = 0.290) had the greatest single-factor explanatory power. Their interaction yielded the highest explanatory value (q = 0.47), indicating that human land use and topographic conditions jointly shaped the spatial differentiation of LEH. This study advances coastal-city LEH assessment from uniform citywide weighting to an explicit spatial integration rule, providing a transferable framework for long-term ecological monitoring and differentiated spatial management in coastal cities.

title: Divergent responses of cropland GPP and SIF to compound drought and heatwave across China's climatic zones
abstract: Compound drought and heatwave events (CDHWs) pose severe threats to cropland productivity. Yet, climatic zone-specific responses of cropland gross primary productivity (GPP) and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) to CDHWs remain unclear. This study utilized the machine learning framework coupled with SHAP analysis to reveal the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of CDHWs in China and quantify their impacts on GPP and SIF across different climatic zones. Results showed that moderate, severe, and extreme CDHWs increased significantly in frequency at rates of 0.263, 0.283, and 0.068 events per decade (p < 0.05), respectively, with corresponding increases in duration of 0.158, 0.159, and 0.147 days per decade from 1981 to 2024. Spatially, severe and extreme CDHWs were concentrated in the arid and semi-arid regions of Northwest China, northern North China, and Southwest China. In terms of cropland productivity responses, heatwave-only events increased GPP by 2.74% relative to normal conditions, while drought-only events reduced GPP by 7.10%. Interestingly, CDHWs induced the largest GPP reduction of 12.77%. SHAP analysis further identified relative humidity (RHum) as the dominant negative contributor to GPP under CDHW conditions. For SIF, it exhibited larger response magnitudes to extreme events, declining by 11.72% under drought-only conditions, rising by 73.83% under heatwave-only conditions, and remaining elevated by 61.10% under CDHWs. This elevation was primarily attributed to downward longwave radiation (LRad). Climatic zone-specific analysis demonstrated that LRad, temperature (Temp), and RHum were the three core factors influencing GPP. Notably, Prec exerted the weakest influence, ranging from 0.111 to 0.161. However, LRad was the dominant factor for SIF across all climatic zones, with minimal regional variability. Additionally, RHum contributed nearly as much as Temp to GPP in the BWk zone and ranked as the third-most-important driver of SIF in this region, highlighting the sensitivity of arid ecosystems to atmospheric moisture. This study elucidates the nonlinear impacts of CDHWs on cropland productivity and their climate zone-dependent mechanisms over China, providing critical scientific support for the development of national climate change adaptation strategies and the construction of climate-resilient agricultural systems.

title: Quantifying impacts of nutrient inputs on basal resources and carbon cycling in Arctic lake food webs
abstract: Climate change is altering carbon and nitrogen cycling in freshwater ecosystems, potentially generating ecosystem–climate feedback loops. In the Arctic, warming promotes tundra greening and herbivore expansion. Herbivores supply nitrogen-rich inputs to lakes, modifying basal resource quality, potentially affecting their consumption, carbon transfer within food webs and lake carbon sink capacity. We assessed nine lakes in Svalbard using a space-for-time substitution to evaluate how climate-driven increase in migratory geese affects nutrient enrichment, resource quality, consumer trophic niches, and carbon transfer in lake food webs. Stable isotope analyses and Bayesian mixing models revealed that goose-derived inputs contributed up to 22% of sediment organic matter and increased nitrogen in sediments and vegetation. Improved resource quality drove a dietary shift in the abundant tadpole shrimp Lepidurus arcticus from carnivory in nitrogen-poor lakes to herbivory–detritivory in enriched lakes. Consequently, carbon extraction from basal resources, which act as long-term storage pools, rose from 2.62 ± 0.25 to 1054.93 ± 152.73 mgCm −2 during summer. Isotopic patterns in aquatic vegetation, the contribution of excreta to sediment organic matter, and the trophic response of L. arcticus served as effective ecological indicators of herbivore-mediated organic enrichment and its impact on carbon retention. Our findings suggest that managing migratory birds in the Northern Hemisphere has significant consequences for food webs and carbon cycling in high-latitude freshwater ecosystems, with potential consequences for their carbon sink capacity. Stable isotopes and mixing models applied to sediments and key food-web components could detect causes of organic enrichment and its effects on carbon cycling across diverse lentic ecosystems.

title: Evolution of water-footprint supply-chain sustainability across climate, supply-chain, and socioeconomic scenarios
abstract: Influenced by the combined effects of climate change, socioeconomic factors, and supply-chain management, the evolution of the water-footprint (WF) supply-chain exhibited highly complexity and uncertainty. From the perspective of meta-coupling and Nexus thinking, this study innovatively constructed a comprehensive scenario framework integrating climate change background, supply-chain orientation, and socioeconomic behavior, namely the Background-Orientation-Behavior (BOB) framework. Using a system dynamics model, the study simulated the dynamic evolution of WF supply-chain at the regional departmental scale under six future scenarios from 2000 to 2050. It further conducted a comprehensive evaluation of the WF supply-chain across different scenarios, focusing on efficiency, stability, resilience, and sustainability. By combining the Shapley value decomposition method, the study quantified the sustainability differences in the WF supply-chain and their driving factors across scenarios, thereby enhancing the explanatory power for the complex mechanisms underlying regional sustainable water resource management. The results showed that: (1) The total WF of Heilongjiang Province exhibited scenario-specific characteristics. Except under the climate islands scenario, the total WF showed a declining trend in all other scenarios, with the most significant reductions observed under the sustainability-driven transition and technological leapfrogging scenarios, where it decreased to approximately 473.3 × 10 9 m 3 and 453.1 × 10 9 m 3 , respectively. Agricultural WF demonstrated strong path dependence and uncertainty, whereas the trend in the industrial sector was relatively clear. (2) The sustainability evolution of the WF supply-chain differed significantly across scenarios, with the sustainability-driven transition, technological leapfrogging, and civic awakening scenarios generally performing better. Specifically, the technological leapfrogging scenario improved efficiency as well as environmental and economic sustainability, but it often did so at the expense of resilience. In contrast, the civic awakening scenario was more conducive to enhancing stability and social sustainability. (3) Attribution analysis indicates that, within the scenario framework of this study, socioeconomic behavior contributes the largest share to scenario-based differences in the comprehensive sustainability of the WF supply-chain, followed by supply-chain orientation, while the direct contribution of the climate change context is relatively small. This study expanded research on regional sustainable water resource management from the perspective of the WF supply-chain and provided a new analytical framework for collaborative water governance under complex scenarios.

title: Projecting the impacts of climate change on Chinese wetlands using Phragmites australis as an indicator
abstract: Wetlands are climate-sensitive ecosystems, yet the future distribution patterns of wetland plants across China under different climate scenarios remain poorly understood, hindering the development of proactive conservation and restoration strategies. In this study, we address this gap by using the widely distributed foundational species Phragmites australis as an indicator to project climate-driven shifts in wetland ecosystems. This study employed 627 occurrence records of P. australis alongside 18 environmental variables covering climate, topography, soil, land use, and human footprint. Using the ENMeval package, we optimized a MaxEnt model to project the species' potential distribution under current conditions and across three future periods (2050s, 2070s, 2090s) under the SSP126, SSP370, and SSP585 scenarios. The objectives were to determine the key environmental drivers of its distribution and to evaluate associated spatial restructuring risks for China's wetland ecosystems in a changing climate. The results show that the MaxEnt model with a regularization multiplier (RM) of 3 and a feature combination (FC) of LQPHT performed with high consistency and accuracy. The dominant environmental factors and their thresholds were: human footprint ≥14.31, elevation ≤2256.88 m, temperature annual range (bio7) ≥ 17.25 °C, mean temperature of warmest quarter (bio10) ≥ 13.75 °C, and mean diurnal temperature range (bio2) ≤ 14.11 °C. The most suitable land use types included paddy fields, dry farmland, other forest land, rivers and canals, lakes, reservoirs and ponds, urban land, rural settlements, other construction land, and saline-alkali land. Under current climatic conditions, suitable distribution for P. australis in China is mainly distributed across North China, Northeast China, Northwest China, and South China. The areas of high and low-suitability distribution is 139.93 × 10 4 km 2 and 380.78 × 10 4 km 2 , respectively. Under future climate scenarios, both high- and low-suitability distribution is projected to decrease to varying degrees, with increased fragmentation. The suitable distribution centroids are expected to shift northwestward. The findings of this study provide a quantitative scientific basis for implementing climate-adaptive wetland conservation and restoration strategies, particularly for optimizing the national ecological conservation spatial layout and establishing early-warning mechanisms.

title: Development of a marine environmental baseline database with enhanced spatiotemporal completeness: a case study of the Bohai Sea, China
abstract: Long-term marine environmental assessment requires baseline data with consistent spatiotemporal coverage; yet, inadequate standardization and integration of monitoring data often hinder oceanographic assessment and management. This study developed a gap-filling framework based on spatiotemporal distribution baseline paradigms and a baseline database for dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) and phosphate (PO 4 -P) in the Bohai Sea (BS), China's only semi-enclosed inland sea. Multi-source raw data from 1982 to 2023 were standardized and assessed using station coverage (SC), granularity of station distribution (GS), and seasonal balance (SB). Datasets classified as mid-high quality or higher were used to identify spatial, seasonal, and interannual distribution paradigms. Incomplete data were matched to suitable paradigms using a back-propagation neural network (BPNN), adjusted with available raw data, gap-filled, and integrated into a database. DIN and PO 4 -P data were highly uneven spatially and temporally, and only 25.17% and 23.13% of the datasets were suitable for paradigm identification. The 0.1° × 0.1° grid scheme provided the best balance between spatial consistency and numerical deviation. The BPNN-based method outperformed reference methods, with mean root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 0.25 and 0.07 μmol/L for DIN and PO 4 -P, respectively. Gap-filling increased spatial and seasonal completeness by 41% and 52%, respectively, and interannual reconstruction achieved an RMSE of 0.032. The reconstructed baseline data provide a consistent basis for describing nutrient patterns and may support eutrophication assessment in the BS. Their application to other environmental parameters or coastal seas requires further testing.

title: Integrating the actual benefits of ecosystem services to assess ecosystem health and its drivers in the Sichuan-Yunnan ecological barrier zone
abstract: The synergistic supply of ecosystem services (ESs) is crucial for maintaining regional ecosystem health (EH) and achieving sustainable development goals. However, traditional EH assessments, when considering the potential supply of ESs, overlook the actual benefits generated by trade-offs among them, thereby failing to reveal the actual ecological conditions. Thus, taking the Sichuan-Yunnan ecological barrier zone (SYEBZ) as a case study, this study integrated ecosystem integrity and ESs benefits to evaluate the spatiotemporal dynamic of EH from 2000 to 2025, then employed multiple spatial analysis models to identify the dominant factors, interactions and regional variations affecting EH from both global and local perspectives. We found that (1) this improved method better reflects the actual state of EH under human disturbance compared to traditional methods. (2) The EH level showed a trend of first decreasing and then increasing during 2000–2025, with ecological degradation primarily occurring in Chengdu city and its surrounding areas. (3) Socioeconomic factors (i.e., POP and GDP) as the dominant influence on regional EH, followed by topography, while other natural factors primarily exert their effects through regulating ecological baselines and carrying capacity. (4) The impact of dominant factors on EH exhibited spatial heterogeneity, for which differentiated ecological management strategies have been formulated. The research findings can provide practical guidance for the ecosystem management and healthy development of SYEBZ.

title: Nonlinear impacts and threshold effects of 2D and 3D morphology on ecological resilience across urban functional zones: A case study of Shanghai, China
abstract: Ecological resilience is a key element for urban sustainable development. Understanding spatial morphology's impact mechanism on ecological resilience can help improve ecological resilience under spatial resource constraints. However, existing research lacks systematic exploration of how 2D and 3D morphology affect ecological resilience across different functional zones of megacities. Based on “Tolerance–Absorption–Restoration” framework, this study built an Ecological Resilience Index (ERI) model and taking Shanghai as a case, used Random Forest model and SHAP algorithm for uncovering nonlinear influence and threshold characteristics of 2D and 3D morphology on ecological resilience across functional zones. Results showed that: (1) ERI model can effectively assess ecological resilience across functional zones using multi-source, high-resolution remote sensing data; (2) Ecological resilience in Shanghai presents a “low center, high periphery” pattern. Public service zones exhibit the highest ecological resilience while commercial zones exhibit the lowest, corresponding to spatial distribution gradients of buildings and greenspaces; (3) 2D building morphological indicators exert dominant influence on ecological resilience, while influences of 3D morphology and 2D greenspace morphology exhibit notable scale dependence and regional sensitivity, respectively. Indicators' influences generally show a hierarchy of coverage > cohesion > shape complexity; (4) Morphological impacts exhibit threshold characteristics across functional zones: Zones with higher development intensity show higher thresholds for negative indicators and lower ones for positive indicators. These findings provide quantitative evidence and planning references for differentiated management and ecological resilience improvement across urban functional zones.

title: Overestimated temperature sensitivity in future net primary productivity projections
abstract: Terrestrial net primary productivity (NPP) is a fundamental indicator of ecosystem functioning and carbon sequestration capacity, playing a crucial role in regulating the strength of the land carbon sink. Earth system models (ESMs) are the primary tools for simulating historical NPP variations and projecting future changes. However, NPP projections by ESMs remain subject to substantial uncertainty and bias due to differences in model structure and parameterization. Here, we develop an observation-constrained transfer learning framework that integrates 21 CMIP6 ESMs with satellite-derived NPP to reduce structural biases and constrain future projections. The results indicate that the framework effectively reduces the mean absolute historical bias between ESM simulations and satellite-derived observations by 75.7%. Raw ESM projections show increases in global NPP of 85.88 ± 41.90 and 121.83 ± 67.09 gC m −2 yr −1 under SSP245 and SSP585, respectively. In contrast, observation-constrained projections reduce these increases to 55.23 ± 9.59 and 89.51 ± 18.46 gC m −2 yr −1 , while narrowing the 5th–95th percentile uncertainty range by 78%–82%. Factorial attribution shows that temperature dominates the projected NPP trend among the climatic drivers considered, while precipitation and interaction effects are comparatively small. Temperature-sensitivity analyses further indicate stronger NPP responses to warming in unconstrained ESMs, particularly in tropical regions, whereas observational constraints moderate these responses and lead to lower future NPP projections. Overall, our results suggest that the stronger temperature sensitivity identified in unconstrained ESMs is associated with larger projected increases in terrestrial NPP.

title: Corrigendum to “A WEE-RDH framework for resilience assessment of the water-ecology-economy system in the Tarim River basin” [Ecol. Indic. 191 (2026) 115476]
Spatial heterogeneity of nitrogen-enriched sediment microbial communities and their environmental drivers in shallow eutrophic Honghu Lake, China
abstract: Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of sediment microbial communities and their potential environmental drivers is crucial for effectively managing eutrophication in the shallow Honghu Lake. Overall, the entire lake was classified as moderately eutrophic (mean TLIΣ = 64.17) with nitrogen-enriched in sediment (Severe Pollution, mean S TN = 4.87). Regionally, sediment microbial communities and some environmental factors exhibited spatial heterogeneity. Specifically, sedimentary manganese (S Mn) in the North Lake District (NLD) was 74.65% and 95.44% higher than in West (WLD) and East (ELD) Lake Districts; conversely, sediment total nitrogen (S-TN) in the NLD was 45.66% and 41.98% lower than that in WLD and ELD; the NLD recorded the lowest trophic state, characterized by the highest Secchi depth (SD), the lowest chemical oxygen demand (COD Mn ), relatively higher water total nitrogen (W-TN) and phosphorus (W-TP), and the lowest chlorophyll a (Chl.a). Sediment microbial diversity followed the trend: NLD > WLD > ELD, with NLD communities being structurally distinct from the similar WLD/ELD groups. Redundancy analysis (RDA) and Mantel tests identified S Mn, SD and S-TN as the primary drivers shaping these spatial variations, with S Mn and SD positively correlated to the NLD communities and S-TN positively correlated to the WLD/ELD communities. Functional microorganisms also exhibited spatial heterogeneity with NLD group was enriched with C/N-cycling taxa whereas WLD/ELD groups were enriched in C/S-cycling taxa. These findings elucidate the divergent roles of heavy metals and nutrients in shaping microbial niches, providing valuable insights into the biogeochemical cycling and ecological health of shallow lakes.

title: All that glitters is not gold: genetic and post-mortem monitoring indicate dispersal risks for a semi-aquatic apex predator in a protected marshland
abstract: Protected areas are expected to provide suitable habitats for wildlife even within human-altered landscapes, but environmental cues can be misleading. We evaluated whether a strictly protected, rehabilitated marshland (Kis-Balaton, KB) acts as an ecological trap for the Eurasian otter ( Lutra lutra ), a sentinel apex predator. Using non-invasive genetic sampling within the marshland (90 individuals) and nationwide post-mortem monitoring (462 individuals), we found a spatially heterogeneous population, with a genetically insulated peripheral group. Kinship and group sex ratios indicated kin-structured residents, among which frequent attack-related injuries were consistent with strong territorial behaviour. Net gene flow was directed towards the marshland's core area, mainly via the Zala River. However, immigrants were mainly detected in peripheral areas near settlements and roads, where recovered carcasses showed a higher prevalence of attack-related injuries (KB: 35.7%, other regions: 13.1%), and body condition was poorer in injured than in uninjured otters. These patterns indicate that immigrants rarely integrate into the resident population. The core population remains demographically viable, so the marshland is not a classical ecological trap but a dead-end for dispersers rather than a true refuge. Failure of immigrants to establish, despite apparent habitat connectivity, suggests intrinsic constraints that may be set by the area's ecological carrying capacity. We recommend restoring habitat connectivity, improving legal protection and suitability of small watercourses, and implementing road mitigation and free-ranging dog control to reduce mortality risks. These actions are crucial for gene flow and long-term otter population viability in wetland ecosystems.

title: Divergent climate–phenology–carbon mechanisms in deciduous needleleaf and broadleaf forests across the northern hemisphere
abstract: Global climate is shifting the phenological rhythms of deciduous forests, yet how phenology affects subsequent carbon sequestration, and whether these dynamics vary by leaf functional type, remains unclear. Using satellite records, we investigated the spatial-temporal variations in the start of the growing season (SOS) and net primary productivity (NPP), along with their responses to climate variations across the Northern Hemisphere, and further the differences in their relationships between deciduous needleleaf forests (DNF) and deciduous broadleaf forests (DBF). From 2001 to 2021, DNF advanced its SOS 3.8 times faster than DBF (−0.34 vs. −0.09 d·yr −1 ), but this pattern largely reflects the concentration of DNF in rapidly warming high-latitude regions. After controlling for spatial and climatic background, the intrinsic SOS advancement was stronger in DBF (LMM coefficient: −0.605). DBF and DNF showed comparable and significant NPP increases (2.28 and 2.17 g C·m −2 ·yr −1 , respectively). These similar productivity gains were achieved through fundamentally different pathways: In DBF, NPP was decoupled from SOS and driven directly by current and prior-year precipitation increases. In DNF, earlier SOS and increased precipitation were jointly associated with productivity. Specifically, prior-year and winter precipitation can influence the SOS of DNF; increased winter precipitation was associated with DNF NPP directly through its influence on physiological performance and indirectly by mediating spring leaf-out. With each day of advancement yielding ∼3.505 g C·m −2 of additional NPP (non-standardized coefficient), ∼45.3% of winter precipitation's effects on NPP were mediated through this phenological pathway. Interestingly, spring temperature was the common SOS driver for both DNF and DBF, but legacy precipitation effects uniquely amplified DNF's phenological sensitivity. These results highlight a fundamental divergence in climate–phenology–carbon sequestration potential coupling between leaf forms, underscoring the need for leaf-form-specific approaches in carbon sink projections under future climate scenarios.

title: Ecosystem stability trajectories identify mangrove conservation priorities in China
abstract: Assessing mangrove ecosystem stability across space and time remains challenging due to the multidimensional nature of ecological structure and function and the lack of integrative indicators. Here, we developed a Mangrove Ecosystem Stability Index (MESI) based on multiple remote sensing indicators to quantify the spatiotemporal dynamics of mangroves across China from 2000 to 2021. During this period, mangrove forests expanded by 38.5%, largely through the conversion of aquaculture ponds and water bodies under active restoration programs, while the mean MESI increased from 0.49 to 0.55. Bayesian models revealed scale-dependent drivers of stability, with soil organic carbon dominating at the national scale and urbanization intensity and population density shaping patterns at provincial and reserve scales. Spatiotemporal trajectory analysis showed that over 55% of China's mangroves remained stable, with positive changes (23%) slightly exceeding declines (22%). Integrating stability trajectories with spatial prioritization identified 32% of mangroves outside current reserves as high-priority conservation areas, particularly in Guangxi, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area, and Hainan. These findings provide a scalable framework for linking ecosystem stability assessment with conservation planning to support adaptive mangrove management under increasing climatic and anthropogenic pressures.

title: Interpretable machine learning reveals environmental controls on carbon-water flux dynamics in a humid subtropical evergreen forest
abstract: Carbon-water coupling in humid subtropical forests is shaped by monsoon variability, yet coordinated changes in carbon uptake, respiration, and water loss remain unclear. We analyzed daily eddy-covariance and meteorological observations across six growing seasons (2020–2025) at Xin'anjiang, Southeast China, including net ecosystem exchange (NEE), gross primary productivity (GPP), ecosystem respiration (R eco ), evapotranspiration (ET), and water-use efficiency (WUE). To distinguish predictive contributions, nonlinear model responses, and covariate-adjusted associations under correlated predictors, we combined nested leave-one-growing-season-out XGBoost with SHAP, ALE, and EconML and paired gap-filled/non-gap-filled analyses. The forest remained a net carbon sink, but indicators varied asynchronously. During DOY 160–190, clustered rainfall and high humidity coincided with lower radiation; reduced GPP and net carbon uptake, comparatively high ET, and the seasonal WUE minimum. Interannually, NEE reflected the balance between GPP and R eco , whereas WUE depended on relative changes in GPP and total ET. Out-of-year R 2 ranged from 0.66 to 0.82, and the schemes shared 70–90% of their Top-10 predictors. Current atmospheric-energy conditions dominated NEE, GPP, and ET predictions; R eco was associated with temperature and antecedent moisture, whereas WUE retained information from atmospheric pressure and soil moisture. Nonlinear responses were clearest for radiation, temperature, and atmospheric pressure, while pairwise interactions were generally weak and covariate-adjusted associations were consistent across schemes. Together, monsoon-related carbon-water variation reflected immediate atmospheric-energy variability conditioned by slower hydrological memory. Although site-specific quantitative results require multi-site evaluation, this multi-flux framework may inform carbon-water-coupling studies in other monsoon-affected forests.

title: Spatio-temporal monitoring of agricultural drought in China based on downscaled soil moisture data
abstract: Abstract. Agricultural drought threatens China's food and ecological security, and accurate spatio-temporal monitoring is key for disaster mitigation. Soil moisture is critical for drought assessment, but the accuracy of existing remote sensing-based SM products in China remains to be improved. This study develops a framework that synergistically integrates a spatiotemporally adaptive gap-filling algorithm with a machine learning-based downscaling approach, generating a seamless 0.05° monthly SM dataset for China from 2003 to 2023. The methodology harnesses the complementary strengths of random forest modeling and spatiotemporal reconstruction techniques to effectively fuse multi-source satellite observations, achieving dual improvements in SM data accuracy and spatial coverage. Using this dataset, the standardized soil moisture index was applied to characterize the spatio-temporal evolution of agricultural drought. Results demonstrate that (1) The downscaled SM dataset achieves significant improvements in both spatial resolution and accuracy, showing a 2.3–34.4 % reduction in ubRMSE and 1.2–52.7 % improvement in correlation coefficients compared to benchmark datasets. (2) Drought characterization based on the downscaled SM dataset and SSI accurately identified the extent of agricultural drought, showing a significant spatiotemporal consistency with agricultural disaster area. (3) Agricultural drought intensified significantly across China during the study period, characterized by northward migration of drought center and spatially heterogeneous aridification patterns – decreasing severity from northwest to southeast while increasing from northeast to southwest. High-frequency drought zones were predominantly clustered in ecologically vulnerable regions, particularly the agro-pastoral ecotone of northern China. (4) Distinct intra-annual drought dynamics emerged, with a southwest-to-northeast expansion dominating from January to June, followed by bidirectional propagation from the Yellow River-Huaihe River Basin (YRB-HRB) to northwestern and southeastern regions from June to December. This study provides high-accuracy data support for agricultural drought monitoring and offers scientific insights for developing regional differentiated drought mitigation strategies, which are of great significance for ensuring national food security.

title: Food-web reorganization in an artificial reef revealed by flow-based indicators
abstract: Artificial-reef assessments often rely on abundance and biomass, but whether reef-associated differences extend to trophic pathways requires process-oriented indicators. We tested whether 2023 reef-control differences at Xiaoheishan were accompanied by coherent changes in community structure, trophic-resource use and Ecopath flows, and evaluated the Benthic Coupling Index (BCI) and Reef Fish Support Index (RFSI). Three reef and three adjacent control stations were sampled in March, June, August and November and integrated to characterize the annual ecological state. Reef-control differences in abundance and biomass reversed among seasons, whereas the reef area contained more small and intermediate consumers and higher biomass of reef-associated fishes. The sample-size-corrected standard ellipse area (SEAc) point estimate was larger in the reef assemblage (13.54 vs. 8.83 ‰ 2 ), although the 95% interval for the difference included zero; basal-resource profiles remained highly similar. The reef Ecopath model combined higher total living biomass and stronger benthic-detrital routing with lower total system throughput. BCI increased from 0.229 to 0.451 and retained separation under ±20% directional perturbation; RFSI increased from 0.544 to 0.595 but overlapped under ±10%, identifying reef-fish diet allocation as a key source of sensitivity. These results support local food-web reorganization within the reef-control system and show that matched Ecopath flow matrices can be summarized by two indicators with different sensitivities. Cross-system and interannual validation are needed before either index is used as a general management threshold; regional production and spillover were not evaluated.

title: Multiscenario simulation of LUCC and landscape ecological risk in the Tarim River basin based on the intPLUS model
abstract: Land use and cover change (LUCC) is a primary driving force that shapes the spatiotemporal patterns of landscape ecological risk (LER), particularly in ecologically fragile arid regions. We investigated the Tarim River Basin, the largest endorheic basin and a critical ecological security zone in arid northwestern China, with the aim to address the lack of quantitative evidence on how future policy pathways will reshape the LER. LUCC and LER changes were simulated under four 2035 scenarios: business-as-usual (BAU), prioritizing urban development (PUD), prioritizing ecological protection (PEP), and balanced urban–rural development (BUE). By coupling historical LUCC data (2010−2020) with the intPLUS model, we developed a spatially explicit framework integrating LUCC simulation with landscape ecological risk assessment. (1) After calibration against the observed 2020 pattern, the intPLUS model reproduced the 2020 land use at the 1-km scale (kappa = 0.941; OA = 0.972; FOM = 0.184), supporting its use for subsequent multiscenario forecasting. (2) From 2010 to 2020, cropland and developed land expanded by 10,694 and 1536 km 2 , respectively, whereas grassland decreased by 16,440 km 2 , increasing the mean LER from 0.031 to 0.034, with high-risk areas expanding by 28,283 km 2 . (3) By 2035, compared with the BAU scenario, the PEP, PUD, and BUE scenarios reduced high-risk areas by 1.16%, 1.24%, and 1.27%, respectively. Higher-risk areas were most policy-sensitive. Notably, under the selected scenario settings, the balanced urban–rural development scenario (BUE) compressed the high-risk core slightly more than the other intervention scenarios, whereas the prioritizing ecological protection (PEP) scenario produced a smaller reduction than the prioritizing urban development (PUD) scenario; these scenario-conditional comparisons indicate that the ranking of outcomes is not simply ordered by protection intensity. (4) LISA revealed a robust desert hotspot ring versus mountain cold-spot core structure ( p < 0.001), with policy interventions providing gradient buffering only in transition zones.

title: What drives the uphill expansion of cultivated land in hilly regions? Nonlinear responses and threshold effects from the Jiangnan hilly region, China
abstract: Amid the severe challenges to global food security and sustainable development, changes in cultivated land resources have become a key issue in global development research. However, in the context of rapid urbanization, high-quality cultivated land in hilly regions continues to be lost, forcing agricultural activities onto marginal lands. This has led to the phenomenon of uphill expansion of cultivated land, which affects both agricultural sustainability and ecological security. This research characterizes the spatiotemporal evolution of cultivated land expansion in the Jiangnan hilly region of China, revealing a shift from low-gradient areas to increasing encroachment into medium- and high-gradient regions. The results show that while cultivated land continues to expand into higher slopes, the process slows significantly beyond a 10° slope due to topographic limitations. To explore the underlying driving mechanisms, a Geographically Weighted Random Forest model is employed to examine the spatial heterogeneity of these driving factors. The findings indicate that net income per farmer is the primary driver, reflecting the dominant role of farmers' economic decisions. Additionally, built-up land expansion area exerts a spatial compression effect, driving cultivated land into steeper areas. Ultimately, the uphill expansion of cultivated land is a nonlinear response to socio-economic pressures exceeding the region's ecological carrying capacity. This study provides policy implications for hilly regions, suggesting the integration of slope-based ecological constraints within the “land occupation–compensation balance” framework to promote sustainable land use.

title: An ecological Indicator framework for conservation status assessment: promoting the sustainability of natural remnant habitats in the Montado agroecosystem
abstract: Natural Remnant Habitats (NRHs) are native natural landscape elements that persist within agroecosystem landscapes and provide ecosystem goods and services, contributing significantly to landscape heterogeneity and high biodiversity. However, these habitats patches are increasingly threatened by both agricultural intensification and land abandonment, making the characterization and assessment of their Conservation Status (CS) essential to their effective conservation. With this study we aimed to develop a field-based, multi-criteria ecological indicator framework for the practical assessment of the CS of NRHs within the Montado, a High Nature Value agroecosystem. We conducted fieldwork in Alentejo (Portugal) over three spring seasons where we sampled 226 NRHs, representing six NRH types—Forest and Shrub Patches, Rocky Outcrops, Riparian Galleries, Temporary and Permanent Ponds. We recorded several biophysical parameters based on their expected relevance as potential CS indicators. We used two complementary CS assessments approaches — expert-based and field indicator-based—to identify NRH patches with excellent CS and to select indicators that effectively discriminate among groups distributed along a continuum of CS conditions. We then compared these approaches to validate the framework. Our results show that CS assessment varies strongly among NRH types, and that no universal set of indicators is suitable. Although the proposed framework still requires further refinement, it provides a practical tool for translating ecological complexity into an operational CS assessment based on NRH-specific and easily observable field indicators, thus reducing the need for specialized expertise. It enables clear discrimination between the most contrasting CS (excellent vs poor) and supports evidence-based conservation, land management, and policy development in Mediterranean farming landscapes.

title: Carbon balance zoning-informed multi-objective water allocation under the water-carbon nexus in economically developed regions
abstract: Focusing on water supply-demand and carbon balance challenges in economically developed regions, this study develops a systematic framework of “carbon balance analysis→ water demand prediction→ water-carbon nexus→ multi-objective optimization→ scheme evaluation”. The InVEST model estimates carbon sink capacity and identifies regions with severe carbon imbalance (Suzhou, Wuxi, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Nanjing) based on carbon supply-demand ratios. Current development and low-carbon scenarios are set considering population, urbanization, and industrial structure. A multi-objective optimization model is constructed to minimize water deficit and carbon emissions, solved by NSGA-II. An entropy weight-TOPSIS method integrated with carbon zoning results is applied for scheme screening. Results show: (1) Carbon sinks exhibited a “high north, low south” pattern with declining totals from 2005 to 2020, while emissions concentrated in the south and nearly doubled. (2) Under 2030 P = 75% inflow frequency, water shortages occur under both scenarios; however, the low-carbon scenario significantly improves the shortage rate from 13.90% to 6.07%. (3) Carbon emissions are reduced by 13.02 Mt. and 11.17 Mt. under 50% and 75% frequencies, with the five imbalanced regions contributing 56.85% and 62.37% of total reductions under low-carbon scenario. The five carbon-deficit regions serve as the primary contributors to these reductions, highlighting the spatial effectiveness of low-carbon water allocation. This study reveals water-carbon synergistic regulation patterns and provides quantitative decision support for sustainable water management under the “dual carbon” goals.

title: Infrequent, high-volume rainfall events modulate acorn production for two common oak species in Western North Carolina, USA
abstract: Variations in landscape-scale acorn production have been studied across the Quercus genera to understand its role in ecosystem ecology and forest regeneration. Multiple weather conditions may influence annual acorn crops, especially the positive influence of seasonal rainfall. Prior studies have assessed the effects of rainfall measured over monthly and seasonal scales, but have not focused on the potential influence of daily rainfall events (e.g., frequency and intensity) on acorn production. Here, we examined 19 years of daily rainfall data with annual acorn data collected from Quercus montana and Quercus alba at the Bent Creek Experimental Forest, North Carolina, USA to understand how daily rainfall modulates acorn production. We organized daily rainfall data into three percentile thresholds (50th, 90th, and 99th) and examined how well linear models were able to explain variations in mean annual acorn production with and without high-volume daily rainfall (i.e., the most intense rainfall days). We discovered model strength remained strong, and sometimes improved, when removing the frequent, low-volume rain events, and daily rainfall at or above the 90th percentile (21.9 mm/day) was crucial for establishing statistical relationships with annual acorn production. Our results indicate the importance for intense daily rainfall events to explain precipitation-acorn production relationships for two common oak species in North Carolina. Further, our results provide insights into the importance of daily high-volume rainfall for large acorn crops, which could have implications under future climate change.

title: Threshold responses of land surface temperature to local moisture recycling in a mountain-lake-forest composite system
abstract: Quantifying water-heat coupling in mountain-lake-forest composite systems is important for alleviating surface heat stress in low-latitude mountain tourist cities, yet existing indicators fail to resolve nonlinear threshold transitions between local recycled water vapor contribution ratio( f local ) and land surface temperature(LST). This study proposes a threshold-based indicator approach by integrating stable isotope end-member analysis with multi-scale land surface temperature remote sensing, and applies it to three subsystems (mountain forest-grassland, basin composite, and lake-water) in the Erhai Basin. The Erhai Basin is dominated by advected water vapor in the rainy season(57.90%) and local recycled moisture in the dry season(61.10%). Distinct thermal response regimes emerge across the three subsystems. The mountain forest-grassland system shows significant negative correlations when f local < 30% in the rainy season and < 45% in the dry season; the basin composite system switches from positive to negative correlation at approximately 50% in the rainy season and exhibits strong negative correlation in the dry season; and in the lake water system, advection water vapor masks the local evaporation cooling signal during the rainy season, while sustained lake-surface evaporation maintains stable heat-sink functionality during the dry season. These divergent thresholds reflect differential synergies between surface evaporation and sub-cloud secondary evaporation across ecosystems. This demonstrates that peripheral lake-forest composite ecosystems can effectively alleviate regional surface heat through local moisture recycling and latent heat exchange, offering a nature-based pathway for thermal management in such composite systems, in which subsystem thresholds provide quantitative evidence for heat mitigation strategies.

title: Typical thermokarst alters soil organic carbon fractions controlled by soil water content in the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau
abstract: The ongoing climate warming has accelerated permafrost thaw worldwide, resulting in rapid thermokarst development. However, a comprehensive quantification of the responses of soil organic carbon (SOC) fractions to thermokarst development is still lacking. This study evaluated the changes in SOC fraction concentrations in typical thermokarst landscapes. The results showed that thaw slumps, thermo-erosion gullies, and mature thermokarst lakes exhibited a drastic decrease in SOC concentration, whereas the single-site observation of developing thermokarst lake exhibited an increase of 23.47%. Particulate organic carbon (POC), rather than mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC), dominated the SOC changes. POC decreased significantly from control stage to drape (of thaw slumps) / collapsing (of thermo-erosion gullies) / mid-lakeside (of mature thermokarst lakes) stages. Mature thermokarst lakes featured the reductions in POC from control stage (57.04 g/kg) to near-lakeside stage (33.72 g/kg), with a drastic decrease occurring in the mid-lakeside stage (30.91%). The developing thermokarst lake site exhibited a continuous increase in POC concentrations. Basic soil properties and microbial properties played dominant roles in explaining SOC variance during thermokarst development. Soil water content (SWC) was the most important factor controlling SOC concentrations in all thermokarst landscapes. SOC variations of thaw slumps might be positively correlated with precipitation, whereas those of thermo-erosion gullies might be negatively correlated with elevation. Path analysis confirmed that SWC controlled the dynamics of SOC through both direct (via organic matter transport) and indirect (microbially mediated) pathways. The preliminary order-of-magnitude estimate suggests a cumulative loss in SOC stock of up to 6.30 Tg C by 2100 due to the future expansion in thermokarst landscapes under climate change. This study provided new insights into potential dynamics of permafrost‑carbon feedbacks.

title: Toward equitable green welfare: Integrating biodiversity and accessibility in the development of urban green space networks
abstract: Existing studies on urban green space (UGS) network development have focused on identifying potential corridors, with their spatial extent frequently defined through subjective assessments, while human needs have rarely been considered. This study developed a framework for constructing UGS networks that delineates corridor spatial extent and leverages the synergy between ecological and accessible aspects. The proposed framework was applied to develop a UGS network in Suwon City, South Korea. Corridor spatial extent was identified through a weighted overlay analysis considering the quality of current corridors in terms of biodiversity and UGS provision. Forty-four pinch points and eight barrier points were determined representing strategic points for conservation and restoration, respectively. Spatial characteristic analysis revealed that residential, roadside greening and arable land were the primary UGS types with restoration potential. The proposed method provides a new approach to UGS network development by integrating the accessible aspect with spatial guidance for corridor implementation, helping cities achieve both biodiversity conservation and equitable UGS distribution.

title: Interpretable metaheuristic-optimized machine learning for predicting biodiversity indices in the Hyrcanian forest
abstract: Operational biodiversity indicators are essential for tracking ecological change and evaluating forest management effectiveness. However, predicting multiple biodiversity indices remains challenging because their associations with environmental and stand-structural conditions are nonlinear, context-dependent, and index-specific. We developed an interpretable machine learning framework that integrates metaheuristic optimization, multi-index biodiversity assessment, and model-based ecological interpretation using data from 811 national forest inventory plots across the Hyrcanian forest of northern Iran. Species richness, Shannon–Wiener diversity, Gini–Simpson diversity, inverse Simpson diversity, and Pielou's evenness were derived from tree-level species composition, with basal-area proportions used where appropriate for the abundance-based indices. Topographic, stand structural, edaphic, and bioclimatic variables were used as predictors. Random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbors (kNN) were independently optimized for each biodiversity index using four population-based metaheuristic algorithms to select model-specific hyperparameters by minimizing validation RMSE; final model performance was evaluated on held-out test data using R 2 , RMSE, and MAE. Predictive performance differed substantially among biodiversity indices: optimized SVM performed best for Shannon–Wiener, Gini–Simpson, and inverse Simpson diversity, with test R 2 values of 0.7408, 0.8472, and 0.7387, respectively, whereas RF achieved the highest test R 2 for species richness and Pielou's evenness, with values of 0.4125 and 0.2670, respectively. Thus, abundance-weighted diversity indices were considerably more predictable than richness and evenness, highlighting the need for index-specific predictive models rather than a single universal modeling approach. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), partial dependence, and interaction analyses consistently identified elevation as the dominant predictor across biodiversity indices, whereas diameter at breast height, basal area, and slope showed distinct nonlinear response patterns. By combining index-specific hyperparameter optimization with ecological interpretation, the proposed framework supports the comparison and interpretation of biodiversity predictions for monitoring and ecological indicator development in structurally complex forests.

title: Metabolomic indicators anticipate permafrost peatland ecosystem transition before visible change
abstract: Climate change is accelerating ecosystem transitions worldwide, yet these changes often go undetected until visible damage occurs. Reliable early warning indicators are therefore needed. Here, we present a chemical indicator framework developed from a decade of permafrost thaw monitoring in subarctic Sweden. We show that declining soil chemical heterogeneity, measured as metabolomic mosaic diversity, preceded the documented collapse of palsa, a permafrost peat mound, at nearby sites by an estimated 2 to 7 years. This decline reflected a simpler metabolomic landscape, in which chemical variation followed fewer dominant biogeochemical gradients. Logistic regression of metabolomic fingerprints further revealed habitat specific chemical signatures. Deep soils kept a palsa signature after surface thaw, which shows that thaw proceeds in layers and in a nonlinear way. Finally, we identified metabolites with ecological functions. Catechin, a natural inhibitor of methane production, declined over time and may link ecosystem change to methane feedbacks. Together, these results show how untargeted metabolomics can be translated into measurable indicators of ecosystem change. Although developed for permafrost systems, this approach addresses a broader need to turn complex biochemical data into practical indicators, explain how ecosystems change, and identify sites that need closer monitoring before visible change occurs.

title: Mangrove structural correlates of predicted suitability for the understory shrub Acanthus ilicifolius in coastal forests of southeastern China
abstract: Acanthus ilicifolius L., a typical mangrove-associated shrub, is an important component of coastal wetland communities. It commonly occurs in mangrove understories, forest edges, estuarine margins, and tidal-channel habitats. Under the combined influence of biotic and abiotic factors, however, the spatial distribution patterns of A. ilicifolius and their relationships with mangrove ecosystems remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we modeled the relative habitat suitability of A. ilicifolius along the southeastern coast of China using ensemble species distribution models implemented in biomod2, with presence data from 35 occupied 1 km grid cells. Climatic, topographic, coastal, marine thermal, and mangrove structural variables were integrated to evaluate the environmental controls on habitat suitability. The models showed high internal discriminatory performance under repeated random five-fold cross-validation. High predicted relative suitability was mainly concentrated along the southern coast, while the corresponding classified area was sensitive to the selected suitability threshold. Variable importance and response analyses showed that wet-season temperature was the dominant predictor, followed by elevation and cold-season precipitation. Mangrove structural variables had substantially lower relative importance, particularly maximum canopy height and basal-area-weighted height. Nevertheless, incorporating these structural variables still affected model predictions in some areas. High-suitability areas within mapped mangrove areas were associated with lower mangrove aboveground biomass, lower basal-area weighted height, and lower maximum canopy height. Overall, these findings show that the predicted suitability of A. ilicifolius is primarily associated with broad climatic and coastal-position gradients, while its association with mangrove structural context supports a novel, field-testable hypothesis that this species may serve as a candidate indicator of open-canopy, low-biomass, or early-stage restoration contexts, providing useful information for coastal wetland restoration assessment and adaptive management.

title: Three-dimensional assessment of watershed health resilience and low-resilience risk analysis under the coupling of water resources, ecological, and socioeconomic subsystems
abstract: Abstract Watershed resilience under compounded climate variability and intensifying human disturbances has become a critical prerequisite for sustainable development in semi-arid inland basins. This study developed a spatially explicit watershed health resilience (WHR) framework that integrates three resilience dimensions (resistance, restoration, and adaptability) within the water resources, ecosystem, and Socioeconomic subsystems. Using the upper Xilin River Basin (XRB) as a case study, this study constructed a grid-based indicator system and quantified WHR dynamics during 2010–2023 based on multi-source hydro-climatic, remote sensing, and Socioeconomic datasets. The obstacle degree model and GeoDetector were employed to diagnose key constraints and attribute spatial heterogeneity, while KDE-based marginal estimation and copula models are used to characterize dependence structures and joint and conditional low-resilience risks among subsystems. WHR exhibits persistent spatial heterogeneity, with stable low-resilience clusters along the main river course, tributary confluences, and the reservoir-affected reach, whereas upstream areas remain consistently higher. Basin-averaged WHR increases from 0.41 (2010) to a peak of 0.59 (2021). Obstacle analysis reveals that the water resources subsystem constitutes the primary bottleneck, mainly constrained by the surface runoff restoration coefficient and the seasonal rebound amplitude of groundwater level. GeoDetector demonstrates that vegetation-water coupling factors are the main drivers of WHR spatial heterogeneity, led by seasonal rebound amplitude of NDVI and water use efficiency. Copula-based analysis indicates the strongest lower-tail dependence and the highest joint low-resilience risk for the water resources-ecosystem pair, suggesting a higher likelihood of co-failure under adverse states. This framework supports resilience-oriented hotspot targeting and cross-subsystem risk-informed watershed management.

title: Evaluation of water resources carrying capacity in Ordos City based on DPSIR -TOPSIS
abstract: Ordos City is located in the arid and semi-arid region of northwestern China, where the contradiction between water resource supply and demand is particularly prominent. Assessing water resources carrying capacity (WRCC) is therefore an important basis for achieving sustainable water resource development and utilization in this region. This study constructed an evaluation indicator system by integrating the DPSIR framework based on the synergistic concept of the water resources-water environment-water ecology system. An improved CRITIC method combined with the entropy weight method was applied to determine indicator weights, thereby reducing the excessive homogenization of weights and deviations from practical conditions caused by a single weighting method. Furthermore, the TOPSIS model and obstacle degree model were employed to comprehensively evaluate and diagnose the WRCC of Ordos City. The results showed that: (1) During the study period, the WRCC of Ordos City exhibited an overall trend of “steady improvement-fluctuating adjustment”. The comprehensive evaluation score increased from 0.3871 in 2000 to 0.5605 in 2023, with the overall carrying status improving from Level IV (overloaded state) to Level III (critical state), although it did not reach Level II. All administrative units showed varying degrees of improvement in WRCC, with evaluation results gradually shifting from lower levels toward critical and weak carrying states, accompanied by evident spatial differentiation. (2) Among the five DPSIR subsystems, the Impact subsystem contributed most significantly to WRCC improvement, with its score increasing from 0.2426 to 0.8766. The Driving forces and Response subsystems showed overall increasing trends, whereas the Pressure subsystem declined from 0.7199 to 0.3327, and the State subsystem exhibited considerable fluctuations. These results indicate asynchronous evolutionary patterns among the internal components of the WRCC system. (3) The obstacle degree analysis showed that the Driving forces and Response subsystems had the highest average obstacle degrees, accounting for 32.46% and 24.29%, respectively. During the early study period, ecological water replenishment and green coverage rate were the main obstacles restricting WRCC improvement. By 2023, urbanization rate, population density, ecological flow guarantee rate, ecological water replenishment, and total water use became the major obstacle factors, with total water use remaining among the leading obstacles during 2020–2023. This study reveals the dynamic characteristics of the coexistence between overall WRCC improvement and persistent subsystem constraints in arid resource-dependent regions. It provides an analytical framework for identifying key limiting factors during WRCC evolution and offers references for water resource optimization, ecological protection, and sustainable development management in similar arid and semi-arid regions.

title: A composite disturbance index for monitoring Sudanian dryland forests: structural and compositional indicators diverge under anthropogenic pressure
abstract: We developed and tested a field-based Composite Disturbance Index (CDI) for monitoring anthropogenic pressure in Sudan dryland forest, integrating stump density, partial extraction, grazing, agriculture, and fire into a single normalized score, and evaluated its performance against structural and compositional indicators of forest condition in Abu-Gadaf Natural Reserved Forest (AGNRF), Sudan. Using field plots combined with remote sensing covariates, we tested the CDI and its component metrics against tree diversity and forest structure using partial redundancy analysis, boosted regression trees, and AIC-based model comparison, keeping the aggregated index and its components in separate models to avoid structural collinearity. Anthropogenic predictors accounted for an adjusted 15.0% of variation in the multivariate diversity matrix ( p = 0.001), while the pure environmental fraction was indistinguishable from zero ( p = 0.939). Stump density was the strongest single correlate of compositional indicators, accounting for 60.7% of relative influence in boosted regression trees, whereas the composite index was the better predictor of size-weighted structural metrics. Critically, structural and compositional indicators diverged in their sensitivity to disturbance: basal area ( p = 0.002), stem density ( p = 0.0004) and aboveground biomass ( p = 0.007) all differed significantly among disturbance classes, while Shannon diversity ( p = 0.152) and species richness ( p = 0.147) did not, and aboveground biomass was predicted almost entirely by basal area regardless of disturbance intensity. No unimodal disturbance–diversity relationship was supported for any indicator. This divergence means that monitoring frameworks built on a single indicator class risk an incomplete read of forest condition: structural indicators central to carbon-focused reporting (e.g. UNFCCC/REDD+) responded sharply to the same disturbance gradient that biodiversity-focused indices (e.g. IPBES) did not detect. We recommend basal area and stump density as complementary, cost-effective indicators for dryland forest monitoring, and argue that safeguard frameworks pairing structural and compositional metrics are needed to avoid systematically overlooking degradation in reserves like AGNRF.

title: Nonlinear associations between comprehensive extreme climate hazard and regional grain supply performance in China: evidence from explainable XGBoost–SHAP models
abstract: Extreme climate events may increasingly undermine the stability of regional grain supply in China. Yet systematic evidence remains limited on where composite climate hazards coincide with strong regional grain supply performance and how individual climate extremes are nonlinearly associated with such performance. Using a prefecture-level panel for 2000–2024, we construct a comprehensive extreme climate hazard index (CECHI) encompassing extreme heat, extreme cold, extreme precipitation, persistent drought, and compound events. We then integrate spatiotemporal analysis, quantile-based spatial matching, and an XGBoost–SHAP framework to characterize hazard–supply performance configurations, identify climate variables with relatively high explanatory importance, and detect empirical breakpoints in their statistical associations with regional grain supply performance (RGSP). The results indicate that: (1) CECHI declined overall with substantial temporal fluctuations, while its broad spatial pattern remained relatively stable. Composite climate hazards were persistently higher in western and northeastern China than in eastern and central China. Climate hazard and RGSP did not exhibit a simple inverse spatial relationship; high-hazard–high-RGSP areas were concentrated in Northeast China, Inner Mongolia, and the Hexi Corridor. (2) The annual minimum daily minimum temperature (TNn), tropical nights (TR), and frost days (FD) showed the largest explanatory contributions to variation in RGSP, while the relative importance of persistent drought and compound dry-cold and dry-hot events increased over time. (3) Most climate indicators exhibited nonlinear, asymmetric, and region-dependent statistical associations with RGSP, and the highest-importance climate variables varied across prefecture-level cities and the nine agricultural regions. These findings indicate that food-security planning should consider not only regions with relatively weak grain supply performance but also major grain-supplying regions exposed to comparatively high levels of climate hazard, while adaptation measures should be tailored to region-specific climatic constraints.

title: A scale-invariant framework for integrating nature-based solutions into dense urban areas to improve accessibility and equity of access to urban blue and green spaces
abstract: Improving accessibility and spatial equity of access to Urban Blue and Green Spaces (UB&GS) could potentially benefit biodiversity and urban sustainability. Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), serving as small-scale decentralised forms of UB&GS, can enhance both environmental quality and human well-being by fostering positive interactions between humans and the natural environment. While there is growing interest in assessing the spatial distribution of UB&GS at multiple scales, existing evaluations commonly examine each spatial scale separately.
