We investigated wild plant diversity, distribution patterns, and the socio-ecological factors shaping plant composition across 58 traditional markets in Riau, Indonesia. Using semi-structured interviews ( n = 195) and multivariate ordinations, we assessed species composition in relation to ethnic usage, land-use types, and environmental gradients. During the study, we recorded 172 plant species, alongside 5 fungi and 1 lichen, with food plants comprising the largest use category (54.1%). None of the traded species are legally protected, although several key taxa (e.g., Litsea elliptica ) showed high risk values, indicating potential decline in their availability in the market trade. Markets were clustered geographically into three groups: the capital city, eastern, and western regions, reflecting differences in socio-ecological conditions and ethnic diversity. Markets surrounded by monoculture plantations of oil palm, had significantly lower species richness and greater compositional homogeneity than those in mixed-agricultural and inhabited areas. Our findings indicate that landscape and cultural diversity both shape wild plant diversity in traditional markets. In particular, the expansion of monoculture plantations is associated with lower plant diversity, highlighting the importance of conserving natural habitats for sustaining biocultural diversity and food security.

title: A receptor-based framework for comparing multi-hazard aggregation operators in forest ecosystem exposure assessment
abstract: Forest ecosystems in mountainous regions are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards, yet multi-hazard assessments commonly rely on single aggregation approaches that overlook how methodological choices influence ecosystem exposure patterns. This study proposes a receptor-based framework for comparing multi-hazard aggregation operators and demonstrates its application for forest ecosystem exposure assessment in Ilam Province, located in the Zagros Mountains of western Iran. The framework integrates hazard susceptibility modeling, aggregation operator comparison, and receptor-specific spatial analyses to systematically examine how different aggregation logics influence the magnitude and spatial configuration of ecosystem exposure. Four hazards, i.e., flood, landslide, wildfire, and drought, were modeled to generate susceptibility layers for forest exposure assessment using Random Forest models for flood, landslide, and wildfire, and the standardized precipitation index (SPI) for drought. Hazard layers were spatially harmonized and aggregated using five operators: Sum, Maximum, Fuzzy OR, Fuzzy AND, and Overlap. Forest ecosystems were treated as explicit receptors, enabling quantitative exposure evaluation through hazard dominance analysis, coincidence patterns, hotspot fragmentation metrics, and edge-to-core gradients. Wildfires (50.82%) and landslides (32.86%) dominated forest exposure, and 59.57% of forest areas were simultaneously exposed to two or more hazards, indicating widespread multi-hazard conditions. Aggregation choice substantially influenced both exposure magnitude and spatial configuration. Additive and union-based operators (Sum, Maximum, and Fuzzy OR) produced large, spatially continuous hotspot zones (largest patch index (LPI) >82%), highlighting broad forest areas subject to cumulative hazard pressure. In contrast, restrictive operators (Fuzzy AND and Overlap) generated smaller and more fragmented clusters, identifying localized sites of intense multi-hazard interaction. These results demonstrate that aggregation logic fundamentally shapes the interpretation and spatial representation of multi-hazard exposure, underscoring the value of systematically comparing aggregation strategies when assessing ecosystem risk and supporting more transparent multi-hazard decision-making.

title: Legacy effects of cropland use trajectories on stream environments and insects across contrasting change contexts
abstract: Agricultural land-use change can leave persistent legacies in freshwater ecosystems, yet the consequences of contrasting cropland-use trajectories, particularly expansion and contraction, remain poorly understood. In this study, we examined how multi-decadal cropland-use trajectories were associated with contemporary stream environmental conditions and aquatic insect communities at selected stream sites within Zhejiang Province, China. Using snapshot measurements of stream habitat, water quality, and aquatic insect assemblages, we related historical cropland-use trajectory attributes at the sub-catchment scale to current environmental conditions and to taxonomic and functional community composition under expansion and contraction contexts. Historical cropland-use trajectory attributes were significantly associated with most contemporary environmental variables and with both taxonomic and functional community composition. Although community-level comparisons provided no conclusive evidence that the strength of historical effects differed between expansion and contraction contexts, separate Threshold Indicator Taxa Analysis (TITAN) revealed distinct threshold-response patterns among individual taxa and functional groups within each context. Under cropland contraction, several sensitive taxa showed threshold responses along recovery-related trajectory attributes, whereas under cropland expansion, some disturbance-tolerant taxa increased along disturbance-enhancing attributes. These results indicate that cropland-use legacies are associated with multiple environmental and biological responses, while analyses of indicator taxa and functional groups provide complementary information to community-level assessments. Our study highlights the importance of considering long-term land-use trajectories, particularly the direction of change, and integrating taxonomic and functional responses when assessing the long-term consequences of agricultural change and informing stream restoration and land-use management.

title: Identification of ecosystem service trade-off mitigation zones and nonlinear response mechanisms in natural and planted forests in the context of climate change
abstract: Forests, as ecological land, serve as vital carriers for improving the ecological environment and mitigating trade-offs in ecosystem services (ESs), offering a natural solution for achieving sustainable ecosystem development. Clarifying spatial heterogeneity in mitigating ES trade-offs between natural forests (NF) and planted forests (PF) (PF refer to forests established through planting or deliberate seeding, including ecological restoration forests, and shelter forests) under climate change, and differences in dominant factor regulation, remains urgent. This study focused on China's NF and PF, with carbon storage (CS) and habitat quality (HQ) as the target ESs. Climate variables were considered indicators of natural environmental conditions, and population density was used as a proxy for human activity. Utilizing a MaxEnt_XGBoost_SHAP model framework, we identified trade-off mitigation zones and optimal thresholds, analyzed the differential nonlinear responses of forest types to dominant factors, and explored effective pathways for mitigating forest ES trade-offs. The results indicated that: (1) The CS–HQ trade-off intensity decreased in NFs but increased in PF. (2) High-level CS was mainly distributed in the southern coastal regions, whereas high-level HQ was concentrated in Southwest China for NF and Southeast China for PF. (3) CS–HQ trade-off mitigation zones in NF were primarily located around the Sichuan Basin, where the optimal threshold range for CS increased significantly, while that for HQ decreased. In PF, mitigation zones were mainly distributed in southern China, with significant declines in the optimal threshold ranges for both CS and HQ. (4) The overall response intensity of environmental variables was higher in NFs than in PF. Environmental variables associated with HQ exhibited greater explanatory contributions in NF, whereas CS-related variables contributed more substantially in PF. From a forest management perspective, conservation of HQ should be prioritized in NF while maintaining carbon sequestration capacity. For PF, mixed-species PF and close-to-nature management should be implemented to synergistically enhance CS and habitat functions. This study provides a methodological framework and decision-making support for identifying the differentiated roles of NF and PF in mitigating ES trade-offs and promoting sustainable ecosystem development.

title: Methodological divergence in river health assessment: A comparative study of integrated assessment versus multi-taxon IBI
abstract: Different approaches to river health assessment may yield contrasting evaluation outcomes; however, their applicability under varying disturbance regimes remains insufficiently understood. Using the Chishui River as a case study, the performance of an integrated assessment approach was compared with that of the Phytoplankton Index of Biotic Integrity (P-IBI), Zooplankton Index of Biotic Integrity ( Z -IBI), and Benthic Macroinvertebrate Index of Biotic Integrity (B-IBI). Environmental drivers underlying differences among assessment outcomes were also examined. The integrated assessment approach and B-IBI consistently indicated better ecological health in the upstream and midstream reaches than in the downstream reach, as well as higher ecological health during the dry season than during the wet season. In contrast, P-IBI and Z -IBI generally assigned higher health grades to downstream reaches and wet-season conditions. Analyses of environmental drivers revealed distinct responses of biological assemblages to nutrient enrichment and associated environmental gradients. Consequently, different assessment approaches reflected different ecological responses to environmental stressors and varied in their applicability across disturbance gradients. Overall, B-IBI showed a high level of concordance with the integrated assessment approach and was better suited to evaluating river health in heavily disturbed reaches. In contrast, plankton-based IBIs appeared more suitable for rapid ecological assessments in relatively undisturbed river systems. Based on these findings, a disturbance-based framework for selecting river health assessment approaches was proposed, providing a scientific basis for river health evaluation and watershed management decision-making. • Different river health assessment approaches showed contrasting ecological outcomes. • Biological assemblages exhibited distinct responses to nutrient enrichment gradients. • B-IBI showed high concordance with integrated assessment in disturbed reaches. • A disturbance-based framework was developed for selecting assessment approaches.

title: Uncovering nonlinear thresholds and functional zoning of ecosystem services: Evidence from the cities along the Yellow River in Shandong, China
abstract: Rapid urban expansion along the Yellow River has exerted increasing pressure on ecosystem functions and ecological sustainability, highlighting the need for precise quantification of ecosystem service ( ES ) supply and identification of key driving thresholds for effective ecological management. This study focuses on riparian cities in Shandong Province, evaluating seven critical ES . Utilizing the XGBoost-SHAP framework, we identified dominant drivers and their non-linear threshold effects, while Self-Organizing Map was applied to delineate functional zones. Spatially, Carbon storage ( CS ), Habitat quality ( HQ ), Soil retention ( SR ), Water conservation ( WC ), Water purification ( WP ), and Wind and sand stabilization ( WS ) cluster in central-southern mountainous regions, whereas Food production ( FP ) shows an opposite pattern. Spatiotemporal analysis from 2000 to 2020 reveals increasing trends in CS and FP supply alongside a general decline in other services. The responses of ES to drivers display clear differentiation: vegetation and human activities jointly regulate CS and FP ; topography dominates SR , WC , WP , and WS ; and cumulative anthropogenic disturbance shapes HQ . Furthermore, distinct service bundles and thresholds are observed across zones; for instance, zones B2, B4, and B5 are severely constrained when population density exceeds 833–837 persons/km 2 [810–860]. These findings provide a robust scientific basis for ES -based ecological management and spatial optimization in rapidly urbanizing regions along the Yellow River.

title: Corrigendum to “Landscape spatial configuration determines seasonal nitrate transport rather than land-use proportions in mountainous rivers” [Ecol. Indic. 191 (2026) 115651]
Excessive pesticide input drives deterministic reassembly of soil fungal communities through niche broadening and reduced phylogenetic clustering
abstract: Excessive fertilizer and pesticide inputs are widespread in intensive agriculture, yet their combined effects on soil fungal communities and the mechanisms underlying community reassembly remain poorly understood. We conducted a six-year field experiment in the North China Plain with four treatments: conventional fertilizer and pesticide inputs, excessive fertilizer, excessive pesticide, and combined excessive inputs. We assessed fungal diversity, composition, co-occurrence networks, habitat niche breadth, phylogenetic structure, and assembly processes. Excessive fertilization increased soil carbon and nutrient availability, crop yield, and fungal diversity, but did not broaden mean habitat niche breadth, indicating that resource enrichment mainly relaxed substrate limitation and promoted taxon coexistence. In contrast, excessive pesticide input reduced fungal diversity, crop biomass, yield, and biological indicators, while increasing habitat niche breadth and weakening phylogenetic clustering. Mean niche breadth was negatively related to the nearest taxon index, suggesting that pesticide filtering favored broad-niche taxa from relatively distant fungal lineages. Null-model analysis showed that stochastic processes dominated under conventional management, whereas heterogeneous selection increased under excessive pesticide input and was strongest under combined excessive inputs. These findings show that pesticide pressure reduced fungal taxonomic diversity while increasing the average habitat breadth and phylogenetic separation of the remaining taxa. Nutrient enrichment did not offset pesticide-associated ecological stress under combined excessive inputs. Overall, excessive pesticide input was the primary driver of deterministic fungal community reassembly, and the coordinated shifts in niche breadth and phylogenetic structure highlight their potential as sensitive indicators of agrochemical disturbance in intensively managed croplands.

title: Efficient improvement of ecosystem service quality through green space morphology optimization in cold-arid regions: evidence from the Hexi Corridor, China
abstract: Ecosystem services (ESs) in cold-arid regions are constrained by climate-driven threshold effects and may decline nonlinearly under extreme hydrothermal stress. Under water and land constraints, simply expanding green space may increase water consumption and ES trade-offs, necessitating green space morphology optimization integrating area and spatial configuration. However, its nonlinear effects on ESs and favorable ranges for coordinated improvement under cold-arid conditions remain unclear. Using the Hexi Corridor, China, as a case study, this study used 2024 multi-source data, including land-use and climate variables, and developed an integrated framework combining morphological indicator dimensionality reduction and reconstruction, Priority Optimization Areas (POA) identification, and machine-learning-based nonlinear interpretation to examine how green space morphology improves ES quality efficiently. The results showed that: (1) POAs for four ESs, namely water yield (WY), soil conservation (SC), carbon sequestration (CS), and habitat quality (HQ), were mainly concentrated in the Qilian Mountains ecological conservation area, each covering about 30%; (2) climatic factors dominated ES spatial differentiation, with precipitation (PRE) showing stable positive effects, the highest contributions (31.4%–66.0%), and clear nonlinear thresholds, whereas temperature (TEM) generally exerted negative effects; (3) green space morphology showed weaker but service-specific effects, with area size (G1) most strongly promoting CS and HQ, while patch morphology (G2) and spatial connectivity (G3) had differentiated or even contrasting effects; and (4) threshold ranges associated with the coordinated improvement of four ESs in the Hexi Corridor in 2024 were identified. These findings provide scientific support for efficient ecological spatial governance in cold-arid regions under climate change.

title: When more green is not always better: Nonlinear and spatially dependent effects of green space morphology on subjective well-being in compact cities
abstract: In high-density urban environments, limited green space challenges residents' subjective well-being (SWB) and social interaction (SI), yet the nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous mechanisms linking spatial morphology to human experiences remain underexplored. This study investigates the nonlinear and spatially dependent effects of community green-space configurations on well-being outcomes. Using Suzhou, China, as a case study, we integrate high-resolution remote-sensing imagery, GIS-based park POIs, social media check-ins, and community-level statistics. Key landscape metrics include Green Distribution Equality (GDE), diversity (GD), shape index (SHAPE), patch density (PD), and mean patch area (MPS). Analyses were conducted using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and spatial autocorrelation models (Moran's I and LISA). Results show that: (1) GDE and GD emerge as the strongest positive correlates of both SWB and SI, with pronounced effects on SI. (2) Nonlinear responses reveal diminishing marginal effects of GDE on SWB (plateauing after index ∼3), with MPS exerting maximal influence within an intermediate range. (3) Spatial patterns exhibit core-periphery differentiation; SWB displays a “southern high-northern low” gradient, with high–high clusters of SWB concentrated in Gusu District and SIP cores; SI shows “core agglomeration,” with high values aligning with commercial and transport nodes. The study develops a multi-source, data-driven framework that reveals the nonlinear threshold effects and spatially heterogeneous pathways through which urban green morphology influences SWB and SI, thereby extending existing research beyond linear and average-effect explanations and offering actionable insights for optimizing green-space design in compact cities.

title: Estimating the urban heat island effect with lichens and bryophytes: a citizen science protocol
abstract: The urban heat island effect (UHI), whereby urban areas are warmer than the surrounding rural areas, has become an increasing threat to human health and affects biodiversity. Counteracting this public health concern requires large-scale monitoring of urban heat. One cost-effective way to obtain this data is by using bioindicators, such as lichens and bryophytes. They are well-known bioindicators readily available in the urban environment, and have proven to respond to the UHI. Gathering large amounts of data in a short time span may prove difficult for many institutes or municipalities, but can be resolved by incorporating citizen science. However, lichen and bryophyte species identification with no prior experience may prove problematic for citizen scientists. Therefore, we developed a citizen science protocol that requires scoring the presence of easily recognisable morphotypes of epiphytic lichens and bryophytes, instead of individual species. Data was collected in urban environments in the Netherlands by participants at three knowledge levels: an expert in lichenology and bryology, university biology students, and citizen scientists. Using the expert dataset, we trained a baseline multiple linear model (LM) and a random forest (RF) model, which predicted local UHI with low root-mean-square errors (RMSE = 0.29 °C and 0.20 °C, respectively). Prediction accuracy declined with decreasing participants' expertise. We conclude that a simplified protocol using morphotypes of lichens and bryophytes can be an effective, low-cost way of monitoring the UHI. However, some training or experience is required to obtain sufficiently accurate observations.

title: Assessing ecological monitoring design using a hybrid approach to guide changes to long term monitoring: A zooplankton case study
abstract: Ecosystem monitoring frequently focuses on populations, but a community perspective better reflects food web ecology. We asked a common question among natural resource managers – how much sampling is needed to understand the community in my system? We identified two objectives: (1) provide a community perspective and (2) ensure computational effort does not become unwieldy. In the San Francisco Estuary, five decades of zooplankton samples have been collected due to their importance as prey for fishes. We conducted a thorough investigation into the gaps and strengths of these data using a combination of three analytical approaches: representative taxa selections, power analysis, and a simulated reduced sampling. A principal tensor analysis divided the zooplankton community into co-occurring subassemblages and a silhouette analysis allowed us to select representative taxa from each subassemblage. We used univariate statistical analyses for each representative taxon to find gaps or overlaps in sampling that span the zooplankton community. We conducted power analyses on generalized linear mixed effect models and found that statistical power varied depending on the combination of temporal and spatial scale and across the effect sizes we tested (0.1, 0.2, 0.5, and 1). For mesozooplankton, which had greater statistical power, we simulated reductions in sampling effort and determined its impact on abundance estimates using Bayesian models; we observed less redundancy for temporal reductions compared with spatial reductions in sampling. Our approach is generally transferrable to evaluating the sampling effort needed to monitor changes in a biological community over time and space.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution of water conservation and its driving factors in the Weihe River basin based on the InVEST model
abstract: Elucidating the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of water conservation (WC) is fundamental to basin-scale ecological restoration. This study quantified an InVEST-based WC index across the Weihe River Basin from 2000 to 2025. Annual water yield was first estimated using the InVEST Annual Water Yield module and was subsequently adjusted using topographic, soil-hydraulic, and flow-velocity factors to characterize the relative water conservation potential. Geodetector was then used to examine spatial associations between the modeled WC index and eight selected factors. Eight physical and ecological factors, namely elevation (DEM), mean annual temperature (TEMP), slope, nighttime light (NTL), population density (POP), gross domestic product (GDP), net primary productivity (NPP), and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), were evaluated at the pixel scale. The mean annual InVEST-based WC index was 120.78 mm, showing a long-term upward trend despite interannual climate variability. Spatially, WC exhibited a persistent south-high and north-low pattern, with high-value areas progressively extending northward. This spatial evolution coincided with pronounced land-use restructuring, characterized by cropland contraction and forest and grassland expansion. The corresponding decline in the cropland share of basin-total WC and increases in the forest and grassland shares indicate a close spatiotemporal association between land-use restructuring and WC redistribution. DEM and TEMP generally exhibited high spatial explanatory power, reaching q-values of 0.477 and 0.456 in 2020, respectively, whereas NDVI ranked first in 2010. The largest joint q-value occurred for DEM ∩ NPP in 2020 (q = 0.657), highlighting the spatial correspondence between WC and combined terrain-vegetation stratification. These findings characterize regional patterns in the modeled WC index and their associations with the selected factors.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of ecological quality across frozen-ground zones in Northeast China: A modified RSEI and explainable GeoAI framework
abstract: Reliable ecological quality assessment is essential for early detection of environmental risks in cold regions. However, conventional indices such as the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) often overlook snow cover and ground thermal conditions that shape ecosystem functioning. Using northeast China, a representative mid-latitude permafrost transition zone, as a case study, we developed a modified remote sensing ecological index (MRSEI) incorporating snow cover fraction (SCF) and soil temperature (ST), and established an explainable geospatial artificial intelligence (XGeoAI) framework to quantify the spatially heterogeneous effects of natural and anthropogenic drivers. Results show that: (1) ecological quality in the NCPR exhibited a dual-phase pattern, with degradation during 2005–2015 followed by restoration during 2015–2020; (2) mean MRSEI values across the four frozen-ground zones decreased progressively from 0.662 in the predominantly continuous permafrost zone to 0.313 in the moderately thick seasonally frozen ground zone, representing an overall decline of 0.349 (52.7%), with intermediate values of 0.547 and 0.421 in the predominantly continuous and island permafrost zone and the sparsely island permafrost zone, respectively; and (3) ecological quality variation was governed by nonlinear, spatially heterogeneous, and interactive effects, with natural background conditions playing stronger roles in northern and mountainous permafrost areas, whereas human disturbance factors exerted stronger negative effects in the central–southern regions and the moderately thick seasonally frozen ground zone. These findings demonstrate the suitability of MRSEI for cryospheric ecological monitoring and the value of XGeoAI for supporting spatially targeted ecological management.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of carbon sequestration services in the middle Yellow River Basin and gradient responses to ecological restoration in mining areas
abstract: Mining and ecological restoration frequently overlap in environmentally fragile regions, yet the spatial extent and temporal evolution of restoration-related carbon recovery remain poorly quantified. We developed an integrated indicator framework for the middle Yellow River Basin (MYRB) using multisource data from 2000 to 2025. The framework combined an a net primary productivity (NPP)-adjusted InVEST carbon model, Theil–Sen slope estimation, the Mann–Kendall trend test, Pettitt change-point detection, multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR), and an exponential asymptotic recovery model. The results showed that carbon sequestration service (CS) increased from 101.93 Mg·hm −2 in 2000 to 105.49 Mg·hm −2 in 2025, with a Theil–Sen slope of 0.15 Mg·hm −2 ·yr −1 , while total ecosystem carbon stock rose from approximately 3.27 to 3.33 Pg. A regional transition was detected around 2017, after which the rate of increase was higher. Natural predictors, particularly precipitation, evapotranspiration, and radiation, showed broad-scale associations with CS, whereas nighttime light, population density, and human activity intensity showed more localized associations. The combined coefficient-based contribution of anthropogenic factors increased from 47.07% to 50.29% after 2017. Mean CS within mining areas was 77.29 Mg·hm −2 , approximately 25.45% below the basin-wide multi-year mean CS density. CS increased nonlinearly with distance from mine boundaries. The proposed 95% recovery-distance indicator decreased from 2.58 to 8.49 km during 2000–2011 to 1.25–2.46 km during 2012–2025, indicating a shorter modeled distance to near-background conditions. This framework links long-term carbon dynamics, scale-dependent associations, and a recovery-distance indicator to support regional monitoring priorities and carbon-oriented land-use planning.

title: Identifying spatiotemporal patterns and associated determinants of stable natural vegetation resilience across China
abstract: Vegetation resilience (VR) is a critical factor in ecosystem stability. Previous studies in China have mainly focused on vegetation restoration monitoring rather than resilience dynamic identification and their heterogeneous drivers, which may be insufficient for ensuring ecosystem restoration efficacy as well as afforestation management and optimization. Therefore, the present work quantified VR as the negative first-order autoregressive coefficient (−AR(1)) of detrended and deseasonalized vegetation anomalies obtained from MODIS kNDVI (kernel normalized difference vegetation index) from 2000 to 2025. We combined 60-month sliding windows with interpretable machine learning, ecosystem-specific models, and geographically weighted regression to examine spatial patterns, temporal trajectories, and environmental determinants of VR. VR was generally higher in southern and eastern China, with relatively low values in parts of the Inner Mongolian and Loess Plateau. Grassland resilience declined substantially with latitude, whereas the corresponding relationship for forests was weak. Although most of the vegetated areas lacked monotonic trends, nonlinear trajectories were widespread. The dominant increase-then-decrease mode of VR change accounted for approximately one-third of the classified area, indicating that earlier improvements of VR were often unsustainable. Climatic variables accounted for 61.8% of the total model importance for VR, with mean soil moisture contributing to approximately one-third. Soil moisture, vapor pressure deficit, and topography showed threshold-dependent or non-monotonic associations with VR. Grasslands were more sensitive to vapor pressure deficit variability, soil moisture, and soil organic carbon than forests, and the local regression coefficient revealed strong spatial nonstationarity. These findings reveal the complex climatic drivers of VR and provide a scientific basis upon which ecosystem restoration efforts can be optimized across China and beyond.

title: Developing age-site-density integrated biomass carbon storage models and accumulation tables for warm temperate forests in China
abstract: Forest carbon sequestration rate is closely linked to stand growth dynamics; however, existing carbon storage models for warm-temperate forests in China have largely focused on individual factors such as stand age or density, without jointly accounting for site quality and stand density. This limitation constrains their applicability for multi-factor carbon accounting across varying site and management conditions. Using data from China's 7th- 9th National Forest Resource Inventories (2004–2018), we developed carbon storage accumulation models and corresponding tables for typical warm-temperate forest types incorporating forest age, site class, and stand density index (SDI) as predictors. The models achieved satisfactory performance ( R 2 ≥ 0.647), with higher accuracy for natural forests than plantations, and for coniferous than broad-leaved species. Site quality was the primary factor associated with the asymptotic carbon storage parameter ( a ), which decreased from site class I to V. High-density stands stored more carbon than low-density stands, and the relationship between stand density and carbon storage was stronger in natural forests than in plantations. Taking Pinus tabuliformis as a representative species, dynamic simulations driven by the accumulation tables revealed that plantations accumulated carbon more rapidly-during the early stage (<30 years); however, beyond 65 years, plantation growth slowed markedly and the annual carbon sequestration of natural forests began to exceed that of plantations, underscoring the superior long-term sequestration potential of natural forests. Collectively, these models, tables, and comparative analyses provide methodological and technical support for accurate carbon measurement, potential assessment, and the formulation of differentiated, carbon-oriented management strategies for warm-temperate forests in the context of carbon neutrality.

title: Optimizing land-use for biodiversity conservation and wind prevention and sand fixation in northern China's agro-pastoral ecotone
abstract: The Northern China's agro-pastoral ecotone is a critical ecological barrier for central and eastern China but is also highly ecologically vulnerable. Competition between cultivated land and grassland, together with climatic variability, has accelerated land degradation, soil erosion, and biodiversity loss. Optimizing land-use configurations is essential for enhancing ecological functions, yet practical multi-objective optimization remains limited in this region. This study examined cultivated land–grassland dynamics between 2000 and 2020 and developed an integrated optimization framework combining the Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and the Future Land Use Simulation (FLUS) model to evaluate three representative land-use scenarios with different trade-offs between biodiversity conservation and wind prevention and sand fixation (WPSF). The results showed that reciprocal conversions between cultivated land and grassland dominated land-use changes during 2000–2020 and closely corresponded to shifts in the 400 mm precipitation isohyet. All three optimized scenarios improved species richness-based biodiversity and WPSF benefits relative to the 2020 baseline, with biodiversity gains primarily linked to forest expansion and WPSF gains to grassland expansion. More importantly, spatial optimization exhibited substantially greater potential for enhancing WPSF than for biodiversity across the three scenarios, with >98.5% of the study area showing changes in WPSF compared with ∼44% showing changes in biodiversity. These findings imply that, to enhance WPSF, grassland conservation and restoration should be prioritized, whereas biodiversity conservation requires broader ecological restoration and governance strategies beyond spatial optimization. Beyond these regional implications, the proposed framework offers a transferable approach to support multi-objective land-use planning across agro-pastoral ecotones.

title: Decoupling of spatiotemporal variations of lake CO2 emissions in China: Inconsistency between seasonal and spatial dominant factors
abstract: Lake CO 2 emissions have become a critical component shaping the stability of terrestrial carbon sinks and regional carbon budgets, yet existing studies often neglect the spatial heterogeneity and scale effects of the explanatory variables, resulting in substantial uncertainties in the assessment of lake CO 2 emissions. In this study, we examined seasonally dominant explanatory variables and their scale-dependent spatial associations with lake CO 2 fluxes across China. The results showed that lake CO 2 fluxes exhibited a spatiotemporal pattern, with higher mean values in winter (−0.36 to 10.53 mmol m −2 d −1 ; 1.54 ± 1.45 mmol m −2 d −1 ) and lower values in summer (−0.40 to 7.00 mmol m −2 d −1 ; 1.01 ± 1.32 mmol m −2 d −1 ; p < 0.001); annual mean values were highest in the Northeast Plain and Mountain Lake Zone (2.27 ± 1.55 mmol m −2 d −1 ) and lowest in the Inner Mongolia-Xinjiang Lake Zone (0.63 ± 0.69 mmol m −2 d −1 ). The global spatial autocorrelation of CO 2 fluxes strengthened from spring to winter (Moran's I = 0.348–0.411). The multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model achieved the best goodness of fit in all seasons (R 2 = 0.68–0.86), effectively capturing the spatial heterogeneity of the explanatory variables. Lake area exhibited the highest explanatory power in spring and winter (Q = 0.489 and 0.287, respectively), whereas DO ranked highest in summer and autumn (Q = 0.381 and 0.196, respectively). OPGD interaction detection showed that nonlinear enhancement was the predominant interaction type, suggesting that spatial heterogeneity in CO 2 fluxes reflects the joint influence of multiple explanatory variables. Scale-effect analysis based on MGWR bandwidths revealed that lake attributes (lake area, average depth, and average discharge) exhibited broad-scale effects, with relatively stable influences across larger spatial ranges (bandwidths: 159–181 km). In contrast, water quality indicators (DO and NH 4 + ) and climatic factors (PRE and SSR) showed localized effects due to their smaller bandwidths (23–40 km). The detector analysis further identified high-emission zones associated with small lakes and conditions of low DO, underscoring the necessity of differentiated management for small waterbodies and environmentally sensitive regions in lake‑carbon governance. Overall, this study demonstrates that explicitly incorporating spatial heterogeneity and multiscale effects is essential for accurately assessing lake CO 2 emissions and for designing spatially and seasonally targeted carbon-mitigation strategies.

title: Spatially nonstationary drivers of aboveground biomass carbon across China’s terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Understanding how environmental contributions to aboveground biomass carbon (AGBC) vary across space and ecosystem types is important for large-scale carbon assessment. Although machine-learning approaches can capture nonlinear relationships between AGBC and environmental variables, conventional global interpretation may obscure geographic variation in these relationships. Here, we integrated eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), GeoShapley, conventional SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and generalized additive models (GAMs) to analyze field-based AGBC observations and multisource environmental variables across China's terrestrial ecosystems. XGBoost was used to characterize nonlinear predictor–AGBC relationships, GeoShapley to separate environmental and geographic contributions and their interactions, and GAMs to examine ecosystem-specific nonlinear attribution patterns. Spatial block cross-validation and an ablation analysis of the encoded ecosystem-type variable were further used to assess the robustness of model interpretation. Net primary productivity (NPP) remained among the environmental variables with the largest contributions, and removal of the ecosystem-type encoding produced highly consistent rankings of the remaining variables (Spearma n's r s = 0.976 , p < 0.001 ). GeoShapley–SHAP differences showed clear regional variation in the contributions of altitude, precipitation, and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI)-derived vegetation-cover index (TCC), whereas NPP exhibited a less distinct spatial boundary. Ecosystem-specific analyses further revealed contrasting nonlinear attribution patterns between forests and grasslands, consistent with differences in carbon retention, allocation, turnover, and environmental constraints. These results show that environmental contributions to AGBC are both geographically and ecosystem dependent, and that spatial attribution combined with ecosystem-specific interpretation provides a more informative framework than a single global variable-importance analysis for understanding national-scale AGBC variation.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and path differentiation of Park City development outcomes from the perspective of ecosystem service value: A case study of Chengdu, China
abstract: The Park City initiative represents a new urban development paradigm that embeds ecological value into urban systems. However, systematic quantitative evaluations of its development outcomes remain limited. Taking Chengdu, where the Park City concept was first proposed, as the study area, this study assesses Park City implementation from the perspective of ecosystem service value (ESV), focusing on the differentiated roles of natural, suburban, and urban parks. The results show that Chengdu's ESV followed an overall decline–recovery trajectory from 2003 to 2022, while its spatial structure remained highly stable, with hot spots concentrated mainly in the eastern and western mountainous areas. The three park types exhibited clear path differentiation. Natural parks most closely tracked the citywide trajectory and constituted the ecological foundation of Park City development. Suburban parks functioned as transitional buffers between ecological conservation and urban expansion. Urban parks showed the most unstable trajectories under stronger construction intensity and management interventions, serving as an embedded regulator of human–land relationships. Natural factors remained dominant overall, whereas the influence of socioeconomic factors became progressively stronger from natural parks to suburban parks and urban parks. Coupling coordination analysis further revealed a distinct three-circle structure, with low coordination in the urban core, intermediate coordination in the suburban ring, and relatively high coordination in the outer areas underpinned by natural parks. These findings deepen understanding of the ecological effects and differentiated evolutionary mechanisms of Park City development, providing scientific support for ecological spatial optimization, differentiated governance, and the refinement of Park City practice in mega-cities.

title: Ecosystem services that enhance synergy through coordinated spatial zoning and management: A network analysis and machine learning approach
abstract: Elucidating the complex interactions within the water–food–ecology nexus is crucial for ensuring the sustainable management of fragile ecosystems. However, traditional pairwise analyses often fail to capture system network dynamics and nonlinear driver responses. The Loess Plateau, where the largest ecological restoration project in the world has been implemented, is facing increasing conflicts over ecosystem services (ESs). In this study, the spatiotemporal dynamics of four key ESs (water yield, soil conservation, carbon fixation, and food provision) on the Loess Plateau from 2000 to 2024 were assessed at the county level. Signed partial correlation networks were used to quantify the trade-off degree (TD) and synergy degree (SD). Extreme gradient boosting coupled with out-of-fold SHapley additive exPlanations (XGBoost–SHAP) was used to identify predictive drivers and model response variations. A stability-screened self-organizing map delineated ES bundles and classification-sensitive transition zones. Our results showed that carbon fixation, soil conservation, and food provision increased; however, the network remained dominated by trade-offs. Carbon fixation–soil conservation had the most extensive synergy, whereas food provision–soil conservation had the most extensive trade-off degree. Moreover, 37.31% of counties experienced increasing TDs and declining SDs. TD was most strongly associated with the impervious surface proportion (IMP; 24.0%), grassland cover (13.8%), and population density (12.2%), whereas SD was driven primarily by precipitation (26.0%), slope (10.5%), and fractional vegetation cover (9.8%). The IMP response changed its sign near 0.033, while the FVC transition varied from approximately 0.47 to 0.51 across predictor sets and hydrothermal strata, indicating a conditional assessment range rather than a universal vegetation cover cap. By integrating bundle function, classification stability, and model response signals, we provide an adaptive basis for spatial management. This study provides a reference framework for alleviating socio-ecological conflicts in water-scarce regions around the world.

title: A site suitability index framework for mangrove afforestation in dynamic coastal char lands of Bangladesh
abstract: Successful mangrove afforestation in newly accreted coastal char lands depends strongly on appropriate site selection. The assessment based on individual environmental variables may not capture the multiple factors influencing mangrove establishment. Eighty-five sampling units across 157 uniform 25 ha grids were selected using stratified random sampling. These sites were distributed across 18 pre-screened potential mangrove afforestation sites in Barguna, Bhola, and Patuakhali districts of Bangladesh. The present study developed a field-based Site Suitability Index (SSI) using five sub-indices: Land Cover Index (LCI), Ecological Condition Index (ECI), Soil-Hydrology Index (SHI), Sediment Stability Index (SedI), and Disturbance Index (DI). Sensitivity analysis examined how changes in sub-index weights affected SSI classifications. About 92% of the assessed area was classified as Suitable or Highly Suitable, about 7% as Unsuitable, and the remaining area consisted of existing mangrove plantations. Soil-hydrological conditions and sediment stability were important components of overall suitability, whereas sandy substrates represented a major constraint in unsuitable areas. SSI classifications were relatively stable under alternative weighting scenarios, with 91.8–100% of sampling units retaining their baseline classes under ±20% changes in individual sub-index weights. The high proportion of suitable areas should be interpreted in the context of the preliminary screening of the study sites. The SSI provides a structured field-based approach for assessing potential mangrove afforestation sites; however, follow-up monitoring of plantation establishment, survival, growth, and natural regeneration is required to validate and, where necessary, refine the framework.

title: Corrigendum to “Spatial lock-in, blue carbon stock contributions, and source-sink mismatches: assessing low-carbon target feasibility on Hainan Island, China” [Ecol. Indic. 191 (2026) 115605]
Assessing vegetation recovery following wrack disturbances in salt marshes using UAS data
abstract: Wrack can smother underlying vegetation in salt marshes, reducing plant productivity. Recovery time for vegetation damaged from wrack disturbances is often dictated by specific wrack or environmental characteristics. We used Unoccupied Aerial Systems (UAS) imagery collected at Dean Creek marsh on Sapelo Island, GA, USA to evaluate vegetation recovery length following wrack disturbances and relate it to wrack characteristics. We implemented a buffering and kriging technique to estimate the NDVI values of wrack-damaged areas and assess vegetation recovery. This method was tested on 24 control polygons and we found that using Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) values in a 1-m buffer offset by 1 m for kriging provided consistent estimates of NDVI. We used 176 wrack patches identified in 2021, and applied this method to evaluate recovery lengths using a survivability model. We found that ∼75% of damaged vegetation recovered within 6 months and ∼ 90% within 1 year. We also used a generalized additive model (GAM) to identify how wrack characteristics might influence recovery length and found duration and arrival season were both significant. We found that vegetation damaged by wrack patches that arrived in the fall recovered faster than vegetation damaged by wrack from other seasons; patches with a 1-month duration recovered 2–3 months faster than patches with durations of ≥2 months, and there was little difference in recovery length based on patch area. This study introduces a new framework for evaluating vegetation recovery, showcases the importance of frequent UAS data collection for disturbance assessment, and helps to explain potential drivers of recovery following wrack disturbances.

title: Impacts of climate change on the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors in Northeast China and implications for the Post-2020 global biodiversity framework
abstract: Global warming has substantially altered the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors. However, the mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, we developed a coupled climate–habitat–ecological corridor analytical framework integrating the least-cost path model, circuit theory, the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model, and the eXtreme Gradient Boosting–SHapley Additive exPlanations interpretation approach. Using Northeast China as the study area, the framework was applied to simulate and predict the distribution of least-cost corridors, ecological nodes, and habitat suitability for three waterbird species ( Grus japonensis , Cygnus cygnus , and Mergus squamatus ) during the historical period and three future time periods (the 2030s, 2050s, and 2070s). The framework was further used to quantify the relative contributions of environmental drivers to the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors. The results indicate that: (1) under climatic filtering, non-narrow-range species with broader niche breadth generally maintained relatively stable corridor number and length, whereas narrow-range species exhibited greater temporal variability in corridor patterns, particularly in habitat area and corridor number density; and (2) at the regional scale, climatic factors are strongly associated with the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors, likely through their effects on physiological suitability and resource availability. Elevation and local habitat attributes provide additional environmental constraints that drive these climate–corridor associations. By examining the associations among climate, elevation, habitat, and ecological corridor distribution within a coupled-system framework, this study highlights the urgent need to integrate climatic considerations into corridor conservation planning in support of the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework.

title: Assessing the cross-lake generalization of satellite-driven machine learning models for lake metabolism estimation
abstract: Lake metabolism, including gross primary production (GPP) and ecosystem respiration (R), is a fundamental indicator of ecosystem functioning and aquatic carbon cycling, but in situ estimates are spatially sparse and difficult to scale across heterogeneous lakes. Satellite observations and machine learning provide a potential solution, yet the extent to which such models generalize across lakes remains poorly understood. This work presents a satellite-driven machine learning framework for estimating lake GPP and R across 164 lakes. Six machine learning algorithms, including linear regression, support vector regression, random forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), artificial neural networks, and tabular prior-data fitted network (TabPFN), were trained using in-situ GPP and R derived from high-frequency dissolved oxygen observations, together with Landsat spectral variables, solar radiance, and lake surface temperature. The performance of these models was evaluated in terms of cross-lake generalization, uncertainty, and consistency between point-based and whole-lake estimates. First, the models were evaluated using four validation strategies: random, temporal, spatial, and leave-one-lake-out (LOLO) splits. Model performance deteriorated consistently as validation became more stringent (random, temporal, spatial, and LOLO), revealing substantial generalization gaps across all models. As validation stringency increased, performance deteriorated markedly: GPP R 2 dropped from 0.575 (random) to 0.419 (LOLO), and R R 2 fell from 0.470 to 0.341. These results demonstrate that conventional random-split validation systematically overestimates transferable predictive skill, while non-linear models, despite strong interpolation performance, exhibit limited cross-lake generalization—particularly for R, which showed greater sensitivity to validation strictness than GPP. Second, prediction sensitivity to input noise was quantified through a feature-specific Monte Carlo perturbation analysis under three scenarios, yielding mean sensitivity estimates of 0.106 for GPP and 0.090 for R under the baseline scenario. Third, we evaluated the consistency between point-based and whole-lake estimates for GPP (slope = 0.84) and R (slope = 0.77), respectively. Finally, these results demonstrate that ecological heterogeneity and distribution shifts fundamentally constrain the cross-lake generalization of satellite-driven lake metabolism models, underscoring the need for validation frameworks that explicitly account for increasing extrapolation difficulty.

title: Beyond fixed-radius footprints: boundary-referenced ecological effects of three Chinese greenfield hub airports
abstract: Attributing ecological change around large infrastructure is difficult because a fixed-radius “footprint” mixes on-site land take, off-site land-use transition and off-site ecological response. We develop a boundary-referenced protocol that measures each process with its own estimand. We apply it to three Chinese greenfield hub airports: Beijing Daxing, Chengdu Tianfu and Qingdao Jiaodong. Annual Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) maps for 2013–2025 were built from Landsat 8/9 composites that share one seasonal window and require three clear observations per pixel-year. A single pooled principal-component transform was used for each airport. Each pixel was referenced to its signed distance from the operational perimeter. Change was the post-opening mean minus a pre-construction baseline, adjusted by a control ring 15–20 km beyond the perimeter. Inference used a spatial-block bootstrap and one-sided non-inferiority tests in twelve off-site bands. Control-adjusted RSEI inside the perimeter declined by 0.36, 0.49 and 0.27, and this result held across compositing, principal-component and covariate-balancing choices. RSEI rose by 0.22–0.35 across the perimeter, more than ten times the largest step at 101 placebo boundaries, whereas the break-point location was site-specific and imprecise. Off-site decline was largest within 3 km of the perimeter (−0.068, −0.091 and − 0.018). It occurred mainly on land that remained cropland and was corroborated by MODIS net primary productivity (NPP). Between 3 and 10 km the decline was small at Daxing (−0.020) and Jiaodong (−0.002) but persisted at Tianfu (−0.056). This extended Tianfu signal depended on compositing and detrending and was not reproduced by NPP. Near-field cropland-status transition exceeded the regional background at Tianfu and Jiaodong, and about half of the cropland lost within 3 km became impervious surface. Boundary-referenced estimands thus separate a large on-site loss from a smaller, partly site-specific near-boundary response that a fixed-radius footprint would merge.

title: Global patterns and projected shifts in factors influencing staple crop yield stability
abstract: Climate change is increasingly destabilizing global agricultural systems by amplifying climate variability and intensifying extreme weather and climate events, yet the factors associated with variation in crop yield stability remain insufficiently quantified. Using global crop-yield data at a 0.5° spatial resolution, we developed a multilevel framework integrating random forest modeling and SHAP-based interpretation of predictor contributions at the variable, factor-category, and contribution-direction levels. We quantified associations of climate, management, and soil factors with yield stability in winter wheat, spring wheat, soybean, and maize, and assessed potential shifts in the leading predictors under three future climate scenarios. Historical yield stability exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Areas with low stability (yield stability <4) accounted for 13.3%, 30.1%, 0.86%, and 8.03% of the cultivated areas of winter wheat, spring wheat, soybean, and maize, respectively, and were concentrated mainly in low- to mid-latitudes and hot, dry transition zones. Mean climate was the leading factor category associated with historical stability in winter wheat, spring wheat, and soybean, whereas climate variability contributed more prominently for maize. Under future scenarios, global mean yield stability during 2031–2100 was projected to decline by 6–33%, 11–34%, and 13–41% under SSP1–RCP2.6, SSP2–RCP4.5, and SSP5–RCP8.5, respectively. The area fraction in which climate variability or extremes made the largest SHAP contribution increased by more than 30% relative to the historical period, with the greatest expansion under SSP5–RCP8.5. Although management–soil contributions partially offset negative climate contributions in some regions, the projections suggest that maintaining historical conditions may be insufficient to counter future climatic risks. Overall, our results reveal a systematic shift in the leading correlates of yield stability from mean climate toward climate variability and extremes, highlighting escalating risks to global food security.

title: Life-cycle carbon emission accounting and intensity assessment for coal mining areas of Liulin, China: from source identification to simplified quantitative modeling
abstract: In response to the global imperative for carbon mitigation, decarbonization of the coal industry is essential for achieving carbon neutrality. This study developed a simplified quantitative model that avoids the complexities of component-based emission-factor calculations while maintaining acceptable accuracy. A comprehensive life-cycle assessment (LCA) of carbon emissions from coal mining areas was conducted, encompassing the construction ( E C ), operation ( E O ), and regeneration ( E R ) phases. Results show strong heterogeneity among life-cycle stages, among which E O is the dominant contributor, accounting for 79.07%–88.80% of total emissions. Among ten identified emission sources, gas leakage emissions ( E CG , E OG , and E RG ) contribute over 90% of the total, forming a clear bipolar distribution relative to other sources. Carbon emissions also exhibit distinct temporal characteristics: E C and E R show emission peaks driven by intensive human activities, whereas E O follows a pattern of rapid growth, prolonged stability, and gradual decline. To simplify carbon accounting, a linear relationship was established between carbon emission intensity ( I ) and raw coal output ( Q coal ). Construction ( I C ) and regeneration ( I R ) intensities increase linearly with Q coal , while operational intensity ( I O ) remains constant at 52,993.57 tCO 2 /10 4 t coal regardless of production scale. For high-gas mines, incorporating gas content ( C ) and drainage rate ( R ) as correction variables reduces the model error to 13.28%. The model also demonstrates strong transferability across regions, with absolute boundary errors ranging from -2.74% to 5.85%. This “output-intensity” model establishes a standardized system for life-cycle carbon accounting in coal mining areas, providing a generalizable framework for carbon footprint monitoring and regional management decision-making.

title: Uncovering spatiotemporal dynamics and directional shifts in habitat suitability for migratory locusts using ensemble SDMs
abstract: Migratory locust habitats in arid and semi-arid grasslands are shaped by heat, moisture, and vegetation changes. To characterise their interannual habitat-suitability dynamics, we applied a locust-specific environmental framework and ensemble species distribution models (SDMs) to assess annual patterns of habitat suitability across China–Kazakhstan grasslands during 2015–2024 for Calliptamus italicus , locusta migratoria migratoria , and Gomphocerus sibiricus . Centroid and standard deviation ellipse (SDE) metrics tracked shifts in habitat position, extent, and orientation. The ensemble models showed relatively stable performance across 2015–2024 (AUC-ROC: 0.84–0.96; TSS: 0.60–0.87; kappa: 0.39–0.84), with low interannual variation in AUC-ROC (SD: 0.01–0.02), TSS (SD: 0.02–0.05), and kappa (SD: 0.02–0.07). Temperature, precipitation, and moisture repeatedly showed high relative contributions across the annual models, with some exceeding 40%. Suitable habitats were generally persistent, but trajectories differed among species. Highly suitable habitat for C. italicus accounted for 8.8–11.9% of the study area and shifted from contraction to expansion; L. migratoria migratoria accounted for 4.8–12.3% and net expansion and spatial redistribution; and G. sibiricus occupied 5.3–8.6%, the smallest proportion. Centroid displacement and SDE analyses revealed directional rather than random habitat shifts. Species-specific habitats covered 24.96% of the study area, whereas the shared core habitat jointly suitable for all three species accounted for 3.66% and was concentrated along transboundary mountain–foothill corridors. These persistent habitats, expansion fronts, and shared core areas indicate where coordinated cross-border monitoring and early warning could be prioritised

title: Corrigendum to “Coupling minimum cumulative resistance and circuit theory for intangible cultural heritage corridor construction: A case study of the Jin-Shaan gorge” [Ecol. Indicat. 192 (2026) 115642]
Desertification control and carbon sequestration in temperate sandy lands: synergies and trade-offs
abstract: While land desertification control (SDG 15.3) and climate change mitigation (SDG 13) are generally considered synergistic, their trade-offs in heavily human-modified temperate monsoon sandy ecosystems remain unclear. Focusing on the southern margin of China's Horqin Sandy Land, this study quantified the spatiotemporal synergies and trade-offs between desertification control and carbon sequestration (2000−2020) using a cross-classification matrix coupling an improved Mediterranean Desertification and Land Use (MEDALUS)-Environmentally Sensitive Area Index (ESAI) with soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics. Results indicate: (1) A spatially divergent pattern emerged. The central-western sandy lands successfully established an extensive resilient baseline (“Stable”), interspersed with localized carbon accumulation patches (“Synergy”). Conversely, the southeastern agro-pastoral ecotone suffered a contiguous “Double loss” (heightened environmental sensitivity and carbon depletion), spatially corresponding to agricultural intensification and potential groundwater overdraft. (2) In some marginal ecotones, patches with reduced desertification sensitivity exhibited constrained soil carbon accumulation. This spatial mismatch suggests that early high-density afforestation might have exceeded local soil moisture carrying capacities, posing a hidden “green desert” risk that overdraws long-term ecological resilience. (3) Zones subject to severe composite wind-water erosion frequently overlapped with delayed SOC responses despite observed surface ecological improvements (a potential “time-lag” effect). This alignment indicates that erosion likely compromises the physical soil carbon protection, delaying the translation of ecological recovery into long-term carbon sinks. Consequently, dryland spatial planning should move beyond focusing solely on apparent vegetation coverage. Adopting differentiated Nature-based Solutions (NbS) governed by strict soil moisture constraints and drought early-warning systems is essential to achieve SDG synergies in global drylands.

title: An indicator-based assessment of cultural ecosystem service structure in coastal recreational spaces using social media data and large language model
abstract: Understanding the compositional and structural characteristics of cultural ecosystem services (CES) is essential for enhancing the multifunctionality and sustainable governance of coastal recreational spaces. However, existing studies mainly focused on CES composition while paying limited attention to CES structure. This study investigated the composition, structure, and their explanatory factors of 148 coastal recreational spaces within a 10-km coastal buffer zone of Qingdao, China. Social media reviews from three platforms between 2023 and 2025 were classified into eight CES categories using a large language model (LLM)-based multi-label classification framework. Six structural indicators, including abundance, intensity, richness, diversity, evenness, and dominance, were quantified based on community ecology theory. The Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) was employed to identify the explanatory factors of CES composition and structure. The results showed that recreational experience (33.07%), aesthetic appreciation (32.05%), and mental healing (11.55%) were the most frequently expressed CES categories across the social media reviews. Significant spatial heterogeneity was observed across space types and coastal gradients. Near-shore recreational spaces exhibited higher CES abundance, richness, diversity, and evenness, whereas far-coastal spaces were characterized by higher dominance. Distance to coastline, area, and transportation accessibility emerged as the primary explanatory factors of CES structure. By integrating multi-platform social media data and LLM, this study advances CES assessment from individual service to structural analysis and provides practical insights for the management of coastal recreational spaces.

title: Translating tree-ring evidence into spatially continuous estimates of severe growth-decline risk across black spruce forests using Landsat time series
abstract: Although climate-driven growth decline is well documented from tree-ring studies, translating this knowledge into spatially continuous information on forest vulnerability remains a challenge. To address this limitation, we developed a scalable approach integrating tree-ring data, climate variables, and Landsat-derived metrics to estimate severe growth-decline probability as a spatially explicit indicator of reduced tree vigor and vulnerability in black spruce (Picea mariana) across the Canadian boreal forest from 1988 to 2019. Severe declines were defined from multi-year tree-ring growth change using regionally calibrated thresholds. We then modelled severe growth-decline probability as a function of climate and Landsat-derived predictors, evaluated performance using repeated site-level cross-validation, and generated annual, spatially continuous predictions to identify recurrent high-risk areas.We found that severe growth-decline probability was highest in warm, moisture-limited climates, whereas the marginal effects of climate variation were stronger and more consistent under intermediate to moist conditions and weaker or contrasting in drier regimes. Repeated cross-validation showed moderate but consistent ability of the model to rank locations by severe growth decline probability (mean Spearman’s ρ = 0.40; mean AUC = 0.70). Out-of-fold calibration indicated that observed severe-decline frequency increased monotonically with predicted-probability classes, supporting model calibration. Landsat-derived metrics improved predictive performance beyond climate alone (Δ Spearman’s ρ = +0.08; Δ AUC = +0.08), indicating that spectral trajectories helped refine spatial discrimination of decline probability.These results demonstrate the capacity of the approach to generate spatially explicit estimates of severe growth-decline probability across broad boreal landscapes, supporting wall-to-wall assessment of forest vulnerability to changing climate.

title: Multifactor habitat modeling and circuit theory reveal transboundary conservation gaps and connectivity bottlenecks in François' langur (Trachypithecus francoisi)
abstract: Habitat fragmentation induced by global climate change and intensive anthropogenic disturbances severely impact landscape connectivity, forest regeneration, and the survival of threatened species. Here, we used the Endangered François' langur as a focal conservation surrogate for fragmented transboundary karst landscapes and integrated multi-source environmental variables, ensemble species distribution modeling, and circuit theory to evaluate habitat dynamics and potential ecological connectivity networks. The results indicate that climatic conditions including mean diurnal temperature range (Bio2), isothermality (Bio3), and precipitation of the coldest quarter (Bio19) delineate the potential geographic boundaries of the species, while an expanding human footprint continues to result in severe fragmentation of their current suitable habitat. Future scenario projections showed that climate change is expected to trigger significant habitat contraction and create a severe spatial mismatch between areas of remaining suitable habitat for François' langurs and their existing system of protected areas. Furthermore, circuit theory revealed distinct spatial heterogeneity in their remaining habitat, which is characterized by a compact northern network of relatively lower-resistance and more spatially continuous corridors and a loose southern network of long-distance corridors restricted by severe spatial bottlenecks. We recommend prioritizing the creation of a wildlife management plan that constructs crossing structures at their northern ecological barriers and establishing a transboundary conservation network along the Sino-Vietnamese border to safeguard their highly vulnerable southern ecological connectivity network. This study offers a quantitative framework for the proactive creation of spatially explicit conservation measures to protect threatened primate populations facing severe habitat fragmentation.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of urban flood resilience in urban agglomerations using explainable machine learning: a case study of the middle reaches of the Yangtze River urban agglomeration
abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization are intensifying urban flood risks. Improving urban flood resilience (UFR) requires identifying key influencing factors, their effective ranges, interactions, and critical thresholds. This study examines the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River Urban Agglomeration using multi-source data from 2012 to 2023. A Driving forces–Pressure–State–Impact–Response (DPSIR) framework was developed to assess UFR. Spatial statistics and the Space-Time Cube were used to reveal its spatiotemporal evolution. XGBoost, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and partial dependence plots (PDPs) were applied to identify nonlinear thresholds and interactions among influencing factors. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was further used to examine structural associations between influencing factors and DPSIR dimensions and among the dimensions themselves. Results show an overall improvement in UFR, with Wuhan, Changsha, and Nanchang forming major high-resilience cores. Low-value lock-in persisted around Wuhan, whereas Changsha and Nanchang exhibited outward-spreading spatial patterns. Technology level (Tech) and fiscal self-sufficiency rate (FSR) remained the most important factors, while most key associations showed clear nonlinear and threshold characteristics. Tech–FSR interactions were consistently the strongest, but the interaction structure gradually expanded to include natural factors such as elevation (DEM) and slope (SLO). SEM results revealed generally stable but stage-dependent structural associations, with natural geographic factors becoming more strongly associated with the State dimension in later years. These findings clarify the spatiotemporal evolution, nonlinear influences, and structural relationships of UFR, providing evidence for cross-regional flood governance and targeted resource allocation in urban agglomerations.

title: Unpacking the relationships between compact urban form and green space exposure: Machine learning evidence from Shanghai
abstract: The tension between urban densification and green space availability is a critical concern in compact development, yet how integrated urban form features shape multi-dimensional green space exposure remains underexplored. Based on 2358 residential blocks within Shanghai ' s outer ring road, this study aims to fill this gap by investigating the nonlinear and interactive relationships between compact urban form features and green space availability (GSA), park green accessibility (PGA), and street green visibility (SGV). Using Amap ' s real-time accessibility model, a DeepLab streetscape segmentation model, and an XGBoost-SHAP machine learning model, our findings reveal heterogeneous relationships between population density, development density, and green space exposure. Development density exhibits a predominantly “L-shaped” relationship with GSA, with this negative pattern becoming less pronounced at higher levels of land-use diversity. By contrast, population density is associated with lower PGA and thus better accessibility. Street connectivity is also associated with lower PGA and higher SGV. However, interaction analyses reveal that these relationships are context-dependent, with favorable associations weakening in highly populated or densely developed areas. We situate these findings within China ' s urban development and green management frameworks, highlighting green-inclusive, mixed-use development and human-scale urban form design to foster a sustainable urban future.

title: Inter-domain microbial networks reveal keystone taxa as bio-indicators for metal(loid)s and pesticide pollution in Mediterranean wetlands
abstract: Mediterranean wetlands, critical ecosystems that rely on complex microbial communities to drive essential biogeochemical processes, are threatened by increasing pressure from human activity. We conducted a comparative analysis of inter-domain microbial networks across six Mediterranean wetlands (Algeria, Morocco, Portugal, Spain, Tunisia lake, and Tunisia river) including freshwater, saline, and hypersaline ecosystems exposed to varying levels of metal(loid)s and pesticide contents as revealed by the pressure index (PI mean metal(loid)s 2.74 ± 2.00; and pesticides 1.25 ± 0.98). By integrating 16S/18S rRNA gene sequencing with chemical data, we demonstrated that inferred inter-domain microbial co-occurrence networks exhibited consistently high modularity across the six wetlands (mean 0.85 ± 0.09; range: 0.71–0.94). Networks included a mean of 574.67 ± 334.79 ASVs (249–1128 ASVs per network), and keystone taxa, often representing <1% of relative abundance, were identified in all sites (1–7 taxa per network). Functional prediction suggested that keystone taxa might harbor functional traits associated with pollutant degradation, redox processes, and trophic interactions. Consistently, the keystone taxa, often not the most abundant, were correlated to salinity, and pollutant (metal(loid)s: PI up to 5 and pesticides: PI up to 2.54) content, indicating that they likely play key roles in biogeochemical cycling, pollutant tolerance, and trophic regulation. The structural centrality of keystone taxa in microbial networks may reflect functional traits and trophic interactions compatible with environmental constraints, including those associated with PI. In addition to revealing the ecological role of keystone taxa, our results provide quantitative support to their use as potential bioindicators for reporting ecosystem status as they exhibited features strongly linked with environmental conditions.

title: Integrating environmental DNA and species distribution modelling reveals the spatiotemporal distribution and habitat dynamics of the Chinese sturgeon (Acipenser sinensis)
abstract: The Chinese sturgeon ( Acipenser sinensis ), a flagship species of the Yangtze River basin, is among the world's most endangered anadromous fishes. Traditional monitoring approaches largely rely on field observations, which are labor-intensive and inefficient. In the present study, we conducted general environmental DNA (eDNA) surveys at 44 sites and depth-stratified sampling at 4 representative regions across the currently recognized riverine range of Acipenser sinensis in the Yangtze River. eDNA-derived occurrence records were used as presence data in MaxEnt species distribution modelling. The model was used to identify current suitable habitats and project future changes in potential habitat across the basin. The results showed that the Chinese sturgeon eDNA was widely detected throughout this study area, and redundancy analysis suggested that COD Mn is the environmental variable most strongly associated with the eDNA occurrence. The final MaxEnt model achieved a mean test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.809, with current habitat suitability concentrated in the middle and lower Yangtze River network. Slope and precipitation seasonality contributed most to the model, whereas temperature seasonality and annual mean temperature had the highest permutation importance. Future projections indicated habitat expansion, with all currently suitable reaches retained and suitable river-network length increasing by 31.69–53.96%. These projections provide a spatial basis for prioritizing persistent suitable reaches and maintaining connectivity to areas that may become suitable under future climate conditions. Thus, the eDNA-based occurrence detection offers a non-invasive, less labor-intensive way to identify distribution and suitable habitat for threatened species.

title: Assessing grassland herb richness through remote sensing
abstract: Assessing herb richness of grasslands on a large scale is important for monitoring nature qualityand biodiversity. Here, we present an approach based on remote sensing, which allows yearlypredictions with a reasonable accuracy. As an indicator of herb richness, the so-called Q valueis used, ranging from 1 (very herb-poor) to 6 (very herb-rich). Based on an observational dataset of over 1,000 parcels, we achieve prediction accuracies of around 0.7 units. Although thisaccuracy is already very useful for many applications, we expect that with a suitably designedsampling campaign, sustained for a few years, it can be improved further.
